title: Capability catalog
text:
# Capability catalog

Every action from the current machine-readable catalog, including its HTTP route, typed client method, terminal command, and failure classes. Health is public; the runtime protects its other API routes with the private bearer token. The documentation assistant never calls these APIs.

const REPLAN = "Create the next plan revision to continue.";

// First match wins, so specific reasons precede the generic words they contain.
const STEPS: Step[] = [
  { match: /rejected this token/, step: "Check the LUUNA_API_TOKEN value the service was started with, then connect again." },
  { match: /did not answer|could not be reached/, step: "" },
  { match: /shutting down/, step: "The runtime is stopping and admits no new work. Start it again with the same data directory and token; this panel reconnects by itself, then retry." },
  { match: /runtime request failed \(http 422\)|failed to deserialize the json body/, step: "The runtime could not read this request: a field is missing, misspelled or of the wrong type. A manifest draft must follow schemas/project.schema.json." },
  { match: /revision conflict/, step: "The record changed since this panel read it. Refresh, and run Discover again before confirming a manifest draft for the next revision." },
  { match: IDENTITY, step: "If the change is intended, use Rebind repository in the project panel, then confirm a manifest revision whose remote matches; otherwise restore the registered checkout." },
  { match: BASELINE_RUNNING, step: "Wait for the running baseline to settle, or cancel it from the baseline list, then run it again." },

Runtime configuration
text:
# Runtime configuration

The runtime reads the process environment, not a .env file automatically. Never use a documented example as an actual secret. The docs assistant has its own separate server key and cannot access runtime credentials.

| Setting | Purpose and default |
| --- | --- |
| `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` | Required private bearer token of at least 32 visible ASCII characters, with no spaces or line breaks; provide the same token to the client |
| `LUUNA_PI_COMMAND` | Pi executable, default `pi`; may be an absolute path. On Windows an npm `pi.cmd` shim found through PATH and PATHEXT is started as `node.exe` with its `dist/bundle/cli.js`; other batch launchers are refused, so point this at `node.exe` and pass `cli.js` in `LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON` for any other layout |
| `LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON` | Optional JSON array of launcher arguments, useful with a direct Node executable |
| `LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER`, `LUUNA_PI_MODEL` | Explicit provider/model defaults; may also be selected per run in the client |

ADR 0001: desktop-first delivery with one runtime
text:
# ADR 0001: desktop-first delivery with one runtime

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: accepted.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The original reference starts with browser/TUI clients. The later desktop proposal chooses Tauri while preserving full-v1 capabilities. Without a delivery decision, implementations could create competing backends or claim client parity too early.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

Deliver Tauri 2 with React/TypeScript first. Keep authoritative policy in a separate Rust service, using Tokio, Axum, and SQLite. Pi RPC supplies the agent engine; Luuna does not implement a competing model/tool loop. Shared HTTP contracts and event semantics must allow future browser and TUI clients.

Browser/TUI capability parity remains a full-v1 requirement. Desktop-first changes sequence, not that obligation. A single-repository foundation is M0/M1 evidence, not full-v1 completion.

title: Alternatives and consequences
text:
## Alternatives and consequences

A browser-first client remains feasible later. A Tauri-only business layer would couple policies to a client and is rejected. Do not fork OpenCode for the initial implementation. Prove a real Pi vertical slice before expanding orchestration or UI scope. Native desktop builds and distribution require platform evidence beyond frontend compilation.

title: ADR 0002: maintained Luuna component distributions in a monorepo
text:
# ADR 0002: maintained Luuna component distributions in a monorepo

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: accepted for the foundation; hosted repository extraction deferred.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The repository imported Seeds, Mulch, and Canopy source with original package identities, repository links, and MIT notices. The architecture audit recommends separate maintained repositories, while an upstream-only dependency would reduce maintenance. The owner explicitly chose Luuna-branded distributions integrated through compatible underlying APIs.

Separate repository creation was attempted but the available GitHub integration lacks creation permission. On October 16, 2026, the owner explicitly directed that the current work be pushed to the existing `brodynelly/luuna` repository and that separation be handled later. This is the current delivery decision, not a task waiting for a new creation credential. Deleting source in anticipation of an unverified migration would risk losing a reproducible foundation. Rebranding a package also does not prove it has been published.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

Keep the application and these independently identified CLI packages together in `brodynelly/luuna`. Continue product implementation here; do not create component repositories or remove these directories as an onboarding prerequisite.

| Component | Source ancestry | Directory | Package | Primary commands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Luuna Missions | Seeds | `components/missions/` | `@luuna/missions-cli` | `luuna-missions`, `lm` |
| Luuna Atlas | Mulch | `components/atlas/` | `@luuna/atlas-cli` | `luuna-atlas`, `la` |
| Luuna Beacon | Canopy | `components/beacon/` | `@luuna/beacon-cli` | `luuna-beacon`, `lb` |

Preserve compatible underlying APIs and data formats. Legacy commands may remain compatibility aliases. Preserve upstream copyright, MIT licenses, source provenance, and notices. The product and new Luuna contributions use MIT. Names are distribution identities, not permission to rewrite the tools in Rust.

Keep each tool behind a versioned adapter boundary. Do not automatically consume its task databases, personal histories, prompts, or package-local instructions as Luuna policy. Nested installation lifecycle scripts must not change the root repository's Git hooks configuration.

title: Later extraction
text:
## Later extraction

Separate hosted repositories are deferred. Revisit extraction when the owner chooses to resume it and it improves maintenance; it does not block M0, M1, or subsequent product milestones. Before removal from the monorepo:

1. Verify destination ownership, read/write access, and release responsibility.
2. Preserve source history/provenance and upstream notices; verify the migrated revision.
3. Establish component CI, compatible APIs, pinned consumers, and release credentials.
4. Test installation/integration from the actual destination.
5. Remove duplicated source only after those checks pass and update dependency/setup records.

The local directory layout does not claim separate repositories or registry packages exist. No publication or remote resource creation is implied by this ADR.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

The initial repository stays reproducible and changes remain reviewable. Luuna accepts responsibility for testing its branded distributions. Adapter behavior tests remain distinct from component suites. Private authoring histories and stale imported task records are removed from current tracking after review and are not product fixtures; removing them does not erase Git history.

title: ADR 0003: Missions ticket authority and SQLite execution state
text:
# ADR 0003: Missions ticket authority and SQLite execution state

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: accepted.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The original architecture assigns work records to Seeds, while the desktop proposal lists SQLite ticket tables. Two writable copies would allow stale approvals and lost updates when tickets are edited outside Luuna. Luuna Missions is the maintained Seeds-derived tool.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

After integration, Missions is authoritative for ticket intent, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and source revision. Luuna writes those fields through a serialized adapter with optimistic revision checks. SQLite stores a derived ticket projection and is authoritative for Luuna's immutable plans, approvals, runs, attempts, evidence, events, and publication state.

A minimal local SQLite ticket record is allowed for M0/M1 before the Missions adapter exists. It must be identified as temporary and must not claim external synchronization. Migration/reconciliation must preserve identifiers and revisions before enabling the adapter. Do not enable independent writes to both stores.

title: Consequences and validation
text:
## Consequences and validation

Bind a plan to a ticket source revision. Detect external edits and reject stale writes or scheduling until reconciled; do not silently overwrite them. Adapter tests must cover duplicate delivery, revision conflict, unavailable Missions, and recovery after an uncertain write. An external ticket status is not evidence that a Luuna execution gate passed.

title: ADR 0004: independent service lifetime and explicit shutdown
text:
# ADR 0004: independent service lifetime and explicit shutdown

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: accepted development contract; packaged supervision strategy pending platform proof. Amended 2026-10-21: the implementation note and the lifecycle hardening amendment below.

title: Context
text:
## Context

Runs must survive client disconnection. A desktop sidecar may inherit the application's lifetime, so merely spawning one does not establish runtime independence.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

The Rust service owns runs, workers, durable events, and lifecycle transitions. In development, launch it as an explicitly managed foreground process separate from the desktop. The client discovers/connects to an authenticated loopback endpoint and resumes event delivery by cursor. Window close, refresh, or dropped SSE does not request cancellation or service shutdown.

Shutdown is an explicit authenticated service action or an operating-system termination path. Stop or terminate only owned workers, preserve artifacts and work, and durably record interrupted attempts. On restart, reconcile incomplete attempts before scheduling or publishing; never infer success from a vanished process. Cancellation is a distinct run command and is idempotent.

Implementation note (2026-10-21): until this date the runtime's Ctrl+C/SIGTERM path reused the cancellation signal and so recorded work stopped by shutdown as `cancelled`, a terminal state with no recovery, while a hard kill left the same work `interrupted` and resumable. The runtime now sets a shutdown flag before signalling owned workers; every settlement that would have recorded `cancelled` records `interrupted` with the reason prefixed "interrupted by runtime shutdown" (demo runs, baselines, writers, candidate checks and reviews), so an orderly stop is never worse for the developer than a crash. Spend accounting is unchanged: a model turn stopped mid-flight still reserve

title: Decision
text:
s the remaining approved cost. The desktop client treats a lost runtime as an outage shown beside the connection state, reconnects by itself, and reloads every panel when the runtime answers again.

Amendment (2026-10-21, lifecycle hardening): an orderly stop always ends. Every step is bounded: admitted mutation requests drain for at most five seconds (a request that never finishes its body cannot hold the stop open; work it registers later is still signalled), owned work settles for at most five seconds, and open connections drain for at most ten seconds, after which the process exits with status 1. Every SSE stream ends when shutdown begins, so a follower of an idle workflow no longer keeps the process, its port and the data-directory lock alive. A second Ctrl+C or SIGTERM exits at once (status 130) and leaves unsettled work to restart recovery, as the default signal action would. On Windows, Ctrl+Break, console close and system shutdown also take the orderly path, best effort because Windows ends the process within seconds; supervisors use the ADR 0010 endpoint. Once shutdown begins, every mutation is refused with 503 `{"error":"runtime is shutting down"}`. Each owned worker runs under a supervisor: a worker that panics settles its run `failed` with an internal-error reason, releases its concurrency slot, abandons an active lease with its files preserved, and reserves unreported spend exactly as restart recovery does (a run

title: Decision
text: ning attempt takes the remaining approved time and cost; a candidate stage keeps its elapsed time and a review also the remaining cost), so no retry can exceed the approved budgets. Cancellation of a run whose worker already returned answers with the settled state instead of an error. A `failed` or `interrupted` workflow keeps its event stream open, because repair and re-validation continue on the same run id. On Unix an existing data directory and its `worktrees` directory are made owner-only at startup. Individual check results stopped by shutdown still carry the executor's `cancelled` check status beneath the `interrupted` baseline or candidate; recording `interrupted` at the check level belongs to the baseline and candidate check recording, not to this lifecycle path.

title: Consequences and validation
text:
## Consequences and validation

The authenticated action and scheduling-admission implementation are specified
by [ADR 0010](0010-authenticated-service-shutdown.md). Windows development launch
and clean-stop evidence is recorded in `docs/WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md`; installed
service supervision and signed distribution remain distinct requirements.

Distribution needs a tested Mac/Windows startup, supervision, token storage, and shutdown strategy. A Tauri sidecar is allowed only if measured lifecycle behavior satisfies the contract. Validate disconnect/reconnect, cancellation, forced process exit, restart reconciliation, and no duplicate external side effects. Do not claim these properties from unit fixtures alone.

title: ADR 0005: project-scoped ticket creation
text:
# ADR 0005: project-scoped ticket creation

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: accepted.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The original API uses project-scoped creation, while the desktop proposal includes a global `/tickets` example and asks the implementer to choose one route. Implementing both without a contract would introduce ambiguous ownership and duplicate behavior.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

Use **`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`** as the single canonical create-ticket route. Resolve and validate project identity from the path; reject conflicting body identity or unknown repositories. Subsequent operations may address global ticket IDs, such as `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans`.

The runtime applies authentication, input validation, an idempotency key for repeatable delivery, and ticket revision guards where appropriate. Before Missions integration, persistence follows the temporary model in ADR 0003; afterward creation goes through the Missions adapter.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

Do not add `POST /api/v1/tickets` as a second creation route. Update generated contracts/clients from the implemented canonical route. Verify project isolation, malformed input, duplicate requests, and stale revisions as the API is implemented. This decision establishes a contract, not a claim that the endpoint already exists.

title: ADR 0006: read-only repository import, machine registry and project event stream
text:
# ADR 0006: read-only repository import, machine registry and project event stream

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: accepted; amended 2026-10-21 (identity robustness, explicit rebind, registration overlap rules and inspection hardening; see the amendment below, which supersedes points 1, 2 and 4 where they differ).

title: Context
text:
## Context

M2a registers an existing repository, proposes its check recipes and persists a confirmed manifest without changing the developer's checkout. The current architecture separates the versioned manifest from machine-specific paths and requires that discovery propose commands rather than execute repository text. The event envelope and SQLite outbox were defined for runs, and project-level facts had no durable stream.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Inspection is read-only and executes nothing from the repository.** `luuna-git` shells out to the host `git` with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `--no-pager`, and `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, every inherited `GIT_*` variable cleared, and every configured `filter.<driver>` clean/smudge/process command overridden to empty with `required=false`, so `status`, `rev-parse`, `rev-list`, `symbolic-ref`, `for-each-ref` and `remote get-url` leave the index and working tree byte-identical and cannot be redirected or made to execute repository-selected commands. Output is capped per stream while it is read. No fetch, push, checkout, hook or filter ever runs. Remote URLs are redacted (userinfo, query and fragment) before they are stored or returned.

title: Decision
text:
2. **Repository identity** is the redacted `origin` fetch URL, the redacted push URL when it differs, and the sorted parentless commits reachable from HEAD (empty for shallow clones, which must then have a remote; more than 64 roots is rejected). Filesystem origins (paths or `file:` URLs) are machine-specific and are observed as no remote. Registration stores that identity; discovery and confirmation re-observe the path and reject a different repository at the same path with a conflict instead of silently re-binding. A repository without a portable remote carries an explicit `local:` identity in the manifest, and confirmation enforces that.
3. **The manifest is machine-independent and hashed with `luuna-json-v1`.** Local paths, observed commits, branches and dirty state live only in the private SQLite machine registry (`repositories` table) and in evidence records. `PlanRevision.manifest_hash` refers to this manifest hash.

title: Decision
text:
4. **Discovery proposes; the developer confirms.** `luuna-discovery` reads a bounded set of well-known manifest files and proposes recipes as executable plus argument arrays with file-level evidence, observed/inferred confidence and open questions. Shell interpreters require an explicit `shell` capability, absolute executables are rejected, and the proposal is stored as a `Discovery` record, never executed. Confirmation requires the project's current revision, revision `n+1`, an identity match, the observed remote and an observed default branch, and records the exact HEAD commit per repository as the base.
5. **Project-scoped events reuse the run event envelope.** They are stored in `project_events` with their own monotonic sequence, `project_id` set to the project, and `run_id` set to the stream identifier `project:<project_id>`. Clients deduplicate and replay them with the same cursor rules as run events, and `manifest.confirmed` carries the complete manifest so replay reconstructs the confirmed map.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

The routes `POST /api/v1/projects`, `GET /api/v1/projects[/{id}]`, `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/discover`, `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/manifest` and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events` implement the contract table in `docs/07-contracts.md`. `schemas/project.schema.json` gains an optional `cwd` per check (default `.`). Nothing in this slice enables repository writes, command execution or the storage guard's removal; M2b supplies the executor and baseline evidence, and M2c the approved writer. A multi-repository manifest is accepted by the contracts but relationships and integration remain M4 work.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening
text:
## Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening

An audit found that legitimate changes made a registered project permanently unusable while the errors advised a re-registration the API refuses, and that parts of point 1 did not hold. The rules below keep rejecting a different repository at a registered path; they stop treating a machine-local spelling or a grown history as one, and give the developer an explicit, evented way to re-point a registration.

1. **Remote identity is the configured URL, compared by equivalence.** Inspection reads the first `remote.origin.url` and `remote.origin.pushurl` values instead of `git remote get-url`, which applies machine-local `url.<base>.insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf` rewrites. Two remotes are the same when only their spelling differs: scp-like `user@host:/path` and `ssh://host/path` (also `git+ssh`/`ssh+git`), `http` and `https`, the user name, a default port, host case and a trailing `/` or `.git`. A different transport family (HTTPS versus SSH), host, non-default port or path is a different remote. Manifest confirmation compares the manifest's remote the same way, so the manifest stays machine-independent. A registration recorded earlier with a rewritten URL reports a mismatch once; a rebind (point 3) records the configured URL.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening
text:
2. **A registered root set must be contained in the observed one.** Registration (and a rebind) still records the parentless commits reachable from HEAD, at most 64. Every later observation records the roots reachable from HEAD or any local branch (at most 4096) and must contain each registered root. Added roots, from a merge of unrelated history (`git subtree add`) or a checked-out orphan branch, are the same repository. A registered root that no local branch or HEAD reaches any more is a different repository or rewritten history and is rejected as before.
3. **An explicit rebind is the only way to change a binding.** `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repositories/{repository_id}/rebind` takes `{"local_path"?: "<absolute root>"}` (the registered path when omitted), inspects that checkout read-only and replaces the machine-registry entry. Sending the request is the developer's confirmation. It records `repository.rebound` with the old and new path and identity, the new observation and whether the confirmed manifest's remote still matches; an unchanged binding records nothing. It is refused while a run of the project is queued, running, exploring or implementing, because that work may be using the checkout. The manifest is not changed. Base commits, baselines and approvals stay bound to exact commits, and a manifest whose remote no longer matches must be confirmed again; confirmation enforces the match. Every identity-mismatch error

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening
text:
names this route, and a vanished checkout's error names it with `local_path`. Archiving a project is still not implemented.
4. **A checkout is registered once and never overlaps Luuna's data directory.** Registration and rebind refuse a canonical path already registered by any project with 409. They refuse with 422, naming `LUUNA_DATA_DIR`, a repository inside the data directory (where Luuna-owned worktrees live) and a repository that contains the data directory (a runtime started inside the checkout would otherwise put its private database and worktrees there).
5. **Filters configured in submodules are neutralised too.** The `filter.<driver>` names are also collected from each populated submodule's own configuration, nested submodules included. Inspection finds the submodules from the index gitlinks with a streamed `ls-files --stage`, and refuses more than 256 populated ones; recorded but uninitialised submodules are not counted, because Git does not recurse into them. Submodules nested more than 8 levels deep are refused as well, because their drivers would be unknown. The names are passed as `-c` overrides, which Git propagates to the `status` it runs inside each submodule, so uncommitted submodule content still makes the checkout dirty. Configuration is listed with `-z`, so subsection names are read exactly. Git splits a `-c` setting at its first `=`, so no override can name a driver whose name contains `=`; such configur

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening
text:
ation is refused with a reason instead of being left to run.
6. **The output cap stops a command at once.** When either stream passes the cap, both reads end, the child is killed and the error is "git output too large". Registration and discovery return it as 422 with advice, instead of a 30-second stall reported as a timeout.
7. **Git's reason is kept.** A failed repository probe is "not a Git repository" only when Git says so. Git's dubious-ownership refusal is reported with advice to add the path to `safe.directory` in the developer's global configuration; Luuna never changes that setting. Any other failure carries Git's own message. Only the line terminator is removed from `--show-toplevel`, so a root whose name ends in whitespace is accepted.
8. **Branches are read by full reference name.** `symbolic-ref` and `for-each-ref` output is stripped of exactly `refs/heads/` or `refs/remotes/origin/`. A tag with a branch's name therefore no longer turns `main` into `heads/main` or hides origin's HEAD. Confirmation also accepts a default branch that exists only as an `origin/<name>` remote-tracking ref, as in a fresh clone.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): identity robustness, explicit rebind and inspection hardening
text:
9. **Discovery asks instead of overstating.** A recipe whose evidence file has uncommitted changes, or whose checkout has too many changed paths to tell, is downgraded to `inferred` and raises an `uncommitted-evidence` question: baselines and Luuna worktrees use HEAD, not the working tree. No question promises a testing-prerequisite task, because none is implemented. Instead, the questions tell the developer to add and commit tests and rediscover, or to confirm a required recipe for an existing command. The local-only remote question names the rebind needed after a URL remote is added. `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events` also accepts `?limit=1..10000`, and a cursor above `i64::MAX` is a 400, not a 500.

PR 11 follow-up: SSH home-relative (`host:path`) and absolute (`host:/path` or
`ssh://host/path`) paths remain distinct. An identity-changing rebind withdraws
the current manifest hash while preserving its revision and append-only history.
Baseline, approval and execution remain closed until a new manifest is confirmed.
Moving the same identity alone does not withdraw confirmation.

title: ADR 0007: supervised check execution and baseline-bound implementation gate
text:
# ADR 0007: supervised check execution and baseline-bound implementation gate

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: accepted; amended 2026-10-21 (evidence hardening, below).

title: Context
text:
## Context

M2a records confirmed check recipes but executes nothing, and the storage layer rejected `Implementing` with a placeholder guard. R08 requires a usable testing setup and a passing baseline before feature work, and the validation chapter requires evidence that binds to recorded commits, environments and artifacts rather than to a model's claim.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **A recipe is an executable plus an argument array.** `luuna-executor` resolves the executable on `PATH` or as a repository-relative file under the registered root, verifies declared host capabilities against installed tools, runs in an explicit directory that must stay inside the root, applies the recipe's deadline, and owns the whole process group (Unix) so cancellation and timeouts reap descendants. The child, and every version probe, receives a cleared environment with Luuna configuration, `GIT_*` variables and anything credential-shaped removed. A descendant that keeps the output pipes open after the command exits is given a short grace, then the whole group is terminated and the check fails rather than hanging; cancellation and the deadline remain the recorded status whatever happens to capture. Windows has no process group here, so only the direct child is killed and a surviving descendant is named in the result's reason. Artifact directories and logs are created private (0700/0600 on Unix) whatever the parent directory or umask allows. Native execution keeps host permissions; the container profile is recorded as blocked until an isolation mechanism exists.

title: Decision
text:
2. **Every outcome is deterministic runtime evidence.** Exit 0 is `passed` only when no recognised test runner reported an empty suite; any non-zero exit, deadline or signal is `failed`; a missing executable, incapable host, dirty checkout, container profile or empty suite is `blocked`; cancellation and runtime restart are `cancelled` and `interrupted`. Output streams into bounded private artifacts whose SHA-256 digests are part of the record, and only short excerpts enter the event stream.
3. **A baseline is a run.** It uses the shared run lifecycle, durable events, replay, SSE, cancellation and restart interruption. It binds to a `BaselineIdentity` (manifest hash, repository, exact HEAD commit and tree) whose hash is each result's `candidate_hash`, and to an environment fingerprint derived from the resolved executables and their versions. A checkout with uncommitted changes is not an exact commit, so its baseline is blocked rather than measured, before any probe runs; the checkout is inspected again after the last check, and a pass is withheld (the baseline fails) if HEAD moved, any tracked file was modified or the identity changed while checks ran; untracked files a check creates (build caches, reports) do not change the recorded commit or tree and are recorded in a `checkout.untracked` event instead; Luuna-owned worktrees (M2c) will remove that limitation.

title: Decision
text:
4. **Implementation is entered only through `begin_implementation`.** Inside one write transaction it re-reads the durable approval, the bound plan, the project's current confirmed manifest and the latest baseline for every repository in the plan, and requires each baseline to be passed, bound to the plan's manifest hash and base commit, and recorded with the same environment fingerprint. Each required recipe must have its own passed result bound to the baseline's candidate hash, commit and fingerprint (optional results never count either way), and the baseline's run must have settled as `completed`; startup recovery interrupts a passed verdict whose run never settled, so the verdict/run crash window cannot authorize a writer. The placeholder guard is gone; a direct `Implementing` transition remains rejected.
5. **Artifacts are addressed by record identity.** `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{recipe}.{stdout|stderr}` serves the private log for a run the caller is authorised to see; no request names a filesystem path.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines` and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines` implement the baseline part of R08. Required recipes decide the verdict; optional recipes run on request and are recorded without affecting it. Empty-suite detection covers cargo, go, pytest and vitest/jest summaries and is a floor, not proof that a suite is meaningful. The first approved writer, worktree ownership and revalidation at scheduling time remain M2c.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text:
## Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening

An audit found checks whose evidence overstated what ran or what the executor contained. These rules now hold for baseline and candidate checks alike:

1. **Nothing a check started outlives its result.** After the direct child exits normally and its output drains, the executor terminates whatever is still in the check's process group (a server started with redirected output, a daemon) before the result is recorded, names it in the execution's `reaped_descendants`, and the runtime appends `check.reaped`. A descendant that called `setsid` left the group and stays out of reach without a sandbox. On Windows each check is assigned to a kill-on-close job object right after spawn, so cancellation, deadlines and the post-exit reap end the tree, and the operating system ends it if the runtime dies; processes the child starts before assignment escape. This path is compile-checked for Windows and macOS but has not been executed on those hosts. Where a tree is not contained, the recorded reason says that only the direct child was terminated instead of claiming the group was.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text:
2. **Process groups survive a hard kill only until restart.** Every check, baseline or candidate, records `check.spawned` with its `process_group`: group ID, the leader's start time (Linux boot ID included) and a per-execution marker exported as `LUUNA_CHECK_GROUP`. Before startup recovery interrupts the runs, the runtime reconciles each recorded group: survivors are terminated only when verified as that check's (the leader alive with its recorded start time, or on Linux the marker in a member's environment), never on a matching ID alone, and are named in `check.orphans_reaped`; processes that may belong to the group but cannot be verified are left alone and named in `check.orphans_unverified`. On macOS the reconciliation relies on the leader's start time and is compile-checked only.
3. **An empty suite is judged on executed tests.** Runner summaries (cargo, go test, pytest, jest, vitest, unittest, Gradle test tasks) are parsed from every line of both whole output streams while they are captured, not from the size-capped artifacts, and count executed tests only. A recognised summary reporting that nothing executed (no tests, all skipped, ignored or deselected, `[no tests to run]`, `NO-SOURCE`) blocks an exit-0 check as an empty suite; a line that merely resembles a summary (`Tests passed!`) is not one. `Artifact.retained_bytes` records what the digest covers next to the stream's total `bytes`.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text: 4. **Missing infrastructure is blocked, not failed.** An executable that cannot be found or started is blocked as before. A repository-relative executable that does not exist (`node_modules/.bin/...`, `.venv/bin/...`), exit status 127, a shell's "command not found", Python's `ModuleNotFoundError` for a module that is not in the repository, or an unresolved bare Node package is recorded as `blocked` with a reason that asks for a dependency-preparation recipe (for example `npm ci`) ordered before the tests in the manifest; a name the reason quotes from check output must look like a name and is withheld when it is credential-shaped, because check reasons reach model prompts; candidate checks run in a fresh worktree without ignored files such as `node_modules/` or `.venv/`, so the developer checkout's installed state is not evidence for them. Automatic repair never treats such a result as actionable. A required candidate check that the remaining workflow time ends before its own deadline is `blocked` with a "workflow time budget exhausted" reason, and the candidate pauses with "workflow time budget exhausted during required checks; re-plan required".

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text:
5. **Fingerprints describe the toolchain the recipe runs.** Version probes run in the recipe's working directory (where rustup, asdf, mise, volta, pyenv and corepack select a version), with the same sanitised environment, in their own process group; `go` is probed with `go version`. A probe that cannot start, times out or exits non-zero records no version and its failure becomes part of the fingerprint, so a baseline recorded when a probe failed (or from another directory) no longer matches and must be re-run.
6. **Resolution and naming are platform-safe.** On Windows a bare executable name is resolved only with the startable `PATHEXT` extensions in `PATHEXT` order, never as the extensionless POSIX shim Node, npm and Flutter install beside their `.cmd`/`.bat` files; on Unix a `PATH` entry must be executable; empty and relative `PATH` entries are ignored. Artifact files for recipe IDs with upper-case letters or a Windows device stem (`nul`, `con`, `com1`, ...) get an escaped, digest-suffixed name, so IDs that differ only in case never share a log on case-insensitive filesystems.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text:
7. **Credential stripping covers more shapes.** Besides the earlier markers, vault sessions (`BW_SESSION`, `OP_SESSION_*`), `*_PASS`, `*_PWD`, `*_PAT`, `*_DSN`, webhook URLs, connection strings and database URLs are withheld from checks and probes; `is_credential_name` is exported for repair-feedback redaction, whose token-shape line removal now uses the executor's `line_carries_token` (per-format minimum lengths, so a real `AKIA` key ID matches, plus GitHub app, Stripe live, npm, Hugging Face, PyPI and Slack app tokens, `Authorization: Basic|token`, `aws_secret_access_key` and `_authToken=` lines); it stays best effort (ADR 0009). Repair feedback opens each log under the file name of point 6 above.
8. **Baselines are exclusive and settle.** A second baseline for a repository whose baseline run is still active is refused with 409 naming that run (storage refuses a second running record in the same transaction). Baseline results record `artifact_refs` and `artifact_hashes` keys as `{recipe}.{stdout|stderr}`, the identity decision 5 serves (earlier records keep their `artifact:` refs). A failure to persist a result or the verdict settles the baseline as failed, retried once, instead of leaving it `running`. A dirty checkout's blocked reason names the paths; when only untracked files block it, the reason says they may be an earlier check's output and that adding them to `.gitignore` resolves it, because Git-ignored files never b

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): evidence hardening
text: lock a baseline. Baselines still run in the developer checkout.

title: ADR 0008: exact approval, Luuna-owned worktrees and one scoped writer
text:
# ADR 0008: exact approval, Luuna-owned worktrees and one scoped writer

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: accepted; amended 2026-10-21 (worktree integrity and plan scope bounds; Pi launch limits and portability; see below).

title: Context
text:
## Context

M2a records confirmed manifests and M2b records baseline evidence, but no run could modify a repository and no API exposed plans or approvals. The handoff for M2c asked for exact plan approval through the API, revalidation at scheduling, Luuna-owned worktrees with durable ownership, and one bounded writer whose scope and budgets are enforced by the runtime rather than promised by a prompt. ADR 0003 allows a temporary local ticket before the Missions adapter exists; ADR 0005 fixes the canonical ticket route.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **The ticket is a temporary local record.** `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets` creates a revisioned SQLite ticket whose `source` is `luuna_sqlite_temporary`, idempotent per project and key, scoped to registered repositories. Plans bind to `ticket_id` and `ticket_revision`; revising a ticket makes every earlier plan stale and scheduling refuses it until re-planned. The Missions adapter (M6) replaces this source behind the same binding; identifiers and revisions are preserved, and no second writable authority is introduced in the meantime.
2. **The runtime builds plans; clients only describe tasks.** `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans` takes a task (repository, paths, operations, optional criteria), optional permission prefixes and budgets. The runtime fills the project, the ticket revision, the current confirmed manifest hash, that manifest's recorded base commit, the manifest's recipes as the required checks, `max_workers = 1`, and seals the hash. Each submission is the next immutable revision and opens a workflow run already bound to it (`plan_ready`).
3. **Approval names one exact hash.** `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/approvals` carries the revision, the hash the approver saw and who approved; permissions are copied from the plan so a client cannot widen them. A different hash, a newer revision or a workflow not waiting for approval is refused.

title: Decision
text: 4. **Scheduling revalidates everything before any state changes.** `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` requires an `approved` workflow, recomputes the host's environment fingerprint from the manifest's required recipes, re-inspects the repository and refuses a moved HEAD or changed identity, refuses an active lease on the repository (one writer per repository), refuses an exhausted attempt budget, and only then calls `Store::begin_implementation`, which in one transaction re-checks the durable approval, the ticket revision, the current manifest hash and its recorded base commits, and a passed baseline per repository whose run settled as `completed` and whose required recipes each have a passed result bound to the baseline's candidate hash and commit. Any failure leaves the workflow `approved` and returns 409 or 422 with the reason.

title: Decision
text:
5. **Writers work only in Luuna-owned detached worktrees.** The worktree lives under the private data directory (`worktrees/<run>/<attempt>/<repository>`), is created at the planned base commit and verified, and is recorded as a lease in the database with a unique active lease per repository. `git worktree add` writes bookkeeping under the developer repository's `.git/worktrees` and the candidate's objects into its shared object store; the developer's files, index, HEAD and branch are never touched, which tests assert byte for byte. Worktrees are preserved on success, failure, cancellation and restart; startup recovery marks leases of interrupted runs `abandoned` and running attempts `interrupted`.
6. **Scope is enforced twice, and neither is an OS boundary.** Pi runs with only the built-in file tools the task's operations allow (`read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`; `edit`, `write`), with resource discovery, sessions, MCP, skills and context files disabled, and with the Luuna scope guard loaded explicitly. The guard blocks every tool call outside the leased worktree (resolving symlinks in the existing prefix) and every write outside the task paths. After the session the runtime lists the worktree's changed paths with `git status` and rejects the attempt if any path, including both ends of a rename, is outside the task's paths or the approved permissions. Only an in-scope, non-empty change set is committed by the Luuna writer identit

title: Decision
text:
y and recorded as a `CandidateSet`; the workflow then enters `validating`, the next gate (M3). Native execution keeps host permissions: a hostile model could still reach what the account can reach, and the documentation says so.
7. **Budgets fail closed.** Attempts count against `max_attempts` durably; `timeout_seconds` is the session deadline; provider-reported cost is compared against `cost_usd_micros` on every event; `max_workers` is one. Exceeding any of them stops Pi, fails the attempt, releases the lease and preserves the worktree.

title: Consequences and validation
text:
## Consequences and validation

Tests cover: idempotent and conflicting ticket creation; plan binding to ticket revision, manifest hash and base; stale approval after a new revision; missing or stale baseline; a changed recipe (new manifest); a moved HEAD; an unrelated repository; a second writer; cost, attempt and empty-result budgets; out-of-scope changes rejected with the worktree preserved; cancellation reaping Pi and preserving the worktree; restart abandoning the lease and interrupting the attempt; and a full in-scope writer whose candidate commit is authored by the Luuna writer while the developer checkout is byte-identical. The scope guard's path logic has its own Node tests. Genuine evidence with the pinned Pi and a real provider is recorded in the status report. The dirty-checkout limitation on baselines remains until baselines also run in leased worktrees.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): worktree integrity and plan scope bounds
text:
## Amendment (2026-10-21): worktree integrity and plan scope bounds

An audit showed that a writer with the documented `.` scope could rewrite the worktree's `.git` gitfile so that the runtime's own `git add --all`/`git commit` advanced the developer's branch and rewrote their index, breaking point 5; that Pi resolves `@`-prefixed, `~` and `file://` paths after the guard has judged the raw string; that writes through a tracked dangling symlink or into ignored files and gitlink directories escaped the post-session judgement; and that plans accepted spellings, operations and budgets the runtime cannot honour.

1. **No managed Git command trusts the gitfile.** Every operation on a Luuna-owned worktree (status, add, commit, rev-parse, ls-files, diff and candidate verification) first verifies the binding from both ends: `.git` must be the regular file `git worktree add` wrote, naming an absolute `<common>/worktrees/<name>` whose own `gitdir` names this worktree back and whose common directory lies outside it. Git then runs with explicit `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`. Before the post-session judgement the writer also requires that common directory to be the registered repository's. A changed binding fails the attempt as a scope violation with the worktree preserved; nothing is committed anywhere. Worktrees are created with an absolute gitfile and without populating submodules, whatever the developer's configuration.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): worktree integrity and plan scope bounds
text:
2. **Repository metadata is never scope.** A `.git` component (any ASCII case, with the trailing dots or spaces Windows ignores, an NTFS stream suffix, or `GIT~1`) is refused in task paths, permission prefixes and changed paths, and the scope guard refuses tool calls naming it for reads and writes, even under `.`.
3. **Plans name only canonical, grantable scope within bounded budgets.** `.` alone is the whole repository; `./src`, `src/.`, `src/` and empty components are refused with a reason naming the field and entry (task paths are reported first). Plans may request only `read` and `write`; the contract enum keeps `shell`, `network` and `publish` for later milestones but no approval records them now. Task operations are sealed in one order. Budgets are bounded (422 naming the field and limit): `max_workers` exactly 1, `max_attempts` 1..=10, `timeout_seconds` 1..=86400, `cost_usd_micros` 1..=1000000000. A stage fails when usage exceeds a budget; a new model stage needs headroom, so a zero cost budget is refused instead of producing a candidate that can never be validated. Writer deadlines cannot overflow.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): worktree integrity and plan scope bounds
text:
4. **The judgement sees what Git hides.** Changed paths include ignored files (`--ignored=matching`); they are judged against scope and then fail the attempt by name, because `add --all` would leave them out of a candidate whose checks and review still see them. Before the session the runtime records the targets of tracked symbolic links that resolve outside the worktree (dangling ones included) and the contents of unpopulated gitlink directories; any change after the session fails the attempt naming the link or gitlink. Writes deep under an existing outward directory link are not visible to that record; the guard refuses them because it resolves the existing prefix.
5. **The guard judges what Pi will touch.** It refuses paths starting with `@` or `~` and URL schemes, maps Unicode spaces and (on Windows) Git Bash drive paths exactly as pinned Pi 1.3.0 does, follows dangling links to their targets, and refuses writes whose final component is a symbolic link. A Node test compares its decisions with the pinned Pi's own `resolveToCwd` when the package is installed.
6. **Candidates carry only the writer identity.** `author.*` and `committer.*` are pinned with `user.*`; signing, hooks and automatic maintenance stay off; the new commit is read back and must have the previous HEAD as its only parent, the Luuna writer as author and committer and no signature.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): worktree integrity and plan scope bounds
text:
Unchanged: managed checkouts keep the effective line-ending configuration, because pinning LF would mismatch the usual CRLF Windows developer checkout where baselines still run; recording that configuration in the baseline fingerprint, or running baselines in leased worktrees, remains follow-up work. Content filters stay disabled as recorded in the current architecture, and repositories whose checks need populated submodules remain unsupported in managed worktrees. None of this is an operating-system boundary; native execution keeps host permissions.

Amendment (2026-10-21, [ADR 0016](0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md)): startup recovery now abandons every lease still `active` and interrupts every `running` attempt, whatever the state of its run. No writer runs before the runtime admits work, so all of them are orphans. This includes a lease whose run settled while its release failed, which previously refused every later writer on that repository. The recorded reason states that a commit made before the restart may exist unrecorded in the preserved worktree; it is never a candidate.

title: Amendment 2026-10-21: Pi launch limits and portability
text:
## Amendment 2026-10-21: Pi launch limits and portability

- The worktree path is `worktrees/<run>/<attempt number>/<repository>`. The attempt's number is unique within its run and replaces its 44-character identifier, keeping managed checkouts about 40 characters further from Windows' 260-character `MAX_PATH`. The `<run>` component and the candidate check that a worktree stays under `worktrees/<run>` are unchanged.
- Session system prompts, including the writer's approved acceptance criteria, reach Pi as a mode-0600 file in the attempt's private agent directory (`--system-prompt <path>`, which Pi 1.3.0 reads as file contents). They are no longer argv text: tickets the API accepts exceeded Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit and failed at spawn after approval, Windows limits a whole command line to 32,767 characters, and argv is visible to other local accounts.
- Point 6's tools are declared only when Pi can run them. Pi 1.3.0's `grep` and `find` start ripgrep and fd (`fdfind`), which it downloads only when online; Luuna always runs it with `--offline` and a fresh agent directory. A tool whose helper is not on PATH is omitted, and `pi.spawned` (writers) and `review.started` (reviewers) record `omitted_tools` with the reason. An empty selection disables tools rather than falling back to Pi's defaults.

title: Amendment 2026-10-21: Pi launch limits and portability
text:
- On Windows a bare launcher name is resolved through PATH, executables first and then PATHEXT, and an npm `pi.cmd` shim is replaced by the Node executable and `dist/bundle/cli.js` it would start; other batch launchers are refused, never run through cmd.exe.
- Pi's `turn_end` and `agent_end` repeat every message and tool result of a run, so normal sessions exceed the 1 MiB record cap. Oversized session events of known kinds are streamed into a bounded summary (completion, error and usage fields, at most 65 message summaries, marked `luuna_summary`) instead of failing the attempt and reserving its remaining cost; other oversized records remain protocol errors. Startup and transport failures carry Pi's exit status and a redacted 2 KiB tail of its stderr, and the version probe runs with the session's private agent directory.

title: ADR 0009: candidate-bound checks, independent review and bounded repair
text:
# ADR 0009: candidate-bound checks, independent review and bounded repair

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: accepted; amended 2026-10-17 (repair feedback content, genuine-provider evidence; developer decision that v1 ships no OS sandbox and keeps bounded, redacted repair feedback on by default) and 2026-10-21 (point 7: a fresh validation generation after a review that left no verdict).

title: Context
text:
## Context

M2c freezes an approved writer's candidate and stops in `validating`. R09 requires actual required checks plus a fresh independent review; R10 requires durable bounded repairs and useful recovery. A model's self-assessment cannot establish either gate.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Freeze candidate evidence.** Migration 5 records each candidate's exact commits, repository trees, approved plan hash, writer attempt identity and sequential revision. Required command results and structured reviews bind to that exact candidate. Old candidate revisions and validation generations remain audit records. Generic run transitions cannot enter validation/review success or bypass the implementation/repair gates.
2. **Explicit candidate validation.** `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` names the expected candidate hash and reviewer provider/model (or configured defaults). The runtime claims the durable stage once, verifies the owned worktree and its HEAD/tree/tracked content, executes the immutable plan's required recipes through `luuna-executor`, records hashed private artifacts and checks identity again before accepting results. Optional or missing checks cannot satisfy the gate; infrastructure/empty-suite failures are blocked separately from assertion failures. Build output may be untracked; tracked mutation or a moved HEAD fails. Artifact identities include candidate revision and validation generation so a repair/retry cannot overwrite old logs.

title: Decision
text:
3. **Independent review is a fresh Pi process.** Only after all required checks pass does the runtime enter `reviewing`. The new isolated configuration has fixed read-only file tools and a read-only scope guard. Its context contains requirements, exact diff/current code and runtime check evidence, without the writer conversation, Pi history or personal context. Output must deserialize to `ReviewResult` and name the exact candidate and assigned reviewer session; the runtime assigns the review record ID. Blocking findings cannot pass. Invalid JSON, model/transport errors, cancellation, timeout and post-review candidate drift fail closed. Diffs disable external drivers, text conversion and content filters.
4. **Repair is separately gated reuse of an existing approval.** `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/repair` names the exact failed/paused candidate. It rechecks current approval, ticket/manifest/base binding, host-matching passed baseline, repository identity/HEAD, remaining attempts/time/cost and confirmed `max_task_repairs`. A new scoped writer starts in a new owned worktree from the preceding candidate commit, with recorded check/review feedback: the previous reason, check records, structured review and a bounded tail (2 KiB per artifact, 16 KiB encoded in aggregate, at most 32 artifacts and 64 MiB read) of each failed check's private stdout/stderr log with configured credential values redacted and private-key/token shapes removed bes

title: Decision
text: t effort (native checks keep host permissions, so the developer-confirmed manifest remains the boundary on what a check may read), because the writer has no shell and the first genuine-provider run showed a repair writer that only saw an exit code guessing wrong. It creates the next candidate revision; prior checks/review never authorize that revision. Validation may opt into `auto_repair`; ordinary nonzero check exits and `changes_required` reviews then run bounded repair/check/review cycles under one cancellable active operation. Missing infrastructure, signals, deadlines, drift, transport errors or invalid model output stop without automatic edits. Exhaustion pauses with retained evidence and a re-plan recommendation. Manual repair remains available through the same gates. No implicit publication occurs.

title: Decision
text:
5. **Accounting and restart are durable.** Writer attempts plus validation/review usage share the approved aggregate budgets. Per-message model cost is accumulated once, including multi-turn reviews. Interrupted checks preserve elapsed time from durable stage checkpoints and require a fresh validation generation. Interrupted model stages have unknown final provider spend: recovery conservatively reserves the remaining approved cost budget and requires re-planning rather than granting fresh budget. Worktrees, check artifacts and previous evidence remain intact. Native execution retains host permissions; no OS isolation is claimed. Developer decision (2026-10-17, PR #5 review): v1 does not sandbox native checks, so repair feedback stays enabled by default, bounded and redacted as described above, with the developer-confirmed manifest as the boundary on what a check may read; an opt-in flag or sandbox is deferred beyond v1.
6. **Clients display runtime evidence.** Candidate/diff endpoints expose exact identity, check results, findings, failure reasons and permitted repair availability. Controls use active work status; an idle `validating` candidate has no process to cancel. A reviewed candidate is evidence for its exact frozen identity, not permission to publish or merge.

title: Decision
text: 7. **A review that left no verdict costs a generation, not a revision (2026-10-21).** The genuine-provider runs showed small models violating the reviewer JSON contract after every required check had passed; the runtime failed those candidates closed, and the only recovery was a repair revision, which spent a writer attempt on a candidate nothing was wrong with. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` therefore also accepts a `failed` candidate whose every required recipe has a passed result in its current validation generation and whose review is absent: invalid or self-inconsistent reviewer output, a refused reviewer session, or a reviewer that returned nothing. Storage admits `Failed -> Validating` only under that condition and the existing headroom check, in the same transaction that opens generation `n+1` (`candidate.validation_started` carries `revalidation: true`); the candidate revision, approval, plan hash, worktree and attempt count are unchanged, the checks run again and a fresh reviewer session starts, and the reviewer prompt names the generation (never the earlier reviewer's output). Nothing else qualifies: a failed, blocked, missing or interrupted check keeps its repair/retry path; any recorded verdict, passing or not, is review evidence and stays; a reviewer lost mid-turn reserved the remaining approved cost, which closes this gate exactly as it closes repair, so no new budget is ever granted. `GET …/candidate` repor

title: Decision
text:
ts the decision as `revalidate_allowed` and the desktop offers the control only then.

**Amendment (2026-10-21, candidate content and review evidence).** An audit found evidence that did not bind to candidate content, diffs that hid changes and refusals that changed no state. Each item below amends the point it names.

- *Point 2, generation reset.* Every validation generation resolves the leased worktree and verifies HEAD, tree and tracked content. It then removes every untracked and ignored path (`git clean -ffdx` with the work tree named explicitly) and records them in `candidate.worktree_cleaned`. Checks may still leave untracked output within a generation, but a later generation (resumption, re-validation) no longer inherits it. Tracked edits are never reset.
- *Points 2, 6 and 7, content drift.* The claimed generation detects a worktree that no longer holds the candidate: before or between checks, after them, after the review, or missing. The candidate then fails with a reason that starts `candidate content drift:` and names the changed paths, the check or review it followed, and the next steps (repair in a fresh worktree, or the next plan revision). Such a candidate is marked `content_drift` and point 7 excludes it, because its worktree is no longer evidence of the candidate. `POST …/validate` no longer answers drift with a 409 that records nothing. `GET …/diff` serves the frozen commit pair with a `worktree_drift` note

title: Decision
text:
instead of refusing.
- *Point 3, diffs.* Review and display diffs use `--text`, so `-diff`/`binary` attributes from the tree, `info/attributes` or `core.attributesFile` cannot turn source changes into binary patches, and `--ignore-submodules=none`, so configuration cannot hide a gitlink change. Content with a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 becomes a one-line summary naming both blobs rather than lossy text. The reviewer receives whole file sections up to 256 KiB, every changed path with how it is shown (`text`, `summary`, `omitted`), a truncation notice, and `attention_paths` for changed `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore` and `.gitmodules`. A larger candidate is reviewed with that bounded diff instead of being refused without a state change. Candidate verification reads index listings up to 64 MiB, so large repositories validate.
- *Point 3, review consistency.* `changes_required` and `blocked` must name at least one finding, and a pass cannot carry a blocking finding. Finding paths must be relative, and every string must be bounded, non-blank and free of control characters (`schemas/review-result.schema.json` says the same; the reviewer's instructions state the verdict and path rules). Any other output is no verdict: point 7 re-validation applies, and automatic repair never spends an attempt on it.

title: Decision
text:
- *Point 3, reviewer traceability.* `review.tool_call` events record the reviewer's tool calls with the tool name and `path` argument only. Failed or refused calls are marked `failed`, at most 256 per session. Rejected output is kept as the private artifact `<reviewer session>.stdout`, named with its digest in the failure reason and never given to a later session. The reviewer's conversation is still not persisted.
- *Point 4, repair evidence.* The evidence block is delimited by markers that carry a random per-prompt token, so check output cannot forge the end of the block. The wording points at the acceptance criteria that follow it.
- *Point 6, decisions.* `GET …/candidate` adds `validate_allowed` and `decision_reasons` (`validate`, `repair`, `revalidate`). Each reason is the refusal the route would give, or null, and is computed by the same storage gates; `repair_allowed` also applies the one-writer lease rule. Repository, host and component-source checks stay with the routes. Paths passed to Git and to the reviewer's scope guard drop the Windows `\\?\` verbatim prefix.

title: Evidence and remaining gates
text:
## Evidence and remaining gates

Synthetic Pi fixtures make failure/recovery paths deterministic; required checks execute real host commands. Current platform and real-provider evidence are listed separately in `FOUNDATION-STATUS.md`, including the `scripts/m3-smoke.mjs` genuine-provider run (OpenRouter, pinned Pi 1.3.0) that closed the provider exit on Linux. Native Mac/Windows service lifecycle evidence remains open. Publication, merging, native service packaging, distributed clients and multi-repository scheduling remain later milestones. The developer controls merging.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): accounting, restart recovery and repair provenance
text:
## Amendment (2026-10-21): accounting, restart recovery and repair provenance

An audit of the M3 implementation found recovery charging outages as stage time, reserving spend for reviewers that were never prompted, cost the budget never saw, and usage and failure reasons clients could not see. Points 4 and 5 are refined as follows; nothing grants fresh budget or relaxes a gate.

- **Restart charges only what was durably observed.** An active validation or review stage stamps a heartbeat (`stage_checkpoint_at`) every five seconds. Recovery charges an interrupted stage up to its last heartbeat plus one interval rather than up to the restart, so downtime cannot close the documented "validate again" path; a record without a heartbeat (written before this amendment) is still charged up to the restart.
- **Unknown review spend begins with a durable marker.** `review.prompt_sent` is written immediately before the reviewer prompt and `review.usage_settled` after `agent_settled`, once the final usage is charged. Recovery reserves the remaining approved cost budget only between the two, exactly as the live path's in-flight rule does; a reviewer interrupted before its prompt, or after it settled, is resumable like an interrupted check with a fresh generation. A reviewer recorded by an earlier runtime, which wrote no markers, stays conservative. Interrupted writers keep the conservative reservation of point 5.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): accounting, restart recovery and repair provenance
text:
- **Cost accounting covers what Pi reports.** Compaction (summarization) usage from `compaction_end` is charged with the session. A message or summary that reports tokens without a cost is not refused, since the cost budget is enforced against Pi's price table, but it is recorded once per session as `usage.cost_unreported` and reported as `cost_unreported`, so the gap is visible instead of silently counted as zero. The reviewer checks its budgets on every record but persists usage when a message completes, the session ends or a check fails, and a charge of nothing appends no `candidate.usage` event. The reviewer tolerates a provider error Pi retries itself (`agent_end` with `willRetry`) exactly like the writer; the verdict waits for `agent_settled`.
- **Usage is visible where decisions are made.** `GET …/candidate` reports `usage` for the whole workflow (writer attempts, validation and review) against `max_attempts`, `timeout_seconds`, `cost_usd_micros` and the confirmed `max_task_repairs`. `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}` reports `usage` summed over every workflow of the ticket's plan revisions and the plan-creation response repeats it as `ticket_usage`. A new plan revision still carries its own approved budgets, approved by exact hash; what earlier revisions spent is shown to the approver rather than silently reset. No ticket-wide hard ceiling is added: that remains a developer policy decision.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): accounting, restart recovery and repair provenance
text: - **Repair keeps its causes and provenance.** An automatic repair whose writer fails pauses with that writer's own reason (`automatic repair writer failed: …`), the repair gate's refusal when no further repair may follow (for example a spent budget and the re-plan requirement) and the candidate's earlier reason. Attempts keep the provider, model, host fingerprint, Pi version and trigger they were admitted with after they settle; automatic repair writers run on the validation request's provider and model, which `review.started` also records. A repair writer is told it starts from the previous candidate's commit and revision, and quoted check output names files relative to the repository root instead of the previous attempt's worktree. Repair-feedback redaction treats the extended credential names (vault sessions, `*_PASS`, `*_PWD`, `*_PAT`, `*_DSN`, webhook, connection-string and database URLs) as credentials, and URL credentials are taken from every variable, inherited or not.

title: Amendment (2026-10-21): accounting, restart recovery and repair provenance
text:
- **Related scheduling guards (ADR 0008 points 2 and 4).** `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans` accepts an optional `idempotency_key`: the same key and request return the plan and workflow it created (200), a different request is 409 (storage migration 8, `plan_requests`). A new revision settles earlier `plan_ready` or `approved` workflows of the plan as `cancelled` with `plan.superseded`, since they can never be approved or scheduled again. One writer per repository is re-checked inside the transaction that admits a writer or repair, so a concurrent second workflow is refused with 409 and stays `approved`.

PR 11 follow-up: the storage transaction refuses a new plan for a ticket while
any of its workflows has a live writer, check, reviewer, attempt or owned lease,
even if the caller chooses a different plan ID. Idempotent replay still returns
the original operation. An idle pending candidate may be superseded. The desktop
shows cumulative ticket usage, unpriced usage and explicit truncated-diff notices.

title: ADR 0010: authenticated service shutdown and scheduling admission
text:
# ADR 0010: authenticated service shutdown and scheduling admission

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted; implements ADR 0004's explicit service action.

title: Context
text:
## Context

Node process signals terminate Windows processes instead of delivering the
runtime's console Ctrl+C path. Hidden development services therefore lacked a
portable way to stop orderly. Windows browser smoke tests showed crash recovery,
but not the promised explicit shutdown interruption and clean process exit.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

`POST /api/v1/shutdown` is a bearer-authenticated, idempotent service action.
It returns 202 and notifies the main process to use the existing owned-worker
shutdown path. A fair admission lock drains previously accepted mutation
handlers before stopping workers; new mutations receive 503 after shutdown is
requested. Authenticated reads remain available while interruption is persisted.
The endpoint never publishes, merges, widens approval, or treats client closure
as shutdown. Main exits normally after the HTTP server drains.

The Windows stop command decrypts the existing local connection token with
DPAPI, submits the request only to the fixed loopback endpoint, and waits for the
verified runtime process to exit. It does not force-kill on failure. Launchers
reuse the encrypted connection token and data directory across restarts so an
open client can reconnect. Native desktop and runtime remain independent sibling
processes. This is a development launcher, not a signed installer or installed
Windows service.

Windows smoke harnesses use the authenticated action for orderly stops and
retain hard kills for crash scenarios. Unix SIGTERM coverage is retained.
Native smoke drives the actual bundled Tauri frontend through a temporary
test-owned WebView2 debugging endpoint; production launch enables no debugging
endpoint. Native form entry through CDP is not keyboard-only evidence.

title: Validation
text:
## Validation

Tests must reject unauthenticated shutdown, accept repeated authorized requests,
block scheduling after admission closes, retain reads, record active work as
interrupted with the shutdown reason, and prove clean exit plus restart recovery.
Native launch must identify the executable and exercise its own embedded view,
not substitute the Vite browser client. Evidence is recorded separately in
`docs/WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md`.

title: ADR 0011: automatic Windows development runtime connection
text:
# ADR 0011: automatic Windows development runtime connection

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted for the checkout-based Windows app.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The native app required a separate launcher and copying a bearer token for every
new view. ADR 0004 requires the service to survive client closure; automatic
startup must retain that independent lifetime and the existing durable state.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

The bundled main window receives one narrowly scoped Tauri command,
`ensure_local_runtime`. It accepts no executable, arguments, endpoint, token or
filesystem path from the view. On Windows it invokes the fixed repository-owned
`scripts/ensure-windows-runtime.ps1` with hidden Windows PowerShell, independently
of the app's working directory. The helper uses a per-account named startup
mutex, verifies the occupied port's executable identity and authenticates before
reuse, or starts the built runtime on loopback port 4242 with the saved provider
configuration. Unknown listeners are refused before sending any HTTP request.

Connection and provider records use current-account Windows DPAPI in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\credentials`. The resolver copies existing encrypted
LocalAppData records only when the new files are absent, leaving the originals
intact. This stable path avoids Store-host filesystem redirection. Runtime logs
are in `.luuna/logs`; the existing data directory and token survive restarts.
Token identity is persisted before spawning and the verified PID immediately
afterward so uncertain startup can be authenticated and reconciled. A bounded
helper failure does not force-kill a runtime.

title: Decision
text:
The helper returns the runtime URL and token through a captured private stdout
pipe and local-window IPC. On Windows a descendant can retain an inherited pipe
handle; the native reader consumes one bounded JSON line with a timeout rather
than waiting for EOF from a runtime that intentionally stays alive.
The provider key never crosses that boundary. The
client holds the connection only in memory, deduplicates concurrent startup
calls and authenticates against the API before marking itself connected. Reload
and explicit retry request fresh startup/reuse checks. Explicit disconnect stays
disconnected until retry or reload. Browser connections remain manual. Only the
local main window has the custom command permission; no general shell or
filesystem plugin is enabled.

Normal window closure does not stop the runtime or cancel work. Authenticated
explicit shutdown remains ADR 0010. Runtime approval and execution policies are
unchanged. DPAPI and same-account IPC are credential handling, not a sandbox.

title: Validation and limits
text:
## Validation and limits

`scripts/windows-native-startup-smoke.mjs` drives the actual bundled WebView2
frontend: warm reuse, normal close, explicit runtime stop, refusal of a foreign
listener without transmitting credentials, retry/cold start, reload, concurrent
windows, disconnect, preserved history/key bytes and empty browser storage.
It uses temporary test-owned debugging profiles and makes no model calls.
Normal launch enables no debugging endpoint. Run only against idle development
state. See `docs/WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md` for measured results.

The executable still depends on this checkout, its built runtime, pinned Pi
dependencies, Node and saved provider configuration. This is not an installed
Windows service, automatic login startup, signed installer or packaged portable
distribution. Other platforms retain manual startup pending their own proof.

title: ADR 0012: independent public component repositories and pinned consumption
text:
# ADR 0012: independent public component repositories and pinned consumption

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted by explicit owner instruction. Supersedes ADR 0002's hosted-extraction deferral; its compatibility and attribution requirements remain.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The owner requested completion of Missions, Atlas and Beacon extraction and continued Luuna consumption, then explicitly requested public repositories. Luuna has concurrent native-platform work in progress; that work must not be included in the extraction commit. Runtime component integration remains a separate M6 obligation.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. Maintain source in public `brodynelly/luuna-missions`, `brodynelly/luuna-atlas` and `brodynelly/luuna-beacon`. brodynelly owns review, CI and release decisions. Luuna remains private. Registry packages remain private and unpublished; no npm release credentials or deploy keys are needed for Git source consumption.
2. Preserve the component-scoped maintained history using `git subtree split`, verified against the exact source subtree at Luuna commit `fd42d59c5f608b9120d9cdc2e2354b66f945a5ed`. The earlier pre-branding history remains in Luuna and is identified by UPSTREAM.md. Each repository records extraction provenance in MIGRATION.md. Do not publish monorepo history, authoring stores, sessions, credentials or unrelated Luuna source in these repositories.
3. Preserve TypeScript implementations, package versions, compatible data directories, JSON contracts, primary and legacy aliases, frozen Bun dependency graphs and exact upstream LICENSE bytes. Change only repository metadata, ownership, current instructions and standalone CI during extraction.

title: Decision
text:
4. Consume each repository as an exact-commit Git submodule at its existing `components/<name>` path. `components/manifest.json` records the repository, immutable commit, CLI contract and license digest. The manifest commit and staged gitlink must agree. Setup checks out committed pins, installs with Bun 1.4.3 and `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, and checks that root hooks configuration did not change. No floating-branch updates or registry lookalikes are used.
5. Each public repository runs its own full typecheck, instruction checks and Bun suite. Luuna CI installs the pinned submodules and exercises real CLI JSON ticket, knowledge and prompt operations on disposable stores on Linux, macOS and Windows. Consumer checks reject missing, dirty, moved or incompatible checkouts. Public source fetches need no private cross-repository credential.
6. Source copies become gitlinks only after destination identity, remote commit, preserved source/license/lock and actual destination installation have been verified. Retain local rollback copies until the migration is accepted. Changes to Luuna are reviewed through a PR; the developer controls merging.

title: Integration boundary
text:
## Integration boundary

The consumer launcher is a developer and CI tool. It does not replace Luuna's temporary SQLite ticket authority, reconcile external Missions edits, retrieve Atlas private memory, or turn Beacon output into Pi resources. Those M6 adapters must still implement revision, provenance, privacy and runtime approval guards. Extraction must not alter those authorities or weaken any existing policy.

title: Validation
text:
## Validation

See `docs/COMPONENT-EXTRACTION.md` for exact pins, source and license comparisons, independent CI results, consumer checks and observed platform results. Original documentation delivery validation remains separate from this product/dependency evidence.

title: ADR 0013: one token-based design system for the desktop client
text:
# ADR 0013: one token-based design system for the desktop client

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The desktop client grew one panel per milestone on a single dark-only stylesheet of hex literals. State badges were coloured by runtime state name, so a `completed` demo session was painted green although the client itself says a completed session is not a validation result. Interrupted work looked like failure. The light half of the declared `color-scheme: dark light` was never designed. Nothing checked contrast, so two text runs sat below WCAG AA. Browser/TUI parity is a full-v1 obligation (R02), so the meaning of each state has to be defined once, not per screen.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision
