1. **Presentation follows evidence.** Six tones (success, active, danger, attention, neutral, interrupted) are mapped from the `@luuna/api-client` unions in `apps/desktop/src/design/tone.ts` as exhaustive typed records, so a new runtime state fails the type check until it has a tone. Only passed durable evidence and a live connection are success. Interruption is never danger. The runtime still decides every state, permission, reason and next step; the client only chooses how to show them.
2. **Three channels.** Every state shows its unchanged runtime text, a colour family and a shape mark. Colour is never the only signal.
3. **Tokens only, both schemes.** Literal colours, lengths and durations live in `design/tokens.css`. Dark stays the default; `prefers-color-scheme: light` redefines every colour. Stylesheets are layered (tokens, base, components, screens) and bundled from `'self'`, which the Tauri CSP already allows. No font or stylesheet is fetched.

title: Decision
text:
4. **Enforced, not advised.** `design/design-system.test.ts` runs under `npm test`. It lints every stylesheet, resolves every `var()`, checks scheme parity, computes WCAG contrast for every semantic pair in both schemes, pins screen structure (heading levels, no inline styles, badges through one primitive, dismissible alerts) and pins the tone taxonomy. `scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` checks the rendered page: contrast against painted backgrounds in both schemes, scheme following, and no horizontal scroll at the 760 px window minimum.

The reference is [docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](../DESIGN-SYSTEM.md).

title: Alternatives and consequences
text:
## Alternatives and consequences

A CSS framework or component library was rejected: it would add dependencies, fetch nothing useful under the CSP, and hide the tone semantics in class soup. A runtime-provided "display tone" field was rejected: tone is presentation, and the runtime already exposes the authoritative state each client maps. A manual light/dark switch was deferred: there is no setting surface yet, and the system scheme is enough for the MVP.

A future TUI or browser client should reuse the same tone table (`tone.ts` and the DESIGN-SYSTEM table) so a state reads the same everywhere. Adding a colour now costs a token in both schemes and a contrast pair. Adding a runtime state costs a tone entry. The smoke's contrast audit exempts disabled controls only, so the design system uses disabled colour tokens instead of opacity.

title: ADR 0014: explicit managed component workflows and approved context
text:
# ADR 0014: explicit managed component workflows and approved context

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted for the owner's requested runtime integration. Implements the ticket authority boundary of ADR 0003 and the runtime adapters deferred by ADR 0012. Existing approval, baseline, candidate and publication decisions remain in force.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The public `luuna-missions`, `luuna-atlas` and `luuna-beacon` repositories are already consumed as exact-commit submodules. Installing or smoke-testing those CLIs does not make the application use their records. The owner requested actual ticket, memory and prompt workflows through Luuna without importing development history, exposing personal stores or weakening exact-plan authorization.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Activate explicitly per project.** `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/components` reports state; `POST` to that route initializes the three stores and migrates legacy tickets. The durable `initializing` state freezes affected ticket actions until activation is reconciled and becomes `enabled` only after successful initialization and migration. Component discovery alone never changes an existing project's authority. An enabled project fails closed if its pinned toolchain or managed store is unavailable; there is no silent SQLite fallback.

2. **Use managed private stores.** Each project uses `<data_dir>/components/projects/<project_id>`. Explicit user-scoped memory uses `<data_dir>/components/user`; project/process memory stays in the selected project's workspace. Existing developer checkouts, imported `.seeds`/`.mulch`/`.canopy` directories, user Pi state and personal memory are never adopted automatically. Compatible component data formats, JSON APIs, CLI aliases and upstream notices remain intact. Luuna invokes the public CLIs and does not mutate their internal files directly.

title: Decision
text:
3. **Missions owns enabled ticket intent.** The canonical creation route remains `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`. A compatible Missions description contains a versioned Luuna envelope with immutable Luuna ticket/project identity and editable intent, acceptance criteria and registered repository IDs; the ordinary Missions title, status and dependencies retain their meanings. SQLite keeps a revision-aware projection, immutable original delivery intent, source identity/fingerprint and Luuna's execution state. It cannot independently edit Missions-owned fields. Initial migration preserves Luuna ticket IDs, numeric revisions and creation timestamps; existing plans and approvals remain durable.

4. **Reconcile external edits explicitly.** Ticket GET/list routes return the last reconciled projection so a client can still display a stale ticket and offer recovery. `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/source` observes authoritative source identity, fingerprint, status and reconciliation need. `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/reconcile` requires `{expected_revision}`. A changed source or direct dependency snapshot advances the projection revision, including status/dependency changes that leave visible intent unchanged; a stale expected revision is refused. Planning, approval, implementation, repair and candidate evidence consumption re-observe source freshness. Closed tickets and unresolved dependencies block work. Reconciliation never renews an

title: Decision
text:
old plan's authorization: changed revisions require a new plan and approval. The current slice intentionally has no Luuna ticket-edit endpoint because the existing component CLI offers no atomic cross-process optimistic edit contract.

5. **Persist before external side effects.** Ticket creation reserves original content and records that delivery started before invoking Missions. A stable label and the envelope identity allow lookup of an uncertain successful create before acknowledging or retrying. Duplicate identities, changed reserved content, or an attempted delivery with no recoverable identity fail closed instead of creating another issue. The Atlas/Beacon operation ledger similarly binds a project/request key to original content and reconciles uncertain writes. Recovery may require restoring an externally removed identity or inspecting the managed source; retries do not invent new authority.

title: Decision
text: 6. **Select memory and prompts as exact plan inputs.** Atlas-backed memory has explicit project/process/user scope and provenance. User scope requires explicit retrieval/selection. Only records bound by Luuna are returned as application memory; arbitrary imported records do not enter context. Beacon prompts have a current version and rendered-content hash; updating an existing name requires its expected version. The application previews and selects resources, then the runtime stores their exact content, provenance, versions and hashes in optional `component_context` inside the canonical immutable plan. The complete plan remains visible before exact-hash approval. At approval and execution boundaries the runtime resolves the selected records again and refuses changes, deletion or scope drift. Only those approved snapshots become bounded worker resources; component text never grants authority to skip runtime rules. Omitting `component_context` preserves existing plan hashes and the legacy workflow.

title: Decision
text: 7. **Supervise a bounded native process boundary.** `luuna-components` verifies the committed manifest, `.gitmodules`, Git HEAD/index gitlink, clean component checkout, package identity/aliases and Bun 1.4.3 before invoking the pinned TypeScript entrypoint. A fixed bridge receives bounded JSON on stdin and starts the actual CLI with explicit arguments and no shell. Processes receive an allowlisted environment, isolated HOME/config, disabled Bun `.env` loading/automatic installation and Git discovery/config controls. Links/reparse points in workspace ancestors and component stores, plus configured executable Atlas hooks, are refused. Each process has a 30-second deadline, 1 MiB input, 4 MiB stdout and 64 KiB stderr bounds; owned descendants are stopped through Unix process groups or a Windows Job Object. Arguments and child output are not reflected in API errors. These are native host processes with host permissions, not an OS sandbox.

title: Consequences and validation
text:
## Consequences and validation

The application now has real component adapters while retaining explicit activation, legacy compatibility and immutable approval. Source inspection is deliberately conservative: external mutations after a freshness observation cannot be made atomic with a SQLite transaction by the current CLI API; subsequent runtime boundaries re-observe and refuse drift. Missions delivery searches only the selected identity and reads known source/dependency snapshots through public commands; at most 64 direct dependencies and 10,000 identity-search matches are accepted. Oversized or malformed contracts fail visibly rather than truncate.

Focused storage tests cover migration identity, restart durability, idempotency, projection-only writes, stale revisions and old-plan invalidation. Explicit real-component tests exercise actual Bun/CLI migration, external edits, dependencies, reconciliation, removed-marker recovery, duplicate/uncertain writes and unavailable integrations in disposable private stores. The runner's real test covers all three CLIs, a large ticket, Atlas CRUD/search, Beacon version changes and executable-hook refusal. Commands, platforms and observed results are recorded in [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](../FOUNDATION-STATUS.md#runtime-component-workflows-october-21-2026).

title: Consequences and validation
text: Synthetic Pi remains synthetic even when ticket/memory/prompt storage uses real component CLIs. A passing browser smoke does not establish native Tauri UI behavior or a new genuine-provider exit. Browser/TUI parity, broader memory policy/retention, packaging and supported-platform evidence remain full-v1 obligations; publication and developer-controlled merging remain separate gates.

title: ADR 0015: Bounded runtime dispatch, display history and check progress
text:
# ADR 0015: Bounded runtime dispatch, display history and check progress

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted for the existing foundation.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

Preserve SQLite's synchronous, transactional authority and FULL durability. Run
authenticated handlers on at most 32 admitted blocking tasks; admission remains
owned by the task if its HTTP caller disconnects. Run the already capped four
workers and baseline relays on blocking tasks too. This prevents synchronous
SQLite contention from occupying Tokio's I/O threads. Public health and
authenticated shutdown remain reachable when request capacity is exhausted.
SSE admits at most 16 streams, uses bounded blocking reads, and drains terminal
history fully before closing. Capacity exhaustion returns a retryable error.

Existing complete-history routes remain compatible. Optional `limit` on runs
and events selects pages of at most 200 records. Runs use `(created_at DESC,id)`
keyset order, indexed globally and by project, with `before` naming the last run
of the preceding page. Events support ascending `after` or descending `before`
(returned in ascending order), with approximately 1 MiB of encoded envelopes
per page. One oversized historical event is returned alone to guarantee forward
progress; no stored event is discarded or silently skipped.

title: Decision
text:
The session client uses these pages, retains at most 200 live event payloads and
approximately 1 MiB of UTF-16 JSON (one oversized event is permitted), and loads
one historical page on demand. Assistant text is accumulated incrementally,
with a clearly marked 1 Mi-character display limit; complete records stay in
SQLite. Initial replay still reads every page to reconstruct assistant output.
The session list holds one page; idle refresh slows to five seconds. Workflow
requests have concurrency four. Settled display snapshots are reused while
active runs advance; manual refresh, actions, reconnect and component changes
invalidate them. Component-source observations are snapshots; all existing
approval/execution freshness and immutable identity guards remain mandatory.

Check progress uses a 64-message nonblocking channel and at most 100 excerpts
per stream. Display excerpts may be dropped under load and explicitly identify
themselves as truncated/display-only. File capture still drains both pipes,
stores up to 16 MiB per stream and hashes the actual recorded artifacts. Version
probes have bounded output too. Windows checks start suspended, join an owned
kill-on-close Job Object, then resume; cancellation, deadlines and cleanup stop
the descendant tree. Unix checks retain dedicated process groups. Neither is a
sandbox or a new authorization mechanism.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

This bounds active request/thread pressure and normal session display memory
without splitting transactions or changing execution evidence. Legacy callers
can still request complete history. Workflow ticket enumeration and the first
assistant replay remain proportional to history size; future projections or
workflow pagination must preserve discovery of every ticket and approval.
Measured performance and platform/provider coverage belong in the performance
review, separately from historical documentation validation.

Amendment (2026-10-22, merge with the audit-hardening branch and
[ADR 0016](0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md)): the run-history
indexes are versioned storage migration 9 rather than an unversioned startup
statement. Supervised workers (panic settlement and active-map release) run
through the bounded `dispatch::worker` pool. `limit` keeps its 1 to 10,000
validation, but run pages answer at most 200 records (and about 1 MiB of
events), so `readEventPages` and the desktop continue until an empty page
rather than stopping at the first short one. `before` is accepted only with
`limit`. The Windows suspended-spawn job ownership is the executor's single
process-tree owner, and display progress reserves channel slots for the
final reaping record.

title: ADR 0016: storage schema compatibility, integrity checks and backup/restore
text:
# ADR 0016: storage schema compatibility, integrity checks and backup/restore

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted; implements the MVP gate's backup and
migration-recovery drill, the consistent SQLite backup procedure required by
`docs/03-architecture.md`, and the forward-migration and explicit-downgrade
requirements of `docs/12-decisions-risks.md`.

title: Context
text:
## Context

The runtime's SQLite database runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL`.
Committed state can live in `luuna.sqlite3-wal` until a checkpoint, so a copy of
the main file taken while the runtime runs can lose every record, and an older
main file placed beside a newer `-wal` (a plausible manual restore after a
crash) is replayed into a malformed database. The audit found no backup
command or procedure, no integrity check (a malformed database started,
served partial data and accepted new approvals), and no schema gate: every
migration re-ran on each open, `schema_migrations` was never read, an older
build silently wrote into a newer database or failed late with a serde message
naming no table, and a non-idempotent migration could not be written at all.
Startup recovery decoded every run in full, so one damaged row stopped the
service. A lease left `active` by a run that settled while its release failed
survived every restart and refused every later writer on that repository. The
implementation gate chose the latest baseline by wall-clock `started_at`.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Versioned, append-only migrations.** `schema_migrations` is the record of
   applied versions and `DATABASE_SCHEMA_VERSION` is the highest this build
   knows (9). Opening applies only the versions the file lacks, in order. Each
   script commits its own version row and stays idempotent, because two
   processes may race to initialize a new file. A shipped script is never
   edited; a test pins their digests. A change that writes values an older
   build cannot decode (a new state, a new required field) must also add a
   migration, even one that only records its version, so that older builds
   refuse the file instead of failing on a row. The component tables of
   ADR 0014 are still created idempotently at every open, outside this list;
   moving them into a migration is a follow-up.
2. **Gate before any write.** Before opening for writing, a read-only
   connection runs `PRAGMA quick_check` and reads the schema version. A
   malformed file is refused with its first findings and the restore command.
   A file whose version is newer than this build's is refused with both
   versions. Neither is written, not even by a closing writer's checkpoint.
3. **Automatic pre-migration snapshot.** Before migrating an existing database
   (version 1 or later), the runtime writes
   `<data>/backups/pre-migration-v<old>-<timestamp>.sqlite3` with
   `VACUUM INTO`. A failed snapshot stops the upgrade. Snapshots are never

title: Decision
text:
deleted automatically. To step back to an older build, restore its
   pre-migration snapshot with `luuna-runtime restore` and start that build;
   downgrading a migrated database in place is not supported.
4. **Online backup.** `luuna-runtime backup --output <file>` takes a `VACUUM
   INTO` snapshot through a read-only connection. WAL readers do not block the
   running service, so the snapshot is consistent and includes commits still in
   the log. The result is one self-contained file: private (0600), synced, and
   checked with `quick_check` before it is moved into place. It never
   overwrites a file. The command prints the schema version, size and SHA-256.
5. **Offline restore.** `luuna-runtime restore --input <file>` takes the data
   directory's owner lock, so it is refused while a runtime owns the directory.
   It refuses an input that has a non-empty `-wal` or `-journal` beside it.
   Otherwise it copies the input, verifies the copy's integrity and schema
   version (1 to the supported version), and converts it to a single
   rollback-journal file. It then moves the current database and any `-wal`,
   `-shm` or `-journal` beside it to `<data>/backups/replaced-<timestamp>/`,
   and installs the copy. A synced restore intent is atomically published before
   any original file moves. If the process stops or a move fails, the next open
   or restore resumes that exact operation before SQLite may open or create the

title: Decision
text:
main database. Already preserved files are not moved twice; unexpected files
   or an unreadable intent fail closed. A stale log never meets the restored file.
   This guarantees recovery from process interruption, not hardware power-loss
   durability on filesystems that cannot sync directory entries. The next start migrates an older snapshot,
   with its own pre-migration snapshot. It also performs ordinary restart
   recovery, so work active when the snapshot was taken becomes `interrupted`,
   never successful.
6. **Check.** `luuna-runtime check` reports integrity and schema version
   read-only, safe while the runtime runs, and exits non-zero on a problem. All
   three commands take `--data-dir`; the default is the service's data
   directory. Without arguments the binary starts the service as before.
7. **What a snapshot covers.** The database snapshot covers projects,
   manifests, plans, approvals, runs, events, leases, attempts, check and
   review evidence records, and component bindings. Check artifacts,
   worktrees, attempt directories and the managed component stores are files
   in the data directory. A complete backup is a copy of the whole data
   directory while the runtime is stopped (an orderly stop checkpoints the
   log). Copying a running data directory is not a supported backup. A
   restored database can reference artifacts or worktrees that are absent or

title: Decision
text:
newer than its records; restore the matching directory copy for full
   fidelity.
8. **Recovery that one row cannot stop.** Startup recovery selects active
   runs by their state column, and a transition no longer decodes run
   metadata. A record recovery cannot decode is skipped and logged to stderr by
   table and ID. Logs and events describe the decode error by category and
   position, never by content. Where the table has an authoritative state
   column, that column is settled and a durable event records the reason:
   - a lease is abandoned, which frees the repository;
   - an attempt is interrupted, and if its usage cannot be read it reserves
     the full approved budgets;
   - a baseline or candidate is interrupted. The gates decode these records
     and fail closed anyway.

title: Decision
text:
A run whose state cannot be decoded is left unchanged and reported on every
   start. No gate can use it, because each one decodes it. SQLite errors still
   stop startup.
9. **Every orphan is released.** This amends ADR 0008. No writer runs before
   the runtime admits work, so at startup every lease still `active` is
   abandoned and every `running` attempt is interrupted, whatever its run's
   state. That includes a run that settled while its release failed. The
   recorded reason says that a commit the writer made before the restart may
   exist unrecorded in the preserved worktree and is never a candidate.
   Reading the worktree HEAD at startup, as the live interruption path does,
   remains a follow-up.
10. **Insertion order, not wall clock.** The latest baseline (the
    implementation and repair gate), the baseline listing, the latest discovery
    and a plan's workflow run are chosen by rowid. Rowid is insertion order:
    these rows are never deleted, and `VACUUM INTO` copies rows in rowid order.
    A clock stepped backwards can no longer let an older passed baseline mask
    a newer failed one.
11. **Migration 7** adds lookup indexes for check results by baseline,
    baselines by project and repository, runs by plan revision, leases by run
    and discoveries by project. Baseline listing previously scanned every
    check result per baseline while holding the store lock.

title: Validation
Validation
text:
a new baseline reaches a verdict. After an orderly stop, it restores the
  mid-check snapshot and confirms the restored state.

The process test and the file-permission assertions run on Unix only. Windows
and macOS restore semantics (renaming files another process may hold) have not
been exercised by these tests.

title: PR 11 follow-up: preservation and interrupted restore
text:
## PR 11 follow-up: preservation and interrupted restore

Backup publication uses an atomic no-replace hard link on the output filesystem;
unsupported filesystems fail rather than falling back to overwrite. Restore keeps
all original files and a durable intent until installation is verified, and
startup completes an interrupted restore before database creation. Windows tests
exercise every file-move boundary and the post-install/pre-finalization boundary.
Orphan-process recovery reads only the state columns and individual event rows;
damaged metadata or a malformed unrelated event cannot abort all startup recovery.
No malformed ownership record authorizes terminating a process.

title: ADR 0017: multi-repository coordination (M4)
text:
# ADR 0017: multi-repository coordination (M4)

Date: 2026-10-22. Status: accepted; implements the M4 slice of
`docs/IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md` (P40 manifest and discovery, P41 graph
confirmation, P43 scheduler and locks, P45 cross-repository integration) on
top of ADR 0008 (approval, worktrees, one scoped writer) and ADR 0009
(candidate-bound checks, review and repair). P42 (delegated roles) and P44
(dependency overrides) remain open; see "What remains".

title: Context
text:
## Context

M3 runs one writer in one repository, validates its candidate with that
repository's required recipes and reviews it in a fresh session. R05 requires
a confirmed repository graph and an integration candidate across repositories;
R06 requires scoped coordination with traces; A12 and A13 require independent
work to overlap within limits and an incompatible consumer to block
integration; A20 requires a killed service to leave recoverable evidence. The
contracts already carried `PlanTask.depends_on`, `Relationship.confirmed` and
`CandidateSet.dependency_bindings`, but nothing validated the task DAG,
discovered relationships, scheduled more than one task, or ran checks against
another repository's candidate.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **The plan's task graph is a validated contract.** `PlanRevision`
   validation now names what is wrong with the graph: a task that depends on
   itself, on an unknown task or on the same task twice, and any dependency
   cycle (`task dependencies contain a cycle: a -> c -> b -> a`). Every task
   repository must be in the plan's permissions, as before. A plan's
   `budgets.max_workers` lies between 1 and `min(tasks, 4)` (`MAX_PLAN_WORKERS`),
   so a single-task plan still requires exactly 1 and no plan asks for more
   writers than it has tasks or than the runtime's four-run limit. Required
   recipe IDs are unique per repository (results bind to the pair), so every
   repository of a plan carries its manifest's `unit`. Serialization is
   unchanged: a single-task plan hashes exactly as before
   (`fixtures/domain/plan.valid.json` is unchanged).
2. **Tasks target distinct repositories.** `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans`
   accepts `tasks` (a list, each with `depends_on`) in place of `task`, and
   `budgets.max_workers`. Two tasks in one repository are refused: the
   candidate set freezes one commit per repository, and a dependent change
   inside one repository is one task, or the next plan revision. Base
   commits, required checks and default permissions are collected for every
   task repository from the confirmed manifest, as for one task.

title: Decision
text:
3. **Relationships are proposed from evidence and confirmed by the
   developer.** Discovery (`luuna-discovery::relationships`) proposes
   `package` relationships between registered repositories: a `package.json`
   whose `dependencies` or `devDependencies` name another repository's package
   `name`, a `Cargo.toml` `path` dependency resolving to another repository's
   root, and a `go.mod` `replace` directive with a relative path into another
   repository. Each carries `confirmed: false` and an evidence string naming
   the files. Confirming a manifest that still lists an unconfirmed
   relationship is refused with the relationships named; the developer sets
   `confirmed: true` or removes each. Confirmed relationships must be acyclic
   (`confirmed relationships form a cycle: a -> b -> a`); proposed ones do not
   count, since nothing schedules against them.
4. **Per-task state is durable (migration 10, `run_tasks`).** One row per plan
   task: state (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`,
   `blocked`, `cancelled`), attempt, candidate commit and tree, dependency
   task IDs, reason and `updated_at`. Events `task.scheduled`,
   `task.completed`, `task.failed`, `task.interrupted`, `task.blocked` and
   `task.cancelled` carry the reason. `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/tasks` lists
   them. Startup recovery marks running tasks `interrupted` in the same
   transaction that interrupts attempts and abandons leases.

title: Decision
text:
5. **The scheduler dispatches in dependency order under the existing
   gates.** `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` on a plan with several tasks
   rechecks, before any state changes, what `begin_implementation` checks for
   one writer (approval, ticket, manifest and base binding, a passed baseline
   per repository, free repositories) with one environment fingerprint per
   repository, since each repository's required recipes fingerprint its own
   tools; every task repository must be at its planned base with its
   registered identity; the attempt budget must hold every task that will run
   (`used + to_run <= max_attempts`, each task is one attempt). The graph is
   one active run against the global limit of four. The scheduler dispatches
   every queued task whose dependencies completed, concurrently up to
   `max_workers`, never two writers in one repository (the lease stays the
   durable rule), each task a writer attempt in its own Luuna-owned worktree
   through the M2c writer path unchanged (scope guard, post-session
   judgement, Luuna writer identity). A task whose dependency failed, was
   blocked, cancelled or interrupted is recorded `blocked` with the
   dependency's reason; independent tasks still run. A consumer's writer and
   its repository's checks receive, for each completed producer it depends
   on, `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_<REPOSITORY>_PATH` (the producer's preserved

title: Decision
text:
candidate worktree) and `…_COMMIT`, with the repository ID uppercased and
   dashes as underscores, and the writer's system prompt states them. When
   every task completed, one `CandidateSet` is recorded whose
   `repository_commits` holds every repository's exact commit and whose
   `dependency_bindings` maps `<consumer>:<producer>` to the producer commit
   (the domain validates that both name repositories of the set and the
   producer's exact commit); the run then waits in `validating` as today.
6. **Validation runs every repository's recipes in its own candidate
   worktree with the bindings.** A validation generation resolves and verifies
   one worktree per repository, resets each (`candidate.worktree_cleaned`
   names the repository), runs every required recipe of every repository
   inside that repository's worktree with the same `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_*`
   variables the writer saw (the executor's `CommandSpec.environment`), binds
   each result to its repository's exact commit, verifies every worktree
   between stages, and gives the fresh reviewer one bounded combined diff
   (per-repository sections under `# repository <id>: <base>..<commit>`
   headers, every changed path listed with its `repository_id`, attention
   paths prefixed by repository) plus the set's repositories and bindings.
   A failing required check names its repository and recipe and, for a

title: Decision
text:
multi-repository set, states `integration blocked: the candidate set is
   not accepted`; a producer's own passing check never stands for integration
   success. `GET …/diff` adds `repositories` (one entry per repository) and
   `dependency_bindings`; its top-level fields repeat the first repository's,
   so a single-repository candidate reads as before.
7. **Repair of a multi-repository set is re-planning.** `POST …/repair` and
   the `repair_allowed` decision refuse a set with more than one repository
   (`repair is not available for a multi-repository candidate set: create the
   next plan revision (re-plan) …`): a repair writer in one repository cannot
   re-establish the other repositories' bindings, so no single-repository fix
   stands for the set. Automatic repair stops with the same reason. The
   chosen limitation is recorded here rather than implemented halfway.
8. **Resumption by task under the original approval, within the approved
   budgets.** `POST …/implement` with `task_id` on an `interrupted` or
   `failed` workflow whose named task is `interrupted`, `failed` or `blocked`
   re-enters implementation (the domain admits `Interrupted -> Implementing`
   structurally for this gate only), requeues every task that did not
   complete and keeps completed tasks' commits, worktrees and evidence.
   Attempts still count against the plan budget. An attempt lost mid-prompt

title: Decision
text:
reserves the remaining approved cost budget exactly as ADR 0009 point 5
   records for one writer, so after a hard kill or an orderly shutdown of a
   writer that was mid-prompt the task-state gate admits the resumption and
   the budget gate refuses it with its re-plan requirement before anything
   runs; a task that failed with reported usage resumes. Cancellation stops
   every running task's writer and records the tasks and the run cancelled;
   queued tasks never start.

title: Consequences and validation
text:
## Consequences and validation

`crates/luuna-runtime/tests/multirepo.rs` drives a three-repository Python
fixture (`api -> shared -> consumer`, real `python -m unittest` checks, the
consumer importing the shared package through `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_SHARED_PATH`)
with the synthetic Pi fixture: a compatible change producing three exact
candidate commits, bindings in the consumer writer's environment and prompt,
three check results bound to exact commits and a reviewed set; an
incompatible shared change (`write_rename_function`) that passes the shared
check and fails the consumer check, blocking the set with the integration
reason and refusing repair; three independent tasks overlapping within
`max_workers = 2` while a fourth worker is refused; a failed producer blocking
its consumer with the reason and the failed task resuming by `task_id`
(`write_if_released`); a hard kill (startup recovery on the live database)
and an orderly shutdown leaving the completed task's commit and worktree
intact, the graph visible after restart and resumption refused by the budget
reservation; cancellation recording every task cancelled; and a cyclic plan,
a self or unknown dependency, two tasks in one repository, a confirmed cycle
and an unconfirmed proposed relationship each refused. Domain unit tests
cover the DAG rules, `max_workers` bounds and binding validation; discovery
unit tests cover the three relationship sources. Everything is synthetic:

title: Consequences and validation
text:
no model or provider is involved, and the developer checkouts are byte
identical afterwards.

The executor gained an additive `CommandSpec.environment`, set after the
sanitized host environment, so checks can receive bindings; the candidate
check index column keys a multi-repository set's results by
`<repository>/<recipe>` (the payload names both; single-repository rows are
unchanged), and artifact identities of such sets carry the repository.

title: What remains for full M4
text:
## What remains for full M4

- **P42 delegated roles.** Every task still runs with the `implementer` role
  and the same Pi writer profile; project orchestrator and repository-lead
  roles with their own context and assignment traces are not implemented.
- **P44 dependency overrides.** A plan's `depends_on` is taken as written;
  no override of a confirmed relationship (adding or waiving an edge with a
  reason) is recorded, and plans are not yet checked against the confirmed
  relationship graph.
- Shared contract artifacts beyond the producer worktree and commit (for
  example generated API schemas as named artifacts) are not modelled.
- A dependent change inside one repository in the same plan, and repair of a
  multi-repository set, remain re-planning.
- Desktop and client wiring of `tasks`, `max_workers`, `GET …/tasks`, the
  task events and the multi-repository diff view is client work outside this
  ADR.

title: ADR 0018: GitHub publication with an intent ledger, observed-only merges, and the doctor diagnostic
text:
# ADR 0018: GitHub publication with an intent ledger, observed-only merges, and the `doctor` diagnostic

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted for the M7 publication slice and the host
diagnostic. Implements R11 (automatic linked pull requests) and R12 (the
developer controls merging) on the candidate guards of ADR 0009, with the
durable intent-and-reconcile pattern of ADR 0014 applied to Git and GitHub
writes. Existing approval, baseline, candidate and review decisions remain in
force; nothing here relaxes them.

title: Context
text:
## Context

A reviewed candidate (ADR 0009: required checks passed, fresh independent
review passed, exact candidate hash) had no way out of the runtime: there was
no publisher, no PR tracking and no way to tell "CI failed on the PR" from
"not integrated". The roadmap's M7 exit requires linked pull requests created
once, recovery from a timeout after remote success and from partial
publication without duplicates, failing CI reported distinctly from
integration, and no automatic merge path. It also requires a diagnostic that
tells a developer on a fresh host what is missing before they start the
service. Publication needs a credential, which the runtime had no mechanism to
hold or pass to Git without exposing it in arguments, logs or events.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **GitHub only, by registered identity.** Publication parses `<owner>/<repo>`
   from the repository's confirmed manifest remote: `https://github.com/…`,
   `ssh://git@github.com/…` or `git@github.com:…`, with or without `.git`.
   Any other host or shape is refused with the reason. Before pushing, the
   runtime reads the developer checkout's configured `remote.origin.url`
   (read-only) and refuses unless it redacts to an identity equivalent to the
   registered one. The effective push URL is `git remote get-url --push
   origin`, that is, after the developer's own `url.<base>.insteadOf` /
   `pushInsteadOf` rewrites; those are machine-local transport choices, not a
   change of identity. The push names that URL rather than the remote name, so
   no remote-tracking reference is written into the developer checkout.

title: Decision
text:
2. **Credential mechanism.** `LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN` is read once at startup into
   the publication settings; only its presence is ever reported (health,
   `doctor`, logs, `Debug`). Git receives it through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` /
   `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n=http.https://github.com/.extraheader` /
   `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n=Authorization: Bearer …`, scoped to the GitHub HTTPS
   origin so a push to any other host never carries it; `credential.helper` is
   cleared and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`/`GIT_ASKPASS=` prevent prompts and
   helpers. The REST API receives it as a bearer header from the runtime's own
   HTTP client (reqwest with rustls and the `ring` provider; no system TLS
   toolchain is required to build). `LUUNA_GITHUB_API_URL` selects the REST
   base (default `https://api.github.com`); only `https://` or a loopback
   `http://` address is accepted, so tests can point it at a fake server.

title: Decision
text:
3. **One publication per run and candidate hash; branches are derived.**
   `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publish` with `{expected_hash, idempotency_key}` is
   refused, naming the next allowed step, unless the current candidate is
   `reviewed` with a `passed` verdict, its hash matches, no writer is active
   for the run or for any of its repositories, the ticket source is current
   (the Missions freshness check of ADR 0014) and the confirmed manifest is
   the one the plan was made for. The branch is
   `luuna/<ticket_id>/<first 12 hex of the candidate hash>`; the pull request
   targets the manifest's default branch and its body names the ticket,
   candidate hash, run and evidence summary. Repeating the same key returns
   the existing record without side effects; a different key for the same
   candidate is refused.

title: Decision
text:
4. **Intent ledger before every external write.** Each repository step (`push`,
   `pull_request`, `link`) records an intent under a stable key
   (`<run>:<hash>:<repository>:<step>:<branch>:<commit>`) before the call and
   settles it `succeeded`, `failed` or `uncertain` after. A push first runs
   `git ls-remote`: a branch already at the candidate commit is success
   without a push (timeout after success); a branch at another commit is a
   failure that leaves the remote alone. A pull request is first looked up by
   head (`pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=all`) and reused when it exists;
   a creation that times out is `uncertain`, never retried blindly. Partial
   success leaves the record `failed` with per-repository detail;
   `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publication/reconcile` re-runs only steps the
   ledger does not show succeeded, looking at the remote first, so a timeout
   after remote success and a push without a PR both recover without a
   duplicate. With several repositories, every PR body links the others once
   all exist.

title: Decision
text:
5. **Observation only; no merge anywhere.** `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/publication`
   refreshes CI (`check-runs` plus the combined commit status) and merge state
   (`merged`, `merged_at`, `merged_by`) per pull request under bounded
   timeouts. An observation failure leaves `ci.state: unknown` with its
   reason; a failing check is `ci.state: failure` and changes nothing else:
   candidate evidence, the run state and the publication state stay as they
   are. `integrated` is set, once, only when every pull request is observed
   merged on GitHub; the event names that a person merged it. There is no
   merge route, no merge client call and a test asserts both. The developer
   controls merging (R12); an automatic merge is out of v1 by decision, not by
   omission.

6. **Durable events.** `publication.requested`, `publication.pushed` (per
   repository, with `already_on_remote`), `publication.pr_opened` (per
   repository, with `reused_existing`), `publication.failed` (with per-step
   reasons), `publication.reconciled` and `publication.integrated` are run
   events, so a client replays them like every other state change.

title: Decision
text:
7. **`luuna-runtime doctor [--data-dir <dir>] [--json]`.** Reports Git, Python
   and Node versions, the resolved Pi launcher and its `--version` probe (the
   engine's own probe, in a private temporary directory, no model call), the
   data directory's existence and writability, the database's integrity and
   schema version (the `check` inspection), the presence of `LUUNA_API_TOKEN`
   and `LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN`, the names of configured provider credentials,
   whether the service port (`LUUNA_PORT`, default 4242) is free or already
   answers `/health` as Luuna, and whether the pinned component toolchain is
   discoverable. Git, Pi and a writable data directory are required; an
   existing database that is damaged or too new also fails the report because
   the service would refuse it. The exit status is 1 in those cases. No value
   of any credential is printed.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

- Storage migration 11 adds `publications` (one row per run and candidate
  hash; state and the full record) and `publication_intents` (the ledger).
  Records are rewritten in place as steps settle; the run event stream keeps
  the history.
- Publication runs as a supervised owned worker like a writer: it holds the
  run's active slot, so it is counted against the four-run bound, is signalled
  by shutdown and is never duplicated by a concurrent request.
- The ADR 0014 rule applies to GitHub: an uncertain write is looked up by its
  stable identity (branch name, PR head) before any retry; retries never
  invent new authority and never force-push.
- A developer's `insteadOf` rewrite is honoured for transport; the identity
  check still runs on the configured URL. The fixture tests rely on exactly
  this to publish into a local bare repository under a GitHub-shaped identity.
- Deleting or rewriting the remote branch outside Luuna is not repaired: a
  branch at another commit fails the push step with its reason and the
  developer resolves it.

title: What remains
text:
## What remains

- **Real GitHub evidence.** Every test runs against a local bare repository
  and a fake REST server. A genuine push and pull request with a real token,
  CI observation on a real workflow and a human merge on GitHub are the M7
  exit evidence and have not been produced.
- **Multi-repository candidate sets** are handled by the publisher (one
  branch per repository, linked bodies), but M4 has not produced such a set
  through the runtime, so the linking path has no end-to-end evidence.
- **Signed installers and a host update policy** (M7's portable installation
  half) are untouched by this decision; `doctor` is the diagnostic they will
  ship with.
- **Repair after CI failure** (A24's bounded repair that invalidates affected
  evidence) is reported by `ci.state: failure` but not yet driven into the
  repair workflow; the developer chooses to repair or re-plan.

title: ADR 0019: verified stack profiles, host capability probing and approved scaffolding
text:
# ADR 0019: verified stack profiles, host capability probing and approved scaffolding

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted; implements the M5 work packages P50–P55
(`docs/10-roadmap.md`) for R04 and R13 and the A05, A06, A18 and A31 scenarios.

title: Context
text:
## Context

M2a discovery proposed recipes for Rust, Node, Go, Python, Flutter, Gradle,
Android and iOS repositories but said nothing about whether the host could run
them: a `flutter test` recipe on a Windows laptop without Flutter looked the same
as one on a capable runner, and iOS raised a question instead of a recipe. R04
also requires creating new projects, and A05 requires that an approved scaffold
establishes tests before any feature work. The roadmap exit for M5 forbids
calling an unavailable platform passing, and ADR 0007 already records a missing
tool as `blocked`, never `failed`.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Discovery annotates checks with observed host capability.** Before a
   discovery proposal is computed, the runtime probes the host once (cached for
   two minutes) in `luuna-discovery::capabilities`: each tool a profile may need
   (`git`, `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `cargo`, `rustc`,
   `cargo-clippy`, `go`, `python3`, `python`, `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`,
   `flutter`, `dart`, `java`, `gradle`, `adb`; `xcodebuild` and `swift` on macOS
   only) is resolved on `PATH` with the executor's `PATHEXT` rules and run only
   with its own version argument (`--version`, `go version`, `java -version`,
   `adb version`, `xcodebuild -version`) under a 15-second deadline, a 64 KiB
   output bound and the sanitised environment of ADR 0007 (Luuna configuration,
   `GIT_*` and credential-shaped variables removed). A Microsoft Store
   app-execution alias whose probe fails is `missing`, not an available
   interpreter. `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` is recorded as the pseudo-tool
   `android-sdk`. Nothing read from a repository is executed, and the probe
   result (`Discovery.host_capabilities`) is machine evidence, never part of a
   manifest or its hash.
2. **Every proposed check carries `capability: available | missing` and
   `missing_tools`.** The annotation uses the executor's capability table, so
   it predicts what execution will find: a required check whose tool is

title: Decision
text:
missing stays proposed (it is never dropped silently), discovery raises one
   `missing-tool` question per tool naming the profile, the checks, the probe's
   reason and the install step, and the executor records the check `blocked`
   (incapable host) if it is confirmed and run. The domain fields are additive
   and default, so discoveries recorded before this decision still decode.
3. **Every advertised profile proposes meaningful recipes.** Node, React,
   Next.js and TypeScript propose `test`, `typecheck`, `lint` and `build` from
   `package.json` scripts with the detected runner (vitest, jest, `node --test`,
   mocha, ava, playwright) as evidence; Go proposes `go test ./...` and
   `go vet ./...`; Python proposes `<python> -m pytest -q` only when pytest is
   configured or declared, otherwise `<python> -m unittest -v` for a `tests/`
   package, plus `ruff check .` and `mypy .` when configured, where `<python>`
   is the interpreter the host actually has (`python` on Windows, `python3`
   elsewhere); Flutter proposes `flutter test` and `flutter analyze`; native
   Android proposes the Gradle wrapper's `testDebugUnitTest` (required,
   capabilities `jdk` and `android-sdk`; `gradlew.bat` on Windows) and
   `connectedAndroidTest` (optional, capability `android-device`); native iOS
   proposes `xcodebuild test` against the workspace or project with
   placeholder scheme and destination raised as `ios-scheme` and

title: Decision
text:
`ios-destination` questions and the `xcode` capability, which is `missing`
   on every non-macOS host.
4. **Scaffolding is proposed, hashed, confirmed and executed under policy.**
   `POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose` (`{profile, name, parent_dir}`)
   returns a deterministic `ScaffoldProposal` hashed with `luuna-json-v1`: the
   files that will be written from templates embedded in
   `luuna-discovery::scaffold`, the exact baseline recipes (identical to what
   discovery proposes for the result), declared generator and network steps,
   the probe results for the tools the profile needs, questions, and a
   `ready | blocked` status with the reason. Template profiles (`node`,
   `node-typescript`, `python`, `go`, `rust`) need no network: the TypeScript
   template relies on Node's built-in type stripping, and the Rust template
   ships a dependency-free `Cargo.lock` so `cargo test --locked` runs offline.
   `react` declares `npm install` as a network step. `flutter` declares
   `flutter create` as the generator (with its pub.dev resolution as a network
   step) and is blocked when `flutter` is missing. `android` and `ios` are
   always blocked: their generators are Android Studio and Xcode, the proposal
   says so and lists the recipes a later import will propose, and iOS is
   additionally blocked off macOS. A proposal writes nothing and is stored
   under `<data>/scaffolds/proposals/`.

title: Decision
text:
5. **`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold` executes exactly one proposal.** The
   body `{proposal_hash, idempotency_key, confirm: true, confirm_network?}` is
   refused for a hash that names no current proposal or whose stored content
   no longer hashes to it (409), a blocked proposal (422), unconfirmed network
   steps (422), a target that exists and is not empty (409), a target or parent
   inside the runtime data directory or containing it (422), and a project ID
   already registered (409). Otherwise the runtime writes the files (or runs
   the generator through the supervised executor), runs `git init -b main`,
   commits with hooks, signing and inherited `GIT_*` neutralised, runs the
   confirmed network steps and then the proposal's required baseline recipe
   through `luuna-executor` as a real check with private artifacts, registers
   the project through the ordinary registration path, runs discovery, and
   records `project.scaffolded` (proposal hash, commit, check outcome,
   discovery ID) in the project event stream. A failing or blocked baseline is
   returned as such with the registered project; the directory is left for the
   developer and nothing is reported passing. The result is recorded under
   `<data>/scaffolds/results/` and replayed for the same idempotency key; the
   same key with another hash is a 409. Executions are serialised.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

Discovery responses and stored discoveries gain `host_capabilities`, and each
proposed check gains `capability` and `missing_tools`; clients show them and
the `missing-tool` questions, and confirmation remains the developer's.
Nothing here bypasses the baseline gate of ADR 0007: a scaffolded project still
confirms its manifest and records a baseline run before implementation. No
storage migration was needed; proposals and idempotency records are private
JSON files, and `project.scaffolded` uses the existing project stream.

title: What remains
text:
## What remains

- **Capable-runner evidence per platform.** This decision was implemented and
  tested on Windows 11 x64 with Node, npm, Python, cargo and git present; the
  Node, TypeScript, Python and Rust scaffolds ran real passing baselines there.
  `go` was absent, so the Go profile and scaffold are proved only as a correctly
  blocked proposal and annotated discovery; the Go template's `go test ./...`
  has not been executed. Flutter, Android (JDK, SDK, device) and iOS (Xcode)
  checks were exercised only in their blocked form. M5's exit (every advertised
  profile establishing a baseline on a capable runner; Mac-specific checks
  demonstrated on a Mac) needs those hosts and remains open.
- **`flutter create` as a generator** is implemented but has not run anywhere;
  its first run on a host with Flutter is release evidence, not an assumption.
- **The React template** needs `npm install`; without network confirmation its
  baseline is blocked and the scaffold reports that.
- **Device and simulator checks** (`connectedAndroidTest`, `xcodebuild test`)
  need an `android-device`/`xcode` capability the probe can only detect as a
  tool's presence; a connected device or booted simulator is not probed.

title: ADR 0020: one capability catalog, shared failure explanations and a terminal client
text:
# ADR 0020: one capability catalog, shared failure explanations and a terminal client

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted. Implements the client-parity slice of M6 (R02, A19, A33); the publication, multi-repository and scaffolding actions of M4/M5/M7 join the catalog as they land.

title: Context
text:
## Context

R02 requires that the browser and the terminal expose equivalent product actions, and A33 that every client capability has an equivalent action and a consistent failure explanation in each client. Until now the desktop client (ADR 0001, ADR 0013) was the only client: its actions were spread over five React panels, the refusal and next-step text lived in `apps/desktop/src/failures.ts`, and nothing enumerated what "every product action" meant. Adding a second client by hand would have copied that table and drifted from it. The runtime's router (`crates/luuna-runtime/src/lib.rs`) is the only authoritative list of actions, and it changes with every milestone.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **One catalog of product actions.** `schemas/capability-catalog.json` lists every action the clients expose, once: its runtime method and route, the `@luuna/api-client` method, the desktop control (a `data-capability` attribute value; a control that triggers several reads carries several values separated by spaces), the TUI command, the failure classes that apply, and, where the clients reach the same action differently, a note saying how. `schemas/capability-catalog.schema.json` is its contract. `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` (run by `npm test`) validates the catalog, requires unique ids, commands and desktop markers, parses the runtime's `.route(` declarations read-only and refuses a catalog entry whose route or method the runtime does not serve, checks that every `client_method` exists on `LuunaClient` and every failure mode is a shared class, and names every runtime mutation that no client exposes yet (`LUUNA_CATALOG_STRICT=1` turns that report into a failure once parity is complete).

title: Decision
text:
2. **One source of failure explanations.** The pure logic of the desktop's `failures.ts` moved to `packages/api-client/src/failures.ts`: `describeFailure`, `nextStep`, `baselineStep`, `actionFailure`, plus `classifyFailure` and `explainFailure`, which return the failure class and the sentence `"<Action> refused: <reason> <next step>"`. The desktop re-exports it; the TUI imports it. Transport failures and 5xx stay plain sentences; a server body is never shown. The runtime still decides every state, permission, reason and refusal: the explanation only maps the runtime's recorded reason to the next step the runtime admits.
3. **A terminal client with parity.** `packages/tui` (`@luuna/tui`) is a Node client with no dependency beyond `@luuna/api-client`, built on `node:readline`. `luuna-tui` alone opens a keyboard-driven workbench (lists navigated with the arrow keys, Enter, Esc, `r` to reload, `q` to quit) whose menus are generated from the command table, so every cataloged action is reachable; authoritative state is re-read from the runtime after each action; `/health` is polled, an outage is shown in the header and every list reloads when the runtime answers again. `luuna-tui <command> [args] [--json]` runs one catalog action for scripts and tests. The connection comes from `LUUNA_URL` (loopback only) and `LUUNA_API_TOKEN`, prompted hidden on a terminal and never echoed. Approval requires the developer to acknowledge the comple

title: Decision
text:
te plan hash (typed, or `--acknowledge-hash`), exactly as the desktop checkbox stands for the hash shown beside it; a mismatch is refused before anything is sent. Run events are followed live over the runtime's SSE stream with `Last-Event-ID` resumption (`LuunaClient.streamEvents`/`followEvents`), reconnecting after an outage from the last received sequence and ending when the run settles.
4. **Parity evidence.** `packages/tui/test/commands.test.mjs` proves that every catalog entry has one command and that each command issues the cataloged method and route against a mocked fetch; `apps/desktop/src/capabilities.test.ts` proves that every catalog id is carried by a desktop control and that every marker is cataloged; `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs` drives the documented walkthrough through the TUI against a built runtime and the synthetic Pi fixture (import, discovery, confirmation, baseline, ticket, plan, exact-hash approval, writer, candidate, diff, validation with `fixture:review_malformed_once`, re-validation, a hard kill during a held check with the outage and the reconnection observed by a live follower, restart, recovery, orderly shutdown) and asserts that the TUI reports the same authoritative states the runtime's API shows, writing `report.json`/`report.md` outside Git.

title: Decision
text: Adding a product action costs one catalog entry (the contract check refuses a route the runtime does not serve), one `LuunaClient` method, one `data-capability` marker on the desktop control and one object in `packages/tui/src/commands.mjs` with its `example`; the three parity tests then cover it without further changes.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

The desktop gained two small controls so that every cataloged action has a control: "Show writer attempts" on a ticket and "Stop runtime" (ADR 0010) beside Disconnect. The design system (ADR 0013) is untouched; the TUI shows every state as the runtime's unchanged text, as the design system requires, but has no tones: a terminal colour mapping of the same six tones is future work. The `@luuna/api-client` source is loaded by Node directly (type stripping), so it uses no TypeScript syntax that needs transformation (no parameter properties, no enums) and imports its own modules with `.ts` extensions.

`npm test` fails when a catalog entry names a route the runtime does not serve, a client method that does not exist, a failure class that is not shared, a TUI command that is missing or an action no desktop control exposes. It does not yet fail for a runtime mutation that no client exposes: those are reported, so that M4/M5/M7 routes can land in the runtime first.

title: What remains
text:
## What remains

- Parity for later actions: the scaffolding proposals and scaffolds of ADR 0019, the publication, publication record and reconciliation of ADR 0018, the memory promotion and project export of ADR 0021 and the multi-repository task listing of ADR 0017 were cataloged the same day with their client methods, desktop controls and TUI commands (49 actions); `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` names any later runtime mutation until it is cataloged.
- A full keyboard audit of the interactive TUI (every menu by keyboard only, screen-reader friendliness of the list output, terminal width handling) comparable to the desktop's accessibility audit in `scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs`; the smoke covers the non-interactive mode only.
- Terminal tones for the six outcome tones of ADR 0013, so a state reads the same in colour everywhere.
- The browser client of P61 is the desktop's web build; it shares the desktop markers and needs no separate catalog work, but its own smoke evidence belongs to M8.

title: ADR 0021: scoped memory promotion and scope-safe project export
text:
# ADR 0021: scoped memory promotion and scope-safe project export

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: accepted; extends ADR 0014's bounded M6 slice toward
R14 (scoped user, project and process memory) and acceptance scenarios A28 and
A29 (private memory from another project is excluded; a project export carries
no credentials, personal memory or required absolute paths).

title: Context
text:
## Context

ADR 0014 gave Atlas memory three explicit scopes (`process`, `project`, `user`),
provenance, lexical retrieval (`GET …/memory?q=`), explicit user opt-in on
listing and selection, and reconciled deletion. Two M6 obligations stayed open:
a developer could not widen a memory's scope without retyping it under a new
provenance, and nothing produced a project artifact another machine or person
could receive while proving that user memory, credentials and this host's paths
stayed home. The desktop's component status deliberately shows the private
workspace path; an export must not.

title: Decision
text:
## Decision

1. **Promotion widens scope one step, never narrows it.** `POST
   /api/v1/projects/{id}/memory/{memory_id}/promote` with `{idempotency_key,
   expected_hash, to_scope}` accepts only `process -> project` and `project ->
   user`. It refuses a stale displayed hash (409), a skipped or backward step
   (422) and a deleted memory (404). It creates the record in the wider Atlas
   store with provenance `promoted from <scope> memory <id>: <original
   provenance>` (clipped to the 1000-byte bound), then deletes the narrower
   record through the existing reconciled delete. Both steps run under the
   durable component-operation ledger of ADR 0014: the promotion intent is
   recorded first, the create uses the derived key `<key>:promote-create`, and
   a retry after a crash between the two steps finishes the promotion from the
   recorded create instead of duplicating it; a tombstoned source with no
   recorded create fails closed with the next step named. Replaying the key
   returns the recorded response. Narrowing is an ordinary delete plus a new
   record, because a narrower copy of a wider memory would create two
   independently writable records of one fact.
2. **Export fails closed.** `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/export` returns the
   confirmed machine-independent manifest, the project's ticket projections,
   its `project` and `process` memory and the current rendered prompts, with

title: Decision
text:
an `omitted` list naming user memory, credentials, machine-registry paths,
   worktrees and private artifacts. Before answering, the runtime walks every
   string of the export and refuses (409, "Export refused: it would include …")
   any that contains a known credential value (the API token, provider keys and
   credential-shaped environment values the repair redaction already knows),
   the data directory, a registered checkout path, the home directory, an
   absolute path of this host's shapes, or a memory record whose `scope` is
   `user`. Refusal is preferred to redaction: a redacted export would still
   prove that private text reached the export path.
3. **Clients.** Both clients expose promotion beside deletion with the same
   displayed-hash acknowledgment and show the export as a download of the
   returned JSON; neither client composes an export itself.

title: Consequences
text:
## Consequences

- R14's promotion/deletion obligation is implemented and reconciled; retrieval
  stays lexical (substring over content and provenance), as ADR 0014 bounded it.
- A29 has a runtime guard and a real-CLI regression
  (`components_real_promotion_widens_scope_and_export_keeps_private_memory_home`)
  that promotes a process memory to project and then to user, checks the lists,
  exports with a user memory present, and shows an export refused when a ticket
  quotes a host path. The pure guard has its own unit test.
- Export is a read model; importing an export on another machine (registering
  the repositories there and reconciling tickets against a Missions store) is
  not implemented and is recorded as remaining M6 work with browser/TUI parity
  of every cataloged action (ADR 0020).

title: Luuna Atlas
text:
# Luuna Atlas

Structured expertise and project memory. This is Luuna's maintained MIT-licensed component. The Luuna package identity is **@luuna/atlas-cli**. It is maintained in [luuna-ai/luuna-atlas](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas). The npm package remains private and unpublished.

The CLI and library behavior are implemented in Go. For development, install Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3, then run from this directory:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run build:native
bun src/cli.ts --help
bun run verify
```

The standalone executable is `luuna-atlas`; `lat` is the Luuna suite shortcut and `la` remains a compatibility alias. The build writes all three executables to `.atlas-bin/` (with `.exe` on Windows). Run the native binary directly, or continue using `bun src/cli.ts <args>`; the compatibility entry point builds Go when needed and forwards arguments, input, output and exit status. `luuna atlas <args>` remains the entry through Luuna's installed launcher. Registry publication is disabled; use the Luuna CLI installer from the main checkout to make the commands available on PATH.

title: Luuna Atlas
text:
The native executable needs neither Bun nor Node. To build it directly with the pinned Go toolchain, use `go build -mod=vendor -trimpath -o luuna-atlas ./cmd/luuna-atlas`. Go dependencies are included in `vendor/`, so building does not fetch modules. Bun remains necessary for the source launcher, TypeScript library transport, development compatibility checks and user-provided TypeScript/npm provider recipes. Set `LUUNA_ATLAS_GO` to a Go executable when it is installed outside PATH, or `LUUNA_ATLAS_BINARY` to an existing native executable for the compatibility transport.

Project data lives in `.luuna/atlas/` (configuration in `.luuna/atlas/config.yaml`). A project that still has the pre-Luuna data directory is moved there automatically the first time a command needs the store, with one notice on stderr; record formats are unchanged. Luuna consumes a pinned Git submodule and integrates through the CLI/JSON boundary. The existing TypeScript library exports call the native Go implementation. Runtime policy and approvals remain Luuna's responsibility.

Self-upgrade is disabled while the package is private. Update through a reviewed commit in this repository; never replace this fork with a similarly named registry package. Dependency installs do not change Git hooks.

title: Luuna Atlas
text:
Read [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-atlas-upstream) for attribution and provenance, [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-atlas-agents) for development rules and [MIGRATION.md](/docs/components-atlas-migration) for layout changes. Upstream release/runbook documents are historical references and do not authorize publication.

For the command, record, configuration and integration tour used as the rewrite baseline, read the [CLI and system map](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/CLI-SYSTEM-MAP.md). The companion [CLI reference](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/CLI-REFERENCE.md) captures help for every command and config subcommand. The [Go rewrite report](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/GO-REWRITE-REPORT.md) maps the current architecture, command coverage and verification. Baseline source links resolve to the frozen TypeScript oracle in `compat/reference/`; current Go source is in `cmd/luuna-atlas/` and `internal/atlas/`.

title: Origin / attribution
text:
## Origin / attribution

Luuna Atlas is derived from Mulch 0.11.0 by Jaymin West (MIT), https://github.com/jayminwest/mulch. The original license notice is preserved in [LICENSE](/docs/components-atlas-license); see [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-atlas-upstream) for provenance.

title: Maintenance and releases
text:
## Maintenance and releases

The repository is maintained by the luuna-ai organization. CI is configured to run the supported `bun run verify` surface on Linux and Windows with Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3. It checks Go formatting, builds native executable aliases, runs go vet and Go tests, then type checks the compatibility surface, validates repository instructions and runs Bun tests. Differential tests compare Go outputs and persisted state with the frozen oracle; historical internal Bun unit tests validate that reference, while public CLI/API tests exercise Go. Race detection is available separately through `bun run go:test:race` on a host with a supported C compiler.

Registry publishing is disabled and requires no npm token. Luuna pins a reviewed commit, never a floating branch; update its submodule only after CI and the consumer smoke pass. See [MIGRATION.md](/docs/components-atlas-migration) for the verified source baseline. Dependency installation does not build executables or change Git hooks.

title: Atlas Configuration Guide
text:
# Atlas Configuration Guide

This guide covers `config.yaml` and the surrounding `.luuna/atlas/` surface for **v0.10.7**. It is the reference doc for orgs running Atlas across many repos and many ICs.

If you're new to Atlas, start with the [README](/docs/components-atlas-readme) — it covers what Atlas is and the day-one commands. This document assumes you already know `luuna-atlas record` / `luuna-atlas prime` and want to tune them.

Conventions in this doc:

- Every config key states its **default** next to its name.
- YAML examples are minimal and copy-pasteable.
- Cross-references look like `(see §Hooks)` and link to a section below.
- Two audiences: **Part 1** for platform engineers rolling Atlas out; **Part 2** for ICs working inside a rollout.

---

title: Why customize Atlas
text:
## Why customize Atlas

The defaults work fine for a solo repo or a five-person team. At 50+ ICs writing into the same expertise store, four kinds of entropy start to bite:

**Vocabulary drift.** Three different teams independently invent `incident`, `postmortem`, and `outage` records. None of them validate against each other, none of them surface to `luuna-atlas prime` consistently, and reviewers can't tell which kind of record they're reading. The fix is `custom_types` plus `disabled_types` to retire the losing names without breaking peer repos (see §Custom record types, §Retiring types).

**Ungoverned writes.** Without per-domain rules, anyone can drop a `pattern` into a `security` domain without naming an owner. Six months later, no one knows who to ask about the rule. The fix is `domains.<name>.required_fields` — say "every record in `security` must carry `owner`" and validation enforces it (see §Per-domain rules).

**Stale records crowding `luuna-atlas prime`.** Tactical records are 14-day by default. On a monolith, that's still hundreds of records on day 15. Two levers: drop `luuna-atlas prime` into `manifest` mode for large repos (see §Prime), and tighten `classification_defaults.shelf_life` so prune walks records out faster (see §Classification defaults).

title: Why customize Atlas
text:
**Integration sprawl.** Slack wants a webhook on every new failure. Compliance wants an audit log on every record. Each repo solving this independently produces six implementations and three of them break silently. The fix is `hooks` — a single shell script per repo, deployed from a template, doing the integration work in one place (see §Hooks).

**Provider fragmentation.** Your org standardized on an internal coding agent runtime three months ago. The built-in `claude` / `cursor` / `codex` recipes don't know about it. Filesystem recipes let you ship a custom recipe through repo scaffolding without forking Atlas (see §Provider recipes).

---

title: Quick tour: scenarios for large orgs
text:
## Quick tour: scenarios for large orgs

Eight motivating scenarios. Each one is short on purpose — the section it points to has the working example.

**Slack-notify the team on every new failure record.** Drop a `post-record` hook that reads `payload.type === "failure"` from stdin and POSTs to a webhook. Non-zero exit warns but doesn't block, so a Slack outage can't take down `luuna-atlas record`. → §Hooks.

**Gate the `infra` domain to only `decision` and `runbook` types.** Set `domains.infra.allowed_types: [decision, runbook]`. ICs writing `failure` records into `infra` get a validation error pointing at the violating field, plus a copy-paste retry hint. → §Per-domain rules.

**Add a custom `incident` type that extends `failure`.** Declare it under `custom_types.incident` with `extends: failure` and add `pager_link` / `severity` to `required`. Inherits dedup, summary, and compact strategy from `failure`. → §Custom record types.

**Retire the `reference` type org-wide without breaking peer repos.** Add `reference` to `disabled_types`. New writes emit a deprecation warning; existing records still read; CLI `--type` choices still include it so peer repos that haven't synced the config aren't surprised mid-command. → §Retiring types.

title: Quick tour: scenarios for large orgs
text:
**Ship a custom Cursor recipe to every repo in the org.** Drop a `.luuna/atlas/recipes/cursor.ts` shipping with your repo scaffolding. Filesystem recipes win over built-ins, so the org variant takes precedence without anyone running `npm install`. → §Provider recipes.

**Drop `luuna-atlas prime` output size on a monolith from 12k tokens to 800.** Set `prime.default_mode: manifest`. Agents see a domain index and per-domain counts up front, then call `luuna-atlas prime <domain>` or `luuna-atlas prime --files <path>` to scope-load. → §Prime output tuning.

**Force every record in `security` to carry an `owner` field.** Set `domains.security.required_fields: [owner]`. ICs running `luuna-atlas record security ...` without `--owner` get a targeted error before the write hits disk. → §Per-domain rules.

**Auto-archive observational records older than 14 days, not 30.** Set `classification_defaults.shelf_life.observational: 14`. The demotion ladder is unchanged — records still walk one tier per `luuna-atlas prune` pass — but the threshold to enter the walk shrinks. → §Classification defaults.

---

title: Part 1 — Admin guide
text: # Part 1 — Admin guide

title: The .luuna/atlas/ directory layout
text:
## The `.luuna/atlas/` directory layout

```
.luuna/atlas/
├── config.yaml         # config (this doc); commit
├── expertise/
│   └── <domain>.jsonl        # append-only records; commit
├── archive/
│   └── <domain>.jsonl        # soft-archived records; commit
├── recipes/                  # optional; commit if shared org-wide
│   ├── <name>.ts
│   └── <name>.sh
├── hooks/                    # optional; commit
│   └── *.sh
└── README.md                 # auto-generated; commit
```

**Commit everything.** `.luuna/atlas/` is intentionally checked in — expertise is a team artifact, not a per-developer cache. The auto-generated `README.md` describes the layout for first-time visitors to the repo.

**`.gitattributes` setup.** At the repo root (not inside `.luuna/atlas/`):

```
.luuna/atlas/expertise/*.jsonl merge=union
.luuna/atlas/archive/*.jsonl   merge=union
```

`merge=union` makes concurrent record writes from two branches concatenate instead of conflicting on the merge. Combined with atomic writes and file locking inside Atlas itself, two agents writing to the same domain on different worktrees never collide.

**What not to read directly.** `.luuna/atlas/archive/<domain>.jsonl` is stale by definition. `luuna-atlas prime` and `luuna-atlas search` (without `--archived`) both skip it. Don't `cat` it during a coding session; use `luuna-atlas search --archived <query>` instead.

---

title: config.yaml — top-level shape
text:
## `config.yaml` — top-level shape

A fully-populated config, with comments:

```yaml
version: "1"

title: Per-domain write rules. Empty map (the default) means any registered type
text: # Per-domain write rules. Empty map (the default) means any registered type

title: is accepted in any domain.
text:
# is accepted in any domain.
domains:
  security:
    allowed_types: [decision, failure]
    required_fields: [owner]
  infra:
    allowed_types: [decision, runbook]
  frontend: {}                   # no extra constraints

title: Soft / warn / hard caps per domain. Defaults shown.
text:
# Soft / warn / hard caps per domain. Defaults shown.
governance:
  max_entries: 100
  warn_entries: 150
  hard_limit: 200

title: Days before a record demotes one tier on luuna-atlas prune. foundational is
text: # Days before a record demotes one tier on `luuna-atlas prune`. foundational is

title: permanent and not configurable here.
text:
# permanent and not configurable here.
classification_defaults:
  shelf_life:
    tactical: 14
    observational: 30
```
