
**Required keys** (omit and Atlas refuses to start): `version`, `domains`, `governance`, `classification_defaults`. Atlas ships sensible defaults for the latter three; the typical real-world config overrides governance caps and adds domains.

**Defaults applied automatically.** Any of the four top-level required keys missing in your file is filled in from `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (see `src/schemas/config.ts`). You only need to spell out the keys you're customizing.

---

title: Per-domain rules (domains)
text:
## Per-domain rules (`domains`)

`domains` is a map from domain name to per-domain config. Keys:

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
|-----|------|---------|--------|
| `allowed_types` | `string[]` | `[]` (all allowed) | Gates `--type` on write. Mismatch fails with a hint listing the allowed types. |
| `required_fields` | `string[]` | `[]` (no extras) | Top-level fields every record in the domain must carry, on top of per-type requirements. |

**Worked example.** Lock down `security` to decisions and failures, and require `owner`:

```yaml
domains:
  security:
    allowed_types: [decision, failure]
    required_fields: [owner]
```

After this lands, `luuna-atlas record security --type pattern ...` fails before writing. So does `luuna-atlas record security --type decision --title "..." --rationale "..."` without `--owner`.

**Overlap with `disabled_types`.** Disabled wins. If `security.allowed_types` contains `failure` and `disabled_types` also contains `failure`, writing a failure record still emits the deprecation warning. This is deliberate — disabling a type at the org level shouldn't be silently re-enabled by a stale per-domain config.

title: Per-domain rules (domains)
text:
**Escape hatch.** Pass `--allow-domain-mismatch` to `luuna-atlas record` or `luuna-atlas validate` to bypass the domain check. This is for worktree/CI lag where the JSONL has landed (via `merge=union`) before the config update has propagated. `luuna-atlas sync` intentionally ignores `--allow-domain-mismatch` — sync is the gate that catches misconfiguration before push.

**Doctor checks.** `luuna-atlas doctor` surfaces two related checks:

- `domain-conformance` (informational) — records that violate per-domain rules but still parse.
- `domain-violations` (failing) — same set, but as a hard fail when run with `--strict`.
- `domain-rules-compatibility` — catches misconfiguration where `required_fields` lists a field no `allowed_types` entry can hold.

---

title: Custom record types (customtypes)
text:
## Custom record types (`custom_types`)

Declare additional types beyond the six built-ins. Each entry under `custom_types` is keyed by type name.

Fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Effect |
|-------|------|----------|--------|
| `extends` | string | recommended | Name of a built-in type to inherit `required` / `optional` / `dedup_key` / `id_key` / `summary` / `compact` / `section_title` / `extracts_files` / `files_field` from. |
| `required` | `string[]` | optional | Additional required fields. Merges as a union with the parent's `required`. |
| `optional` | `string[]` | optional | Additional optional fields. Union with parent. |
| `dedup_key` | string | optional | Field used for dedup. Overrides parent. |
| `id_key` | string | optional | Field used as the human-readable id stem. Overrides parent. |
| `summary` | string | optional | Summary template. `"{field}"` tokens interpolate record fields. |
| `compact` | enum | optional | One of `concat`, `merge_outcomes`, `keep_latest`, `manual`. |
| `section_title` | string | optional | Heading used in `luuna-atlas prime` output. |
| `extracts_files` | bool | optional | Whether `files_field` should be parsed as file anchors. |
| `files_field` | string | optional | Field name holding file paths. |
| `aliases` | `Record<string, string[]>` | optional | Map canonical field name to legacy names. Disk records carrying a legacy field are rewritten to canonical at read time. |

title: Custom record types (customtypes)
text:
**Worked example: `release_decision` extending `decision`.**

```yaml
custom_types:
  release_decision:
    extends: decision
    required: [release_tag]
    optional: [rollback_plan]
    summary: "{title} ({release_tag})"
    section_title: "Release decisions"
```

Use it:

```bash
luuna-atlas record releases \
  --type release_decision \
  --title "Cut v2.4 from main-stable" \
  --rationale "Hotfix for CVE-2026-1234 lands today" \
  --release-tag v2.4.0
```

Validation requires `title`, `rationale` (inherited from `decision`), and `release_tag` (added). `--rollback-plan` is accepted but optional.

**Worked example: `incident` extending `failure`.**

```yaml
custom_types:
  incident:
    extends: failure
    required: [severity, pager_link]
    optional: [postmortem_url]
    summary: "[{severity}] {description}"
    section_title: "Incidents"
    aliases:
      pager_link: [pagerduty_url, page_url]   # accept legacy names on read
```

Records written months ago with `pagerduty_url` get rewritten to `pager_link` on every read — no migration script needed.

**Constraints.**

title: Custom record types (customtypes)
text:
- **Custom-from-custom is not supported in v0.9.0.** `extends` must name one of the six built-ins (`convention`, `pattern`, `failure`, `decision`, `reference`, `guide`). The schema validator rejects custom-from-custom at config load.
- **AJV preserves `additionalProperties: false`.** A custom type cannot accept arbitrary extra fields; everything must be declared in `required` or `optional` (or inherited).
- **Extending a disabled type is rejected.** If `failure` is in `disabled_types`, `custom_types.incident.extends: failure` fails config validation. Retire the parent only after migrating children.

---

title: Retiring types (disabledtypes)
text:
## Retiring types (`disabled_types`)

A list of registered type names (built-in or custom) that are being retired. Writes still succeed but emit a deprecation warning. Reads always succeed. `--type` choices in CLI help still include the type so peer repos that haven't synced the new config aren't surprised mid-command.

```yaml
disabled_types: [reference, runbook_v1]
```

**When to use this vs deleting the custom type entirely.**

- **Use `disabled_types`** when:
  - Peer repos in your org still write the type and haven't pulled the config update yet.
  - Existing records on disk need to remain readable.
  - You want a soft migration window where new writes flag but old code keeps working.
- **Delete the `custom_types` entry entirely** when:
  - All historical records have been migrated to the replacement type.
  - No peer repo writes the type anymore.
  - You're confident `luuna-atlas doctor` reports zero records of this type across all repos.

**Conflict semantics.** `disabled_types` wins over `allowed_types` on overlap (see §Per-domain rules). This is deliberate so a stale `allowed_types` entry doesn't silently un-retire a type.

---

title: Lifecycle hooks (hooks, hooksettings)
text:
## Lifecycle hooks (`hooks`, `hook_settings`)

Hooks run external scripts at lifecycle events. Four events, two semantics each:

| Event | Blocks on non-zero? | Mutable via stdout? | Stdin payload |
|-------|---------------------|---------------------|---------------|
| `pre-record` | yes | yes | `{ event, payload: <ExpertiseRecord> }` |
| `post-record` | no (warns) | no (stdout ignored) | `{ event, payload: <ExpertiseRecord> }` |
| `pre-prime` | yes | yes | `{ event, payload: { domains: [{ domain, records }] } }` |
| `pre-prune` | yes | no (stdout ignored) | `{ event, payload: { candidates: [{ domain, stale, demote, anchor_decay }] } }` |

**Execution contract.**

- **Working directory**: project root (the repo containing `.luuna/atlas/`).
- **Environment**: parent env preserved, plus `LUUNA_ATLAS_HOOK=1`.
- **Process group**: detached, so SIGKILL on timeout cleans up children.
- **stdin**: payload JSON.
- **stdout**: read only on mutable events (`pre-record`, `pre-prime`). Accepts both `{ event, payload }` and bare-payload shapes — pick whichever is convenient.
- **stderr**: forwarded to the calling terminal.
- **Exit code**:
  - `0`: continue.
  - non-zero from `pre-*`: block the operation, print the script's stderr.
  - non-zero from `post-*`: warn, continue.

**Settings.**

```yaml
hook_settings:
  timeout_ms: 5000     # default 5000ms; SIGKILL on timeout
```

title: Lifecycle hooks (hooks, hooksettings)
text: **Dry-run.** `luuna-atlas record --dry-run` and `luuna-atlas prune --dry-run` skip hooks. Preview commands never trigger Slack posts or external confirmation flows.

title: Payload examples
Worked example: Slack-notify on new failures
text:
### Worked example: Slack-notify on new failures

`.luuna/atlas/hooks/slack-failures.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

title: Read payload from stdin.
text:
# Read payload from stdin.
payload=$(cat)

title: Only react to failure records.
text:
# Only react to failure records.
type=$(echo "$payload" | jq -r '.payload.type // empty')
[ "$type" = "failure" ] || exit 0

desc=$(echo "$payload" | jq -r '.payload.description')
id=$(echo "$payload"   | jq -r '.payload.id')
repo=$(basename "$PWD")

title: Fire-and-forget. Non-zero exit warns but does not block the record.
text:
# Fire-and-forget. Non-zero exit warns but does not block the record.
curl -fsS -X POST "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg t "[$repo] new failure: $desc ($id)" '{text: $t}')" \
  > /dev/null

exit 0
```

Wire it up:

```yaml
hooks:
  post-record: [.luuna/atlas/hooks/slack-failures.sh]
```

`SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is read from the parent env, which is preserved into the hook.

---

title: Prune, decay, and archive (decay, --check-anchors)
text:
## Prune, decay, and archive (`decay`, `--check-anchors`)

`luuna-atlas prune` is the demotion engine. Default behavior is **soft-archive**, not delete.

**The demotion ladder (hardcoded):**

```
foundational  →  tactical  →  observational  →  archived
```

One tier per `luuna-atlas prune` pass. `--aggressive` collapses straight to archived in a single pass.

**Soft-archive.** Records demoted past `observational` move to `.luuna/atlas/archive/<domain>.jsonl` with `status: "archived"` and `archived_at: <iso-date>`. Each archive file begins with a `# ARCHIVED — ...` banner. `readExpertiseFile` skips `#`-prefixed lines, so banners never confuse parsers.

**Hard delete.** `luuna-atlas prune --hard` skips the archive and removes records outright. Reserve this for sensitive data that shouldn't persist anywhere.

**Restore.** `luuna-atlas restore <id>` brings a soft-archived record back to live expertise. The classification resets to `observational`.

**Read paths.** `luuna-atlas prime` and the default `luuna-atlas search` never read archive files. `luuna-atlas search --archived <query>` is the only built-in read path that walks `.luuna/atlas/archive/`.

title: Supersession decay
text:
### Supersession decay

When record B has `supersedes: [A]`, A walks one tier per `luuna-atlas prune` pass. Cross-domain by design — if a `frontend` decision supersedes an `infra` decision, the infra record demotes regardless. Each step stamps `supersession_demoted_at: <iso-date>` on A. `--aggressive` collapses A to archived in a single pass.

title: Anchor-validity decay
text:
### Anchor-validity decay

Opt in with `luuna-atlas prune --check-anchors`. Records whose declared file or directory anchors stop resolving (the underlying path was deleted, moved, etc.) demote one tier per pass when **both** of these are true:

- The fraction of valid anchors is below `decay.anchor_validity.threshold`.
- The record's age exceeds `decay.anchor_validity.grace_days`.

Records with zero anchors are exempt — absence is interpreted as "applies globally."

Config:

```yaml
decay:
  anchor_validity:
    threshold: 0.5     # default 0.5; demote when valid_fraction < this. Range [0, 1].
    grace_days: 7      # default 7; records younger than this are exempt.
    weight: 0.3        # reserved for a future fitness blend; currently unused.
```

`threshold` outside `[0, 1]` and negative `grace_days` are validated at command time and produce a human-readable error before any record is touched.

Demotions stamp `anchor_decay_demoted_at: <iso-date>`.

title: Conflict resolution
text:
### Conflict resolution

When supersession decay and anchor-validity decay both want to demote the same record, **staleness wins**. Atlas picks the tier walk caused by classification age and skips the intermediate demotion stamp. `--explain` prints per-record reasons:

```bash
luuna-atlas prune --check-anchors --explain --dry-run
```

emits a line per candidate showing which decay path fired and why.

---

title: Prime output tuning (prime)
text:
## Prime output tuning (`prime`)

```yaml
prime:
  default_mode: full       # "full" (default) or "manifest"
  session_close:
    style: conditional     # directive | conditional (default) | minimal | none
    # custom: |
    #   Verbatim prose to emit instead of the preset. Wins over `style`.
  tier_weights:            # full-mode trust ordering
    star: 100
    foundational: 50
    tactical: 20
    observational: 10
```

**`full`** (the default) emits the record index: one line per record, failures first, capped by `--budget` (default 4000 tokens). `luuna-atlas show <id>` prints a full record.

**`manifest`** emits a domain index and per-domain record counts plus a quick reference of common commands. Agents then scope-load with `luuna-atlas prime <domain>` or `luuna-atlas prime --files <path>`. On a 12k-token expertise store, manifest mode typically drops session-priming output to under 1k tokens.

Override per invocation:

- `luuna-atlas prime --manifest` — manifest mode regardless of config.
- `luuna-atlas prime --full` — full record bodies regardless of config.
- `luuna-atlas prime --files src/foo.ts` — load only records relevant to the listed paths, with per-file framing, classification age, and confirmation scores.

title: Session-close footer (prime.sessionclose)
text:
### Session-close footer (`prime.session_close`)

`luuna-atlas prime` (and the snippet `luuna-atlas setup` / `luuna-atlas onboard` writes into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / `.cursor/rules/luuna-atlas.mdc`) ends with a footer reminding the agent to record insights before closing the session. The footer is configurable so each project can dial in the right voice without forking:

- **`style: directive`** — numbered imperative + inline type glossary + dedup nudge + anti-filler examples. Loudest. Use when the team needs reminding that `luuna-atlas record` exists at all.
- **`style: conditional`** (default) — "if you discovered insights worth preserving, record them; skip if no insight surfaced." The v0.10.0 reframing. Use for teams already recording consistently.
- **`style: minimal`** — one-line nudge.
- **`style: none`** — suppress the footer entirely.
- **`custom: "<prose>"`** — verbatim override. Wins over `style`. Use for org-specific phrasing or non-English voices.

The 🚨 marker is preserved on `directive` for `markdown` / `plain` prime footers (memory anchor in long sessions) and dropped from the embedded variant (which lives at the top of CLAUDE.md, not at end-of-session). Re-run `luuna-atlas setup <provider>` and `luuna-atlas onboard` after changing this knob — the existing files check stale until you do.

---

title: Search tuning (search)
text:
## Search tuning (`search`)

```yaml
search:
  boost_factor: 0.1        # default 0.1; multiplier on confirmation outcomes
```

`luuna-atlas search` ranks results with BM25, then applies a confirmation boost: records with positive `outcomes` (an IC marked the record as having helped) rerank higher. `boost_factor` scales the multiplier. Setting it to `0` disables boost. `luuna-atlas search --no-boost` disables it for a single call.

Tune higher if your team is diligent about marking outcomes and you want confirmed records to dominate ranking. Tune lower (or zero) if outcomes are inconsistently recorded and you want raw text relevance.

---

title: Governance and classifications
text: ## Governance and classifications

title: Governance caps
text:
### Governance caps

```yaml
governance:
  max_entries: 100         # soft target; luuna-atlas status flags above this
  warn_entries: 150        # luuna-atlas record prints a "consider compacting" hint
  hard_limit: 200          # writes past this are refused
```

All three are per-domain, not global. The flow is:

1. Below `max_entries`: silent.
2. Between `max_entries` and `warn_entries`: `luuna-atlas status` warns, writes proceed.
3. Between `warn_entries` and `hard_limit`: every `luuna-atlas record` write prints a "consider compacting" hint.
4. At `hard_limit`: writes are refused with a hint to run `luuna-atlas compact <domain>`.

Tune `hard_limit` up only after auditing prime output cost — every extra record is tokens in the agent's session start.

title: Classification shelf life
text:
### Classification shelf life

```yaml
classification_defaults:
  shelf_life:
    tactical: 14           # days
    observational: 30      # days
```

Records older than the shelf life become demotion candidates on the next `luuna-atlas prune` pass. **Foundational is permanent and not configurable here** — by definition, foundational is "load-bearing forever." If a record should expire, classify it tactical or observational at record time.

The ladder (`foundational → tactical → observational → archived`) is hardcoded. You can change the speed of the walk via shelf life, but not the steps.

---

title: Provider recipes
text:
## Provider recipes

`luuna-atlas setup <name>` wires Atlas into a coding agent runtime. Recipes are pluggable.

title: Discovery order
text:
### Discovery order

1. **Filesystem**: `.luuna/atlas/recipes/<name>.ts` or `.luuna/atlas/recipes/<name>.sh` (TypeScript wins on tie).
2. **npm**: a package named `luuna-atlas-recipe-<name>` resolvable from the repo.
3. **Built-in**: one of the recipes shipped in `src/commands/setup.ts`.

Filesystem wins so an org can shadow built-ins without forking Atlas.

title: Built-ins as of v0.10.2
text:
### Built-ins as of v0.10.2

- `claude` — writes `SessionStart` hook into `.claude/`. `PreCompact` is intentionally not registered because its stdout is discarded across compaction.
- `cursor` — writes Cursor's project rules surface.
- `codex` — writes both an `AGENTS.md` luuna-atlas section (fallback prose) and a `[[hooks.SessionStart]]` block in `.codex/config.toml` fenced by `# luuna-atlas:start` / `# luuna-atlas:end` line comments for idempotency.

**Removed in v0.9.0**: `aider`, `gemini`, `windsurf`. **Removed in v0.10.2**: `pi` (experiment rolled back). Users who relied on any of these can re-create the same behavior as a filesystem recipe under `.luuna/atlas/recipes/<name>.{ts,sh}`.

title: TypeScript recipe shape
Shell recipe contract
text:
### Shell recipe contract

```
<script> install|check|remove
```

- **cwd**: project root.
- **env**: `LUUNA_ATLAS_RECIPE_NAME=<name>`, `LUUNA_ATLAS_RECIPE_ACTION=<install|check|remove>`, plus all parent env.
- **stdout/stderr**: forwarded to the calling terminal.
- **Exit code**: `0` for success, non-zero for failure (the action is reported as failed and the message is the script's stderr).

title: Worked example: an internal windsurf-org recipe
text:
### Worked example: an internal `windsurf-org` recipe

`.luuna/atlas/recipes/windsurf-org.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

action="${1:?action required}"
target_dir=".windsurf-org"
target_file="$target_dir/agent_context.md"
fence_start="<!-- luuna-atlas:start -->"
fence_end="<!-- luuna-atlas:end -->"

case "$action" in
  install)
    mkdir -p "$target_dir"
    touch "$target_file"
    tmp=$(mktemp)
    awk -v s="$fence_start" -v e="$fence_end" '
      $0==s {skip=1; next}
      $0==e {skip=0; next}
      !skip {print}
    ' "$target_file" > "$tmp"
    {
      cat "$tmp"
      echo "$fence_start"
      echo "Run: luuna-atlas prime"
      echo "$fence_end"
    } > "$target_file"
    rm "$tmp"
    echo "windsurf-org installed at $target_file"
    ;;
  check)
    grep -q "$fence_start" "$target_file" 2>/dev/null \
      && { echo "windsurf-org installed"; exit 0; } \
      || { echo "windsurf-org not installed"; exit 1; }
    ;;
  remove)
    [ -f "$target_file" ] || { echo "nothing to remove"; exit 0; }
    tmp=$(mktemp)
    awk -v s="$fence_start" -v e="$fence_end" '
      $0==s {skip=1; next}
      $0==e {skip=0; next}
      !skip {print}
    ' "$target_file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$target_file"
    echo "windsurf-org removed"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "unknown action: $action" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
```

title: Worked example: an internal windsurf-org recipe
text:
Make it executable (`chmod +x`), commit it under `.luuna/atlas/recipes/`, and `luuna-atlas setup windsurf-org` Just Works in every repo that pulls the scaffolding.

`luuna-atlas setup --list` enumerates everything found with source + shadow markers, so it's easy to verify the filesystem recipe is winning over a built-in of the same name.

---

title: Distributing config across an org
text:
## Distributing config across an org

The recommended pattern:

1. **Commit `config.yaml` in every repo.** Don't try to centralize at the org level — repos move at different speeds, and a config out of sync with on-disk records is worse than a stale-but-consistent config.
2. **Seed identical config via repo scaffolding.** A cookiecutter template, an internal `degit` source, or a tool like Backstage that scaffolds new repos with a known `.luuna/atlas/` baseline.
3. **Roll out config changes via PRs.** Every change to `config.yaml` is a code review just like any other. `luuna-atlas sync` is the safety net that catches misconfiguration before the change merges.
4. **Use `disabled_types` and `--allow-unknown-types` to absorb rollout lag.** Two repos sharing expertise (via copy, fork, or external sync) will occasionally disagree on whether a custom type exists. `disabled_types` preserves CLI choices through the transition. `--allow-unknown-types` is the per-invocation escape hatch for reads against records of an unknown type.

title: .gitattributes setup
text:
### `.gitattributes` setup

```
.luuna/atlas/expertise/*.jsonl merge=union
.luuna/atlas/archive/*.jsonl   merge=union
```

`merge=union` is critical at scale. Two ICs working on different branches both running `luuna-atlas record` produces append-only writes that merge cleanly without conflicts. Combined with file locking (advisory, 50ms retry, 5s timeout, 30s stale detection) and atomic writes (temp file + rename), concurrent agents on the same repo never produce partial JSONL.

title: Worktree behavior
text:
### Worktree behavior

`getAtlasDir()` resolves `.luuna/atlas/` to the main repo when invoked from a `git worktree`. Expertise survives worktree cleanup — a record written from `repo.worktrees/feature-x/` lands in `repo/.luuna/atlas/expertise/<domain>.jsonl`, not in the throwaway worktree.

`isInsideWorktree()` guards against a submodule false positive: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` returns `/parent/.git/modules/<name>` for submodules (without a `.git` suffix), which the naive worktree check would treat as a worktree. The guard correctly identifies the submodule case and uses the local `.git`.

title: luuna-atlas sync is the gate
text:
### `luuna-atlas sync` is the gate

`luuna-atlas sync` re-validates every staged record against the on-disk config before committing. It **ignores** `--allow-unknown-types` and `--allow-domain-mismatch` by design — those flags are for unblocking writes during rollout lag, not for bypassing the validation gate that protects the canonical history.

If `luuna-atlas sync` rejects something, the fix is one of:

- Update the record to match current config.
- Update config to accept the record (then commit the config change first).
- If a custom type is being retired, add it to `disabled_types` rather than removing it from `custom_types`.

---

title: Part 2 — IC guide
text: # Part 2 — IC guide

title: Base record fields (available on every type)
text:
## Base record fields (available on every type)

Every record carries these fields regardless of type. Most are set automatically; a few are worth knowing about.

| Field | Type | Set by | Notes |
|-------|------|--------|-------|
| `id` | string | Atlas | Human-readable id stem + date. Stable across edits. |
| `type` | string | you (`--type`) | One of the registered types (built-in or custom). |
| `classification` | enum | you (`--classification`) | `foundational` / `tactical` / `observational`. Default `tactical`. |
| `recorded_at` | ISO 8601 string | Atlas | Set at write time. |
| `evidence` | object | mixed | Sub-fields: `commit`, `date`, `issue`, `file`, `bead`, `missions`, `gh`, `linear`. Commit + changed files auto-populate from git. |
| `tags` | `string[]` | you (`--tags`) | Free-form. Searchable. |
| `relates_to` | `string[]` | you (`--relates-to`) | mx-ids of related records. |
| `supersedes` | `string[]` | you (`--supersedes`) | mx-ids this record replaces. Triggers supersession decay on `luuna-atlas prune`. |
| `outcomes` | object | `luuna-atlas outcome` | Confirmation counts. Drives search boost. |
| `dir_anchors` | `string[]` | mixed | Directory paths the record applies to. Drives `luuna-atlas prime --files` filtering. |
| `owner` | string | you (`--owner`) | Reserved, opaque to Atlas — use it however your org wants. |
| `status` | enum | Atlas | `draft` / `active` / `deprecated` / `archived`. |

title: Built-in record types (the six)
text:
## Built-in record types (the six)

| Type | Required | Optional | Dedup key | Summary template |
|------|----------|----------|-----------|------------------|
| `convention` | `content` | — | `content` | `{content}` |
| `pattern` | `name`, `description` | `files` | `name` | `{name}` |
| `failure` | `description`, `resolution` | — | `description` | `{description}` |
| `decision` | `title`, `rationale` | `date` | `title` | `{title}` |
| `reference` | `name`, `description` | `files` | `name` | `{name}` |
| `guide` | `name`, `description` | `content`, `files` | `name` | `{name}` |

Each example below is the minimum to make `luuna-atlas record` succeed.

```bash

title: convention
text:
# convention
luuna-atlas record style --type convention \
  --content "Use .ts extensions on all relative imports"

title: pattern
text:
# pattern
luuna-atlas record adapters --type pattern \
  --name "Atomic write via temp + rename" \
  --description "Write to <path>.tmp.<pid>, then rename to <path>" \
  --files src/utils/expertise.ts

title: failure
text:
# failure
luuna-atlas record schemas --type failure \
  --description "AJV strict mode rejects schema missing type: object" \
  --resolution "Include type: object alongside required/properties"

title: decision
text:
# decision
luuna-atlas record architecture --type decision \
  --title "Soft-archive over hard-delete on prune" \
  --rationale "Archived records remain searchable via luuna-atlas search --archived"

title: reference
text:
# reference
luuna-atlas record vendors --type reference \
  --name "Bun runtime docs" \
  --description "Bun handles ESM/CJS interop transparently for AJV"

title: guide
text:
# guide
luuna-atlas record onboarding --type guide \
  --name "First-day-on-team setup" \
  --description "Steps for new ICs to get a working dev environment" \
  --content "1. Install bun. 2. bun install. 3. bun test."
```

title: Global CLI flags
text:
## Global CLI flags

| Flag | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `--allow-unknown-types` | Reading expertise that references a type not registered in the local config. Common during org rollout lag. |
| `--allow-domain-mismatch` | Writing a record where per-domain rules don't yet match an on-disk update. Same lag scenario. `luuna-atlas sync` ignores this. |
| `--quiet` / `-q` | Suppress informational output. Useful in scripts. |
| `--json` | Emit JSON instead of formatted text. For piping into `jq` or other tools. |
| `--verbose` | Extra diagnostic output. Use when something looks off. |
| `--format <markdown\|compact\|xml\|plain>` | Output format for read commands. `markdown` is default; `compact` is the IC-friendly TUI mode; `xml` and `plain` are for tool integration. |

---

title: Environment variables
text:
## Environment variables

| Variable | Set by | Available where |
|----------|--------|-----------------|
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_HOOK` | Atlas (set to `1`) | Inside hook scripts. Detect with `[ "${LUUNA_ATLAS_HOOK:-}" = "1" ]`. |
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_RECIPE_NAME` | Atlas | Inside recipe scripts (shell only). |
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_RECIPE_ACTION` | Atlas | Inside recipe scripts. One of `install` / `check` / `remove`. |
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_DEBUG` | You (operator) | Read by `luuna-atlas` at startup. Set to any non-empty value to raise the diagnostic logger to `debug` (hook traces, registry-init failures). Diagnostics go to **stderr** only and never touch stdout / `--json` output. |
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_LOG_LEVEL` | You (operator) | Read by `luuna-atlas` at startup. Authoritative log level (`trace`/`debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error`/`fatal`); overrides `LUUNA_ATLAS_DEBUG`. Default `info` (silent for routine internals). |
| `LUUNA_ATLAS_LOG_JSON` | You (operator) | Read by `luuna-atlas` at startup. Set to `1` to force newline-delimited JSON logs even in a TTY (the default pretty-renders to stderr in an interactive terminal). |

Parent env is preserved into both hooks and recipes. `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`, `OPS_TOKEN`, whatever you have exported in the agent's session is visible to the script.

title: Environment variables
text:
The `LUUNA_ATLAS_*` *logging* variables (`LUUNA_ATLAS_DEBUG`, `LUUNA_ATLAS_LOG_LEVEL`, `LUUNA_ATLAS_LOG_JSON`) control luuna-atlas's diagnostic channel only — they never alter product output. Atlas's user-facing output (the markdown `luuna-atlas prime` emits, status tables, `--json` results) always goes to stdout; the logger writes exclusively to stderr, so turning on `LUUNA_ATLAS_DEBUG` is safe even when piping `--json` to a machine consumer.

---

title: Working in worktrees and across branches
text:
## Working in worktrees and across branches

**Worktree resolution.** `.luuna/atlas/` always resolves to the main repo, even when you invoke `luuna-atlas` from a worktree directory. A record written from `~/repo.worktrees/feat-x/` lands in `~/repo/.luuna/atlas/expertise/<domain>.jsonl`. Worktree cleanup never loses expertise.

**Concurrent writes.** Two ICs writing to the same domain on different branches produce two appends to the same JSONL file. The combination of:

- `.gitattributes` `merge=union` on expertise files,
- Advisory file locking (`withFileLock`),
- Atomic writes (temp + rename),

means concurrent writes never produce partial or corrupt JSONL, and post-merge JSONL is the union of both branches' records.

If two branches write a record with the same `dedup_key`, both records are preserved on disk after merge. Run `luuna-atlas compact <domain>` to collapse them according to the type's compact strategy.

---

title: When your org has custom types
text:
## When your org has custom types

Discovery from the command line:

- `luuna-atlas --help` lists registered types in the description of the `--type` flag.
- `luuna-atlas record --help` shows the allowed `--type` values, including custom types.
- `luuna-atlas record <domain> --type <name> --help` shows required/optional flags for that combination — including any extra `required_fields` from the domain config.

**How required fields surface as CLI flags.** A `required_fields: [owner]` entry in `domains.security` means `luuna-atlas record security ...` accepts (and demands) `--owner`. The flag name follows the field name with `_` replaced by `-`.

**Validate your local records against org rules.** Run `luuna-atlas doctor` to check that everything you've written is conformant. Common checks:

- `domain-conformance` / `domain-violations` — per-domain rule conformance.
- `type-registry` — built-in vs custom types in use; counts; disabled markers.
- `unknown-types` — fails if records reference a type the local config doesn't know about. Pass `--allow-unknown-types` to relax.

`luuna-atlas doctor --fix` strips broken file anchors but does not move records between domains or rewrite fields. Bigger fixes need an explicit `luuna-atlas edit`.

---

title: B. Hook event quick reference
text:
## B. Hook event quick reference

| Event | Blocks on non-zero? | Mutable via stdout? | Payload root |
|-------|---------------------|---------------------|--------------|
| `pre-record` | yes | yes | `{ event, payload: ExpertiseRecord }` |
| `post-record` | no (warns) | no | `{ event, payload: ExpertiseRecord }` |
| `pre-prime` | yes | yes | `{ event, payload: { domains: [...] } }` |
| `pre-prune` | yes | no | `{ event, payload: { candidates: [...] } }` |
| `pre-compact` | yes | yes (`{ replacement: <Record> }`) | `{ event, payload: { domain, candidates, merged } }` |

Common contract for all five:

- `cwd` = project root.
- `LUUNA_ATLAS_HOOK=1` plus all parent env.
- stdin = JSON payload.
- stderr forwarded to caller.
- SIGKILL on `hook_settings.timeout_ms` (default 5000).
- Dry-run skips hooks.

text:

title: D. File path reference
text:
## D. File path reference

Every path Atlas reads or writes under the repo root:

| Path | Purpose | Written by | Read by |
|------|---------|------------|---------|
| `.luuna/atlas/config.yaml` | Configuration | you / `luuna-atlas init` | every command |
| `.luuna/atlas/expertise/<domain>.jsonl` | Live records | `luuna-atlas record`, `luuna-atlas edit`, `luuna-atlas compact`, `luuna-atlas restore`, `luuna-atlas doctor --fix` | `luuna-atlas prime`, `luuna-atlas search`, `luuna-atlas query`, `luuna-atlas rank`, `luuna-atlas status`, `luuna-atlas validate`, `luuna-atlas learn`, `luuna-atlas ready`, `luuna-atlas sync` |
| `.luuna/atlas/archive/<domain>.jsonl` | Soft-archived records | `luuna-atlas prune` | `luuna-atlas search --archived`, `luuna-atlas restore` |
| `.luuna/atlas/recipes/<name>.ts` | TypeScript provider recipe | you | `luuna-atlas setup`, `luuna-atlas setup --list` |
| `.luuna/atlas/recipes/<name>.sh` | Shell provider recipe | you | `luuna-atlas setup`, `luuna-atlas setup --list` |
| `.luuna/atlas/hooks/*.sh` (or anywhere) | Lifecycle hook scripts | you | `luuna-atlas record`, `luuna-atlas prime`, `luuna-atlas prune` |
| `.luuna/atlas/README.md` | Auto-generated layout doc | `luuna-atlas init` | humans |
| `.gitattributes` (repo root) | `merge=union` rules | you | git |

title: D. File path reference
text: Lock files (`.luuna/atlas/expertise/<domain>.jsonl.lock` and similar) are created and removed by `withFileLock` during writes. They should not persist between commands; if you find a stale one, it will self-clear after the 30s stale-lock window.

title: Contributing to Luuna Atlas
text:
# Contributing to Luuna Atlas

Atlas is an independent MIT-licensed Luuna component maintained by the luuna-ai organization. Read [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-atlas-agents) before changing it. Provenance and the original notice are in [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-atlas-upstream) and [LICENSE](/docs/components-atlas-license).

title: Development
text:
## Development

Use Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3. Go dependencies are vendored. From the checkout:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run build:native
bun run verify
```

The build produces `luuna-atlas`, `lat` and `la` under `.atlas-bin/` (`.exe` on Windows). The executable runs without Bun or Node. Existing source consumers can use `bun src/cli.ts <args>`; it builds and launches Go when necessary. `LUUNA_ATLAS_GO` selects a Go executable outside PATH.

Useful focused checks:

```sh
bun run go:test
bun run go:vet
bun run go:fmt:check
bun run typecheck
bun run check:agents
bun test test/native-api.test.ts --timeout 30000
```

`bun run verify` is the supported validation contract: native formatting/build/vet/tests, compatibility TypeScript type checking, instruction validation and Bun tests. Race detection is available through `bun run go:test:race` on a host with a supported C compiler. The devcontainer pins the same Go/Bun versions; container startup was not part of the local rewrite verification.

title: Implementation conventions
text:
## Implementation conventions

- Native entry point: `cmd/luuna-atlas/`; business logic: `internal/atlas/`; public Go API: `atlas.go`.
- Format Go changes with `gofmt`. Preserve advisory locks, atomic writes, secret redaction and schemas.
- `src/` contains strict TypeScript types, the CLI launcher and public API transport. Keep business operations in Go. Relative TypeScript imports use `.ts`.
- Public JSON, flags, aliases, help, terminal styling, streams and exit status are compatibility boundaries. Review existing behavior before changing it.
- Keep legacy names and the one-way store migration centralized in `internal/atlas/legacy_layout.go`.
- Configuration/data live in the user's project under `.luuna/atlas/`. Tests must use disposable projects rather than this checkout or imported authoring stores.

For current source and command coverage, read [GO-REWRITE-REPORT.md](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/GO-REWRITE-REPORT.md). The broader [system map](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/CLI-SYSTEM-MAP.md) documents the compatibility baseline and Luuna integrations.

title: Testing
text:
## Testing

Go tests use real temporary files and processes. Differential tests execute the frozen TypeScript reference in a separate temporary project and compare outputs and persisted state with Go. The oracle in `compat/reference/` is immutable; do not edit it to satisfy new behavior. Its integrity manifest is checked by native tests.

Historical internal Bun unit tests explicitly import that reference. Public CLI subprocess tests and public API tests exercise Go through the compatibility entry points. A passing reference test alone is not native implementation evidence. Add behavior tests at the affected public boundary and include expected error/data effects.

Keep generated binaries, caches, test stores and credentials out of Git. Dependency installs must not change root Git hooks. Ordinary installation does not build or install hooks; explicit development builds and explicit setup commands do their documented work.

title: Review and release
text:
## Review and release

Keep each change focused and describe the resulting behavior and meaningful validation. Use the repository's supported verification before requesting review. Do not commit, push, create issues, update sibling component pins or synchronize component state unless requested.

The package remains private and unpublished. Registry publication and upstream/self-upgrade require a separate reviewed release process. Luuna consumes an exact reviewed Git commit through its submodule; runtime policy and approval enforcement belong in Luuna.

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/issues) when you choose to report a bug. Security guidance is in [SECURITY.md](/docs/components-atlas-security). Contributions retain the [MIT License](/docs/components-atlas-license).

title: Luuna Atlas
text:
# Luuna Atlas

Read [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-atlas-agents) for current development instructions and [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-atlas-upstream) for provenance. This repository owns the component; Luuna owns runtime policy. Archived upstream workflows are reference material.

The implementation is native Go in `cmd/luuna-atlas/` and `internal/atlas/`. `src/` preserves the Bun CLI and TypeScript API as transports to that executable. `compat/reference/` is a frozen test oracle; production code must not execute or import its business logic. Use Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3, and run `bun run verify` for the supported component checks. Preserve the CLI interactions, JSON contracts, stored schemas and existing aliases. No commit, push, release or root Git hook change is implied by development work.

text:
# Luuna Atlas development

This component is a maintained fork of an upstream project, with provenance in `UPSTREAM.md` and the original MIT notice in `LICENSE`.

Use Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3. Go dependencies are vendored; verification disables toolchain downloads and module network access. From this directory:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run build:native
bun run go:test
bun run typecheck

```

The native executable starts in `cmd/luuna-atlas/`; business logic lives in `internal/atlas/`. The strict TypeScript in `src/` is the compatibility launcher and library transport to Go. It must not reimplement business logic. The frozen pre-rewrite implementation in `compat/reference/` is a development oracle, never a production dependency. Bun tests of the CLI and exported library use the native implementation; historical internal unit tests import the reference explicitly. Go tests use real temporary projects and compare observable results against the oracle. Keep advisory locks, atomic writes, JSON output contracts, terminal interactions, command/flag compatibility and secret redaction. Test changes at the appropriate public boundary.

title: Luuna Atlas development
text:
Primary executable: luuna-atlas (lat; compatibility alias la). This component owns structured expertise and project memory. Missions owns tickets/plans; Beacon owns reusable prompts. Project data lives under .luuna/atlas in the user project (config in config.yaml); the one-way migration and legacy names live only in `internal/atlas/legacy_layout.go`. Preserve configuration keys and record schemas unless an explicit migration is designed and tested. Runtime policy and approval enforcement belong in Luuna, not in a rewrite of this component.

Do not load imported dogfooding stores, session histories, or upstream agent skills as Luuna work records. Do not create them as a development ritual. Installations must not alter the root Git hook configuration. This is an independent public repository maintained by brodynelly. Packages remain unpublished; registry publication and upstream self-upgrades require a separate reviewed release process.

title: Luuna Atlas development
text:
`bun run verify` is the supported component validation surface: Go formatting check, native executable/alias build, go vet, Go tests including differential cases, TypeScript type check, instruction check and the Bun suite. `bun run go:test:race` adds race detection when the host has a C compiler supported by Go. The built native executable runs without Bun or Node; user-provided TypeScript/npm recipe extensions still need Bun. Dependency installation never builds the executable or installs hooks. Inherited check:all and quality-budget scripts remain available for upstream maintenance comparison; they reference standalone upstream CI and are not the supported CI contract. Luuna consumes exact Git commits through submodules; changes here do not authorize changes to Luuna runtime policy.

Do not commit or push unless explicitly requested. Report remaining work without automatically creating issues or synchronizing component state.

title: Native release artifacts: status summary
text:
# Native release artifacts: status summary

This page summarizes the native archive work for Atlas (task C-atlas) and where it stands now. The full procedure is in [RELEASING.md](/docs/components-atlas-docs-releasing). The scope comes from [specs/chore-native-release.md](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/specs/chore-native-release.md) and the review fixes from [specs/patch-native-release-review.md](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/specs/patch-native-release-review.md).

title: Scope: manual artifacts only
text:
## Scope: manual artifacts only

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch` with `permissions: contents: read`. It builds on four native runners (`macos-14`, `macos-15-intel`, `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`) and uploads the results with `actions/upload-artifact`, kept for 14 days.
- There is no tag trigger, GitHub Release, registry publish, signing or notarization. The attestation step is present only as a commented-out owner gate. Publishing is an owner decision (see "Owner gates" in RELEASING.md).
- Each archive, `luuna-atlas_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`, contains exactly `bin/luuna-atlas` and `bin/lat`. Both are regular files with mode 0755, owned by uid/gid 0. `LICENSE`, `UPSTREAM.md`, `SHA256SUMS` and `provenance.json` are placed beside the archive, not inside it.

title: Checksums
text:
## Checksums

`package.sh` writes `SHA256SUMS` with entries for the archive, `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`. In `check-archive.sh`, the checksum check is **mandatory**. Each of these fails before anything is extracted:

- `SHA256SUMS` is missing, is a symlink or is not a regular file
- the archive has no entry, or more than one entry
- the checksum does not match

Open item (N3, not implemented): `check-archive.sh` checks only the archive line, not the `LICENSE` or `UPSTREAM.md` lines.

title: Provenance
text:
## Provenance

`provenance.json` records the archive version and the internal `const Version` separately, because that constant is not set by `-ldflags -X`. It also records the commit, ref, runner, target, the exact `go env GOVERSION`, build flags and checksums.

`worktree_dirty` is measured **before** the build by `scripts/release/worktree-state.sh`:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `true` | tracked changes or untracked files (ignored files such as `dist/` do not count) |
| `false` | clean work tree |
| `null` | git is unavailable, or the directory is not a work tree |

This is self-reported metadata (`"attestation": null`), not a verifiable attestation.

title: --require-clean
text:
## `--require-clean`

`package.sh --require-clean` exits with an error unless `worktree_dirty` is `false`, which means `null` also fails. The workflow passes this flag. Local changes must be committed or removed before `--require-clean` succeeds.

title: Time zone and reproducibility
text:
## Time zone and reproducibility

`package.sh` exports `TZ=UTC0` before running `touch -t 200001010000`, so the entry timestamps are always 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z whatever the host time zone. Other measures that keep the build reproducible:

- tar runs in a single invocation with visible errors and no silent fallback, and its owner and mode are checked after building
- `gzip -n`
- `-trimpath -ldflags '-s -w -buildid='`

`test-release.sh` builds under two different `TZ` values and requires byte-identical archives.

title: Verification status (honest)
text:
## Verification status (honest)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final read-only review after the patch | passed |
| Native release regression (`test-release.sh` and the related Go tests) | 72 passed |
| Bun test suite | 1608 passed |
| `bun run verify` (full component contract) | passed with Go 1.27.0 and Bun 1.4.3 |

**Shipping validation:** a checksum-verified Go **1.27.0** SDK was installed repo-locally under `.tac/tools/go1.27.0/go`; the system Go installation and version pins were not changed. The default macOS `TMPDIR` exposed a symlink-path mismatch in the parity test harness. [The test-only patch](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/blob/ce9c9c824c491dcb4fce53e7f6c4735477957147/specs/patch-native-release-parity-paths.md) canonicalizes fixture roots without changing product path semantics, reference outputs or normalization rules. Full `bun run verify` then passed independently with the original `TMPDIR` unchanged.

Also not proven:

- A local run covers only the host platform. The other three targets are proven only by an owner-dispatched workflow run, and none has been dispatched as part of this work.
- Review items N1 (pinning workflow actions to commit SHAs) and N2 (a pre-build step asserting the Go version and `uname`) are still open. The workflow uses the tags `@v4`/`@v5`.
- Gatekeeper behaviour for unsigned macOS binaries, and musl/Alpine compatibility, are not covered.

title: Releasing native Atlas archives
text:
# Releasing native Atlas archives

Nothing in this repository publishes Atlas. The scripts and workflow below produce archives you can verify, and stop there. Tags, GitHub Releases, signing, notarization, attestations and npm packages are owner decisions that are deliberately not automated.

title: What an archive contains
text:
## What an archive contains

`luuna-atlas_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` contains exactly two regular files with mode 0755:

- `bin/luuna-atlas`, the primary executable
- `bin/lat`, the public alias

There are no directories, links or other entries, so the suite installer's strict executable allowlist accepts it. The `la` compatibility alias stays available from source builds (`bun run build:native`) and is not part of the public archive.

`lat` is a byte-identical copy of `luuna-atlas`. `cmd/luuna-atlas/main.go` passes `os.Args[1:]` to the app and nothing branches on `argv[0]`, so both names behave the same and receive every argument unchanged. `check-archive.sh` verifies this on the host.

Licensing and attribution travel beside the archive rather than inside it, because the archive allowlist admits only executables. The output directory and the uploaded artifact contain `LICENSE` (MIT, upstream notice) and `UPSTREAM.md`, and both are listed in `SHA256SUMS`. Anyone redistributing an archive must ship those two files with it.

Platforms: `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/arm64` and `linux/amd64`. Linux binaries are static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). Windows archives are not produced.

title: Versions
text:
## Versions

- **Archive version:** the `--version` you pass, for example `0.12.0`. It names the archive.
- **Internal version:** what `luuna-atlas --version` prints. It comes from `const Version` in `internal/atlas/app.go`.

The internal version is a Go constant, so `-ldflags -X` cannot override it, and the build does not try. `provenance.json` records both values. Keeping them equal is an owner release step: bump the constant (`bun run version:bump`) in a reviewed change before dispatching.

title: Local dry run (host platform only)
text:
## Local dry run (host platform only)

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -p=1 -mod=vendor ./...
sh scripts/release/test-release.sh
out=$(mktemp -d)
sh scripts/release/package.sh --version 0.0.0-local --out "$out"
sh scripts/release/check-archive.sh --require-exec "$out"/luuna-atlas_0.0.0-local_*.tar.gz
```

`package.sh` uses only the local Go toolchain: `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, `GOPROXY=off`, vendored modules and `CGO_ENABLED=0`. It never downloads a toolchain. It builds with `-trimpath -ldflags '-s -w -buildid='` and fixed file timestamps (2000-01-01T00:00:00Z; the script exports `TZ=UTC0`, so the host time zone does not change the tar headers), so identical inputs produce an identical archive. It creates the tar in one invocation with visible errors and no fallback, and it fails unless both entries are 0755 regular files owned by uid/gid 0 (root). It refuses to overwrite an existing archive and rejects a symlinked or non-directory `--out`.

`provenance.json` records `worktree_dirty`, measured before the build by `scripts/release/worktree-state.sh`: `true` when there are tracked changes **or untracked files** (an untracked `*.go` file would be compiled in), `false` for a clean work tree, and `null` when git is unavailable or the checkout is not a work tree. Ignored files such as `dist/` do not count. `--require-clean` makes any state other than `false` a failure; the workflow passes it.

title: Local dry run (host platform only)
text:
`check-archive.sh` checks the archive before extracting it:

1. the file name and `SHA256SUMS`, which is mandatory: a missing, symlinked or non-regular `SHA256SUMS`, a missing entry, a duplicate entry or a mismatch all fail
2. that the entry list is exactly the two executables, with no absolute paths, `..`, links, devices or extra entries
3. that both entries are mode 0755

Only then does it extract into a private temporary directory. On a matching host it also runs `--version` and `--help` through both names, inside an empty sandbox `HOME`. `--require-exec` turns a host mismatch into a failure.

`test-release.sh` covers argument validation, hostile fixture archives (traversal, absolute path, symlink, hardlink, extra or missing entry, wrong mode, bad, missing or duplicate checksum, divergent alias) and the work-tree state against scratch Git repositories, without network access. The real-build section builds under two time zones and requires byte-identical archives, and uses `tar` shims to prove that a tar failure is reported and that an archive not owned by root is rejected. `--skip-build` omits the real builds.

Toolchain pin limitation: `go.mod` declares `go 1.27.0` and CI's `setup-go` installs 1.27.0. Locally, any installed Go 1.27.x satisfies `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so a local archive may come from a newer patch release. `provenance.json` records the exact `go` version used.

title: Workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml)
text:
## Workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)

- **Trigger and permissions:** manual `workflow_dispatch` only, with a `version` input and `permissions: contents: read`. There is no tag trigger.
- **Runners:** each matrix entry runs on a native runner: `macos-14` (darwin/arm64), `macos-15-intel` (darwin/amd64), `ubuntu-latest` (linux/amd64) and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (linux/arm64). The retired `macos-13` label is not used. Because every runner is native, `check-archive.sh --require-exec` executes every archive on its own platform.
- **Steps:** Go tests, then the offline release-script tests, then `package.sh`, then `check-archive.sh`, then `actions/upload-artifact`. Artifacts are kept for 14 days.
- **Bun:** not required. The existing Bun-based `bun run verify` stays in `ci.yml`.
- **Not included:** release creation, registry publish steps and attestations. The attestation step is present only as a commented-out owner gate.

title: Owner gates (not automated)
text:
## Owner gates (not automated)

1. Bump `const Version` if needed, through a reviewed change.
2. Run the workflow with `workflow_dispatch`, download the four artifacts, and verify `SHA256SUMS`, `check-archive.sh` and `provenance.json` on each platform you claim.
3. Decide on signing, notarization (Apple Developer ID) and GitHub build attestations. Enabling attestations needs `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`.
4. Create the tag and GitHub Release and upload the archives, `SHA256SUMS`, `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`.
5. Record the released URLs and checksums in the suite hub's release manifest through its own reviewed process.

title: What a passing run does not prove
text:
## What a passing run does not prove

- A local run proves only the host platform. The other platforms are proven only by an owner-dispatched workflow run.
- `provenance.json` is self-reported metadata, not a verifiable attestation.
- Unsigned macOS binaries downloaded through a browser may be quarantined by Gatekeeper. That case is not covered.
- musl/Alpine compatibility is not claimed, although Go static binaries usually run there.

title: Security Policy
text: # Security Policy

title: Supported Versions
text:
## Supported Versions

| Version | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| 0.2.x   | Yes       |
| < 0.2   | No        |

Only the latest release on the current major version line receives security updates.

title: Reporting a Vulnerability
text:
## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue for security vulnerabilities.**

Please report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/security/advisories).

1. Go to the [Security Advisories page](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/security/advisories)
2. Click **"New draft security advisory"**
3. Fill in a description of the vulnerability, including steps to reproduce if possible

title: Response Timeline
text:
### Response Timeline

- **Acknowledgment**: Within 48 hours of your report
- **Initial assessment**: Within 7 days
- **Fix or mitigation**: Within 30 days for confirmed vulnerabilities

We will keep you informed of progress throughout the process.

title: Scope
text:
## Scope

Atlas is a CLI tool that reads and writes files on the local filesystem. The following are considered security issues:

- **Command injection** -- Unsanitized input passed to shell execution
- **Path traversal** -- Accessing files outside the intended `.luuna/atlas/` directory
- **Arbitrary file access** -- Reading or writing files the user did not intend
- **Symlink attacks** -- Following symlinks to unintended locations
- **Temp file races** -- TOCTOU vulnerabilities in temporary file handling

The following are generally **not** in scope:

- Denial of service via large input files (Atlas is a local tool, not a service)
- Issues that require the attacker to already have local shell access with the same privileges as the user
- Social engineering or phishing

title: Security Measures
text:
## Security Measures

Atlas already implements several hardening measures:

- Atomic writes via temp file + rename to prevent partial/corrupt files
- Advisory file locking to prevent concurrent write corruption
- Input validation via JSON schema (Ajv) on all record types

If you believe any of these measures can be bypassed, please report it through the process above.

title: Atlas: structured knowledge and project memory
text:
# Atlas: structured knowledge and project memory

Atlas is Luuna's maintained, MIT-licensed fork of Mulch. It stores and retrieves structured expertise and project memory for coding agents. The standalone package identity is `@luuna/atlas-cli`; the primary command is `luuna-atlas`, with `la` as its short alias. Compatibility aliases `ml` and `mulch` remain available for inherited integrations.

title: What Atlas does
text:
## What Atlas does

Atlas organizes records by domain, type, lifecycle, and provenance. Its `prime`, search, record-management, validation, and maintenance commands help an agent receive relevant project knowledge without injecting an unbounded memory dump. The full source README, configuration guide, changelog, and inherited upstream reference are included in the Atlas reference pages.

Luuna connects to Atlas through its CLI/JSON boundary; Atlas also exports a TypeScript library. The runtime remains responsible for authorization and plan approval. Knowledge can only influence an approved plan when it is explicitly selected. Atlas does not grant an agent execution permissions.

title: Local data and compatibility
text:
## Local data and compatibility

Atlas preserves the upstream `.mulch/` directory, record types, configuration, markers, and environment variables. Renaming the product does not migrate or rewrite existing data. Do not replace this fork with a registry package that happens to use a similar name. The package is private and unpublished; update it through a reviewed repository commit.

title: Run from source
text:
## Run from source

Use Bun 1.4.3 for the repository's documented workflow:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/cli.ts --help
bun run verify
```

Start with the [Atlas README](/docs/components-atlas-readme), then consult the [configuration guide](/docs/components-atlas-config) and [migration notes](/docs/components-atlas-migration) for current command and data compatibility details. The current Atlas source no longer includes a copied upstream README. Some inherited help text and generated integration snippets retain the `ml` or `mulch` names; the aliases preserve compatibility.

title: Maintenance and provenance
text:
## Maintenance and provenance

Atlas is a pinned Luuna submodule sourced from the public [`luuna-ai/luuna-atlas`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas) repository. In the core Luuna source snapshot documented here, the integration pin is [`76ad209`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-atlas/tree/76ad209daf404dd9a12aeaf46293e05e9f41e517); the reference pages below follow a newer component-repository head. Check the pin before relying on newer behavior in core Luuna. Verify the component's `UPSTREAM.md` and changelog before adopting inherited behavior. The upstream operational runbook is historical reference material; it does not authorize npm publication or override Luuna's release controls.

title: Luuna Beacon
text:
# Luuna Beacon

Prompt composition and versioned agent instructions. It is maintained in [luuna-ai/luuna-beacon](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-beacon).

Run from this directory with Go 1.27.0:

```bash
go run ./cmd/luuna-beacon --help
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./cmd/luuna-beacon ./cmd/lbc ./cmd/lb
```

The standalone executable is `luuna-beacon`; `lbc` is the Luuna suite shortcut and `lb` remains a compatibility alias. `luuna beacon <args>` is the equivalent entry through Luuna's installed launcher. In a checkout, run `go run ./cmd/luuna-beacon <args>` or build the desired command under `cmd/`. Registry publication is disabled; use the Luuna CLI installer from the main checkout to make the commands available on PATH.

Project data lives in `.luuna/beacon/` (`prompts.jsonl`, `schemas.jsonl`, `artifacts.jsonl`, `config.yaml`). A legacy project directory from earlier layouts is moved there automatically on first use, with a one-line notice on stderr. Luuna consumes a pinned Git submodule and integrates through the CLI/JSON boundary (Atlas also exports a TypeScript library); runtime policy and approvals remain Luuna's responsibility.

title: Complete skills, agents, and bundles
text:
## Complete skills, agents, and bundles

Beacon also captures versioned, self-contained file snapshots. Existing prompt commands remain unchanged; `lbc skill`, `lbc agent`, and `lbc bundle` add `import`, `update`, `list`, `show`, `history`, `read`, `verify`, and `export` subcommands. Imports store file bytes and logical relative paths in `artifacts.jsonl`, so the source directory can be removed after import. Each version has a content hash. A repeated identical import does not create another version, and a conflicting version after a Git merge is reported as an error.

```bash
lbc skill import path/to/skill --name review
lbc skill verify review
lbc skill export review --target claude             # .claude/skills/review/
lbc skill export review --target codex              # .agents/skills/review/
lbc agent import path/to/reviewer.md --name reviewer
lbc agent export reviewer --target claude           # .claude/agents/reviewer.md
lbc bundle import path/to/claude-plugin --name tac-final
lbc bundle export tac-final --out path/to/exported-plugin
claude --plugin-dir path/to/exported-plugin
```

title: Complete skills, agents, and bundles
text:
A skill source must contain a root `SKILL.md`; an agent source is a Markdown file; a bundle source must contain `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Bundle export reconstructs a plugin package but does not install or enable it in Claude Code. `--force` replaces a prior Beacon-managed directory export; otherwise existing destinations are preserved. Source symlinks and credential-like files are rejected. Scripts are stored and exported as files, not executed by Beacon. Artifact records are project data, not Luuna runtime policy.

Self-upgrade is disabled while the package is private. Update through a reviewed commit in this repository; never replace this fork with a similarly named registry package. Dependency installs do not change Git hooks.

Read [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-beacon-upstream) for attribution and provenance, [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-beacon-agents) for development rules, and [the original README](/docs/components-beacon-docs-upstream-readme) for inherited command examples. Upstream release/runbook documents are historical references and do not authorize publication.

title: Maintenance and releases
text:
## Maintenance and releases

The repository is maintained by the luuna-ai organization. CI runs Go tests, vet, and builds on Linux and Windows. Registry publishing is disabled. Luuna pins a reviewed commit, never a floating branch; update its submodule only after CI and the consumer smoke pass. See [MIGRATION.md](/docs/components-beacon-migration) for the verified source baseline.

title: Contributing to Luuna Beacon
text:
# Contributing to Luuna Beacon

Luuna Beacon is a Go CLI. Keep changes focused, use ordinary descriptive branch and commit names, and do not publish, push, or change runtime policy as part of component work.

title: Getting started
text:
## Getting started

Install Go 1.27.0, then run:

```bash
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./cmd/luuna-beacon ./cmd/lbc ./cmd/lb
```

`luuna-beacon`, `lbc`, and `lb` are compatibility entrypoints over the same CLI implementation.

title: Code and tests
text:
## Code and tests

- Commands and argument handling live in `internal/cli`.
- CLI entrypoints live in `cmd/`.
- Filesystem stores, migration, and artifact logic live in `internal/`.
- Use real temporary directories for tests; avoid mocks for project-state behavior.
- Preserve JSON response envelopes, JSONL/YAML record contracts, lock behavior, atomic writes, and secret redaction.

Run `gofmt` on changed Go code and include focused tests for externally visible behavior. CI requires `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and builds on Linux and Windows.

title: Pull requests
text:
## Pull requests

Keep one concern per pull request, explain the behavior change and evidence, and ensure all Go validation passes. For security reports, follow [SECURITY.md](/docs/components-beacon-security). Contributions are licensed under [MIT](/docs/components-beacon-license).
