title: Luuna Beacon development
text:
# Luuna Beacon development

This component is a maintained fork of an upstream project; provenance is in `UPSTREAM.md` and the original MIT notice in `LICENSE`.

Use Go 1.27.0. From this directory:

```bash
gofmt -w cmd internal
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./cmd/luuna-beacon ./cmd/lbc ./cmd/lb
```

Source is in `cmd/` and `internal/`; tests use Go and real temporary files. Keep idiomatic, well-tested Go, advisory locks, atomic writes, JSON output contracts, and secret redaction. Test changes at the appropriate public boundary.

Primary executable: luuna-beacon (lbc; compatibility alias lb). This component owns composable agent prompts and instructions. Missions owns tickets/plans; Atlas owns structured expertise and project memory. Project data lives in `.luuna/beacon`; legacy project directories are migrated automatically by `internal/paths`. Preserve configuration keys, record schemas, public contracts, and environment variables unless an explicit migration is designed and tested. Runtime policy and approval enforcement belong in Luuna, not in a rewrite of this component.

title: Luuna Beacon development
text:
Do not load imported dogfooding stores, session histories, or upstream agent skills as Luuna work records. Do not create them as a development ritual. Installations must not alter the root Git hook configuration. This is an independent public repository maintained by brodynelly. Packages remain unpublished; registry publication and upstream self-upgrades require a separate reviewed release process.

`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go build ./cmd/luuna-beacon ./cmd/lbc ./cmd/lb` are the supported component validation surface. Luuna consumes exact Git commits through submodules; changes here do not authorize changes to Luuna runtime policy.

Do not commit or push unless explicitly requested. Report remaining work without automatically creating issues or synchronizing component state.

title: Luuna Beacon specification
text:
# Luuna Beacon specification

Luuna Beacon is a Go CLI for git-native prompt composition and versioned agent artifacts. It is intentionally a component: Luuna runtime policy, approvals, agent execution, Mission planning, and Atlas priming remain outside this repository.

title: Public interface
text:
## Public interface

The executables `luuna-beacon`, `lbc`, and `lb` run the same CLI. Every command supports machine-readable output through `--json`; successful JSON responses include `success: true` and a command identifier, while failures include `success: false`, the command, and an error string.

Public command groups are:

- Prompt lifecycle: `init`, `create`, `update`, `archive`, `show`, `list`, `history`, `tree`, `stats`, `diff`, `pin`, `unpin`, `import`, `render`, `emit`, `validate`, and `sync`.
- Project configuration and schemas: `config schema|show|set|unset` and `schema create|show|list|rule add`.
- Agent-facing context: `prime`, `onboard`, `doctor`, `completions`, and `upgrade` (which deliberately declines unpublished self-upgrades).
- Versioned snapshots: `skill`, `agent`, and `bundle`, each with `import`, `update`, `list`, `show`, `history`, `read`, `verify`, and `export`.

title: Project data contract
text:
## Project data contract

All state lives in `.luuna/beacon/`:

```text
config.yaml       project configuration and emit targets
prompts.jsonl     append-only prompt version history
schemas.jsonl     append-only schema versions
artifacts.jsonl   append-only skill, agent, and bundle snapshots
```

The legacy `.canopy` project directory migrates automatically before normal operations. JSONL is the durable database: records retain stable IDs and versions, mutations append a later version, and ordinary lookup resolves the current record rather than historical aliases. Prompt records preserve names, descriptions, sections, inheritance, mixins, tags, schemas, output settings, pins, frontmatter, atlas metadata, status, and timestamps.

Configuration supports the current `targets` map and reads legacy `emitDir` and `emitDirByTag` routing. Archived prompts are hidden by default but remain addressable in history and explicit status listings.

title: Safety and concurrency
text:
## Safety and concurrency

Mutations use advisory lock files and write complete replacement files through a temporary sibling. Windows uses replace-existing semantics so a normal mutation can overwrite an existing JSONL or config file safely. Locks expire after a bounded stale period. Export staging uses a backup-and-restore path; `--force` only replaces a directory carrying a matching Beacon ownership marker. Artifact imports reject symlinks and credential-like source files, retain file digests and executable mode, and never execute captured content.

title: Composition and emission
text:
## Composition and emission

Rendering resolves parent inheritance first, then mixins from left to right, then the focal prompt. Later sections replace earlier sections of the same name; an empty section removes an inherited one. Rendering detects cycles and enforces a bounded inheritance depth. Emit writes Markdown by default and TypeScript for an `.ts` output name. A per-prompt output directory overrides target routing; target tag routing overrides the default target.

title: Validation and tooling
text:
## Validation and tooling

The supported contributor gate is:

```bash
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build ./cmd/luuna-beacon ./cmd/lbc ./cmd/lb
```

CI runs that gate on Linux and Windows. The project has no registry publication or self-upgrade process; consumers pin reviewed Git commits.

title: Native release packaging
text:
# Native release packaging

This is a summary of the native archive packaging for `luuna-beacon` and `lbc`. The full contract and owner steps are in [RELEASING.md](/docs/components-beacon-docs-releasing). Nothing here publishes, tags, signs or attests anything.

title: What is implemented
text:
## What is implemented

| Piece | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/release/package.sh` | Validates `--version`/`--out`/`--os`/`--arch`. Builds `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w"`. Writes a deterministic tar.gz holding only `bin/luuna-beacon` and `bin/lbc`, plus `SHA256SUMS`, `provenance.json`, `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md` beside it. |
| `scripts/release/check-archive.sh` | Validates the name, requires a matching `SHA256SUMS` entry, and checks for exactly two 0755 regular entries before and after extraction. On a host-matching archive it runs both names to prove `lbc` matches `luuna-beacon`. |
| `scripts/release/test.sh` | Offline tests: bad arguments, plus fixture archives that are valid or have an extra entry, a symlink, a bad mode, a missing entry, a directory, `..`, a bad or missing checksum, or a bad platform name. `--build` adds a real host package/check and a `TZ` reproducibility comparison. |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` only, `contents: read`. Native matrix: darwin/arm64 (`macos-14`), darwin/amd64 (`macos-15-intel`), linux/amd64 (`ubuntu-latest`), linux/arm64 (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Steps: test, then package, then `check-archive.sh --require-run`, then `upload-artifact`. |
| `Makefile` | `release-test` and `release-local` targets. |

`lb` stays a source-build alias and is not shipped in archives.

title: Versions
text:
## Versions

The archive version is the validated `--version` input. It goes in the file name and in `archive_version`. The internal version is the Go `const` in `internal/cli/cli.go` and is recorded as `internal_version`. Because it is a `const`, ldflags cannot override it. Aligning the two is a reviewed source change.

`provenance.json` is self-reported. `source.dirty` covers tracked and untracked (non-ignored) changes. It is `null` when Git cannot tell, and then `source.commit` is `"unknown"`.

title: Commands
text:
## Commands

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local make verify
GOTOOLCHAIN=local make release-test          # sh scripts/release/test.sh --build
out=$(mktemp -d)
GOTOOLCHAIN=local sh scripts/release/package.sh --version 0.0.0-local --out "$out"
sh scripts/release/check-archive.sh --require-run "$out"/luuna-beacon_0.0.0-local_*.tar.gz
make release-local VERSION=0.0.0-local OUT=dist/release-local   # OUT must be new or empty
```

`--os`/`--arch` can cross-build. `check-archive.sh` checks structure for any platform but runs binaries only on the host. With `--require-run`, a non-host archive fails (exit 6).

title: Validation status
text:
## Validation status

- Review passed, including the patch for the two review blockers: `SHA256SUMS` now fails closed, and `dirty` reports `null` when unknown instead of `false`.
- Native release tests reported 60 passing on the local host (darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.3).
- The `release.yml` matrix has not been run. darwin/amd64, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 archives have not been built or executed natively. Only the local host platform has been exercised.
- Local Go (1.27.3) differs from the CI pin (1.27.0), so local and CI binaries are not byte-identical. Tar and gzip metadata are deterministic for a given toolchain. Binary reproducibility across Go patch releases is not claimed.
- musl/Alpine are untested.

title: Deferred (owner gates)
text:
## Deferred (owner gates)

1. Dispatch `release.yml` and download the four artifacts.
2. On each claimed platform, verify `SHA256SUMS`, run `check-archive.sh`, and review `provenance.json`.
3. Decide on macOS signing/notarization and on GitHub build attestations. Attestations need `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`. The step is commented out.
4. Create the tag and GitHub Release and upload all assets, including `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`.
5. Add the hub manifest rows in `luuna-ai-os` through a reviewed PR.

Registry publication (npm or others) remains out of scope. See [RELEASING.md](/docs/components-beacon-docs-releasing#deferred-owner-gates-not-done-here).

title: Releasing Luuna Beacon native archives
text:
# Releasing Luuna Beacon native archives

Nothing in this repository publishes anything. The scripts and workflow below produce **unpublished** archives, checksums and self-reported provenance. Publication (tags, GitHub Releases, signing, attestations, registries) is a separate owner decision. Those steps are listed at the end.

title: Archive contract
text:
## Archive contract

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `luuna-beacon_<version>_<darwin\|linux>_<arm64\|amd64>.tar.gz` |
| Entries | exactly `bin/luuna-beacon` and `bin/lbc`: regular files, mode 0755, uid/gid 0, fixed mtime, no directory entries |
| Excluded | `lb` (a compatibility alias kept for source builds only, too generic for a public `PATH`) |
| Beside the archive | `SHA256SUMS`, `provenance.json`, `LICENSE`, `UPSTREAM.md` |

`LICENSE` (MIT, upstream notice) and `UPSTREAM.md` ship **beside** the archive, not inside it. The hub installer only accepts `bin/<public executable>` entries, so attribution travels as separate release files. Every file is listed in `SHA256SUMS`.

Both executables are built from their own `cmd/` package. All three `cmd/*/main.go` files call `cli.Run(os.Args[1:], …)` and never inspect `argv[0]`, so `lbc` behaves exactly like `luuna-beacon` with the same arguments. `check-archive.sh` asserts this on host-matching archives by comparing `--version` and `--json --version` output.

title: Versions
text:
## Versions

- **Archive version**: the `--version` input. It is validated as `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE]` and appears in the file name and as `archive_version` in `provenance.json`.
- **Internal version**: `const version` in `internal/cli/cli.go` (currently `0.2.6`), printed by `luuna-beacon --version`. It is a Go `const`, so `-ldflags -X` cannot override it, and the build passes only `-s -w`. It is recorded as `internal_version` in `provenance.json`. Making the two match is an owner release action: edit the constant in a reviewed change.

title: Local dry run (host platform only)
text:
## Local dry run (host platform only)

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local make verify
GOTOOLCHAIN=local sh scripts/release/test.sh --build     # offline script tests plus a real host build
out=$(mktemp -d)
GOTOOLCHAIN=local sh scripts/release/package.sh --version 0.0.0-local --out "$out"
sh scripts/release/check-archive.sh --require-run "$out"/luuna-beacon_0.0.0-local_*.tar.gz

title: or: make release-local VERSION=0.0.0-local OUT=dist/release-local (dist/ is git-ignored)
text:
# or: make release-local VERSION=0.0.0-local OUT=dist/release-local   (dist/ is git-ignored)
```

`package.sh --os/--arch` can cross-build, because `CGO_ENABLED=0`. `check-archive.sh` checks the structure of any archive but runs the binaries only when the archive matches the host. `--require-run` makes a non-host archive fail (exit 6) instead of falling back to a structure-only check. CI and `make release-local` use it.

`check-archive.sh` requires a regular, non-symlink `SHA256SUMS` beside the archive that lists the archive name exactly once with a matching SHA-256. A missing, symlinked, duplicate, malformed or mismatched entry fails with exit 4. A missing `sha256sum`/`shasum` fails with exit 3.

`package.sh` stages every output privately and moves the outputs into `--out` only after all steps succeed. A failure, including a failing `tar` (it writes an intermediate file, so its exit status is not masked by `gzip`), removes the known output names again. It also removes `--out` if this run created it and it is empty. `--out` is never deleted recursively.

`provenance.json` `source.dirty` covers tracked and untracked (non-ignored) changes, because `go build` compiles untracked `.go` files. It is `null` when Git is unavailable or the checkout is not the root of its own repository. In that case `source.commit` is `"unknown"`.

title: Toolchain pin limitations
text:
### Toolchain pin limitations

- CI pins Go `1.27.0` through `actions/setup-go` and sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so `go.mod`'s `go 1.27.0` line never triggers a toolchain download.
- Locally, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` uses whatever Go is installed. The local validation for this change used `go1.27.3 darwin/arm64`. That satisfies `go 1.27.0`, but it is not byte-identical to the CI build. `provenance.json` records the exact `go_version`.
- Builds are reproducible in their tar and gzip metadata (owner, mtime, `gzip -n`) for a given toolchain. `package.sh` pins `TZ=UTC`, so the fixed mtime does not depend on the builder's time zone. `test.sh --build` compares archives built under two different `TZ` values. Bit-for-bit binary reproducibility across Go patch releases is not claimed.
- Linux binaries are static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). musl/Alpine are not separately tested.

title: Workflow: .github/workflows/release.yml
text:
## Workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml`

- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` with a `version` input only. There is no tag or push trigger.
- Permissions: `contents: read`. Checkout uses `persist-credentials: false`.
- Matrix, each job building natively on its runner:

  | Runner | Target |
  | --- | --- |
  | `macos-14` | darwin/arm64 |
  | `macos-15-intel` | darwin/amd64 (replaces the retired `macos-13`) |
  | `ubuntu-latest` | linux/amd64 |
  | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` | linux/arm64 |

- Steps: `go test`, then `go vet`, then `scripts/release/test.sh`, then `package.sh`, then `check-archive.sh --require-run` (the job fails if its runner cannot execute the archive it built), then `actions/upload-artifact`.
- The attestation step is present only as a commented-out owner gate. The workflow has no `gh release`, release action, `npm publish` or registry step.

title: Deferred owner gates (not done here)
text:
## Deferred owner gates (not done here)

1. Run `release.yml` manually and download the four artifacts.
2. On each claimed platform, verify `SHA256SUMS`, run `check-archive.sh`, and review `provenance.json`. Provenance is self-reported, not an attestation.
3. Decide on macOS signing/notarization and on GitHub build attestations. Enabling attestations needs `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`.
4. Create the tag and GitHub Release and upload the assets, including `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`.
5. Add the hub manifest rows (URLs and SHA256s copied from the released assets) through a reviewed PR in `luuna-ai-os`.

npm and other registries remain unpublished and are a separate decision.

title: Security Policy
text: # Security Policy

title: Supported Versions
text:
## Supported Versions

| Version | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| 0.1.x   | Yes       |

Only the latest release on the current major version line receives security updates.

title: Reporting a Vulnerability
text:
## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue for security vulnerabilities.**

Please report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-beacon/security/advisories).

1. Go to the [Security Advisories page](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-beacon/security/advisories)
2. Click **"New draft security advisory"**
3. Fill in a description of the vulnerability, including steps to reproduce if possible

title: Response Timeline
text:
### Response Timeline

- **Acknowledgment**: Within 48 hours of your report
- **Initial assessment**: Within 7 days
- **Fix or mitigation**: Within 30 days for confirmed vulnerabilities

We will keep you informed of progress throughout the process.

title: Scope
text:
## Scope

Luuna Beacon is a CLI tool that reads and writes files on the local filesystem. The following are considered security issues:

- **Command injection** -- Unsanitized input passed to shell execution
- **Path traversal** -- Accessing files outside the intended `.luuna/beacon/` directory
- **Arbitrary file access** -- Reading or writing files the user did not intend
- **Symlink attacks** -- Following symlinks to unintended locations
- **Temp file races** -- TOCTOU vulnerabilities in temporary file handling

The following are generally **not** in scope:

- Denial of service via large input files (Luuna Beacon is a local tool, not a service)
- Issues that require the attacker to already have local shell access with the same privileges as the user
- Social engineering or phishing

title: Security Measures
text:
## Security Measures

Luuna Beacon already implements several hardening measures:

- Atomic writes via temp file + rename to prevent partial/corrupt files
- Advisory file locking to prevent concurrent write corruption
- JSONL storage with git-native merge strategies

If you believe any of these measures can be bypassed, please report it through the process above.

title: Beacon: versioned prompts and agent instructions
text:
# Beacon: versioned prompts and agent instructions

Beacon is Luuna's maintained, MIT-licensed fork of Canopy. It composes and versions prompt resources and agent instructions. Its package identity is `@luuna/beacon-cli`; run `luuna-beacon` or the short alias `lb`. The legacy `cn` alias remains available for existing integrations.

title: Resources and composition
text:
## Resources and composition

Beacon keeps its project data in `.canopy/`. Its resource model supports versioned prompts, schemas, sections, inheritance, mixins, validation, history, and rendered output. Consult the [Beacon CLI reference](/docs/components-beacon-docs-cli-reference) for each command and the current [Canopy-derived specification](/docs/components-beacon-spec) for storage, composition, identifiers, lifecycle, and rendering semantics.

Luuna integrates Beacon through its CLI/JSON boundary. An approved plan can bind the exact selected content, version, and hash so a changed resource invalidates approval. Beacon itself does not grant execution authority or replace the runtime's approval checks.

title: Run from source
text:
## Run from source

The repository documents Bun 1.4.3:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/index.ts --help
bun run verify
```

Start with the [Beacon README](/docs/components-beacon-readme). The CLI reference includes `init`, `create`, `list`, `show`, `render`, `diff`, `history`, `pin`, `sync`, `validate`, and related commands. Review the component [migration guide](/docs/components-beacon-migration) before bringing existing Canopy data into a project; Beacon preserves `.canopy/` formats rather than renaming or rewriting them.

title: Maintenance and provenance
text:
## Maintenance and provenance

Beacon is consumed from a reviewed, pinned Git submodule commit in [`luuna-ai/luuna-beacon`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-beacon). In the core Luuna source snapshot documented here, the integration pin is [`072e482`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-beacon/tree/072e482169e0d469c3744ec712222f8b310fa7da); the reference pages below follow a newer component-repository head. Check the pin before relying on newer behavior in core Luuna. The npm package is private and unpublished. Its public repo contains the current README, CLI reference, changelog, security policy, and attributed upstream material. Use the Luuna fork and its recorded commit; do not assume a similarly named package or Canopy release is interchangeable.

title: 🚀 Key Features
text: ## 🚀 Key Features

title: 🏛️ Authentic Turbo Pascal 7.0 / Turbo Vision GUI
text:
### 🏛️ Authentic Turbo Pascal 7.0 / Turbo Vision GUI
- **16-Color DOS/VGA Palette**: Classic Borland royal blue desktop, double-line frames, and 3D shadow buttons.
- **Top Menu Bar (10 Menus)**: `File`, `Edit`, `Search`, `Run`, `Compile`, `Debug`, `Tools`, `Options`, `Window`, `Help` with red mnemonic shortcuts (`Alt+F`..`Alt+H`).
- **Interactive Session Selector**: Browse and resume project sessions with date/time, task previews, and `1`..`9` fast shortcuts (`F3 Open`, `/resume`, `/sessions`).
- **Recent Sessions History**: The `File` menu automatically lists up to 9 recently saved/opened sessions with red numbered shortcuts (`1.` .. `9.`).
- **Complete Mouse Interaction**: Click to focus windows, open menus, select tree files, click window close `[■]` and zoom `[▲]` boxes, scroll lists with mouse wheel, and drag to select & copy text.
- **Vim Navigation**: `h`/`j`/`k`/`l`, `gg`/`G`, `Ctrl+D`/`Ctrl+U`, `:` for the command line, `/` to find files, `Ctrl+W` to switch windows.

title: 🧠 Advanced LLM & Reasoning Workflow
text:
### 🧠 Advanced LLM & Reasoning Workflow
- **Model Switching (`F4 Model`)**: Browse all available models from Pi, or use `[+] Enter custom model ID...` for quick custom models.
- **Custom Model Management**: Add and configure arbitrary models across providers (`openrouter`, `opencode`, `deepseek`, `google`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `groq`, `mistral`, `xai`, `together`) directly from `Options` → `Add custom model...` with automatic `~/.pi/agent/models.json` synchronization.
- **API Key Configuration (`Options` → `Configure API keys...`)**: Dialog to configure and securely save provider API keys to the local `.env`.
- **Reasoning Effort Control (`F5 Effort`)**: Cycles reasoning effort levels (`low` → `medium` → `high` → `off`), with automatic model reasoning flag enablement.
- **PLAN / BUILD Modes (`F6 Mode`)**: Switch between Architectural Planning mode (`[PLAN]`) and Autonomous Code Execution mode (`[BUILD]`).
- **Visual Thinking Distinction**: Model reasoning (`thinking_delta`) renders in **Gray** (`LIGHTGRAY`); the final response renders in **Bright White** (`WHITE`).
- **Built-in Slash Commands**: `/status`, `/help`, `/compact`, `/clear`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/diff`, `/test`, `/save`, `/open`, `/resume`.

title: 📁 Codebase Navigation & Git Tools
text:
### 📁 Codebase Navigation & Git Tools
- **Project Tree Window**: Live filesystem explorer with folder expand/collapse, git-dirty indicators, and instant file preview (`Click` / Enter).
- **Unified Diff Viewer (`F7 Diff`)**: Color-coded unified diff viewer for git changes.
- **Test & Build Integration**: Direct execution of `npm test` (`F8 Test`) and `npm run build` (`F9 Build`) through Pi RPC.

- **Node.js** >= 20 (build-time only — the app itself does not use Node).

title: 🛠️ Installation
text: ## 🛠️ Installation

text:
### Prebuilt installers

- **Windows** — `LUUNA-AI_<version>_x64-setup.exe` (NSIS installer)

text:
### Build from source

cd luuna-ai

> `rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin x86_64-apple-darwin` — then
> `npm run build -- --target universal-apple-darwin`.

---

title: 🪟 The frameless window
text:
## 🪟 The frameless window

The window has **no title bar at all**. It is created with `decorations: false`, so the OS draws neither a caption nor caption buttons, and the app draws no caption strip of its own either — the DOS menu bar is the topmost element and the UI starts at the very top edge of the window.

Window affordances therefore live in the menu bar: drag its background (the empty space after `Help`) to move the window, and double-click that background to toggle maximize. `Alt+X` or `File → Exit` closes the app. Native **Save As** and **Change Directory** dialogs, a right-click **Copy/Paste/Select All** menu, and taskbar/dock app identity all still apply.

Changing the directory from the File menu reconnects Pi in the selected project and starts a new backend session. If spawning Pi fails, the current project and session stay active. Once the replacement starts, connection errors are reported in the selected project.

---

title: 🏗️ Architecture
text:
## 🏗️ Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   LUUNA-AI                       │
│        Tauri v2 shell — Rust backend             │
│  10-Menu Bar │ Project Tree │ Agent Panel (DOS)  │
│  renderer/ — HTML/CSS/JS recreating the VGA look │
└─────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                          │ JSONL over stdio (pi --mode rpc)
                          ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      PI                          │
│  LLM orchestration │ RPC engine │ Git & Context  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Pure Frontend Architecture**: Pi is never modified or forked; Luuna-AI drives Pi strictly via the documented JSONL RPC protocol.
- **No Bundled Browser**: the app uses the OS WebView (WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS), so installers stay around 1–2 MB.
- **Layout**: `src-tauri/` is the Rust backend (Pi subprocess, git, filesystem, sessions, env); `renderer/` is the UI. The renderer never touches the filesystem directly — all backend work goes through the `window.luuna` bridge, which maps 1:1 onto the `luuna_*` Tauri commands.

title: 🏗️ Architecture
text:
- **Bridge contract**: `renderer/luuna-provider.js` and the `luuna_*` commands in `src-tauri/src/main.rs` must stay in sync. The menu tree and help text live in `renderer/renderer.js` and `src-tauri/src/main.rs` — changing an item in one means changing it in the other.

title: CLAUDE.md
text:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

title: What this is
text:
## What this is

LUUNA-AI is a Turbo Pascal 7.0 / Borland DOS styled **native desktop** frontend for the [Pi coding agent](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono). Pi is never modified or forked — LUUNA-AI drives it strictly over Pi's documented JSONL RPC protocol (`pi --mode rpc`).

It is a [Tauri v2](https://tauri.app) application: a Rust backend plus a static HTML/CSS/JS renderer. There is no terminal UI in this repository and no Node code at runtime.

| Part | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | `src-tauri/` — Rust | owns the `pi` subprocess, the JSONL protocol, git/filesystem/session/env operations |
| Renderer | `renderer/` — HTML/CSS/JS | recreates the DOS/VGA UI; never touches the filesystem directly |

title: Commands
text:
## Commands

```bash
npm install        # installs @tauri-apps/cli (build-time only)
npm run dev        # tauri dev — hot-reloads the renderer, rebuilds Rust on change
npm run build      # tauri build — release build + native installer
npm run check      # cargo check
npm test           # cargo test
```

`npm run build` writes the installer to `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`. macOS needs both Rust targets for a universal binary:

```bash
rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin x86_64-apple-darwin
npm run build -- --target universal-apple-darwin
```

title: Architecture
text: ## Architecture

title: The Rust backend (src-tauri/src/main.rs)
text:
### The Rust backend (`src-tauri/src/main.rs`)

`main.rs` retains the Pi desktop; `components.rs` owns standalone workbench operations and workspace identity, and `component_runner.rs` owns bounded native CLI processes. Main is organised as: RPC plumbing → state → commands → the `pi` subprocess.

- **`luuna_*` commands** are the Tauri IPC surface. Every one maps 1:1 onto a `window.luuna` method in the renderer.
- **Push events**: `push:state`, `push:entry`, `push:delta`, `push:textPopup`, `push:bootError`. The renderer subscribes to these; it never polls.
- **`spawn_pi`** starts `pi --mode rpc`. On Windows it goes through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with Rust `raw_arg` for the validated command string (npm `.cmd` shims are not executable directly) and every argument is rejected if it contains `" \r\n&|<>^%!`. On macOS `pi` is executed directly.
- **Cross-platform code** is gated with `#[cfg(windows)]` / `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` — clipboard uses `clip` vs `pbcopy`, "show in folder" uses `explorer /select,` vs `open -R`. Keep new platform-specific code behind the same gates.
- **Tauri config** is split: `tauri.conf.json` is shared, `tauri.windows.conf.json` builds an NSIS installer (no WiX needed), `tauri.macos.conf.json` builds an `.app` and `.dmg`. Do not hardcode one platform's bundle target in the shared config.

title: The renderer (renderer/)
text:
### The renderer (`renderer/`)

Vanilla JS, no build step and no framework — `index.html`, `renderer.css`, `renderer.js`, `luuna-provider.js`.

- `renderer/luuna-provider.js` installs the `window.luuna` bridge over Tauri IPC (`invoke` + `listen`). It returns early if a bridge already exists, so an Electron preload can still provide one.
- `renderer/renderer.js` implements the menus, tiled windows, overlays and slash commands in DOM. The menu tree, key bar and help text live here and in the Rust backend.
- **The renderer must stay WebKit-compatible.** macOS uses WKWebView, not Chromium. Do not introduce Chromium-only APIs (`<dialog>`/`showModal`, `navigator.clipboard`, `backdrop-filter` without the `-webkit-` prefix, `structuredClone`, `ResizeObserver`) or CSS that Safari lacks. `::-webkit-scrollbar` is fine — WebKit and Chromium both support it.
- The window is frameless (`decorations: false`); the menu bar is the topmost element and doubles as the window's drag region and caption.

title: Duplicated data — update all copies
text:
### Duplicated data — update all copies

The menu tree, key bar and help text exist in **two independent places**:

1. `renderer/renderer.js` → `MAIN_MENUS`
2. `src-tauri/src/main.rs` (help / status data)

Changing a menu item, mnemonic, shortcut or action ID means editing both, or the shells drift apart. The same applies to the bridge method list: `renderer/luuna-provider.js` and the `luuna_*` commands in `main.rs` must stay in sync — every bridge method maps 1:1 onto a command.

title: Testing
text:
## Testing

`cargo test` (component unit tests; real CLI lifecycle is opt-in through `npm run test:components`) and the `npm run check` / `npm test` scripts above.

`test/` includes diagnostic probes and the automated `workbench-native-smoke.mjs` regression suite. `test/probe-live-cdp.mjs` inspects the running app's real DOM over the WebView2 CDP port; `test/cdp-eval.mjs` evaluates an expression in it; `test/cdp-shot.mjs` captures a PNG of the app's own rendered surface. These probes need the app launched with `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9333`. Run the separate workbench suite through `npm run test:workbench` after building.

title: Configuration and environment
text:
## Configuration and environment

- **`PI_CMD`** — overrides the Pi executable (default `pi` on PATH).
- **`LUUNA_AI_DIR`** — the project directory to open on launch. Falls back to the legacy `TURBO_AI_DIR`, then to the process working directory.
- **`PI_CONFIG_DIR`** — overrides the Pi config directory (default `~/.pi/agent`).
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` — custom models, written by `luuna_add_custom_model` via atomic temp-file + rename.
- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` — the `enabledModels` array; `filter_enabled_models` narrows the model list to it.
- `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**.jsonl` — Pi session files; `get_project_sessions` scans them and keeps only those whose recorded `cwd` matches the project.
- `.env` in the project directory — API keys, written by `luuna_write_env_key` (validated env var name, single-line value, mode 0600).
- Provider defaults (base URL, API type, env var name) live in `PROVIDER_DEFAULTS` in `src-tauri/src/main.rs`.

title: Conventions
text:
## Conventions

- Rust is formatted with tabs, matching the DOS aesthetic and the renderer's CSS.
- The UI theme is a fixed 16-colour DOS palette. Do not introduce arbitrary colours; add a named entry to the palette instead.
- The app must not bundle a browser. Keep using the OS WebView.
- `prompt.txt` and the original Turbo Pascal spec are not part of this repository.

title: Component workbench
text:
### Component workbench

`renderer/workbench.js` and `.css` provide the three DOS views via `luuna.workbenchStatus`, `workbenchInitialize` and `workbenchAction`; their Tauri counterparts are registered in main.rs. The operation enum is closed; never accept arbitrary CLI arguments/paths from the renderer. Keep all record writes in public CLIs, and never adopt sibling/runtime stores. See `docs/COMPONENT-WORKBENCH.md` and the embedded `components/manifest.json` pins.

Validation: `npm run components:setup`, `npm run check`, `npm test`, `npm run test:components`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:workbench`. The native smoke uses real WebView2/Tauri and CLIs with synthetic Pi, never paid provider calls. Only Windows native behavior is verified here.

title: Component workbench
text:
# Component workbench

- Date: 2026-10-22
- Specs: [Feature](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai/blob/82d7d556d657acb8837b4983057e4e4d094abad7/specs/feature-component-workbench.md), [lifecycle and recovery patch](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai/blob/82d7d556d657acb8837b4983057e4e4d094abad7/specs/patch-workbench-lifecycle.md)

title: Overview
text:
## Overview

LUUNA-AI exposes Missions tickets, Beacon prompts and Atlas expertise as standalone project workflows. The desktop never connects to the Luuna runtime or edits its stores, and does not inherit runtime planning, approval, promotion or publication guarantees. Selected context is appended to the message draft only on an explicit action; Pi is never sent an automatic prompt.

title: Usage
text:
## Usage

Install Bun 1.4.3 and Git, then run `npm run components:setup`. The script clones the three public repositories at exact commits from `components/manifest.json`, verifies package identities and installs frozen dependencies without lifecycle scripts. No private sibling checkout or published npm component package is needed. Set `LUUNA_AI_BUN` to a native Bun executable if it is not found automatically. `LUUNA_AI_COMPONENTS_ROOT` can select an existing compatible source root containing `components/{missions,atlas,beacon}`; it never selects data. Dirty or wrong-pin source checkouts are refused. The application uses an embedded manifest, so editing installation metadata cannot change its allowed pins.

From this checkout run `npm install`, `npm run components:setup`, then `npm run dev`. For an installed desktop, set `LUUNA_AI_COMPONENTS_ROOT` to the checkout's `.tools` directory before launching. Select your project through **File > Change Directory**, or set `LUUNA_AI_DIR` before launch. Open **Tools > Kanban board**, **Prompt library**, or **Expertise memory**, then choose **Initialize private workspace**. **Insert into message** appends context to the current draft for review; Escape closes the workbench and restores focus.

title: How it works
text:
## How it works

[`renderer/workbench.js`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai/blob/82d7d556d657acb8837b4983057e4e4d094abad7/renderer/workbench.js) and its stylesheet provide the views. The bridge in `renderer/luuna-provider.js` maps status, initialization and typed actions to Tauri commands in `src-tauri/src/main.rs`. [`components.rs`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai/blob/82d7d556d657acb8837b4983057e4e4d094abad7/src-tauri/src/components.rs) owns project identity/readiness and CLI workflows; [`component_runner.rs`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai/blob/82d7d556d657acb8837b4983057e4e4d094abad7/src-tauri/src/component_runner.rs) verifies and supervises pinned CLI execution. Project switching installs one Pi child and guards reader events/EOF by process generation so an old process cannot disconnect its replacement.

Opening a view is read-only. Initialize explicitly to create three real CLI stores under the application's data directory in `workbench`, keyed by SHA-256 of canonical project identity. Ownership metadata is checked on every operation. `LUUNA_AI_WORKBENCH_ROOT` can select a new private test/data root; existing foreign roots, linked paths and project/runtime stores are refused. The selected project directory is never initialized by a component. Source and data locations are independent.

title: How it works
text:
The adapter has a closed operation enum. Content goes through bounded JSON stdin, not shell commands or OS command-line arguments. The native runner isolates HOME/config/environment, disables Bun env-file loading and auto-install, rejects linked data and Atlas executable hooks, enforces 30 seconds, 1 MiB input, 4 MiB stdout and 64 KiB stderr, and owns/terminates descendants. This is host execution, not an OS sandbox. A timed-out write has uncertain outcome; refresh and reconcile before trying again.

Beacon edits compare the displayed version before writing and application actions are serialized. This detects stale desktop edits, but is not atomic cross-process compare-and-swap against external CLI writers. Historical previews show source, not falsely rendered historical composition. Atlas classification is not runtime memory scope; no global-memory promotion exists here.

title: Research and attribution
text:
## Research and attribution

Architecture was researched in `../luuna` at `87a7e3fea0416551e9ba61195ec5fff8f90a1989`, especially decisions 0012, 0014, 0020 and 0021, component source command implementations and `crates/luuna-components`. The bounded process runner and stdin bridge are adapted from that MIT implementation. Public component identities, versions, repository URLs, upstream attributions and license hashes are committed in `components/manifest.json`; each clone retains its license. Missions derives from Seeds, Beacon from Canopy, Atlas from Mulch.

title: Supported workflows
text:
## Supported workflows

- Missions: all-status board, create/edit/move, priorities/types, dependency add/remove and unresolved dependency indicators.
- Beacon: active/archived list, search, create, single-section edit preserving other sections, tags, composition render, version/source history, archive/restore.
- Atlas: convention/content; pattern/name+description; failure/description+resolution; decision/title+rationale. Domain/type/classification filters, capture provenance in tags, search/edit/delete. Tags are creation-time provenance; the upstream edit command does not update tags.
- All three: refresh and explicit context insertion preserving the current message draft.

title: Testing
text:
## Testing

Run `npm run check`, `npm test`, `npm run test:components`, `npm run build`, and `npm run test:workbench`. Integration tests use disposable stores and actual pinned CLIs. The native smoke uses the freshly built Windows executable and real Tauri IPC, with a clearly synthetic Pi fixture to avoid provider calls. macOS native behavior is untested on this Windows host.

title: Observed Windows validation (2026-10-22)
text:
### Observed Windows validation (2026-10-22)

The independent tester passed all seven commands, including pinned public setup and `git diff --check`. `npm run check` retained six pre-existing warnings. `npm test` passed 10 unit tests; its two opt-in tests passed separately via `npm run test:components`, covering all three CLI lifecycle workflows and partial-store recovery, >48KiB Unicode stdin, stale Beacon conflict detection, Atlas executable-hook refusal, service reconstruction and project separation. `npm run build` produced `src-tauri/target/release/luuna-ai.exe` and `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/LUUNA-AI_1.0.2_x64-setup.exe`.

Native smoke passed all nine workflow checks on the fresh Windows release: actual ticket and prompt create/edit/move/version/render, draft insertion, Atlas create/search/edit/delete, visible errors, restored focus and body-focused Escape, A-to-B-to-A project switching with isolated records and exactly one new Pi process per switch, real fixture RPC after old-process EOF, restart persistence, and active-child EOF handling. The fixture recorded zero prompt sends. All six normal/minimum 760x480 screenshots were independently inspected. The ignored `.tac/runs/8d2ea719/tester-native/verification.json` records `complete: true` and executable SHA-256 `4a36dd8a99f43160e442b114629aee69c56bc317610a46e178cd0dc345c0ee9c`. DOM controls are clicked through WebView2 CDP; physical-mouse delivery, macOS and

title: Observed Windows validation (2026-10-22)
text: live-provider behavior were not tested. Independent review passed with no blockers and one follow-up for generic CLI refusal messages.

title: Notes and recovery
text:
## Notes and recovery

Readiness now requires all component config/store artifacts, even if ownership metadata says initialized. Empty interrupted Missions/Beacon directories may be removed non-recursively and initialized again. Nonempty incomplete Missions or Beacon stores are refused intact with recovery guidance; restore missing artifacts from backup or use the component's documented recovery tools before refreshing. Atlas uses its idempotent public init to restore missing config/expertise artifacts without rewriting existing records. The real-component partial-recovery suite verifies byte preservation, truthful partial status, blocked actions, safe retries and repeated initialization.

The pinned Missions CLI ignores empty description and assignee edits. The adapter refuses attempted clearing of nonempty values with an actionable error; labels can be cleared using its supported `--set-labels` option. Atlas edit retains creation-time provenance tags. Long Missions IDs reflect its workspace-derived prefix; cards abbreviate their display and retain the full value in accessible labels and titles.

Some CLI failures, such as duplicate prompt names or invalid/circular dependencies, currently return a generic refusal. Refresh to confirm stored state and correct the submitted values; actionable category-specific messages are a review follow-up. Raw stderr and private record text are intentionally excluded from error messages.

title: Notes and recovery
text: The adapted runner's original MIT notice is retained in `docs/LUUNA-RUNNER-LICENSE.txt`.

title: Local Windows setup follow-up (2026-10-22)
text:
## Local Windows setup follow-up (2026-10-22)

Dependencies and all three pinned components are installed. The current user's `LUUNA_AI_COMPONENTS_ROOT` points to this checkout's `.tools`, and `LUUNA_AI_BUN` points to native Bun 1.4.3. The installed Windows app and its Desktop/Start Menu shortcuts open the `luuna-ai` project; its private workspace is initialized. Use **Tools** to open any of the three views. Other project directories have their own workspace and can be initialized when selected.

Setup exposed and fixed Windows argument escaping in the Pi launcher: `cmd.exe` now receives its validated command string through Rust `raw_arg`, including correctly quoted executable paths with spaces. Twelve unit tests pass, including an actual npm-style shim argument round trip. The native fixture now forwards and validates arguments instead of silently ignoring them. Installed Pi 1.3.0 answered RPC health checks successfully; no model prompt was sent. Local installation identity, view screenshots and setup verification are saved under ignored `.tac/runs/workbench-setup/`. The NSIS-installed executable differs from the raw release only in Tauri's documented bundle-type marker.

title: Local Windows setup follow-up (2026-10-22)
text: The follow-up passed Rust checks, both real CLI suites, the rebuilt installer, and all nine native workflow checks with the stricter launcher fixture. Native waits check actual readiness and allow for sequential CLI operations on slower Windows hosts. The installed application was reopened normally from its configured shortcut with debugging disabled.

title: Luuna AI: native Pi desktop client
text:
# Luuna AI: native Pi desktop client

Luuna AI is a native desktop frontend for the Pi coding agent. It uses Tauri v2 and a Turbo Pascal 7 / Borland DOS-inspired interface, then launches `pi --mode rpc` and communicates over Pi's JSONL protocol. It is a client for Pi, not the Luuna Rust runtime, not Atlas/Missions/Beacon, and not the documentation website's Talk to AI feature.

title: Interface and workflows
text:
## Interface and workflows

The desktop app provides project-tree and file previews, session browsing and resume, menus and keyboard shortcuts, model and reasoning-effort selection, PLAN/BUILD modes, diffs, tests, builds, and built-in slash commands. The README documents the current menu and shortcut behavior, platform installers, source builds, and known beta status. Controls include F3 for opening sessions, F4 for model selection, F5 for reasoning effort, F6 for PLAN/BUILD mode, F7 for diffs, F8 for tests, F9 for builds, and F10 for the menu.

The app saves provider credentials locally using its documented settings flow. Treat those values as sensitive. The repository's own `.env` and local Pi configuration are private user state and should never be copied into this public documentation site.

title: Build and run
text:
## Build and run

See the [LUUNA-AI README](/docs/components-ai-readme) for the exact requirements, available prebuilt installers, and platform-specific build instructions. The source repository provides these checks:

```sh
npm run check
npm test
```

The application requires the Pi coding agent to be available as a child process. Its development workflow uses `npm run dev`; native release builds use `npm run build`. Actual platform packaging and provider behavior must be verified on the target machine; a source build alone does not prove a distributed installer works.

title: Source, license, and status
text:
## Source, license, and status

Luuna AI is maintained in the public [`luuna-ai/luuna-ai`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-ai) repository under MIT. Its README identifies it as an early beta and describes the Turbo Pascal homage; it is not affiliated with Borland. Follow the repository's release notes for current platform support and installable artifacts.

title: Luuna components
text:
# Luuna components

Luuna maintains three MIT-licensed distributions with space-themed identities. Each retains its upstream implementation and data contracts behind a separate integration boundary.

| Component | Responsibility | Primary CLI | Short alias | Origin | Data format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Luuna Missions](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-missions/blob/e1b5db171892de653e7462e630d64d4964d01422/README.md) | Tickets and structured plans | luuna-missions | lm | Seeds 0.6.0 | .seeds/ |
| [Luuna Atlas](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-atlas/blob/76ad209daf404dd9a12aeaf46293e05e9f41e517/README.md) | Expertise and project memory | luuna-atlas | la | Mulch 0.11.0 | .mulch/ |
| [Luuna Beacon](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-beacon/blob/072e482169e0d469c3744ec712222f8b310fa7da/README.md) | Composable prompts and instructions | luuna-beacon | lb | Canopy 0.2.6 | .canopy/ |

title: Luuna components
text:
[manifest.json](manifest.json) records package names, versions, entrypoints, and compatible data paths for tooling. Packages are private and unpublished. Source now lives in the public repositories [Luuna Missions](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-missions), [Luuna Atlas](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-atlas), and [Luuna Beacon](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna-beacon). These directories are exact-commit Git submodules. The manifest commit and Git gitlink must agree; see [ADR 0012](../docs/decisions/0012-independent-component-repositories.md).

The existing automation boundary is CLI execution with structured JSON output (consult each command's help for its output contract). Atlas additionally exports a TypeScript library through src/index.ts and src/api.ts. Missions and Beacon expose executable CLI entrypoints; importing their package main as a service API would execute command-line code and is not a supported integration.

Luuna's runtime will translate domain operations into these interfaces through adapters. Persistent ticket, knowledge, and prompt integration is planned work; this rebrand does not claim that the components are wired into the Luuna runtime yet. The runtime must retain approval, validation, and publication policy ownership. Components must not write directly to Luuna's database or bypass those policies.

title: Luuna components
text:
Run `npm run components:setup` after cloning Luuna (or use `git clone --recurse-submodules`). Run `npm run components:verify` to check pins and `npm run test:components` for real isolated ticket, knowledge and prompt CLI operations. `npm run components:run -- luuna-missions -- --help` invokes a pinned CLI from your current project directory (including npm --prefix use via INIT_CWD), preserving stdin, stdout, stderr and the component exit status; use luuna-atlas or luuna-beacon for the other tools. This developer launcher is not a runtime adapter and grants no Luuna approval.

Each component has its own frozen Bun lockfile and can be installed and tested from its directory. Install with `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, then run `bun run verify`. The root frontend npm workspace does not resolve or publish these Bun distributions. Primary and legacy executable names are package bin mappings; run the documented Bun source entrypoint when working directly from a checkout. Existing legacy integration snippets remain usable through compatibility aliases.

Upstream LICENSE files, authorship, versions, and provenance are retained in every component. Original source and imported authoring records were preserved outside this checkout before removal. Session histories, authoring stores, and upstream automation instructions are not Luuna project state.

title: Updating a component
text:
## Updating a component

Make and test source changes in its own repository. After its independent CI passes, fetch and check out the reviewed full commit in Luuna's submodule, update the matching commit in manifest.json, and run components:setup, components:verify and test:components. Commit the gitlink and manifest together for review. Setup uses the committed pin, never --remote; dirty checkouts or incompatible CLI contracts fail visibly. No npm registry publication is required. brodynelly owns component CI and release decisions.

Public component access requires no Luuna credential, deploy key, provider token or private task history. Luuna remains private. Extraction itself did not change ticket authority. The later runtime slice now adds explicit private-store activation, Missions migration/reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon plan resources; see [ADR 0014](../docs/decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md). Broader M6 parity and supported-platform evidence remain open.

title: Luuna components
text:
# Luuna components

Luuna is a family of related tools, not one executable. The Rust Luuna runtime coordinates development work and remains the authority for approvals and execution policy. Four independently maintained components add knowledge, tickets, prompt resources, and a desktop interface.

title: Choose the component you need
text:
## Choose the component you need

| Component | Use it for | Main boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Atlas](/docs/guide-component-atlas) | Structured expertise and project memory | A local CLI and TypeScript library; Luuna only uses memory that a plan explicitly selects. |
| [Missions](/docs/guide-component-missions) | Git-native tickets, dependencies, and work plans | A local CLI and durable project records; it becomes the ticket authority only when explicitly enabled. |
| [Beacon](/docs/guide-component-beacon) | Versioned, composable prompts and agent instructions | A local CLI; the exact resource, version, and content hash can be bound into approval. |
| [Luuna AI](/docs/guide-component-ai) | A native desktop interface for the Pi coding agent | A user-facing Tauri application that speaks Pi's JSONL RPC protocol; it is not the Luuna runtime or the website assistant. |

title: How the pieces fit
text:
## How the pieces fit

The core runtime owns repository registration, baseline checks, plans, approval, worktrees, validation, independent review, bounded repair, and publication. Missions, Atlas, and Beacon are separate command-line tools with their own repositories, data formats, and release histories. Luuna invokes them at explicit integration boundaries; installing or activating one does not transfer runtime policy to it. Luuna AI is another client surface: it launches Pi in RPC mode and renders the interaction in a Turbo Pascal-inspired desktop IDE.

The command-line components are consumed at reviewed Git submodule commits. Their similarly named npm packages are private and unpublished; use the repository's checked-out source rather than assuming an npm install will work. Each repo's README and component references are reproduced below with the source commit recorded on each page.

- [Luuna AI: desktop client](/docs/guide-component-ai), plus its [source README](/docs/components-ai-readme).

text:
## Compatibility and evidence

Component behavior can change independently. This site pins each reference page to the source commit recorded for that component; publishing these docs does not imply that each component was built, run, or provider-tested. The core Luuna organization main snapshot consumes Atlas `27477c313a3049b1579dfdc32c39da600726721f`, Missions `6a4a3c3fb80679a77bbf1d7d2da05033fc15460c`, and Beacon `4b01d37522ef448ada78be08cc7a24f7808dfbbb` as exact Git submodule commits. Luuna AI is maintained independently and is not a core runtime submodule. Review component changelogs and migration guides before changing a local setup; accepted Luuna architecture decisions remain authoritative for runtime behavior.

title: Luuna Missions
text:
# Luuna Missions

Git-native tickets and structured work plans. This is Luuna's maintained MIT-licensed fork of Seeds, imported from upstream version **0.6.0**. The Luuna package identity is **@luuna/missions-cli** in the independent public repository [luuna-ai/luuna-missions](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions). The package remains private and unpublished.

title: Run from a checkout
text:
## Run from a checkout

Use Bun **1.4.3** and Go **1.22 or newer**. Keep `go` on `PATH`, or set `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` to the Go executable. The package bin at `src/index.ts` is a Bun compatibility launcher: it builds the matching native executable on first use, caches it under `dist/`, and forwards arguments, standard streams, signals, and the exit code to Go.

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/index.ts --help
bun run verify
```

`bun run build:native` builds the native cache without running a command. A compiled executable can also run directly without Bun; `go run ./cmd/luuna-missions --help` runs it from source. The cache is local and ignored by Git, so a fresh checkout or package install needs Go for the first launch.

The primary command is `luuna-missions`. Package bin aliases are `lms`, `lm` (compatibility), and `missions`; the consuming Luuna launcher exposes `luuna missions <args>`. Its current pinned Bun entrypoint can continue to use the shim. Updating Luuna's exact submodule pin and installer is a separate reviewed integration, and changes in this repository do not update that consumer automatically.

title: What it manages
text:
## What it manages

`init` creates `.luuna/missions/` with `issues.jsonl`, `plans.jsonl`, `templates.jsonl`, and `config.yaml`. Use `create`, `ready`, `update --claim`, and `close` for tickets; `dep`, `label`, `block`, and `unblock` manage relationships; `plan` manages structured plans and child tickets. `tpl` creates reusable issue convoys. `config`, `doctor`, `sync`, `prime`, `onboard`, `setup claude`, `guard`, and `completions` provide project and agent tooling. Run `luuna-missions --help` or see the [full CLI and system map](/docs/components-missions-docs-cli-system-map) for every command, option family, side effect, and integration.

Project discovery walks upward from the working directory. A legacy `.seeds/` directory may be moved to `.luuna/missions/` on first access; see [MIGRATION.md](/docs/components-missions-migration). Environment variables use the `LUUNA_MISSIONS_` prefix. The Go implementation preserves the JSON and JSONL contracts, advisory locks, atomic writes, and existing project schemas. Luuna owns runtime policy and approval enforcement; Atlas supplies optional plan prior art and decision recording, while Beacon owns reusable prompts.

title: What it manages
text: `sync` stages `.luuna/missions/` and commits the current Git index, including unrelated paths that were already staged. Use `git diff --cached --name-only` to inspect other staged paths before committing. Self-upgrade remains disabled while the package is unpublished. Never replace this fork with a similarly named registry package; update through a reviewed commit and an exact Luuna submodule pin. Dependency installation does not alter root Git hooks.

title: Development and releases
text:
## Development and releases

The runtime is in `cmd/` and `internal/`. `src/index-legacy.ts` and the TypeScript modules under `src/` remain as the compatibility oracle for the differential test corpus. `bun run verify` runs the TypeScript type check, instruction check, Bun tests, Go tests, and Go-versus-TypeScript CLI parity cases. CI declares this surface on Linux and Windows using Bun 1.4.3 and the Go version in `go.mod`. See [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-missions-agents) for repository rules and [the system map](/docs/components-missions-docs-cli-system-map) for validation limits.

The repository is maintained by the luuna-ai organization. Registry publishing is disabled and requires no npm token. Luuna pins a reviewed commit, never a floating branch; update its submodule only after CI and a consumer smoke pass. Read [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-missions-upstream) for provenance and [the original README](/docs/components-missions-docs-upstream-readme) for inherited command examples. Upstream release/runbook documents are historical references and do not authorize publication.

title: Origin and attribution
text:
## Origin and attribution

Luuna Missions is derived from [Seeds](https://github.com/jayminwest/seeds) 0.6.0 by Jaymin West (MIT). The original license is preserved in [LICENSE](/docs/components-missions-license), and provenance is recorded in [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-missions-upstream). Seeds is independent; Luuna Missions is not affiliated with or endorsed by its authors.

title: Contributing to Missions
text:
# Contributing to Missions

Thanks for your interest in contributing to Missions! This guide covers everything you need to get started.

title: Getting Started
text:
## Getting Started

1. **Fork** the repository on GitHub
2. **Clone** your fork locally:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/missions.git
   cd missions
   ```
3. **Install** dependencies:
   ```bash
   bun install
   ```
4. **Create a branch** for your work:
   ```bash
   git checkout -b fix/description-of-change
   ```

title: Branch Naming
text:
## Branch Naming

Use descriptive branch names with a category prefix:

- `fix/` -- Bug fixes
- `feat/` -- New features
- `docs/` -- Documentation changes
- `refactor/` -- Code refactoring
- `test/` -- Test additions or fixes

title: Build & Test Commands
text:
## Build & Test Commands

```bash
bun test              # Run all tests
bun run lint          # Biome check
bun run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
```

Always run all three before submitting a PR.

title: Coding Conventions
text:
## Coding Conventions

- **Tab indentation** (enforced by Biome)
- **100 character line width** (enforced by Biome)
- Strict TypeScript with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` — always handle possible `undefined`
- No `any` — use `unknown` and narrow, or define proper types
- All imports use `.ts` extensions
- Minimal runtime dependencies (chalk + commander only)
- Tests use real filesystems (temp dirs via `mkdtemp`), never mocks

title: Testing
text:
## Testing

- **Framework:** `bun test` (built-in, Jest-compatible API)
- Tests colocated with source: `src/foo.test.ts` next to `src/foo.ts`
- Use real I/O with temp directories, no mocks

title: Pull Request Expectations
text:
## Pull Request Expectations

- **One concern per PR.** Keep changes focused.
- **Tests required.** New features and bug fixes should include tests.
- **Passing CI.** All PRs must pass CI checks before merge.
- **Description.** Briefly explain what and why. Link relevant issues.

title: Reporting Issues
text:
## Reporting Issues

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/issues) for bug reports and feature requests. For security vulnerabilities, see [SECURITY.md](/docs/components-missions-security).

title: Missions: git-native tickets and work plans
text:
# Missions: git-native tickets and work plans

Missions is Luuna's maintained, MIT-licensed fork of Seeds. It provides local, Git-native tickets, dependencies, structured plans, and reusable work templates. Its package identity is `@luuna/missions-cli`; run it as `luuna-missions` or the short alias `lm`. The legacy `sd` and `seeds` aliases remain for existing integrations.

title: Records and workflow
text:
## Records and workflow

Missions stores project work in `.seeds/` and preserves the upstream configuration, JSONL records, markers, and environment variables. Issues carry intent and acceptance criteria; dependencies describe ordering; reusable templates can create structured plans and coordinated work. Review the current [Missions specification](/docs/components-missions-spec) for the data model, CLI, JSON output, concurrency behavior, and migration details.

The core runtime may call Missions through the CLI/JSON boundary. It becomes the ticket authority only after explicit activation. Merely installing it does not change how Luuna records work. Runtime approval, candidate identity, validation, and publication policy remain in Luuna.

title: Run from source
text:
## Run from source

Use the repository's documented Bun 1.4.3 toolchain:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/index.ts --help
bun run verify
```

Start with the [Missions README](/docs/components-missions-readme), then use the [specification](/docs/components-missions-spec) for the command and record details. Review the [migration guide](/docs/components-missions-migration) before moving existing Seeds data. The fork keeps `.seeds/` data compatible and does not silently rewrite it.

title: Maintenance and provenance
text:
## Maintenance and provenance

Missions is consumed by Luuna at a reviewed Git submodule commit from [`luuna-ai/luuna-missions`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions). In the core Luuna source snapshot documented here, the integration pin is [`e1b5db1`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/tree/e1b5db171892de653e7462e630d64d4964d01422); the reference pages below follow a newer component-repository head. Check the pin before relying on newer behavior in core Luuna. Its npm package remains private and unpublished. The original Seeds documentation is retained as attributed historical reference. Follow the component's current changelog and migration notes when upgrading; do not assume a floating branch or registry version is the version used by Luuna.

title: Luuna Missions
text:
# Luuna Missions

Read [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-missions-agents) for current development instructions and [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-missions-upstream) for provenance. This repository owns the component; Luuna owns runtime policy. Archived upstream workflows are reference material.

title: Luuna Missions CLI and system map
text:
# Luuna Missions CLI and system map

This is the command, tooling, data, and integration map of the maintained Missions fork. The live CLI implementation is Go: `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go` registers the built-in commands in `internal/cli/` and the plan family in `internal/plan/`. `src/index.ts` is a Bun launcher for the existing package and Luuna entrypoints. `src/index-legacy.ts` plus the TypeScript modules under `src/` remain a differential behavior oracle. This map describes write and Git side effects; reading it does not authorize running those commands in a user's project.

title: Place in Luuna
text:
## Place in Luuna

Missions owns Git-native tickets and structured plans. Atlas owns structured expertise and project memory, and Beacon owns reusable prompts. The Luuna runtime owns policy, permissions, and approval enforcement. Missions is a separate public repository consumed by Luuna at an exact submodule commit; it communicates with Luuna through command-line arguments, exit codes, JSON output, and `.luuna/missions/` data. A Missions change does not alter the consuming Luuna checkout until that pin and installer are updated in a separate reviewed integration.

```text
user / agent / Luuna launcher (`luuna missions`)
                  |
                  v
  package bin: luuna-missions / lms / lm / missions
                  |
                  v
   Bun compatibility launcher (`src/index.ts`)
                  |
       cached Go executable (`cmd/luuna-missions`)
                  |
        +---------+---------+------------------+
        |                   |                  |
  issues + dependencies   plans + templates  config + tooling
        |                   |                  |
        +-------------------+------------------+
                            |
                   .luuna/missions/ (Git files)
                            |
         optional: luuna-atlas query/record; Claude hooks; Git
```

title: Place in Luuna
text: The package is `@luuna/missions-cli` version 0.6.0 and remains private and unpublished. Its bin entries are `luuna-missions`, `lms`, `lm`, and `missions`, all pointing to `src/index.ts`. The consuming Luuna `components/manifest.json` still pins that Bun path, and its Windows installer writes Bun launchers. These files live in the parent repository. The shim makes that path dispatch to the Go implementation in this checkout; changing this repository alone does not move Luuna's exact submodule pin.

title: Runtime, build, and test tooling
text:
## Runtime, build, and test tooling

The Bun launcher calls `scripts/native-build.ts`, which hashes the package version, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and all files under `cmd/` and `internal/`, including embedded help, completion, schema, and prompt assets. It builds a matching binary once with `go build -trimpath` and injects the package version into `internal/cli.CurrentVersion`. The binary is stored under ignored `dist/<platform>-<architecture>/<digest>/` and is reused for that source revision. The launcher passes CLI arguments, standard streams, signals, working directory, and exit status to the child. Direct native execution needs no Bun after the binary is built.

| Tool or entry | Role | Requirement / output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/index.ts` | Compatibility entry for package bins and Luuna's existing pin | Bun 1.4.3; builds native binary on a cache miss |
| `scripts/native-build.ts` / `bun run build:native` | Source-keyed native build | Go 1.22+ on `PATH`, or `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` set to its executable; writes ignored `dist/` |
| `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go` | Native entry and command registration | Direct `go run ./cmd/luuna-missions <args>` or compiled binary |
| `internal/cli`, `internal/plan` | Parser, commands, plan lifecycle, help and completion text | Go runtime implementation; `internal/plan` registers through `cli.App` |

title: Runtime, build, and test tooling
text:
| `internal/model`, `internal/store`, `internal/config` | Wire records, JSONL/locking/atomic persistence, YAML schema/discovery/migration | Preserve existing project files and public JSON keys |
| `src/index-legacy.ts`, `src/register-all.ts`, `src/commands/` | Previous TypeScript command implementation | Oracle for command parity; not the package bin implementation |
| `scripts/parity.mjs` | Differential CLI corpus in isolated temporary Git projects | Compares Go and TypeScript exit codes, stdout/stderr, JSON values, ordered JSONL records, and non-JSON files |
| `scripts/verify-native.ts` / `bun run verify` | Run Go tests, build native, then run all parity suites after Bun checks | `verify` also runs type checking, instruction checks, and Bun tests |

The Go CLI embeds help snapshots, shell completions, and some `prime` content derived from the TypeScript oracle. Changes to those public strings require updating the Go fixtures and parity cases. `--version --json` deliberately retains `runtime: "bun"` and Node/Bun-style platform names as a wire-compatibility label, even when Go runs directly. `LUUNA_MISSIONS_DEBUG=1` enables a separate diagnostic JSON line on stdout for top-level errors unless a valid `LUUNA_MISSIONS_LOG_LEVEL` overrides it; leave it off when consuming a single JSON response. Go diagnostic stack text is a summary rather than a byte-for-byte Bun stack.

title: Project data and invariants
text:
## Project data and invariants

`init` creates `.luuna/missions/config.yaml`, `issues.jsonl`, `plans.jsonl`, `templates.jsonl`, and a local `.gitignore` for `*.lock`. It adds three `merge=union` lines for the JSONL files to the project's `.gitattributes`. Commands discover the nearest initialized project by walking up from the current directory; a linked Git worktree resolves its main checkout's store. The first access to a legacy `.seeds/` layout may move it to `.luuna/missions/` through `internal/config/legacy.go` and rewrite relevant `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` references. That migration refuses to merge two stores or follow a linked old/new directory; `src/legacy-layout.ts` is the reference implementation.

| File | Record or purpose | Main owners |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issues.jsonl` | One issue per line: ID, title, status, type, priority, optional assignee/description/labels/dependencies/plan links/intent/extensions, timestamps | `create`, `update`, `close`, `dep`, `label`, `block`, `unblock`, template pour, plan child operations, Beads migration |
| `plans.jsonl` | Plan ID, parent seed, template, status, revision, sections, ordered children, adopted-child subset, optional outcome/reviewer, timestamps | `plan` family; child status transitions from `update` and `close` |
| `templates.jsonl` | Named issue template with ordered steps; pouring creates a convoy of issues | `tpl` family |

title: Project data and invariants
text:
| `config.yaml` | Project name, schema version, nested plan display depth, optional custom plan templates | `init`, `config`, plan validation and prompts |

An issue has required `id`, `title`, `status`, `type`, `priority`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. Optional fields are `assignee`, `description`, `closeReason`, `closedAt`, `blocks`, `blockedBy`, `labels`, `convoy`, `plan_id`, `plan_step_index`, `requires_plan`, `discoveredFrom`, Roots `intent`, and `extensions`. Status is `open`, `in_progress`, or `closed`; type is `task`, `bug`, `feature`, or `epic`; priority is 0 (critical) through 4 (backlog). `blocks` and `blockedBy` are reciprocal issue ID relationships. `discoveredFrom` is provenance, not a blocker. Unknown record fields are preserved. A plan stores `id`, parent `seed`, `template`, `name`, lifecycle `status`, `revision`, validated `sections`, ordered `children`, optional `adoptedChildren`, `outcome`, `outcomeNote`, `reviewedBy`, and timestamps. A template stores `id`, `name`, and ordered `steps`; each step has a title and optional type, priority, and `plan_template`. Config has `project`, `version`, optional `max_plan_depth`, and optional `plan_templates`; `config schema` emits the full JSON Schema.

title: Project data and invariants
text:
Writes use advisory per-file `.lock` files, atomic replacement, and JSONL deduplication by ID. Multi-file plan operations acquire the plans lock before the issues lock. JSONL is meant to be mutated through commands, not by hand. IDs, timestamps, human output, JSON field names, and exit behavior are command contracts.

Plan status starts at `approved` after submission or adopt-only creation. A child entering progress makes the plan `active`; all children closed makes it `done`; reopening a child returns it to `active`. A `draft` stays draft, and `outcome` records an assessment without changing status. `plan show` can recurse into child plans up to `max_plan_depth` (default 3). Built-in plan templates are `feature`, `bug`, and `refactor`; custom templates in YAML may override them.

title: Full command inventory
text:
## Full command inventory

Options in the table are command-specific. `--json` is available on most data and mutation commands and yields a stable object with `success` and `command`; list/show/ready/search/blocked/stats also support `--format markdown|compact|plain|ids|json`. `--format` is not a universal option. Top-level flags are `-h/--help`, `-v/--version`, `-q/--quiet` (suppress human status output), `--verbose` (extra diagnostics where supported), and `--timing` (elapsed time on stderr after success); `--version --json` emits version metadata. A command failure returns a nonzero exit and either a JSON error object in JSON mode or an `Error:` line on stderr. Run `<command> --help` (and `<command> <subcommand> --help`) for exact argument ordering and option text.

| Environment variable | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` | Go executable used by the Bun native builder and native verification script; defaults to `go` on `PATH` |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_DEBUG=1` | Enables debug records for top-level command errors unless a valid explicit log level takes precedence |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_LOG_LEVEL` | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, or `silent`; controls those error diagnostics |
| `USER` | Default identity for `update <id> --claim` if `--as` is omitted |

text:
| Command | Use and notable options | Writes / side effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `init` | Initialize current project; `--json` | Creates data files and updates `.gitattributes` |
