title: Plan subcommands
text:
### Plan subcommands

Every plan leaf accepts `--json`; commands that take `<id>` generally accept either a plan ID or its parent seed ID. The leaf help text remains the exact option and argument reference.

| Command | Use and important options | Writes / effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan templates` | List built-in plus configured plan templates | Read only |
| `plan prompt <seed-id>` | Emit a template-shaped planning request; `--template`, `--domain`; optional Atlas prior art | Read only; optional Atlas queries |
| `plan submit <seed-id>` | Validate plan JSON via required `--plan <file|->` (stdin with `-`); `--overwrite`, `--name`, `--record-decision`, `--domain` | Writes plan, parent and child issues; optional Atlas decision write after success |
| `plan show <id>` | Show plan by plan ID or seed ID with child summaries and nested plans | Read only |
| `plan validate <id>` | Recheck stored sections against current template; emits structured diff on stderr when invalid | Read only |
| `plan outcome <id>` | Required `--result success|partial|failure`, optional `--note`; warns about open children | Updates plan assessment only |
| `plan review <id>` | Required `--by <name>`; reviewer is informational | Updates plan |
| `plan edit <id>` | `--name`, text `--section <name> <text>`, or `--step <i>` with `--title`/`--priority`/`--type`; bumps revision and propagates step metadata | Rewrites plan and possibly child issue |

title: Plan subcommands
text:
| `plan create <seed-id>` | Adopt-only approved plan with zero children; `--name`, `--template` | Writes plan and parent link |
| `plan adopt <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Attach existing open missions; optional `--step`, one of `--at`/`--before`/`--after` | Writes plan and issues; keeps seed status/type/priority |
| `plan reorder <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Require an exact permutation of existing children | Rewrites plan order only |
| `plan release <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Detach children without closing them | Rewrites plan and issues |
| `plan list` | Filter by `--seed`, `--status`, `--outcome`, `--template` | Read only |

The plan submission shape is `{ "template": "feature", "name": "optional label", "sections": { ... } }`. `plan prompt` wraps the form in a `plan_request` envelope; remove that envelope when submitting. Submit validates text/list/step shapes and step dependencies before writing. A step may spawn a child from `title` or adopt an existing child with `existing_seed`. `blocks` contains 1-based step indices, while stored `plan_step_index` is 0-based. Step `labels` are normalized and merged onto adopted children. Child descriptions carry a marked plan back-reference; releasing a child strips that marked block while preserving manual description text.

title: Typical workflow and integrations
text:
## Typical workflow and integrations

Run ticket commands from an initialized project, not from this component's own checkout. For example:

```bash
luuna-missions init
luuna-missions create --title "Add import validation" --type feature --priority P1 --json
luuna-missions ready --json
luuna-missions show <issue-id> --json
luuna-missions update <issue-id> --claim --as <agent> --json
luuna-missions close <issue-id> --reason "Verified" --json
```

1. `luuna-missions init` in a Git project, then `create --title ...` to capture work.
2. `ready --json` or `list --json` to select work. `update <id> --claim --as <agent>` claims it atomically; `close <id>` finishes it. Dependencies and plan drafts affect readiness.
3. For larger work, create a parent issue, run `plan prompt <id> --json`, fill the resulting plan template, then `plan submit <id> --plan plan.json --json`. Use `plan show`, `validate`, `edit`, `adopt`, `reorder`, `release`, `review`, and `outcome` as the work evolves.

title: Typical workflow and integrations
text:
4. `prime` emits context for agents. `setup claude` installs a SessionStart `luuna-missions prime --compact` hook and a PreToolUse `luuna-missions guard` hook with a `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` matcher. The guard reads Claude's hook JSON on stdin and emits a deny decision for direct edits to `.luuna/missions/*.jsonl`; other tools and targets pass through. `onboard` writes a marked Missions block in a project instruction file without owning the rest of that file.
5. `sync --status` or `sync --dry-run` shows Missions changes; plain `sync` stages Missions files and commits the current index. Run `git diff --cached --name-only` to inspect unrelated staged paths first. Luuna's policy and approval mechanism is outside this component.

Atlas enrichment is optional: `plan prompt` can query `luuna-atlas` for matching domain records; `plan submit --record-decision` may write an Atlas decision after the local plan is saved. Failures do not roll back the local plan. Beacon has no direct data store integration in this component. `migrate-from-beads` is an explicit import from a prior issue tracker; legacy `.seeds/` layout movement is a separate automatic compatibility path.

title: Development and evidence boundaries
text:
## Development and evidence boundaries

Supported component validation is `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` followed by `bun run verify`. That script runs `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:agents`, `bun test --timeout 30000`, `go test ./...`, a native build, and `scripts/parity.mjs --suite all --require-go`. The differential corpus runs the `smoke`, `core`, `relations`, `config`, `templates`, `misc`, and `plans` suites in temporary stores. It normalizes generated IDs, temporary paths, line endings, and timestamp milliseconds; it compares JSON semantically and ordered JSONL records by value while keeping human output, stderr, exit codes, and other files exact. The inherited `check:all` and quality-budget scripts compare against upstream maintenance and are not the supported CI contract. The GitHub workflow declares the supported `verify` surface on Linux and Windows with Bun 1.4.3 and Go from `go.mod`; a configured workflow is not proof of a completed run on every host or Go version.

title: Development and evidence boundaries
text:
For a focused differential run, use `bun scripts/parity.mjs --go <native-binary> --suite <name|all> --require-go`. The harness also accepts `--self-check` to compare the oracle with itself, `--keep` to retain its temporary fixtures, and `--oracle-entry <path>` or `MISSIONS_ORACLE_ENTRY` to select another TypeScript oracle. `MISSIONS_GO_BIN` and `MISSIONS_BUN_BIN` select executables; these `MISSIONS_*` variables configure the harness, not the public CLI. Never aim a parity run at an imported or live project store.

Current limits matter when operating or integrating this component:

- The package bins still require Bun, and a fresh checkout or package install needs a Go compiler for the first native build. No prebuilt binaries or registry release are shipped here. The cached native executable itself can run without Bun.
- The TypeScript oracle remains in the repository to check command behavior. The parity corpus covers representative success, failure, mutation, help, and output paths; it cannot prove every input or environment. Debug stack text differs from the Bun stack.
- `doctor` currently checks malformed and duplicate issue/template JSONL records; it does not perform the same integrity scan of `plans.jsonl`. `plan validate <id>` rechecks a stored plan against its current template, but is not a whole-store repair command.

title: Development and evidence boundaries
text:
- `setup claude` and `guard` cover the registered Claude hook and supported direct edit tool events. They are not Luuna runtime policy or a universal filesystem permission system. Atlas lookups and decision recording require an available `luuna-atlas` executable; Beacon has no direct store integration.
- Changes in this component do not update the consuming Luuna submodule or installer. An exact pin update, consumer smoke test, and any release or publication need a separate reviewed process. Do not load imported stores, session histories, or upstream skills as Luuna work records for validation.

Sources for this map: `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go`, `internal/cli/`, `internal/plan/`, `internal/model/`, `internal/store/`, `internal/config/`, `scripts/native-build.ts`, `scripts/verify-native.ts`, `scripts/parity.mjs`, `src/index.ts`, `src/index-legacy.ts`, `src/register-all.ts`, `src/types.ts`, `src/commands/`, `README.md`, `MIGRATION.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the consuming Luuna component manifest and Windows installer.

title: Luuna Missions development
text:
# Luuna Missions development

This component is a maintained fork of Missions, with provenance in `UPSTREAM.md` and the original MIT notice in `LICENSE`.

Use Bun 1.4.3 and Go 1.22 or newer. Put `go` on `PATH` or set `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` to its executable. From this directory:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run typecheck
bun run check:agents
bun test --timeout 30000
bun run verify
```

The live CLI is Go source under `cmd/` and `internal/`. `src/index.ts` is the Bun compatibility launcher for the package bins and Luuna's pinned entry; it builds a source-keyed native binary under ignored `dist/`. `src/index-legacy.ts` and the remaining TypeScript modules are the behavior oracle. Keep strict TypeScript for that oracle and launcher, Go formatting and module conventions for the native implementation, and stable command names, help, exit codes, JSON output, record schemas, and public types. Tests use Bun and Go with real temporary files. Test changes at the appropriate public boundary, including the differential corpus in `scripts/parity.mjs` when command behavior changes.

title: Luuna Missions development
text:
Preserve advisory locks, atomic writes, JSONL deduplication, and secret redaction. Multi-file plan and issue mutations take the plans lock before the issues lock. Do not hand-edit project JSONL. `bun run verify` is the supported component validation surface: type check, instruction check, Bun tests, Go tests, and the full TypeScript-versus-Go CLI corpus. Inherited `check:all` and quality-budget scripts remain for upstream maintenance comparison; they reference standalone upstream CI and are not the supported CI contract.

Primary executable: `luuna-missions` (`lms`; compatibility alias `lm`). This component owns Git-native tickets and structured plans. Atlas owns structured expertise and project memory; Beacon owns reusable prompts. Project data lives in .luuna/missions/ (created by `init`); environment variables use the `LUUNA_MISSIONS_` prefix. Legacy layout migration is confined to `internal/config/legacy.go` in Go and `src/legacy-layout.ts` in the TypeScript oracle. Preserve configuration keys, record schemas, and public types unless an explicit migration is designed and tested. Runtime policy and approval enforcement belong in Luuna, not in this component.

title: Luuna Missions development
text:
Do not load imported dogfooding stores, session histories, or upstream agent skills as Luuna work records. Do not create them as a development ritual. Installations must not alter the root Git hook configuration. This is an independent public repository maintained by brodynelly. Packages remain unpublished; registry publication and upstream self-upgrades require a separate reviewed release process. Luuna consumes exact Git commits through submodules; changes here do not authorize changes to Luuna runtime policy or update its pin.

Do not commit or push unless explicitly requested. Report remaining work without automatically creating issues or synchronizing component state.

title: Missions
text:
# Missions

Git-native issue tracker for AI agent workflows. Zero dependencies, JSONL storage, Bun runtime.

Replaces [beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) in the Luuna ecosystem with something purpose-built: no Dolt, no daemon, no binary DB files. The JSONL file IS the database.

title: Why
text:
## Why

Beads works but carries baggage an orchestrator does not need:

- **2.8MB binary `beads.db`** (Dolt-embedded) that can't diff or merge in git
- **286 export-state tracking files** to keep JSONL in sync with the binary DB
- **Pre-commit hook failures** (`bd sync --flush-only` is a no-op post-Dolt migration)
- **Concurrent access contention** — multiple agents fighting over `beads.db` lock
- **Dual source of truth** — binary DB + JSONL export, manually kept in sync

Orchestrators use ~7 beads operations on a simple data model. Missions covers exactly that surface.

title: Design Principles
text:
## Design Principles

1. **JSONL is the database.** No binary files, no export pipeline, no sync step. One file, diffable, mergeable.
2. **Zero runtime dependencies.** Bun built-ins only (`Bun.file`, `Bun.write`, `node:fs`, `node:crypto`).
3. **Concurrent-safe by default.** Advisory file locks + atomic writes. Multiple agents in worktrees can read/write safely.
4. **Git-native.** `merge=union` gitattribute handles parallel branch merges. No custom merge driver needed.
5. **Ecosystem fit.** Same stack as the Luuna runtime tooling (Bun/TS), same patterns as Luuna Atlas (JSONL + locks), same CLI conventions (`--json` flag on everything).

title: On-Disk Format
text:
## On-Disk Format

```
.luuna/missions/
  config.yaml          # Project config (YAML, matches Luuna Atlas convention)
  issues.jsonl         # All issues, one JSON object per line
  templates.jsonl      # Molecule/template definitions
  .gitignore           # Ignores lock files
```

title: config.yaml
text:
### config.yaml

```yaml
project: example-app
version: "1"
```

The `project` field is used as the ID prefix (e.g., `example-app-a1b2`).

YAML parsed by a minimal built-in subset parser (~50 LOC) that handles the flat key-value format missions needs. No external dependency.

title: issues.jsonl
templates.jsonl
text:
### templates.jsonl

Molecule/template definitions, one per line:

```jsonl
{"id":"tpl-a1b2","name":"scout-build-review","steps":[{"title":"Scout: {prefix}","type":"task","priority":2},{"title":"Build: {prefix}","type":"task","priority":1},{"title":"Review: {prefix}","type":"task","priority":3}]}
```

title: .gitignore
text:
### .gitignore

```
*.lock
```

title: .gitattributes (appended to project root)
text:
### .gitattributes (appended to project root)

```
.luuna/missions/issues.jsonl merge=union
.luuna/missions/templates.jsonl merge=union
```

Union merge strategy: on branch merge, git takes lines from both sides. Since each issue is one line with a unique ID, this produces correct results for parallel agent work. Duplicate lines (same issue modified on both branches) are handled by missions' dedup-on-read — last occurrence wins.

title: Data Model
text: ## Data Model

title: Issue
Template (Molecule)
Convoy (Poured Template Instance)
ID Generation
text:
### ID Generation

- Issues: `{project}-{4 random hex chars}` (e.g., `example-app-e7f3`)
- Templates: `tpl-{4 random hex chars}` (e.g., `tpl-b2c9`)
- Collision-checked against existing entries on create
- Falls back to 8 hex chars after 100 collisions (won't happen in practice)
- Matches beads' format for familiarity, eases migration

title: Status Lifecycle
text:
### Status Lifecycle

```
open ──> in_progress ──> closed
  ^          │
  └──────────┘  (reopen via update --status=open)
```

title: Priority Scale
text:
### Priority Scale

| Value | Label    | Use                        |
|-------|----------|----------------------------|
| 0     | Critical | System-breaking, drop everything |
| 1     | High     | Core functionality          |
| 2     | Medium   | Default, important but not urgent |
| 3     | Low      | Nice-to-have               |
| 4     | Backlog  | Future consideration        |

Accepts both numeric (`--priority=2`) and shorthand (`--priority=P2`).

title: CLI
text:
## CLI

Binary name: `luuna-missions` (like `bd` for beads, `luuna-atlas` for Luuna Atlas).

Every command supports `--json` for structured output. Non-JSON output is human-readable with ANSI colors (respects `NO_COLOR`).

title: Issue Commands
text:
### Issue Commands

```

luuna-missions create                              Create a new issue
  --title <text>       (required)
  --type <type>        task|bug|feature|epic (default: task)
  --priority <n>       0-4 or P0-P4 (default: 2)
  --description <text>
  --assignee <name>

luuna-missions show <id>                           Show issue details

luuna-missions list                                List issues with filters
  --status <status>    open|in_progress|closed
  --type <type>        task|bug|feature|epic
  --assignee <name>
  --limit <n>          Max results (default: 50)

luuna-missions ready                               Show open issues with no unresolved blockers

luuna-missions update <id>                         Update issue fields
  --status <status>
  --title <text>
  --priority <n>
  --assignee <name>
  --description <text>

luuna-missions close <id> [<id2> ...]              Close one or more issues
  --reason <text>      Closure summary

luuna-missions dep add <issue> <depends-on>        Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
luuna-missions dep remove <issue> <depends-on>     Remove dependency
luuna-missions dep list <issue>                    Show deps for an issue

  --status             Check for uncommitted changes without committing
```

title: Template (Molecule) Commands
text:
### Template (Molecule) Commands

```

  --name <text>        (required)      Human-readable name

luuna-missions tpl step add <template-id>          Add a step to a template
  --title <text>       (required)      Step title (supports {prefix} interpolation)
  --type <type>        task|bug|feature|epic (default: task)
  --priority <n>       0-4 (default: 2)

  --prefix <text>      Replaces {prefix} in step titles

luuna-missions tpl status <template-id>            Show convoy status (completion of poured issues)
```

title: JSON Output Format
text:
### JSON Output Format

Success:
```json
{ "success": true, "command": "create", "id": "example-app-a1b2" }
```

Error:
```json
{ "success": false, "command": "create", "error": "Title is required" }
```

List results:
```json
{ "success": true, "command": "list", "issues": [...], "count": 12 }
```

Template pour:
```json
{ "success": true, "command": "tpl pour", "ids": ["example-app-a1b2", "example-app-c3d4", "example-app-e5f6"] }
```

title: Concurrency Model
text:
## Concurrency Model

Stolen from Luuna Atlas (which handles multi-agent writes in production today).

title: Advisory File Locking
text:
### Advisory File Locking

```
Lock file:    .luuna/missions/issues.jsonl.lock
Stale after:  30 seconds
Retry:        50ms polling
Timeout:      5 seconds
```

Implementation:
1. Create lock file with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` (atomic, fails if exists)
2. If `EEXIST`: check mtime, delete if stale (>30s), retry
3. Timeout after 5s with error
4. Execute operation under lock
5. Remove lock file in `finally` block (best-effort)

title: Atomic Writes
text:
### Atomic Writes

All mutations (update, close, dep add/remove) follow this pattern:
1. Acquire lock
2. Read `issues.jsonl` into memory
3. Apply mutation
4. Write to `issues.jsonl.tmp.{random}`
5. Rename temp file over `issues.jsonl` (atomic on POSIX)
6. Release lock

Creates (appends) are simpler: acquire lock, append line, release lock.

title: Dedup on Read
text:
### Dedup on Read

After a `merge=union` git merge, `issues.jsonl` may contain duplicate lines for the same issue ID (both branches modified it). On read, missions deduplicates by ID — last occurrence wins (later line = later mutation).

This means:
- No custom merge driver needed
- Parallel branch work just works
- File may grow with duplicates between compactions
- `luuna-missions compact` (future) can remove duplicate lines when needed

title: Migration from Beads
text:
## Migration from Beads

One-time migration script: `luuna-missions migrate-from-beads`

1. Read `.beads/issues.jsonl` (the JSONL export beads already maintains)
2. Map fields: `issue_type` → `type`, `owner` → `assignee`, etc.
3. Write to `.luuna/missions/issues.jsonl`
4. Preserve original IDs (they already use `{project}-{hex}` format)

The beads JSONL export is the source — no need to touch `beads.db`.

title: Integration with orchestrators
text: ## Integration with orchestrators

title: Client Interface
text:
### Client Interface

An orchestrator can wrap missions the same way it wraps beads — via `Bun.spawn(["luuna-missions", ...])` with `--json` parsing. The `BeadsClient` interface maps 1:1:

| BeadsClient method | luuna-missions command |
|--------------------|------------|
| `ready()`          | `luuna-missions ready --json` |
| `show(id)`         | `luuna-missions show <id> --json` |
| `create(title, opts)` | `luuna-missions create --title "..." --json` |
| `claim(id)`        | `luuna-missions update <id> --status=in_progress --json` |
| `close(id, reason)` | `luuna-missions close <id> --reason "..." --json` |
| `list(opts)`       | `luuna-missions list --json` |

Rename the client file from `beads/client.ts` to `missions/client.ts`, update the spawn command, done. The `BeadIssue` → `SeedIssue` type is structurally identical.

title: Molecule Migration
text:
### Molecule Migration

| BeadsMolecule method | luuna-missions command |
|----------------------|------------|
| `createMoleculePrototype()` | `luuna-missions tpl create --name "..." --json` |
| `addStep()` | `luuna-missions tpl step add <id> --title "..." --json` |
| `pourMolecule()` | `luuna-missions tpl pour <id> --json` |
| `getConvoyStatus()` | `luuna-missions tpl status <id> --json` |
| `listPrototypes()` | `luuna-missions tpl list --json` |

title: Agent-Facing Commands
text:
### Agent-Facing Commands

Agents use the same commands they currently use with beads:

```bash

title: Builder agents
text:
# Builder agents
luuna-missions show <task-id>                    # View assigned task
luuna-missions close <task-id> --reason "..."    # Report completion

title: Lead agents
text:
# Lead agents
luuna-missions create --title="..." --type=task --priority=2
luuna-missions show <id>
luuna-missions ready
luuna-missions close <id> --reason "..."
luuna-missions sync
```

title: Hooks Integration
What Missions Does NOT Do
text:
## What Missions Does NOT Do

Explicitly out of scope (keep it minimal):

- **No daemon.** No background process, no socket, no PID files.
- **No binary database.** JSONL only. No SQLite, no Dolt.
- **No audit trail / version history.** Git IS the audit trail. Use `git log .luuna/missions/issues.jsonl`.
- **No custom merge driver.** `merge=union` handles everything. Dedup on read handles edge cases.
- **No user management.** Assignee is a free-text string. No authentication, no permissions.
- **No remote sync.** `luuna-missions sync` commits locally. `git push` handles the rest.
- **No compact command (yet).** Dedup on read is sufficient. Ship `luuna-missions compact` when file bloat becomes a real problem.

title: Tech Stack
text:
## Tech Stack

| Concern | Choice | Rationale |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| Runtime | Bun | Matches example-app, runs TS directly |
| Language | TypeScript (strict) | Matches Luuna Atlas |
| Dependencies | Zero runtime | Matches the project hard rule |
| Config | YAML (minimal built-in parser) | Matches Luuna Atlas convention |
| Storage | JSONL | Git-native, diffable, mergeable |
| Locking | Advisory file locks | Proven in Luuna Atlas for multi-agent |
| Formatting | Biome (tabs, 100 char width) | Matches the Luuna stack |
| Testing | `bun test` (colocated) | Real I/O, no mocks |
| Distribution | `bun link` locally | No npm publish for now |

### Version Management

Bump via: `bun run version:bump <major|minor|patch>`

title: CHANGELOG.md
text:
### CHANGELOG.md

[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) format:


title: /release Slash Command
text:
### /release Slash Command

`.claude/commands/release.md` — standard release workflow:

1. Analyze changes since last release (`git log`, `git diff`)
2. Determine version bump (major/minor/patch, default: patch)
3. Bump version in `package.json` and `src/index.ts`
4. Update `CHANGELOG.md` with categorized changes
5. Update `CLAUDE.md` if command counts or structure changed
6. Update `README.md` if CLI reference or stats changed
7. Present summary — do NOT commit or push

title: CI Workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
text:
### CI Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

Runs on push to main and PRs:

```yaml
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: latest
      - run: bun install
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
```

title: Missions: luuna-missions plan — Planning Facilitation
text:
# Missions: `luuna-missions plan` — Planning Facilitation

Design spec for extending missions beyond issue tracking into a structured planning layer for AI agents.

title: Thesis
text:
## Thesis

Most human and agent attention should be spent in the planning step, not the review step. Plans should be the artifact reviewed; by the time an agent is tasked with implementation, the work should be so straightforward that even a small model can execute it. When an implementation fails, the fix belongs in the planning *process* — adding a new section, validation rule, or risk check that prevents the failure mode next time — not in post-hoc code review.

`luuna-missions plan` makes planning a structured, templated, customizable workflow that lives where the work already lives: alongside the missions it produces.

title: Design Principles
text:
## Design Principles

1. **Structured data, not prose.** Plans are JSONL rows with validated fields. No markdown plan documents anywhere in the artifact path. The plan is queryable, validatable, mechanically traversable.
2. **Plans are first-class.** Plans get their own ID space and their own JSONL file, parallel to issues. They are not a field on a seed.
3. **Bidirectional linking.** Plans know their parent seed and their spawned children; missions know their plan. Navigation is cheap from either direction.
4. **Config-declared templates.** Customization mirrors Luuna Atlas's `custom_types`: declare plan templates in `.luuna/missions/config.yaml` with required/optional sections and validation. AJV schema generated from the template definition.
5. **Soft Luuna Atlas coupling.** `luuna-missions plan` works standalone. If `luuna-atlas` is on PATH, prior art (conventions, patterns, decisions, failures) is injected into the planning prompt automatically. Atlas absent → planning still works.
6. **One-shot with resume.** The LLM receives a structured prompt, produces a complete plan JSON, and submits it. Validation failure returns a patchable partial-state diff — no multi-turn state machine required.
7. **Decomposable, recursively.** A plan step may itself be another plan. Epics decompose into nested plans without context-switching to a different tool.

title: Architecture Overview
text:
## Architecture Overview

```
.luuna/missions/
  config.yaml          # adds plan_templates: block
  issues.jsonl         # unchanged shape; gains optional plan_id field
  plans.jsonl          # NEW — one plan per line
  templates.jsonl      # convoy templates (existing, untouched)
  .gitignore
```

Plans are created via `luuna-missions plan prompt <seed-id>` → LLM → `luuna-missions plan submit <seed-id>`. On successful submit, child missions are spawned with blocking edges wired and `plan_id` back-pointers populated.

title: On-Disk Format
text: ## On-Disk Format

title: config.yaml additions
text:
### config.yaml additions

```yaml
project: example-app
version: "1"

plan_templates:
  feature:
    sections:
      context:
        required: true
        kind: text
        min_length: 50
        prompt: "Why does this work need to happen? What problem or opportunity drives it?"
      approach:
        required: true
        kind: text
        prompt: "What's the chosen approach, and why this over alternatives?"
      alternatives:
        required: false
        kind: list
        item:
          name: { kind: text }
          rejected_because: { kind: text }
        prompt: "What other approaches were considered and rejected?"
      steps:
        required: true
        kind: steps
        min: 2
        prompt: "Decompose into ordered, independent implementation steps. Each becomes a child seed."
      risks:
        required: false
        kind: list
        item: text
        atlas_source: failure
        prompt: "What could go wrong? Known failure modes from prior work are pre-filled when Luuna Atlas is available."
      acceptance:
        required: true
        kind: list
        item: text
        min: 1
        prompt: "Concrete, verifiable conditions for plan completion."
```

Section field reference:

title: config.yaml additions
text:
| Field           | Purpose                                                                                             |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `required`      | Validation gate. Required sections must be non-empty on submit.                                     |
| `kind`          | One of `text`, `list`, `steps`, or a structured object spec.                                        |
| `min_length`    | For `kind: text` — minimum character count.                                                          |
| `min`           | For `kind: list` or `kind: steps` — minimum number of entries.                                       |
| `item`          | For `kind: list` — schema for each entry. Either `text` or a structured object.                      |
| `atlas_source`  | When Luuna Atlas is present, pre-populate this section's `prior_art` from records of this type.            |
| `prompt`        | The natural-language prompt the LLM sees when filling this section.                                 |

title: plans.jsonl
text:
### plans.jsonl

One plan per line, append-on-create, atomic-rewrite on update (same locking model as `issues.jsonl`).

```jsonl
{"id":"pl-a1b2","seed":"missions-9c4d","template":"feature","status":"draft","revision":1,"sections":{"context":"...","approach":"...","alternatives":[],"steps":[{"title":"Add OAuth provider config","type":"task","priority":2,"blocks":[1]},{"title":"Wire callback handler","type":"task","priority":2,"blocks":[]}],"risks":["Token refresh race condition (mx-902)"],"acceptance":["Login flow completes end-to-end","Refresh token rotates on use"]},"children":["missions-aa01","missions-aa02"],"outcome":null,"reviewedBy":null,"createdAt":"2026-05-06T10:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-05-06T10:00:00Z"}
```

Optional `adoptedChildren?: string[]` is a subset of `children` whose entries were
linked via adoption (step `existing_seed` at submit time, or `luuna-missions plan adopt`
post-submit) rather than fresh-spawned. The field is only persisted when
non-empty, so plans that never use adoption stay byte-identical to pre-feature
output. `luuna-missions plan show` renders `(adopted)` next to each entry; `luuna-missions plan submit
--overwrite` preserves entries for adopted children that survive the rewrite.

title: issues.jsonl additions
text:
### issues.jsonl additions

Two optional fields on `Issue`:

- `plan_id?: string` — the plan this seed is part of (parent seed, spawned child, or [adopted](#adoption-and-release) child).
- `plan_step_index?: number` — the 0-based index in the plan's `steps` array (set for spawned children, submit-time adoptions, and `luuna-missions plan adopt --step <i>`; absent on loose adoptions). Enables stale-child detection on plan revisions.

These are additive; existing missions remain valid. `luuna-missions plan release` clears both fields and strips the description's `missions:plan-backref` block (see [Adoption and Release](#adoption-and-release)).

title: Plan Lifecycle
text:
## Plan Lifecycle

```
draft  →  approved  →  active        →  done
              ↓             ↓
        (validation     (children
         passed,         all closed,
         children        outcome
         spawned)        appended)
```

- **draft** — created by `luuna-missions plan prompt`; not yet submitted, no children.
- **approved** — `luuna-missions plan submit` succeeded, validation passed, children spawned.
- **active** — at least one child seed is `in_progress`. Set automatically.
- **done** — all children closed. `luuna-missions plan outcome` may append a result.

Optional human review gate is **suggested, not enforced** (see Reviewer Suggestion below).

title: Command Surface
text:
## Command Surface

```
luuna-missions plan prompt   <seed-id> [--template <name>] [--domain <name>]
                                                       Print structured prompt JSON to stdout.
                                                       Embeds Luuna Atlas prior_art when Luuna Atlas is on PATH.

luuna-missions plan submit   <seed-id> --plan <file> [--overwrite]
                                                       Validate plan JSON, spawn children, write
                                                       plans.jsonl row, update parent seed.
                                                       --overwrite required to replace an existing
                                                       approved plan.

luuna-missions plan show     <pl-id>                               Display plan with sections, children, status.

luuna-missions plan list     [--seed <id>] [--status <s>]          Query plans.
                 [--outcome <r>] [--template <name>]

luuna-missions plan outcome  <pl-id> --result <success|partial|failure>
                 [--note <text>]                       Append outcome on plan close.

luuna-missions plan validate <pl-id>                               Re-run validation against current template
                                                       (useful after template config changes).

title: Command Surface
text:
luuna-missions plan templates                                      List available templates from config.

luuna-missions plan create   <seed-id> [--name <text>]             Create an adopt-only plan: zero spawned
                 [--template <name>]                   children, empty steps blueprint. Populate via
                                                       `luuna-missions plan adopt`. Rejects a pre-existing
                                                       non-draft plan for the seed.

luuna-missions plan adopt    <plan-id> <seed-id...> [--step <i>]   Adopt existing open missions into a plan
                 [--at <i> | --before <s> | --after <s>] (link-only; bumps revision). `--step` is the
                                                       1-based blueprint step index to anchor to.
                                                       --at/--before/--after (mutually exclusive)
                                                       control the children insertion position.

luuna-missions plan reorder  <plan-id> <seed-id...>                Set the exact plan.children order. The ids must
                                                       be a permutation of current children (no adds,
                                                       drops, or dupes). Bumps revision.

title: Command Surface
text:
luuna-missions plan release  <plan-id> <seed-id...>                Detach missions from a plan without closing them
                                                       (link-only; bumps revision).

luuna-missions plan edit     <id>                                  Edit plan fields in place; bumps revision.
  [--name <text>]                                      <id> accepts a plan id or seed id.
  [--section <name> <text>]                            V1: text sections only. --section approach
  [--step <i> --title/--priority/--type ...]           refreshes missions:plan-backref on all children.
                                                       --step is 1-based; metadata edits propagate to
                                                       plan.children[i-1].
```

`luuna-missions ready` is updated to surface plans-in-`draft` for the parent missions it would otherwise return — planning is the highest-priority work when present.

`luuna-missions show <seed>` and `luuna-missions list` gain awareness of `plan_id`: a seed with a plan in `draft` displays a hint, and a seed whose plan is `approved` shows the children inline.

title: Walkthrough Protocol
text:
## Walkthrough Protocol

Hybrid: one-shot with resume on validation failure.

title: Successful path
text:
### Successful path

```bash
$ luuna-missions plan prompt missions-9c4d --template feature > plan.json

title: stdout is the structured prompt: sections, prompts, validation rules,
text: # stdout is the structured prompt: sections, prompts, validation rules,

title: and priorart populated from Luuna Atlas where atlassource matched.
text: # and prior_art populated from Luuna Atlas where atlas_source matched.

title: LLM fills plan.json with answers under sections.
text:
# LLM fills plan.json with answers under sections.

$ luuna-missions plan submit missions-9c4d --plan plan.json
✓ plan pl-a1b2 created (status: approved)
✓ spawned 4 child missions: missions-aa01, missions-aa02, missions-aa03, missions-aa04
✓ missions-9c4d now blocked by 4 children
```

title: Validation-failure path
text:
### Validation-failure path

```bash
$ luuna-missions plan submit missions-9c4d --plan plan.json
✗ validation failed:
  - sections.risks: required, missing
  - sections.steps: must have >=2 entries (got 1)

title: stderr emits a partial-state JSON the LLM patches and resubmits:
text: # stderr emits a partial-state JSON the LLM patches and resubmits:

title: "errors": [
text: #   "errors": [

title: { "path": "sections.risks", "code": "required", "fix": "add a 'risks' array (string entries)" },
text: #     { "path": "sections.risks", "code": "required", "fix": "add a 'risks' array (string entries)" },

title: { "path": "sections.steps", "code": "min", "fix": "add at least 1 more step entry" }
text: #     { "path": "sections.steps", "code": "min", "fix": "add at least 1 more step entry" }

title: "current": { ...plan-as-submitted... }
text: #   "current": { ...plan-as-submitted... }

title: LLM patches plan.json and re-submits.
text:
# LLM patches plan.json and re-submits.
```

The LLM never has to re-run `luuna-missions plan prompt`; the failure response carries enough state to patch and retry.

title: Prompt JSON shape (emitted by luuna-missions plan prompt)
Submission JSON shape (consumed by luuna-missions plan submit)
Plan Templates (Customization)
text:
## Plan Templates (Customization)

Templates are declared in `.luuna/missions/config.yaml` under `plan_templates:`. Each template names a set of sections and validation rules. Templates ship with missions (built-in defaults loaded if not redeclared) and can be overridden or extended per project.

title: Built-in templates
text:
### Built-in templates

| Template   | Use case                                                              |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature`  | New capability or significant change. Default for `type: feature`.    |
| `bug`      | Defect fix. Adds `reproduction` and `root_cause` sections.            |
| `refactor` | Internal restructuring. Adds `behavior_invariant` (must stay equal). |

`luuna-missions plan prompt <seed-id>` infers the template from the seed's `type` if `--template` is not passed.

title: Section kind reference
text:
### Section `kind` reference

| Kind          | Shape                              | Notes                                                       |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`        | string                             | `min_length` optional.                                      |
| `list`        | array                              | `item: text` or `item: { ...object spec... }`. `min` opt.   |
| `steps`       | array of step objects              | Spawns child missions 1:1. Step is `{title?, type, priority, blocks: [step_index], labels?: string[], plan_template?, existing_seed?}`. `blocks` uses 1-based step indices. `labels` is optional; values are normalized (lowercased, trimmed, deduped) and applied to the spawned child or merged additively into an adopted seed's existing labels (never clobbers). `existing_seed` adopts an already-open seed instead of spawning a fresh child (see [Adoption and Release](#adoption-and-release)). `title` is required for fresh-spawn steps and optional for adoption-only steps (where the adopted seed's title is preserved). |
| object spec   | nested record of named fields      | Each field has its own `kind` recursively.                  |

A custom template:

title: Section kind reference
text:
```yaml
plan_templates:
  spike:
    sections:
      hypothesis:
        required: true
        kind: text
        prompt: "What are we trying to learn?"
      timebox:
        required: true
        kind: text
        prompt: "Hard upper bound (hours/days)."
      success_signal:
        required: true
        kind: list
        item: text
        prompt: "What observable signals tell us the spike succeeded?"
      kill_signal:
        required: true
        kind: list
        item: text
        prompt: "What signals tell us to stop and abandon?"
      steps:
        required: false
        kind: steps
        prompt: "Optional: tasks if the spike confirms the hypothesis."
```

Validation is generated from the template config the same way Luuna Atlas generates AJV schemas from `custom_types`.

title: Default feature Template
text:
## Default `feature` Template

Six sections:

1. **context** *(required, text)* — Why the work matters.
2. **approach** *(required, text)* — Chosen approach with rationale.
3. **alternatives** *(optional, list)* — Considered + rejected.
4. **steps** *(required, steps, min 2)* — Decomposition; each becomes a child seed.
5. **risks** *(optional, list, atlas_source: failure)* — Known failure modes.
6. **acceptance** *(required, list, min 1)* — Verifiable completion conditions.

`out_of_scope` and `open_questions` are deliberately omitted from the default. They are workflow-specific and easy to add via custom templates.

title: Nested Plans
text:
## Nested Plans

A step in `kind: steps` may declare `plan_template: <name>` to mark itself as a sub-plan. On submit, the spawned child seed is created with `requires_plan: true`. Calling `luuna-missions plan prompt <child-seed-id>` then walks the LLM through the sub-plan using the named template. This decomposes epics in-place without context switching.

```json
{
  "title": "OAuth integration",
  "type": "epic",
  "priority": 1,
  "plan_template": "feature"
}
```

Bidirectional linking is preserved: the sub-plan's `seed` field points at the spawned child; the spawned child's `plan_id` points at the sub-plan once created. `luuna-missions plan show <pl-id>` recursively displays nested plans up to a configurable depth (default 3).

A child seed marked `requires_plan: true` is excluded from `luuna-missions ready` until its sub-plan reaches `approved`. This guarantees no implementation begins on un-planned epic branches.

title: Atlas Integration (Soft)
text:
## Atlas Integration (Soft)

When `luuna-atlas` is resolvable on PATH, `luuna-missions plan prompt` enriches the prompt JSON with prior art:

1. **Domain inference** — explicit `--domain` flag → seed labels matching declared Luuna Atlas domains → directory anchors derived from `git diff --name-only` against the seed's referenced files.
2. **Per-section enrichment** — for any section with a `atlas_source: <type>` hint (or for sections matching well-known names: `approach` ↔ pattern + decision; `risks` ↔ failure; `acceptance` ↔ guide), missions shells out to `luuna-atlas query --domain <name> --type <type> --json --limit 5` (or calls the programmatic API exported from `luuna-atlas/src/api.ts`).
3. **Embedding** — top-N records become `prior_art` entries on the section: `[{id, type, summary, relevance}]`. The LLM is instructed to ground its answer in these entries when relevant.

Atlas absent → `prior_art` arrays are empty, validation rules are unaffected, planning still works.

title: Optional outbound write
text:
### Optional outbound write

`luuna-missions plan submit --record-decision` (off by default) calls `luuna-atlas record <inferred-domain> --type decision --rationale <approach> --evidence-missions <plan-id>` on success. This back-fills the chosen approach as a Luuna Atlas decision linked to the plan. Defaults to off so missions remains standalone.

title: Validation
text:
## Validation

AJV schema is generated from each template's section spec. Validation runs on `luuna-missions plan submit` and is re-runnable via `luuna-missions plan validate <pl-id>` (e.g., after editing the template config).

Validation covers:

- Required sections are present and non-empty.
- `min_length` on `text` sections.
- `min` on `list` and `steps` sections.
- `steps[].blocks` references valid **1-based** step indices in the range `1..steps.length` (step 1 is the first step). `0` and out-of-range values are rejected with a clear "step indices are 1-based" error; self-references (step `n` listing `n` in its own `blocks`) are also rejected.
- `steps[].existing_seed`, when present, is a non-empty string (AJV check). Existence, status, current-plan, parent-self, mutual exclusion with `plan_template`, and duplicate-across-steps checks run in a pre-write pass alongside the spawn pipeline — see [Adoption and Release](#adoption-and-release).
- Each step declares either `title` (fresh spawn) or `existing_seed` (adoption). A step with both is allowed; the supplied `title` is used only for the mismatch warning. A step with neither is rejected (`step N must declare either 'title' (fresh spawn) or 'existing_seed' (adoption)`). This lets synthesis-style plans — where every child is an adoption — omit titles entirely.
- Object-spec fields match their declared `kind`.
- `template` name resolves in `plan_templates`.

title: Validation
text: Validation failure emits the partial-state diff described in Walkthrough Protocol.

title: Re-submission and Overwrite
text:
## Re-submission and Overwrite

Re-submitting a plan for a seed that already has a non-`draft` plan is rejected by default:

```bash
$ luuna-missions plan submit missions-9c4d --plan plan.json
✗ plan pl-a1b2 already exists for missions-9c4d (status: approved, revision: 1)
  Use --overwrite to replace it. Spawned children will not be auto-closed;
  obsolete steps from the previous revision will be flagged.
```

With `--overwrite`:

1. The existing `plans.jsonl` row is replaced atomically. `revision` is incremented.
2. The new `steps` are diffed against the previous `children` with this precedence:
   1. **`step.existing_seed` id** — matches a current plan-child (rename / reorder pin) or pulls in an external adoption.
   2. **`step.title`** — legacy fallback against any unmatched current plan-children.
   3. **Spawn fresh** — no match either way.

title: Re-submission and Overwrite
text:
Id-first precedence keeps adopted children stable across overwrites and prevents the title-match path from racing with an id-pinned step. Pre-existing overwrite-by-title behavior is unchanged when no step uses `existing_seed`.
3. Children whose corresponding step is gone are listed in stderr as **obsolete** with a suggestion to close them: `luuna-missions close missions-aa03 --reason "obsoleted by plan pl-a1b2 revision 2"`. Missions does not auto-close them — the LLM has the context to decide whether the existing work is still useful.
4. New steps spawn new child missions; existing matching children are kept (their backref block is refreshed in place so the snippet stays in sync with the live plan).
5. `plan.adoptedChildren` is reconciled: prior entries that survive the rewrite are kept, freshly-adopted ids are appended, and the field is dropped if it becomes empty.

Plan revisions are not preserved as separate rows. Git history of `plans.jsonl` is the audit trail. This keeps storage simple and avoids ID-space inflation.

title: Adoption and Release
text:
## Adoption and Release

Adoption links an already-open seed into a plan instead of spawning a fresh child; release is the inverse. Both are **link-only** — they never mutate the seed's `status`, `assignee`, `labels`, `priority`, `type`, or `title`. The plan and seed JSONL rows are updated, edges are wired (or unwired), the `missions:plan-backref` block in `description` is applied (or stripped), and the plan's `revision` is bumped once per command call.

Three surfaces stage adoptions and releases:

1. **Submit-time adoption** — a step in the submitted plan JSON carries `existing_seed: "<seed-id>"`. The named seed is linked into the plan at that step index instead of spawning a new child.
2. **`luuna-missions plan adopt <plan-id> <seed-id...> [--step <i>]`** — post-submit adoption. `--step` is the 1-based blueprint step index to anchor to; omit it for a loose adoption (the seed gets no `plan_step_index` and its backref reads `Adopted into plan <pl-id>` instead of `Step N of plan <pl-id>`).
3. **`luuna-missions plan release <plan-id> <seed-id...>`** — detach without closing. The seed remains open and queryable; only its plan link goes away.

title: Lifecycle
text:
### Lifecycle

Adoption on a fresh-submit or via `luuna-missions plan adopt`:

- `seed.plan_id` ← `<plan-id>`
- `seed.plan_step_index` ← step index (0-based; omitted on loose adoptions)
- `seed.description` ← `applyPlanBackref(...)` — prepends the marker-delimited block, or replaces an existing block in place (manual notes wrapping the markers survive)
- `seed.blocks` ← `appendUnique(seed.blocks, parentSeed.id)`
- `parentSeed.blockedBy` ← gains the adopted seed (deduped)
- `plan.children` ← appends the adopted seed (deduped)
- `plan.adoptedChildren` ← appends the adopted seed (deduped)
- `plan.revision` ← `prev + 1` (single bump per command)

Release inverts each mutation:

- `seed.plan_id` and `seed.plan_step_index` ← cleared (JSON.stringify drops the fields)
- `seed.description` ← `stripPlanBackref(...)` — removes only the marker block, collapses whitespace at the new boundary, returns `undefined` when nothing remained so the field is dropped entirely
- `seed.blocks` ← drops `parentSeed.id` (returns the same array when no change)
- `parentSeed.blockedBy` ← drops the released seed
- `plan.children` ← drops the released seed
- `plan.adoptedChildren` ← drops the released seed; the field is removed from the plan row when it becomes empty
- `plan.revision` ← `prev + 1`

title: Lifecycle
text: `luuna-missions plan show` renders adopted entries with a trailing `(adopted)` muted tag in human output; `--json` includes `adopted: true` on each child summary that's listed in `plan.adoptedChildren`.

title: Adopt-only plans and ordering (luuna-missions plan create, luuna-missions plan reorder, positional adopt)
text:
### Adopt-only plans and ordering (`luuna-missions plan create`, `luuna-missions plan reorder`, positional adopt)

The "release train" use case (missions-3dd1) assembles a set of already-existing missions into a single plan, in a controlled order, ending with a release step — with no spawned or placeholder children. Three additions support it:

- **`luuna-missions plan create <seed-id>`** writes a plan row with `children: []`, `sections: { steps: [] }`, `status: "approved"`, `revision: 1`, and links the parent seed (`seed.plan_id ← <pl-id>`). No children means no `blockedBy` edges yet — those land as missions are adopted. `--name` sets the human label (defaults to the seed title); `--template` overrides the seed-type default. A pre-existing non-draft plan for the seed is rejected (exit non-zero) — adopt into the existing plan instead. Because the steps blueprint is empty, `luuna-missions plan validate` will report missing required sections for the chosen template; this is expected for adopt-only plans and does not affect downstream plan runners, which consume `plan.children`.

title: Adopt-only plans and ordering (luuna-missions plan create, luuna-missions plan reorder, positional adopt)
text:
- **`luuna-missions plan adopt` positioning** — `--at <i>` inserts the adopted batch at a 1-based slot in `plan.children` (valid range `1..len+1`); `--before <seed>` / `--after <seed>` anchor on an existing child id. The three are mutually exclusive; omitting all appends (prior behavior). The adopted ids are inserted as a contiguous block preserving command-line order. Positioning is orthogonal to `--step` (which sets `plan_step_index`); both may be supplied.

- **`luuna-missions plan reorder <plan-id> <seed-id...>`** sets the exact `plan.children` order in one call. The supplied ids must be a permutation of the current children — every child listed exactly once, no extras, no duplicates (use `adopt`/`release` to change membership). Only the plan row's `children` array order changes; seed link state (`plan_id`, `plan_step_index`, `blockedBy` edges) is untouched. Revision bumps once. Lock: `plans.jsonl` only (no issue mutation). downstream plan runners read `plan.children` order verbatim (`seq = index + 1`), so `reorder` is the surface for pinning a release seed last.

`luuna-missions plan create` and `luuna-missions plan reorder` accept a `pl-*` id or the parent seed id wherever a plan id is expected, consistent with the rest of the planning surface.

title: Validation (pre-write, fail-fast)
text:
### Validation (pre-write, fail-fast)

All candidates are resolved before any mutation. Any rejection aborts the command with both `plans.jsonl` and `issues.jsonl` untouched.

**Adoption rejections:**

| Condition                                                            | Error                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `existing_seed` not found                                            | `seed <id> not found`                                                                            |
| `existing_seed` is closed                                            | `seed <id> is closed; only open or in-progress missions can be adopted`                             |
| `existing_seed` already attached to another plan                     | `seed <id> is already attached to plan <pl-id>` (overwrite path allows same-plan adoptions)      |
| `existing_seed` equals the parent seed of the plan                   | `cannot adopt the parent seed <id> into its own plan <pl-id>`                                    |
| Same `existing_seed` listed by two steps in one submit / two CLI args | `existing_seed <id> is already adopted by an earlier step in this plan` / `Duplicate seed id…`   |

title: Validation (pre-write, fail-fast)
text:
| Step sets both `existing_seed` and `plan_template`                   | `existing_seed and plan_template are mutually exclusive`                                          |
| `--step <i>` (adopt) out of range against `plan.sections.steps`      | `--step <i> is out of range (plan <pl-id> has N steps)`                                          |

**Title mismatch warning** — when `seed.title !== step.title` on a submit-time adoption, a `⚠` warning goes to stderr and the seed's title is preserved. Adoption is not silently retitling; agents must reconcile manually if the mismatch is meaningful.

**Release rejections:**

| Condition                                          | Error                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Seed not found                                     | `seed <id> not found`                                              |
| Seed has no plan or is attached to a different one | `seed <id> is not attached to plan <pl-id>` / `…attached to <px>`  |
| Seed equals the parent of the plan                 | `cannot release the parent seed <id> from its own plan <pl-id>`   |
| Duplicate seed ids in args                         | `Duplicate seed id(s) in args: <id>…`                              |

title: Concurrency: lock order
text:
### Concurrency: lock order

Both `luuna-missions plan adopt` and `luuna-missions plan release` follow the global missions convention: **outer lock = `plans.jsonl`, inner lock = `issues.jsonl`** (`mx-f29e43`). Same order as `luuna-missions plan submit`, `luuna-missions plan outcome`, and `luuna-missions plan review` so the lock graph has no cycles. All mutations across both files commit under the combined lock, and a single revision bump per command is guaranteed.

title: Edge cases
text:
### Edge cases

- **Reassignment from another plan is out of scope.** A seed with a non-matching `plan_id` is rejected with a clear error; the caller must `luuna-missions plan release <other-pl> <seed>` first, then adopt. A future `--reassign-from <pl>` flag could collapse the two-step dance into one atomic command (deferred).
- **Loose adoption** (`luuna-missions plan adopt` without `--step`) is intentional: pulling related ad-hoc work into a plan rarely lines up with a specific blueprint step. The backref block reflects this — agents reading the seed see `Adopted into plan <pl-id>` rather than a misleading step anchor.
- **Adopting an in-progress seed** is allowed and intentional. Adoption is link-only; an agent already working the seed keeps working it, now with the plan framing surfaced in `luuna-missions show <seed>` and the plan now blocked by their progress.
- **Manual notes around the backref block survive release.** The `missions:plan-backref:start/end` markers are the only thing `stripPlanBackref` touches; string-based search/replace is explicitly avoided.
- **JSONL byte stability.** `plan.adoptedChildren` is only persisted when non-empty, and is dropped from the row when release empties it. Plans that never use adoption produce the same `plans.jsonl` bytes as before the feature shipped.

title: In-Place Editing (luuna-missions plan edit)
text:
## In-Place Editing (`luuna-missions plan edit`) `luuna-missions plan edit` performs targeted, field-level edits without going through the full `luuna-missions plan submit --overwrite` ceremony. It's the planning analog of `luuna-missions update` for issues. ```bash luuna-missions plan edit [--name ] [--section ] [--step [--title ] [--priority

] [--type ]] [--json] ``` - `` accepts a plan id (`pl-*`) or the parent seed id (resolved via the same `resolvePlanIdArg` used by `luuna-missions plan show`). - All flags compose atomically in one invocation. `plan.revision` is bumped exactly once and `plan.updatedAt` is refreshed regardless of how many fields changed. - Lock order matches the rest of the planning surface: outer `plans.jsonl`, inner `issues.jsonl` (mx-f29e43). Both files are touched under the combined lock so combined edits stay atomic. - Out-of-scope by design: **structural edits** — adding, removing, or reordering steps — still require `luuna-missions plan submit --overwrite`. The edit command never spawns or orphans children and never renumbers `step.blocks`.

title: --name
text:
### `--name <text>`

Replaces `plan.name`. Empty string is rejected. No child missions are touched.

title: --section
text:
### `--section <name> <text>`

Replaces `plan.sections[name]` with the supplied text. V1 supports text sections only (no `list` / `steps` / object-spec kinds); the name must resolve in the template's section spec.

`--section approach` is special-cased: after the section is written, the `missions:plan-backref` block on every entry in `plan.children` is refreshed (`applyPlanBackref`) so the snippet rendered in each child seed's description stays in sync with the live approach. Other sections do not touch children.

title: --step [--title ] [--priority ] [--type ]
text:
### `--step [--title ] [--priority

] [--type ]` `--step` is the **1-based** blueprint step index (matching `step.blocks` and `luuna-missions plan adopt --step `). At least one of `--title` / `--priority` / `--type` must be provided alongside `--step`; conversely, those metadata flags are only meaningful with `--step`. Edits mutate `plan.sections.steps[i-1]` in place and propagate to the child seed at `plan.children[i-1]`: - `--title` updates both the blueprint step's `title` and the child seed's `title`. - `--priority` accepts `0-4` or `P0-P4` (same parser as `luuna-missions update --priority`) and updates the child seed's `priority`. The blueprint step's `priority` is also updated for consistency. - `--type` is validated against `VALID_TYPES` (`task | bug | feature | epic`) and updates the child seed's `type`. Out-of-range `--step` (less than 1 or greater than `plan.sections.steps.length`) is rejected pre-write with a clear error; both JSONL files stay untouched. Adopted children are edited just like spawned ones — the lookup is purely by index. If a step has no corresponding entry in `plan.children` (shouldn't happen on a healthy plan), the command rejects.

title: Concurrency and atomicity
text:
### Concurrency and atomicity

The combined locks acquired by `luuna-missions plan edit` are the same outer/inner pair as `luuna-missions plan submit`, `luuna-missions plan outcome`, `luuna-missions plan review`, `luuna-missions plan adopt`, and `luuna-missions plan release`. Concurrent `luuna-missions plan edit` from multiple agents serializes through the advisory lock model; last-write-wins on the JSONL contents.

title: Outcomes
text:
## Outcomes

Plans gain a lightweight outcome field:

```bash
$ luuna-missions plan outcome pl-a1b2 --result success
$ luuna-missions plan outcome pl-a1b2 --result failure --note "auth provider library deprecated mid-implementation"
```

Outcome values: `success | partial | failure`. Aggregation, retros, template-evolution-from-failures are deliberately out of scope — those workflows are team-specific. Outcomes are stored so external tooling (or future missions commands) can build on them.

title: Reviewer Suggestion (Not Required)
text:
## Reviewer Suggestion (Not Required)

Human review of plans is suggested but not gated:

- `luuna-missions plan submit` transitions `draft → approved` automatically on successful validation.
- `luuna-missions plan show` displays a "review suggested" hint when `reviewedBy` is null.
- `luuna-missions plan review <pl-id> --by <name>` populates `reviewedBy`. This is informational, not a state transition.
- Teams that want a hard gate can wrap `luuna-missions plan submit` in a hook or CI check that blocks the spawned children's `ready` state on a `plan-reviewed` label.

The default optimizes for autonomous swarms; opt-in rigor for teams that need it.

title: Out of Scope (V1)
text:
## Out of Scope (V1)

- **Markdown plan documents.** Plans are structured data, not prose.
- **Failure-feedback automation.** Plans don't auto-evolve templates from outcomes; that's workflow-specific and defers to teams.
- **Beacon integration.** Planning prompts are not stored as Luuna Beacon templates in V1.
- **Plan diffing UI.** Git diff of `plans.jsonl` is the V1 review surface.
- **Cross-repo plans.** A plan lives in one `.luuna/missions/` instance; multi-repo coordination is out of scope.
- **Real-time collaboration.** Same locking model as issues — atomic writes, last-write-wins on conflicts.

title: Open Implementation Questions
text:
## Open Implementation Questions

1. **Section schema vs. `custom_types` reuse.** Should `plan_templates` reuse Luuna Atlas's `custom_types` AJV-schema-generation code (extract into a shared package), or maintain a parallel implementation in missions? Sharing reduces drift; keeping them separate keeps missions dependency-free.
2. **Step ID stability.** `--overwrite` diffing by step title is fragile. Should templates be able to declare stable `step_id` keys that survive title edits, at the cost of more author burden?
3. **Atlas query interface.** Shell out to `luuna-atlas query --json` (works today, language-agnostic) vs. import from `@luuna/atlas-cli` programmatically (faster, tighter coupling, requires npm dep). Soft coupling argues for the shell route.
4. **Default template inference.** Inferring template from seed `type` is convenient but couples the type taxonomy to template names. Should the mapping be configurable, or hard-coded to `task→feature, bug→bug, feature→feature, epic→feature` (with `--template` always overriding)?
5. **Sub-plan depth.** Recursive nested plans risk runaway decomposition. Should there be a configurable `max_plan_depth` in `config.yaml` (default 3)?

title: Open Implementation Questions
text: 6. **Children lifecycle when parent plan moves to `done`.** If a plan is marked `done` but children are still open, is that a validation error, a warning, or allowed? Recommend: warning, not error, so plans can be retroactively closed without forcing child cleanup first.

title: Native release: quick reference
text:
# Native release: quick reference

This page summarizes the native release tooling. [RELEASING.md](/docs/components-missions-docs-releasing) has the full details and the owner gates. Nothing here publishes anything: there is no tag, GitHub Release, npm publish, signing or attestation.

title: Artifacts
text:
## Artifacts

- **Package:** `@luuna/missions-cli` (unpublished). The binary prints `internal_version` `0.6.0`, the upstream compatibility baseline taken from `package.json`.
- **Archive:** `luuna-missions_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` for `darwin|linux` × `arm64|amd64`. It holds exactly `bin/luuna-missions` and `bin/lms`. `lms` is a byte-identical copy. Both entries are mode 0755 with owner `0:0`. The aliases `lm`/`missions` stay Bun package bins only.
- **Fixed UTC mtime:** 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z (`946684800`), so the archive bytes do not depend on the builder's time zone.
- **Files next to the archive:** `LICENSE`, `UPSTREAM.md`, `provenance.json` and `SHA256SUMS`. `SHA256SUMS` covers the archive, `provenance.json`, `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`.
- **Provenance:** `provenance.json` is self-reported metadata, not an attestation. It records the commit, ref, `source_tree_dirty`, run id, runner, Go version, build flags, the archive SHA256, `archive_version` and `internal_version`. Values it cannot determine are JSON `null` rather than guesses.

title: Commands (host platform)
text:
## Commands (host platform)

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./...
sh scripts/release/test-release-scripts.sh   # offline; stub fixtures and stub go
out=$(mktemp -d)
a=$(sh scripts/release/package.sh --version 0.0.0-local --out "$out")
sh scripts/release/check-archive.sh --require-run "$a"
```

`check-archive.sh` validates the name, `SHA256SUMS` and the entry listing before it extracts anything. On the host it then runs `--help`/`--version` through both names and requires identical output. Cross-built targets are checked without being executed. `--require-run` makes that a failure (exit 6). `--require-run` with `--no-run` is a usage error (exit 2). A `SHA256SUMS` problem exits 4.

title: Workflow (manual artifacts only)
text:
## Workflow (manual artifacts only)

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch` with a `version` input. It has `contents: read` and four host-native runners: `macos-14`, `macos-15-intel`, `ubuntu-latest` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. Each job runs Go tests → release-script tests → `package.sh` → `check-archive.sh --require-run` → `actions/upload-artifact` (14-day retention). The attestation step is commented out. Downloading the artifacts, signing and releasing are owner gates.

title: Clean-checkout validation fix
text:
## Clean-checkout validation fix

`AGENTS.md` mentions `dist/`, which is ignored and exists only after a native build. On a fresh clone, `bun run check:agents` (and therefore `bun run verify`) failed with ``referenced path `dist` does not exist``. `check:agents` now passes `--known-missing dist`. `.gitignore` adds `.tac/tools/` next to `.tac/runs/`. No validator logic, placeholder files or `.gitkeep` files were added.

title: Local Bun
text:
## Local Bun

Release builds do not need Bun. For component validation, use the repo-local Bun 1.4.3 in the ignored `.tac/tools/bin/` rather than a global install:

```sh
PATH="$PWD/.tac/tools/bin:$PATH" bun run verify
```

title: Verification limits
text:
## Verification limits

- A local run proves only the host platform. Other targets are claimed only after their native runner (or the owner, on that platform) executes `check-archive.sh --require-run`.
- Linux binaries are static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). musl/Alpine is not claimed. Windows is out of scope.
- macOS binaries are unsigned. Gatekeeper may quarantine them after a browser download.
- The workflow's Go version comes from the `go 1.22` minimum in `go.mod`. Check the exact version in `provenance.json`.

title: Releasing native Luuna Missions archives
text:
# Releasing native Luuna Missions archives

Nothing in this repository publishes anything. The scripts below build and verify archives. The workflow uploads them only as GitHub Actions workflow artifacts. Packages, GitHub Releases, tags, signing and attestations are deliberate owner actions.

title: What an archive contains
text:
## What an archive contains

Each archive is `luuna-missions_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`, where `os` is `darwin` or `linux` and `arch` is `arm64` or `amd64`. It contains exactly two entries:

- `bin/luuna-missions`
- `bin/lms`

Both are regular files with mode 0755, owner `0:0` and a fixed mtime of 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z (`946684800`), set in UTC so the archive bytes do not depend on the builder's time zone. There is no directory entry. The compatibility aliases `lm` and `missions` are deliberately excluded from public archives, but they remain Bun package bins for source use. `lms` is a byte-identical copy of the primary: `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go` passes `os.Args[1:]` and never inspects argv[0], so behavior and arguments are identical under either name. The help text always says `luuna-missions`.

These files sit next to the archive:

title: What an archive contains
text:
- `LICENSE` (the upstream MIT notice) and `UPSTREAM.md` (provenance). The archive's entry allow-list is strict, so attribution ships next to the archive instead of inside it.
- `SHA256SUMS` lists the archive, `provenance.json`, `LICENSE` and `UPSTREAM.md`.
- `provenance.json` is self-reported metadata. It records repository, commit, ref, `source_tree_dirty` (source-tree dirtiness, including untracked non-ignored files; `null` when unknown), workflow run id, runner, Go version, build env/flags/ldflags, the archive SHA256, and two separate versions:
  - `archive_version`: the `--version` you pass, used in the file name.
  - `internal_version`: the version the binary prints for `--version`. It comes from `package.json`, today the `0.6.0` upstream compatibility baseline, and is injected through the existing symbol `github.com/brodynelly/luuna-missions/internal/cli.CurrentVersion`, the same one `scripts/native-build.ts` sets.

  Outside a Git work tree, `commit`, `ref` (unless `GITHUB_REF` is set) and `source_tree_dirty` are JSON `null`; an unknown Go version is also `null`. `provenance.json` is not an attestation.

title: Local dry run (host platform)
text:
## Local dry run (host platform)

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./...
sh scripts/release/test-release-scripts.sh          # offline, stub fixtures and a stub go; needs git
out=$(mktemp -d)
a=$(sh scripts/release/package.sh --version 0.0.0-local --out "$out")
sh scripts/release/check-archive.sh --require-run "$a"
```

- `package.sh` defaults to the host `--os`/`--arch`. It can cross-build the other Go targets with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. In that case `check-archive.sh` verifies entries and checksums but does not execute the binaries, and says so. `--require-run` turns that into a failure (exit 6); combining it with `--no-run` is a usage error (exit 2).
- `package.sh` writes the tar stream to a temporary file and gzips it in a separate step, so a failure of either command fails the run. On any failure it removes the files it wrote to `--out`, and removes `--out` itself if the run created it.
- `package.sh` sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` unless you override it, so it never downloads a Go toolchain.
- The first build may download the `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` module into the Go module cache.
- Use `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` to choose a Go executable.
- `bun run check:agents` treats the ignored `dist/` build output as known-missing, so it passes on a fresh checkout; a local Bun for validation may live in the ignored `.tac/tools/`.

`check-archive.sh` checks these, in order, before it lists or extracts anything (exit 4 on any `SHA256SUMS` problem):

title: Local dry run (host platform)
text:
1. The name pattern.
2. The mandatory `SHA256SUMS`, which must be a regular file, not a symlink, with exactly one matching entry. The entry may use the `*` binary-mode prefix, and its digest must be 64 lowercase hex digits equal to the archive's SHA256.

It then checks the listing:

3. The exact entry set, with no links, directories, devices, absolute or `..` paths, and mode 0755 on every entry.

It then extracts into a private temp dir. On the host platform it runs `--help` and `--version` through both names and requires identical output.

title: Workflow
text:
## Workflow

`.github/workflows/release.yml` has these properties:

- **Trigger:** `workflow_dispatch` with a `version` input only. There is no tag trigger.
- **Permissions:** `contents: read`.
- **Runner matrix:** host-native, one job per target:

  | Runner | Target |
  | --- | --- |
  | `macos-14` | darwin/arm64 |
  | `macos-15-intel` | darwin/amd64 |
  | `ubuntu-latest` | linux/amd64 |
  | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` | linux/arm64 |

  The parent plan named `macos-13`, which GitHub has retired. `macos-15-intel` replaces it.
- **Steps:** Go tests → release-script tests → `package.sh` → `check-archive.sh --require-run` (fails if the binaries were not executed on the runner) → `actions/upload-artifact`.
- **Not included:** `gh release`, `npm publish` and registry steps. The attestation step is present but commented out.
- **Toolchain:** `actions/setup-go` resolves `go-version-file: go.mod`, whose `go 1.22` directive is a minimum, not an exact pin. `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` stops a second toolchain download. Record the exact Go version from `provenance.json`. Exact pinning (for example `go-version: 1.27.x`) is an owner decision.

Bun is not needed for release builds. The existing `bun run verify` CI is unchanged.

title: Deferred owner gates
text:
## Deferred owner gates

1. Run `release.yml` through `workflow_dispatch` and download the four artifacts.
2. On each claimed platform, verify `SHA256SUMS`, re-run `check-archive.sh` and review `provenance.json`.
3. Decide on Apple signing/notarization and on GitHub attestations (uncomment the attest step and add `id-token: write`/`attestations: write`).
4. Choose a distinct Luuna release version (see `UPSTREAM.md`), then create the tag and GitHub Release and upload the assets.
5. Add the hub manifest row (`luuna-ai-os/releases/<v>/manifest.tsv`) through a reviewed PR in that repository.

npm publication of `@luuna/missions-cli` remains separate and unpublished.

title: Limits
text:
## Limits

- A local run proves only the host platform.
- Linux binaries are static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). musl/Alpine is not claimed.
- Unsigned macOS binaries downloaded through a browser may be quarantined by Gatekeeper.
- Windows archives are out of scope.

text:

title: Security Policy
text: # Security Policy

title: Supported Versions
text:
## Supported Versions

| Version | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| 0.2.x   | Yes       |
| < 0.2   | No        |

Only the latest release on the current major version line receives security updates.

title: Reporting a Vulnerability
text:
## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue for security vulnerabilities.**

Please report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/security/advisories).

1. Go to the [Security Advisories page](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/security/advisories)
2. Click **"New draft security advisory"**
3. Fill in a description of the vulnerability, including steps to reproduce if possible

title: Response Timeline
text:
### Response Timeline

- **Acknowledgment**: Within 48 hours of your report
- **Initial assessment**: Within 7 days
- **Fix or mitigation**: Within 30 days for confirmed vulnerabilities

We will keep you informed of progress throughout the process.

title: Scope
text:
## Scope

Missions is a CLI tool that reads and writes files on the local filesystem. The following are considered security issues:

- **Command injection** -- Unsanitized input passed to shell execution
- **Path traversal** -- Accessing files outside the intended `.luuna/missions/` directory
- **Arbitrary file access** -- Reading or writing files the user did not intend
- **Symlink attacks** -- Following symlinks to unintended locations
- **Temp file races** -- TOCTOU vulnerabilities in temporary file handling

The following are generally **not** in scope:

- Denial of service via large input files (Missions is a local tool, not a service)
- Issues that require the attacker to already have local shell access with the same privileges as the user
- Social engineering or phishing

title: Security Measures
text:
## Security Measures

Missions already implements several hardening measures:

- Atomic writes via temp file + rename to prevent partial/corrupt files
- Advisory file locking to prevent concurrent write corruption
- Input validation on all issue fields

title: Development commands
text:
# Development commands

Commands are reproduced from package manifests. Run each from the named package directory. Review a script before executing it; release and publishing scripts require their own intentional release process.

title: @luuna/desktop
text:
## @luuna/desktop

Directory: `apps/desktop`
