title: fixtures/domain/README.md
text:
# fixtures/domain/README.md

These are deterministic M0 contract fixtures, not executable work authorizations.
`manifest.json` pairs each schema with a valid and invalid document for
`node scripts/check-contracts.mjs`. Invalid fixtures cover absent required checks,
zero approval revisions, unknown assignment fields, mutable commit references,
contradictory review verdicts, and publication without a PR URL.

Rust tests additionally enforce cross-record rules JSON Schema cannot establish:
task DAGs and repository scope, exact plan hashes, stale approval rejection,
immutable stored revisions, workflow-to-plan binding, independent review, and
candidate changes invalidating evidence. SQLite integration tests exercise atomic
state/event rollback, concurrent sequences and interruption after reopening.

`luuna-json-v1` hashes UTF-8 JSON with object keys recursively sorted, no
insignificant whitespace, JSON integer/string encodings, and array order
preserved. Only the top-level `hash` property is omitted. Paths are explicit
relative strings, Unicode is preserved, and no lossy normalization occurs.
The complete plan includes project/ticket revision, base commits, optional repair
candidate identity, repository/path/operation permissions, tasks, recipes,
execution profiles and budgets. Changes require a fresh hash and approval.

title: fixtures/domain/README.md
text:
The M1 research-run lifecycle is separate from feature execution. Even a durable,
current approval cannot enter `implementing` until M2 adds observed baseline
evidence. This fixture suite does not claim that a real baseline executor,
publication gate, or multi-repository scheduler has been implemented.

title: Pi protocol corpus
text:
# Pi protocol corpus

The supported adapter baseline is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.3.0`.
Read that installed package's `docs/rpc.md`, `docs/rpc-commands.md`, and
`docs/json.md` when changing the adapter. `agent_end` ends one low-level run;
`agent_settled` finishes all automatic retries and follow-up work. A prompt
response only acknowledges acceptance.

`mock_pi.py` is an explicitly synthetic subprocess fixture. It exercises LF
framing, Unicode separators, acceptance versus completion, unknown events,
rejected commands, provider errors, recovery, crashes, malformed records,
response correlation, and cancellation without network or credentials. It is
never a genuine model run or evidence of provider compatibility. Writer
scenarios are named by `fixture:<name>` markers that tests place in the
acceptance criteria; the reviewer branch answers `fixture:review_*` markers
with a structured verdict. The `repair_in_scope` writer only repairs when its
prompt quotes the failing check output, so the runtime's repair feedback
contract is exercised rather than assumed. `review_malformed_once` answers a
candidate's first validation generation with malformed text and every later
generation with a valid pass, so a fresh validation generation after an
invalid review can be exercised against one immutable ticket.
`review_no_findings` returns `changes_required` without a finding (invalid

title: Pi protocol corpus
text:
review output), `review_tools` emits read, search and refused tool calls whose
patterns and results must never be recorded, and `review_report` passes with
evidence strings that describe the diff and scope it was given. `review_retry` emits a transient provider error that Pi retries itself (the errored `message_end`, `agent_end` with `willRetry`, then the passing review) and `review_stream` streams forty cumulative-usage updates before its verdict. The `write_compaction` writer reports a threshold compaction whose summary usage only `compaction_end` carries, and `write_unpriced` reports tokens with a zero cost, as Pi does for a model without pricing.

As Pi 1.3.0 does, the fixture reads `--system-prompt` from the named file when
it exists; writer `fixture_args` report the prompt's size and whether it came
from a file. The `large_session` writer and the `large_agent_end`,
`large_agent_end_error`, `malformed_large_agent_end` and `oversized_unknown`
demo prompts emit records over 1 MiB, as Pi's `turn_end` and `agent_end` do
after many file reads. Launcher flags select startup behaviour:
`--stall-stdin` stops reading commands, `--fail-startup` prints a diagnostic
(with synthetic credentials to be redacted) to stderr and exits 1, and
`--require-isolated-version` answers `--version` only when the probe runs with
a private `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.

title: Pi protocol corpus
text:
The real compatibility probe is `cargo run -p luuna-engine-pi --example probe`.
Set `LUUNA_PI_COMMAND` to the installed `pi` executable, or to Node and provide
`LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON='["/absolute/path/to/pi/dist/cli.js"]'`. The probe enforces
the version and performs real `get_state`, `get_available_models`, and `abort`
RPC commands without requiring provider credentials. A separately configured
runtime run is required to validate genuine model streaming and cancellation.

title: Security policy
text:
# Security policy

Luuna is an early development project. No released version currently has a supported security maintenance window. Do not use the foundation as a production trust boundary or assume that agent tools are sandboxed.

title: Report a vulnerability privately
text:
## Report a vulnerability privately

Use this repository's GitHub **Security → Report a vulnerability** option when private vulnerability reporting is enabled. Otherwise contact the repository owner through an established private channel to arrange disclosure. Do not put credentials, exploitable details, private transcripts, or affected users' data in a public issue. A public issue may request a private reporting channel without disclosing the vulnerability.

Include the affected revision, reproduction steps using synthetic data, expected and actual behavior, and impact. Remove secrets and personal information from logs before sharing. Do not test against other users' systems or provider accounts.

title: Credentials and repository hygiene
text:
## Credentials and repository hygiene

Store provider/GitHub credentials in private user configuration or secure environment bindings. Never commit real `.env` files, session histories, credential files, private memory, or transcripts. Ignore rules do not remove already tracked data or erase Git history.

If a credential is exposed, revoke or rotate it first, review use, and coordinate any necessary history remediation separately. Removing a file in a later commit does not remove earlier copies, forks, caches, or downloaded artifacts. Secret scanning reduces risk but cannot establish that no secret has ever existed.

title: Runtime boundaries
text:
## Runtime boundaries

The runtime must authenticate local API actions, bind to loopback by default, validate exact approvals, restrict artifact access, supervise owned children, and record interrupted execution. A desktop connection or model response is not authorization. Native process execution has host permissions; stronger isolation requires an explicitly implemented operating-system or container boundary.

Treat repository instructions, imported tool records, agent output, and memory as untrusted inputs. Preserve upstream license notices and review imported development artifacts before using them as model context. Required validation, independent review, publication reconciliation, and developer-controlled merging must not be bypassed to recover from a failure.

Pi remains an external pinned dependency, not a rewritten or bundled agent engine.

title: Component workflows in Luuna
text:
# Component workflows in Luuna

The application uses the pinned public luuna-missions, luuna-atlas and luuna-beacon sources through runtime adapters. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md) for authority and recovery rules.

title: Use the application
text:
## Use the application

1. After a fresh checkout, run `npm ci` and `npm run components:setup`. Build the runtime with `cargo build --locked -p luuna-runtime`, then start or restart that build. The application reports unavailable tools rather than substituting another ticket or memory authority.
2. Open a registered project and select **Enable components**. This explicitly creates private managed component stores and migrates existing tickets while preserving their IDs. Retry the same activation after an interrupted migration. The runtime blocks project mutations while activation is incomplete.
3. Create a ticket in the existing workflow panel. Its source is Missions. After an external CLI edit, refresh its source status and reconcile the displayed expected revision before making a new plan. Old approvals do not transfer to a changed ticket revision.
4. In the component panel, create project/process memory with explicit provenance, search it, and select only the records needed by this task. User memory remains excluded until the user-memory option is enabled and a record is explicitly selected. Delete requires the displayed source hash.
5. Create or preview a Beacon prompt. Updating its name uses the current expected version. Preview and select the current rendered version for the plan.

title: Use the application
text:
6. Create a plan. Review the full immutable plan, including selected memory content/provenance and prompt body. Approve its exact hash before implementation. The runtime checks the source again at approval, implementation, repair and validation/review boundaries. A changed or deleted selected resource requires a new plan and approval.

Deleting memory removes its Atlas source from active retrieval and invalidates selected references. Existing immutable plans and private operation history retain their audit snapshots; complete retention/erasure policy remains a full-v1 obligation.

Existing projects stay on the clearly labelled temporary ticket source until activated. No personal component store, imported task history, Pi configuration or unrelated memory is automatically loaded into a worker. The private source workspace is shown in component status; direct CLI work must use that workspace explicitly.

title: Current API
text:
## Current API

All routes are authenticated under `/api/v1`.

| Method and route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET/POST /projects/{id}/components` | Inspect or explicitly activate/migrate the managed stores. |
| `GET /projects/{id}/memory?include_user=true&q=...` | Search bound records; `include_user` defaults to false. |
| `POST /projects/{id}/memory` | `{idempotency_key, scope, content, provenance}`; scope is project/process/user. |
| `DELETE /projects/{id}/memory/{id}?expected_hash=...` | Optimistic, idempotent deletion; source changes refuse deletion. |
| `GET/POST /projects/{id}/prompts` | List or create/update `{idempotency_key, name, body, expected_version?}`. Missing/zero expected version creates; positive version updates. |
| `GET /projects/{id}/prompts/{name}/render?version=N` | Current-version preview with rendered body and canonical resource hash. Stale versions are refused. |
| `GET /tickets/{id}/source` | Observe source identity/revision and reconciliation need. Ticket GET/list retains the last reconciled projection. |
| `POST /tickets/{id}/reconcile` | `{expected_revision}`; source changes advance the projection and stale old plans. |

title: Current API
text:
Plan creation accepts optional `component_context: {memory_ids: string[], prompt?: {name,version,hash}}`. The resulting plan stores exact approved snapshots as `component_context: {memory: [{id,scope,hash,content,provenance}], prompt: {name,version,hash,body} | null}`. At most sixteen memories and 16,000 encoded bytes of combined resources are accepted. Omitting the optional field preserves older canonical plan hashes.

Operation keys persist across uncertain responses; retries with a different payload are refused. Missing source identity after an attempted create is reported for reconciliation rather than blindly repeated. Prompt source records, inherited sources and configured schemas contribute to the hash; schemas must validate without warnings. External CLI writes cannot be made atomic with a SQLite transaction, so later boundaries recheck source freshness.

title: Reproduce focused verification
text:
## Reproduce focused verification

```
cargo test --locked -p luuna-components --test real -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib missions_real_ -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib components_real_ -- --ignored --nocapture
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime <fresh-runtime-binary> --browser <chromium-or-edge> --out <new-test-directory>
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --native <bundled-desktop-executable> --runtime <fresh-runtime-binary> --runtime-label <build-identity> --out <new-test-directory>
```

The smoke uses disposable Git repositories, private component stores, free loopback ports and its own token. Browser mode uses a test-owned proxy. Windows native mode loads the bundled Tauri frontend in WebView2 and exercises production CORS directly. Native mode first verifies automatic connection to the existing local service, then disconnects and selects the isolated fixture service; it repeats this after reload. It requires a configured local development service but makes no provider calls. It closes only its own test window and verifies that the independent fixture runtime survives before authenticated shutdown. Both modes exercise actual component CLIs and real Git/check commands while using explicitly synthetic Pi writer/reviewer sessions. Fixture screenshots contain synthetic data. See [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md#runtime-component-workflows-octobe

title: Current verification and Windows development startup
text:
## Current verification and Windows development startup

The [recorded Windows browser run](evidence/component-workflows-2026-10-21.json) passed all 23 assertions with actual pinned component CLIs and synthetic Pi writer/reviewer sessions. The final Rust workspace passed 196 tests, plus separate real-component suites. The final runtime subsequently passed [27 native component workflow checks](evidence/native-component-workflows-2026-10-21.json), [46 bundled native lifecycle/recovery checks](evidence/native-lifecycle-2026-10-21.json) and [17 automatic native startup checks](evidence/native-startup-2026-10-21.json). These exercise the actual Tauri WebView2 frontend; synthetic Pi sessions remain explicitly synthetic.

The earlier Application Control block and rollback are retained in the historical evidence. The user explicitly chose unsigned development and turned Smart App Control Off in Windows Security; the observed policy state changed from 1 to 0. The exact previously blocked final runtime was then installed and started successfully. Its SHA-256 is `99d9521784bc373237ef4d65b3bdd6189f3290faf557fad2946705f39d890256`. All three existing saved runs, the token, data directory and encrypted provider bytes were preserved. Project activation has not been forced in personal data. Signed distribution and broader platform/provider acceptance remain separate requirements.

title: Current Luuna architecture
text:
# Current Luuna architecture

Windows native development startup invokes a fixed local bootstrap command,
starts or authenticates/reuses the independent runtime and connects without
manual token entry. DPAPI records live in `%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\credentials`;
existing encrypted LocalAppData records migrate once without deleting them.
Tokens reach the view through local IPC and stay in memory. Closing the window
leaves the service running. See [ADR 0011](decisions/0011-windows-native-bootstrap.md)
for the command boundary, reconciliation and checkout-based distribution limits.

Date: 2026-10-16, updated 2026-10-17 for M2a, M2b, M2c and the M3 implementation, and 2026-10-21 for re-validation after a review that left no verdict, shutdown interruption, client hardening the desktop design system and explicit component runtime workflows. Status: authoritative foundation baseline; implementation evidence is required for each milestone.

title: Purpose and precedence
text:
## Purpose and precedence

Luuna is a local-first development workbench for one developer working across related repositories. Its runtime coordinates scoped Pi sessions, exact-plan approval, actual checks, independent review, durable evidence, and eventually linked pull requests. The developer decides when to merge.

For new work, apply the following order:

1. Explicit current user requirements and repository-wide safety/security rules.
2. This document and accepted records in `docs/decisions/`; a later accepted decision must update this summary.
3. `docs/02-requirements.md` for full-v1 functional requirements not explicitly revised here.
4. The desktop/Pi RPC proposal for detailed design rationale.
5. The numbered design chapters, complete reference reading copies, diagrams, and examples as historical material.

README and AI-START-HERE are entry points, not alternative specifications. Existing source and tests show implemented behavior; they do not silently override a requirement. When an implementation differs, record the gap or an explicit decision.

title: Delivery and boundaries
text:
## Delivery and boundaries

Runtime I/O isolation and bounded session history follow
[ADR 0015](decisions/0015-bounded-runtime-and-history.md): synchronous transactions
run under bounded blocking admission, SSE reads in pages, and the desktop keeps
a bounded live event window with on-demand historical navigation. Check progress
is lossy display data; private artifacts and durable runtime events remain the
evidence. Windows check processes join owned Job Objects before execution.

The initial client is Tauri 2 with React and TypeScript. An independent Rust service uses Tokio, an authenticated Axum API, and local SQLite persistence. Pi RPC subprocesses execute agent assignments. A client cannot directly authorize tools or decide that validation succeeded.

```text
Tauri/React client ── authenticated HTTP + resumable SSE ── Rust runtime
                                                          ├── SQLite + private artifacts
                                                          ├── supervised Pi RPC workers
                                                          ├── Git/worktree ownership
                                                          ├── deterministic check executor
                                                          └── versioned external adapters
```

title: Delivery and boundaries
text:
Desktop-first is a sequencing decision. Browser/TUI capability parity, multiple related repositories, scoped memory, and Mac/Windows support remain full-v1 obligations. They are not exit criteria for the first single-repository foundation demo. No hosted service, mandatory NAS, GPU, automatic merge, custom agent loop, or full IDE replacement is required.

The desktop client's presentation follows one token-based design system ([ADR 0013](decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md), [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)): six outcome tones mapped from the API unions, where only passed evidence is green and interruption is never failure, both colour schemes and WCAG AA enforced by tests. It changes how runtime state is shown, never what the runtime decides.

Client parity (R02, A33) follows one capability catalog ([ADR 0020](decisions/0020-capability-catalog-and-tui.md)): `schemas/capability-catalog.json` lists every product action with its runtime route, `@luuna/api-client` method, desktop control marker and TUI command; `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` validates it against the runtime's served routes and the typed client. The failure explanations (`packages/api-client/src/failures.ts`) are shared by the desktop and the terminal client `packages/tui` (`luuna-tui`, interactive menus and a scriptable non-interactive mode, SSE event following with resumption, hidden token entry, full-hash approval acknowledgment). Parity evidence: the

title: Delivery and boundaries
text:
TUI command test, the desktop marker test and `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs`. Actions still arriving from M4/M5/M7 join the catalog as they land.

The workspace should add crates when they contain a real contract or implementation: domain, storage, runtime/API, engine/Pi, Git, executor, validation, and external adapters. Shared frontend packages are created when an actual shared consumer needs them. Empty placeholders do not establish implementation progress.

title: Runtime ownership
text:
## Runtime ownership

Only the Rust runtime may enforce state transitions, immutable plan hashes, approval scope, execution permissions, task dependencies, limits, retries, candidate identity, check evidence, review acceptance, and publication gates. Agents provide proposals and worker output. Deterministic runtime code produces authoritative domain events.

An approval binds to the complete canonical executable plan, its revision and hash, repository scope, base commits, check recipes, resource profiles, and budgets. Feature implementation requires a valid approval and a passing baseline. New code, rebases, dependency changes, and manual edits invalidate affected evidence. Review and publication refer to exact candidates; model text saying “passed” is never command evidence. The desktop displays the entire immutable plan and full hash and requires acknowledgment before enabling approval. Managed Git checkout, status, staging and commit disable configured clean, smudge and process filters with per-command overrides; these operations do not authorize repository-configured commands.

Native execution uses host permissions. Stronger isolation requires an explicitly configured execution profile with actual operating-system or container boundaries. Preserve developer changes and only clean up resources whose Luuna ownership is verified.

title: Persistence and ticket authority
text:
## Persistence and ticket authority

SQLite owns Luuna projects, immutable plan revisions, approvals, run/attempt lifecycle, sequenced events, check/review evidence, artifact references, and publication reconciliation. State mutation and emitted durable domain events must be committed consistently. Sensitive transcripts and provider data remain private artifacts with controlled access and retention.

The schema is versioned and append-only. At startup the runtime refuses a database that fails SQLite's quick check or was written by a newer schema, before writing anything to it. It applies only missing migrations, after an automatic pre-migration snapshot under `<data>/backups/`. `luuna-runtime backup` takes a consistent online snapshot. `luuna-runtime restore` needs the runtime stopped, verifies the snapshot, and moves the current database and its `-wal`/`-shm` aside before installing it. `luuna-runtime check` reports integrity and schema version. A snapshot covers the database only; artifacts and worktrees are files, so a complete backup is the data directory copied after an orderly stop. Startup recovery skips records it cannot decode, logs them by table and ID, and still settles their state where it can. See [ADR 0016](decisions/0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md).

title: Persistence and ticket authority
text: Baselines are runs: `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines` executes a repository's confirmed required recipes through the supervised executor and records `CheckResult` evidence bound to the manifest hash, exact commit and tree, and an environment fingerprint, with private hashed artifacts. `Implementing` is entered only through the transactional gate that re-checks the approval, the current manifest and a passed matching baseline per repository; see [ADR 0007](decisions/0007-baseline-executor.md). One baseline per repository runs at a time. Every check's process group is recorded; whatever a check leaves running is terminated before its result is recorded, and startup recovery terminates verified survivors of checks a hard-killed runtime left behind (Windows checks run in kill-on-close job objects). Missing tools or dependencies and checks cut short by the workflow budget are blocked infrastructure, never failures a repair is asked to fix (ADR 0007 amendment, 2026-10-21).

title: Persistence and ticket authority
text: Projects are registered from existing repositories. The confirmed **project manifest** (`schemas/project.schema.json`, hashed with `luuna-json-v1`) is machine-independent and append-only by revision; the **machine registry** maps each repository ID to its local path and the identity observed at registration (the redacted configured remote plus the root commits reachable from HEAD). A later observation must show an equivalent remote and contain those roots; only an explicit, evented rebind changes a binding. A checkout is registered once and never overlaps the runtime data directory. Discovery proposals and project-scoped events (`project.registered`, `repository.registered`, `repository.rebound`, `discovery.proposed`, `manifest.confirmed`) are durable, and replaying the project stream reconstructs the confirmed map. Inspection never writes to a repository or executes its text, including filters configured in submodules; see [ADR 0006](decisions/0006-repository-import.md).

title: Persistence and ticket authority
text: Discovery also probes the host once per proposal (`Discovery.host_capabilities`: each profile tool resolved on `PATH` and asked only for its version) and annotates every proposed check with `capability: available | missing` and its missing tools, raising a `missing-tool` question rather than dropping the recipe; a confirmed check whose tool is absent is recorded `blocked`, never `failed`. Every advertised profile (Node, React, Next.js, TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, Flutter, native Android, native iOS) proposes real recipes; iOS and Android device recipes carry capabilities (`xcode`, `android-device`) this host cannot satisfy and say so. New projects are created only through a hashed `ScaffoldProposal` (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose`: files, baseline recipes, generator and network steps, tool probes, `ready | blocked`) that the developer confirms by exact hash (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold`): the runtime writes the files, commits, runs the baseline recipe through the supervised executor as a real check, registers the project and records `project.scaffolded`; a failing baseline is returned as such and never reported passing. Android and iOS scaffolds are blocked proposals naming their platform generators. See [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md); capable-runner evidence for Go, Flutter, Android and iOS remains open.

title: Persistence and ticket authority
text: Legacy projects retain the explicitly temporary SQLite ticket source until component activation. `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/components` durably initializes the private component workspace and migrates tickets while preserving IDs and numeric revisions. Enabled projects use Missions (Seeds-derived) as authority for ticket intent, acceptance criteria, status, dependencies and source fingerprints; SQLite stores its revision-aware projection and Luuna execution state. GET/list return the last reconciled projection; `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/source` reports actual source freshness and `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/reconcile` requires the expected projection revision. External edits advance the reconciled revision and invalidate stale plans; freshness, ticket readiness and dependencies are rechecked at runtime work/evidence boundaries. Missing components fail closed. There are never two independently writable authorities for these fields. See [ADR 0003](decisions/0003-ticket-authority.md) and [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md).

title: Pi and maintained components
text:
## Pi and maintained components

Pi is the agent engine, not the scheduler or validation authority. The engine contract supervises process creation, assignments, followups, events, stop requests, inspection, and disposal. Use a tested pinned release, strict JSONL framing, command correlation, bounded buffers, timeouts, and owned child-process cleanup. Stderr is diagnostic data. Prompt acceptance and agent settlement are separate events. Persist attempts so interrupted processes cannot become successful runs after restart.

Luuna maintains three branded CLI distributions: **Missions** (`@luuna/missions-cli`, Seeds-derived), **Atlas** (`@luuna/atlas-cli`, Mulch-derived), and **Beacon** (`@luuna/beacon-cli`, Canopy-derived). They live under `components/missions`, `components/atlas`, and `components/beacon` as separate package and integration boundaries. Preserve compatible underlying APIs/data formats, upstream copyright and MIT notices. Prefer adapters over rewrites or direct SQLite access to their records.

title: Pi and maintained components
text:
The owner resumed extraction on October 21, 2026 and explicitly authorized public component repositories. Missions, Atlas and Beacon now live in `brodynelly/luuna-missions`, `brodynelly/luuna-atlas` and `brodynelly/luuna-beacon`; Luuna stays private and consumes exact-commit Git submodules at the existing components paths. The manifest and gitlinks bind dependency identity; setup uses frozen Bun locks without lifecycle scripts, and consumer smoke checks exercise real CLI/JSON operations. Each destination owns its CI and source; registry packages remain private and unpublished. See [ADR 0012](decisions/0012-independent-component-repositories.md), superseding ADR 0002's hosted-extraction deferral.

The runtime now invokes these pinned CLIs through `luuna-components` with bounded input/output, a fixed stdin bridge, isolated HOME/config, sanitized environment, source/toolchain verification and owned process cleanup. Explicit per-project activation uses `<data_dir>/components/projects/<id>`; explicit user memory uses `<data_dir>/components/user`. It never adopts developer or imported stores. Atlas memory exposes explicit scope and provenance; Beacon exposes versioned prompt preview/update. A user selects resources for a plan, whose canonical optional `component_context` contains their exact snapshots, identities and hashes. The runtime rejects changed selected sources at approval and execution/evidence boundaries and gives worker

title: Pi and maintained components
text: s only approved bounded content. Durable intent ledgers reconcile uncertain component writes before retry. Imported development metadata is not runtime data or permission to load instructions into agents. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md) for activation, ticket reconciliation, resource selection and native-process limits. Memory promotion widens scope one step at a time (`process -> project -> user`) through `POST …/memory/{id}/promote` with the displayed hash, creating the wider record with provenance naming its origin and deleting the narrower one under the same intent ledger; `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/export` returns the manifest, ticket projections, project and process memory and current prompts, and is refused outright when it would carry user memory, a credential value or a path of this host ([ADR 0021](decisions/0021-memory-promotion-and-project-export.md)). Import of an export, retention policy and supported-platform evidence remain obligations.

title: Candidate validation and review
text:
## Candidate validation and review

Migration 5 stores exact candidate commit/tree identities, append-only validation generations and structured independent reviews. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` names the expected hash and optionally `auto_repair`; it executes the approved required recipes inside the owned candidate worktree and starts a fresh read-only Pi reviewer only after the checks pass. Checks and reviews cannot be reused across candidate revisions or interrupted generations. A `failed` candidate whose required checks all passed in its current generation and whose reviewer left no verdict (invalid or self-inconsistent output, a refused session) may re-enter validation in place as generation `n+1`: same revision, approval and budgets, fresh checks and a fresh reviewer, no writer attempt; `GET …/candidate` reports that decision as `revalidate_allowed`. `GET …/candidate` and `GET …/diff` expose authoritative evidence and exact diffs; `POST …/repair` rechecks current approval, baseline/host and remaining aggregate budgets before creating the next scoped candidate. Model output never supplies command evidence. Repair writers receive the previous candidate's reason, check records, review and a bounded tail of each failed check log, never the private artifact paths. See [ADR 0009](decisions/0009-candidate-validation-review.md).

title: Candidate validation and review
text:
Since the second 2026-10-21 amendment to ADR 0009, every validation generation starts from the candidate tree alone: the owned worktree is verified and its untracked and ignored paths are removed and recorded. Content drift fails the candidate with a reason naming the change and the next step and is never re-validated in place. Review diffs ignore attributes that hide changes and are bounded with every changed path listed; a non-passing review must name a finding; reviewer tool calls are recorded by tool and path. `GET …/candidate` reports `validate_allowed` and `decision_reasons` from the gates the routes apply.

Automatic repair is opt-in and bounded by both the immutable plan and project repair policy. Infrastructure errors stop without repeated edits. Interrupted check and review stages retain elapsed usage up to their last durable heartbeat; a reviewer interrupted after its durable prompt marker, and every interrupted writer, reserve unknown spend and require re-planning when headroom is exhausted. Clients see aggregate workflow usage against the plan budgets and cumulative per-ticket usage, including spend the provider reported without a price. Review success is evidence for an exact candidate only; publication and human-controlled merge remain separate gates.

title: Multi-repository coordination
text:
## Multi-repository coordination

A plan may carry several tasks, each on a distinct registered repository, with `depends_on` naming the tasks that must complete first; the contract refuses self, unknown, duplicate and cyclic dependencies by name, and bounds `budgets.max_workers` to the task count and the runtime's four-run limit. Discovery proposes `package` relationships between registered repositories from `package.json` dependencies, `Cargo.toml` path dependencies and `go.mod` replace directives with evidence and `confirmed: false`; confirming a manifest that still lists an unconfirmed relationship is refused, and confirmed relationships must be acyclic. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` on such a plan runs the task graph: after the same gates as one writer (with one environment fingerprint per repository), tasks whose dependencies completed run concurrently up to `max_workers`, never two writers in one repository, each as a writer attempt in its own owned worktree, with every completed producer bound into the consumer's writer environment and prompt as `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_<REPOSITORY>_PATH`/`…_COMMIT`. Per-task state is durable (migration 10, `GET …/tasks`, `task.*` events); a dependency's failure blocks its dependents with the reason, cancellation records every task, a restart marks running tasks interrupted and keeps completed commits and worktrees, and `implement` with `task_id` resumes a failed, blocked or interrupted

title: Multi-repository coordination
text: task under the original approval within the approved budgets (an attempt lost mid-prompt still reserves the remaining cost budget, so re-planning follows as for one writer). When every task completed, one candidate set freezes every repository's exact commit and the `<consumer>:<producer>` bindings; validation runs every repository's required recipes in its own candidate worktree with the same bindings, binds results to exact commits, fails the set naming the repository and recipe (`integration blocked`) when a consumer check fails, and gives the fresh reviewer one bounded combined diff. Repair of a multi-repository set is re-planning. See [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md); delegated roles (P42) and dependency overrides (P44) remain open.

title: Publication and host diagnostics
text:
## Publication and host diagnostics

A `reviewed` candidate with a `passed` review may be published (`POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publish` with the exact hash and an idempotency key) to GitHub only, by the repository's registered identity: the runtime pushes each repository's exact candidate commit to `luuna/<ticket>/<hash prefix>` and opens one pull request per repository against the manifest's default branch, linking them when there are several. Every external write is preceded by a durable intent (migration 11: `publications`, `publication_intents`) and looked up by its stable identity first (`git ls-remote` for the branch, the pull-request head for the PR), so a timeout after remote success, a partial publication and a replayed key never duplicate anything; `POST …/publication/reconcile` retries only steps the ledger does not show succeeded. `GET …/publication` refreshes CI (check runs and commit status) and merge observation under bounded timeouts; a failing CI is reported distinctly and changes no evidence, and `integrated` is set only when every pull request is observed merged by a person. There is no merge route or call; a test asserts it. The GitHub token (`LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN`) reaches Git only through scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` headers and the REST client as a bearer header; only its presence is ever reported. Events: `publication.requested`, `publication.pushed`, `publication.pr_opened`, `publication.failed`, `publication.rec

title: Publication and host diagnostics
text: onciled`, `publication.integrated`. `luuna-runtime doctor [--json]` reports Git, Python, Node, the pinned Pi probe, the data directory and database, token and credential presence by name, the service port and the component toolchain, exiting 1 when a required item is missing. See [ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md); every publication test runs against a fake GitHub API and a local bare remote, so real GitHub evidence remains M7 exit work. `scripts/package-windows.ps1` builds an unsigned NSIS development installer carrying the desktop, the release runtime, the Windows helper scripts and the pinned Pi tree; the native bootstrap of ADR 0011 prefers that packaged layout when it is present beside the executable.

title: API and service lifetime
text:
## API and service lifetime

All application routes use `/api/v1`. Implemented project routes are `POST /api/v1/projects` (register existing repositories by absolute root path), `GET /api/v1/projects[/{id}]`, `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/discover` (read-only proposal), `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/manifest` (confirm with `expected_revision`), `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repositories/{repository_id}/rebind` (explicitly re-point a moved or re-identified checkout) and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events`. The canonical create-ticket route is **`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`** (implemented in M2c with an idempotency key; enabled projects use the Missions authority of ADRs 0003/0014). Do not add a parallel `POST /api/v1/tickets` alias. Other operations address ticket, plan, and run identities: `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans` records the next immutable plan revision and opens its workflow run, `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/approvals` approves one exact hash, `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` schedules the writer after transactional revalidation, and `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/worktrees` and `/attempts` expose the Luuna-owned worktree leases and attempts (ADR 0008). Commands that can create work require idempotency; operations sensitive to stale state require expected revisions. SSE streams use durable event IDs/cursors for replay and deduplication. Artifacts use authorized IDs, never arbitrary request-supplied filesystem paths.

title: API and service lifetime
text: Bind the development service to loopback and authenticate protected API actions. A development launch may use an explicitly managed foreground process. The desktop reconnects to that service; closing a window or losing SSE does not decide run lifetime. Explicit shutdown stops or reconciles owned workers and persists interruption: since 2026-10-21 work stopped by Ctrl+C or SIGTERM is recorded `interrupted` (resumable after restart), never `cancelled`, and the client shows a lost runtime as an outage, reconnects by itself and reloads authoritative state when the runtime answers again. A Tauri child/sidecar alone does not prove independent lifetime. Platform-specific startup, supervision, token storage, and shutdown must be tested before distribution. See [ADR 0004](decisions/0004-service-lifecycle.md).

title: Milestone evidence
text:
## Milestone evidence

Windows orderly service stop is `POST /api/v1/shutdown`, authenticated with the
existing bearer token. The runtime closes scheduling admission, drains admitted
mutation handlers, interrupts owned work and exits cleanly; window closure is
still only a client disconnect. Windows scripts reuse the DPAPI-encrypted token
and data directory across restart. See [ADR 0010](decisions/0010-authenticated-service-shutdown.md).

The initial tool-free connectivity slice exposes authenticated run creation/history, cursor event replay and SSE, and cancellation. M2a adds read-only repository import, discovery proposals and confirmed manifest revisions; M2b adds supervised baselines with bound evidence; M2c adds temporary local tickets, immutable plan revisions, exact-hash approvals, Luuna-owned worktree leases and one scoped writer whose candidate waits in `validating`. M3 adds candidate-bound required checks, a fresh read-only reviewer, structured findings, optional bounded automatic repairs and conservative restart recovery; its genuine-provider exit is closed on Linux (see the status report) while native Mac/Windows lifecycle evidence remains open. The bounded M6 component slice adds explicit Missions migration/reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon plan resources. Publication, broader M6 parity and supported-platform exits remain separate capabilities.

text:
| Milestone | Required proof | Does not establish completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0 | Locked build, schema fixtures, deterministic approval/transition rejection, durable state checks | Folder creation or documentation checks alone |
| M1 | Real pinned Pi/provider session, streamed API events, persistence, cancellation, error handling and restart evidence | Scripted worker or fixture-only protocol tests |
| M2a | Real and synthetic imports with byte-identical checkouts, rejected invalid/mismatched repositories, proposed (not executed) recipes, confirmed manifest replay after restart | A proposed manifest, a stored recipe, or any claim that a baseline ran |
| M2b | Genuine passing and failing baselines with commit/tree/environment-bound results and hashed artifacts; missing executable, empty suite, dirty checkout, deadline, cancellation and restart recorded as blocked/failed/cancelled/interrupted; stale baseline cannot enter implementation | A writer, a worktree, or any run that modifies a repository |

title: Milestone evidence
text:
| M2c | One approved fixture feature changed only its Luuna-owned worktree with the developer checkout byte-identical; missing or stale approval, changed base, changed recipe, unrelated repository or path, stale baseline, second writer and exceeded budget refused; cancellation and restart preserve the worktree and void the attempt; a genuine pinned-Pi writer run through a real provider | Validation of the candidate, independent review, repair or any publication (M3+); any claim that prompt or guard scoping is an OS boundary |
| M3 | Candidate commit/tree/hash frozen; required checks executed in the owned worktree before any review; a fresh, separately identified read-only reviewer whose structured verdict the runtime enforces; a seeded failing check needing a new repair revision with fresh evidence; bounded automatic repair pausing at the attempt budget; cancellation and hard-kill recovery with reaped children and reserved spend; a genuine provider-backed run of all of the above (closed on Linux, October 17, 2026) | Fixture reviewer verdicts as provider evidence; a model's self-assessment as check evidence; native Mac/Windows lifecycle, which stays open; any publication or merge |

title: Milestone evidence
text:
| Full v1 | Original requirements/acceptance matrix including browser/TUI parity and supported platform evidence | Single-repository Linux demo |

Required foundation checks are schema validation, Rust formatting/tests/lint, frontend type/build checks, and relevant fixture integration tests. Native desktop compilation requires platform prerequisites. Real provider smoke tests require existing credentials/model access and are reported separately. Mac/Windows jobs provide compatibility evidence only when they have actually run.

Luuna's original code and documentation are MIT licensed. Derived component distributions retain separate upstream notices. The original `VALIDATION-REPORT.md` validates a documentation delivery; keep product evidence separate. Registry package publication, signed installers, remote access, and production release still require explicit operational decisions and evidence; [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) is the M8 report that links every requirement and acceptance scenario to what has actually run and names what blocks the v1 label.

title: Milestone evidence
Implementation roadmap and AI handoff
text:
# Implementation roadmap and AI handoff

Date: 2026-10-16. This is the implementation sequence from the audited foundation to a usable MVP and full v1. It supplements [the current architecture](CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md), not a claim that the planned capabilities already exist.

title: Starting point
text:
## Starting point

Keep the application and all three maintained CLI components in **this monorepo**. Missions, Atlas, and Beacon retain independent package/API boundaries, compatible data formats, and upstream MIT notices. Repository separation is a later maintenance decision, not a prerequisite or the next assignment. Do not create repositories, remove component source, or replace these tools with Rust rewrites to advance a milestone.

[FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md) records the observed evidence. Its current Linux baseline is 101 Rust tests, 18 API-client tests, 4 scope-guard tests, 20 positive/negative schema checks, and 3,092 component tests passing, with Rust formatting/lint and frontend type/build checks passing, plus an 18-check synthetic smoke-harness run, the 19-check genuine OpenRouter run, the 15-check M2a browser smoke, a genuine passing baseline of this checkout, the 8-check M2b browser smoke and the genuine M2c writer runs recorded in the status report. Counts describe that audit, not a permanent expected total; future changes must rerun appropriate checks.

| Pi/runtime | Actual Pi 1.3.0 version/RPC handshake, authenticated loopback run API, replay/SSE, timeout/cancel/reap, malformed/error fixtures, durable failed/cancelled attempts | Genuine provider-backed output observed on Linux on October 17, 2026 (OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, 19/19 real-mode smoke checks); Mac/Windows service lifecycle and native client remain unverified |

title: Starting point
text: M0 is substantially established, with remaining API/capability/threat-model details completed alongside their first executable consumers. It is not proof of the operational workflow. M1 is closed on Linux as of October 17, 2026; its native-host step is carried by the MVP native-lifecycle item. M2a, M2b and M2c closed later the same day (see the status report). M3 and the MVP gate closed on Linux and Windows, and the M4–M8 slices recorded under each milestone below landed on October 21, 2026 with the gaps each status names; the next assignments are evidence on hosts this one is not (Mac, capable mobile runners, a clean machine, real GitHub), never a shortcut around them.

title: What counts as a usable product
text:
## What counts as a usable product

A **usable single-repository MVP** imports a real repository, discovers and confirms a meaningful baseline, prepares an exact plan, gets human approval, implements a bounded change in a Luuna-owned worktree, runs real required checks, obtains fresh independent review, and preserves evidence through cancellation or restart. The desktop must show the actual state and allow recovery. It must be demonstrated on the chosen Mac/Windows targets before those targets are advertised.

The MVP can deliver reviewable local commits/diffs without automatic PRs, multi-repository orchestration, all stack profiles, complete memory integration, or a TUI. Those omissions must be explicit.

**Full v1** additionally satisfies all R01–R15 and the [acceptance matrix](11-acceptance.md): multi-repository roles and integration, project creation and supported profiles, scoped memory and component adapters, browser/TUI parity, linked automatic PRs, human-only merging, and supported fresh-host installation. Optional remote workers, NAS hosting, GPU inference, semantic retrieval, team/SaaS features, and a full IDE are later work.

title: Milestones and measurable exits
text:
## Milestones and measurable exits

Follow the existing M0–M8 naming. Desktop work accompanies real runtime slices rather than becoming a separate simulated product.

title: M1 — Finish genuine engine compatibility
text:
### M1 — Finish genuine engine compatibility

**Depends on:** existing foundation, a supported model/provider, private credentials, and usable provider network access.

1. Inspect the installed pinned Pi protocol docs and current adapter. Reuse the credential-free probe and synthetic fixtures.
2. Complete one small genuine provider-backed request through the authenticated local API. Observe actual text/event streaming and the correct `agent_settled` completion semantics.
3. Cancel another genuine in-flight request and show that the owned process exits/reaps and the final state is cancelled. Exercise provider failure/timeout without promoting partial output to success.
4. Disconnect/reconnect the client and stop/restart the service. Replay ordered persisted events, retain completed/failed/cancelled history, and mark an abandoned active attempt interrupted.
5. Run the native desktop against the same service on a capable host; record any platform gap rather than calling a web build a native launch.

**Exit:** sanitized provider/Pi/model/platform evidence, real output, cancellation/error traces, persistent run IDs/cursors, and unchanged privacy/authentication protections. Missing-key failure already has evidence; it does not substitute for model success. Tool-free success closes connectivity, not repository-writing readiness. Map to R03/R15.

title: M2a — Import and read-only discovery
text:
### M2a — Import and read-only discovery

**Depends on:** M1's stable lifecycle and event contract. Read-only fixture/API work can proceed while provider access is being configured.

Register an existing single repository, establish stable identity/remote/base commit, detect dirty state, discover candidate stack/check recipes, and ask the developer to confirm uncertain repository facts. Persist project/manifest revisions and expose them through authenticated API/client contracts. Use canonical `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets` when ticket creation is introduced.

**Exit:** a real and a synthetic repository import without changing their contents; dirty files remain byte-identical; an invalid or mismatched repository is rejected; replay reconstructs the confirmed map. Discovery proposes commands rather than silently executing arbitrary repository text. This begins R04 and supplies M2 inputs.

**Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** `luuna-git`, `luuna-discovery`, the project registry in `luuna-storage`, the five project routes, the client and the desktop panel exist with synthetic and real (this checkout) evidence; see [ADR 0006](decisions/0006-repository-import.md) and the status report. Relationships between repositories are accepted by the contract but not discovered; that is M4.

title: M2b — Baseline and check evidence
text:
### M2b — Baseline and check evidence

**Depends on:** confirmed repository identity and check recipes from M2a.

Build a supervised command executor with executable/argument arrays, explicit cwd/profile, timeouts, capability checks, private artifacts, and process ownership. Record command, environment, exact commit/tree, timestamps, exit/status, and artifact hashes. Establish required baseline evidence before feature writes. Missing testing setup creates a bounded prerequisite workflow requiring its own approval.

**Exit:** genuine passing and deliberately failing fixture baselines; missing executable, empty/missing test setup, cancelled command, and incapable host remain blocked/failed/interrupted as appropriate. A baseline from another commit/environment cannot unlock a writer. Retain the fail-closed storage guard until this evidence is checked transactionally. Map to R08 and support R13.

**Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** `luuna-executor`, baseline contracts, storage migration 3 with `begin_implementation`, the baseline routes, client and desktop controls exist; this checkout's own `cargo test --locked --workspace` and `npm test` baseline passed with bound evidence, and the failure, blocked, cancelled and interrupted paths are tested; see [ADR 0007](decisions/0007-baseline-executor.md) and the status report. A dirty checkout is blocked until M2c worktrees exist.

title: M2c — Exact approval and one scoped writer
text:
### M2c — Exact approval and one scoped writer

**Depends on:** M2b; existing plan/approval domain and SQLite guards.

Expose immutable plan revisions and exact-hash approvals through runtime/API/client. Revalidate ticket/manifest/base revision and baseline evidence when scheduling. Create only Luuna-owned branches/worktrees with durable ownership/leases. Execute one bounded writer assignment with declared resources, operation scope, budgets, and model profile. Separate native-host permissions from any advertised isolation mechanism.

**Exit:** one approved fixture feature changes only its managed worktree; the developer checkout is preserved. Missing/stale approval, changed base, changed recipe, unrelated repository/path, stale baseline, second writer, and exceeded budget are rejected. Cancellation/restart preserves unfinished work and invalidates uncertain evidence. Map to R07/R08. A prompt that promises to obey paths is not an OS security boundary.

title: M2c — Exact approval and one scoped writer
text: **Status (October 17, 2026): closed on Linux.** Temporary local tickets (ADR 0003/0005), runtime-built immutable plan revisions, exact-hash approvals, `begin_implementation` revalidation of ticket, manifest, base, baseline and host fingerprint, worktree leases with one active lease per repository, attempts counted against the budget, the Pi writer profile with the Luuna scope guard, post-session scope judgement of the worktree diff and candidate commits exist; every exit rejection, cancellation and restart is tested, and a genuine pinned-Pi writer through a real provider is recorded in the status report; see [ADR 0008](decisions/0008-approval-worktrees-writer.md). The Missions adapter replaces the temporary ticket in M6; baselines still run on the developer checkout, so a dirty checkout still blocks a baseline.

title: M3 — Candidate checks, independent review, repair and recovery
text:
### M3 — Candidate checks, independent review, repair and recovery

**Depends on:** a real M2 writer and command evidence.

Freeze exact candidate commit/tree identities; bind required checks and structured reviewer results to them. Start the reviewer in a new session with requirements, current code/diff, and evidence, excluding the implementer's conversation. Classify infrastructure failures separately, aggregate attempt/time/cost usage, bound repairs, and pause usefully when exhausted. Every repair/manual edit invalidates affected evidence and review.

**Exit:** a seeded regression is blocked; a stale candidate/review cannot pass; repair exhaustion persists with artifacts; restart does not reset budgets or duplicate work; cancellation covers owned descendants when shell tools are enabled. Demonstrate a complete approved single-repo feature with real checks and independent review. Map to R09/R10.

title: M3 — Candidate checks, independent review, repair and recovery
text: **Implementation status (October 17, 2026):** candidate command checks, fresh read-only Pi reviewer sessions, structured review bindings, bounded manual/opt-in automatic repair, aggregate budgets, restart recovery and desktop diff/evidence views are implemented and fixture-tested. **The genuine-provider exit is closed on Linux** by `scripts/m3-smoke.mjs` through OpenRouter with pinned Pi 1.3.0: real writer, real required checks, fresh independent reviewer, seeded failure → repair r2 → fresh evidence, bounded automatic repair pausing at the attempt budget, cancellation and hard-kill recovery with spend reservation. A real run on the MVP code (`fd42d59`, October 21, 2026) passed 61/61 again. Native Mac/Windows proof remains open, so M3 is not declared fully closed. See [ADR 0009](decisions/0009-candidate-validation-review.md) and the status report.

title: MVP gate — Make the single-repository workflow usable
text:
### MVP gate — Make the single-repository workflow usable

**Depends on:** M1–M3. Develop screens against those working APIs, not alternative frontend state machines.

Complete project import, baseline, plan approval, live execution, diff/evidence/review, history, cancel and recovery flows. Test keyboard access and clear blocked/failure messages. Exercise desktop-to-service reconnection and explicit service shutdown. Smoke native Mac/Windows hosts with declared prerequisites; test backup/migration recovery and document manual service startup limitations.

**Exit:** another developer follows the documented setup and completes the representative fixture workflow without undocumented database edits or fake data. Publish a requirement/evidence report naming MVP omissions. A native package may be a development distribution; signed fresh-host installation remains M7 evidence.

title: MVP gate — Make the single-repository workflow usable
text: **Status (October 21, 2026): the cloud-doable part is closed on Linux; the native-host part remains.** A candidate whose required checks passed but whose reviewer left no verdict can be re-validated in place as a fresh generation of the same revision under the same approval and budgets (ADR 0009, point 7). An orderly shutdown now records interruption, never cancellation (ADR 0004 note). The desktop client shows outages, reconnects and reloads by itself, names the next allowed action with every refusal and recorded reason, and is operable by keyboard; `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` drives it through the documented [walkthrough](MVP-WALKTHROUGH.md) with recovery, refusal, keyboard and accessibility checks, and [MVP-EVIDENCE.md](MVP-EVIDENCE.md) is the requirement/evidence report naming the omissions. **Later on October 21, 2026, on Windows:** the backup/migration recovery drill is scripted (`node scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs`, 31/31 on this host, walkthrough step 7b) and the Windows native smoke is covered by the PR 11 bundled-WebView2 lifecycle run plus `scripts/package-windows.ps1`; the Mac smoke remains open for lack of a host.

title: M4 — Multi-repository coordination
text:
### M4 — Multi-repository coordination

**Depends on:** M3's reliable single-repository execution and candidate guards.

Add confirmed repository relationships, task DAG scheduling, scoped project/repository/specialist roles, leases, bounded concurrency, dependency overrides, and cross-repository candidate sets. Preserve one authoritative runtime.

**Exit:** an API/shared-package/consumer fixture produces three exact candidate commits, independent work runs within limits, incompatible consumer integration blocks completion, and partial failure/restart preserves the graph and evidence. Map to R05/R06; single-repository check success cannot stand in for integration success.

**Status (October 21, 2026): closed with the synthetic writer on Windows.** Validated task graphs, relationship proposals and confirmation, durable per-task state, the dependency-ordered scheduler with `max_workers`, cross-repository candidate sets with bindings, per-repository validation with a combined review diff, integration blocking, and resumption by task exist and are tested by the three-repository fixture (`crates/luuna-runtime/tests/multirepo.rs`, 9 scenarios); see [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md) and the status report. Open: delegated roles (P42), dependency overrides (P44), repair of a multi-repository set (re-planning by decision) and a genuine-provider multi-repository feature.

title: M5 — New projects and verified stack profiles
text:
### M5 — New projects and verified stack profiles

**Depends on:** M2's executor/baseline contracts; end-to-end acceptance uses M3/M4 as appropriate.

Add approved scaffolding and check profiles for React/Next.js/TypeScript, Node, Go, Python, Flutter, native Android and iOS. Probe host capabilities; let the developer confirm discovered recipes.

**Exit:** every advertised profile has a genuine scaffold/import baseline on a capable runner. Required Apple/device/emulator checks have real evidence or explicitly block that workflow. Do not call an unavailable platform passing. Map to R04/R13.

**Status (October 21, 2026): implemented; closed only for the profiles this Windows host can run.** Host capability probing, capability-annotated discovery for every advertised profile, and hashed, confirmed scaffolding with a real baseline exist ([ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md)); Node, TypeScript, Python and Rust scaffolds ran passing baselines here, Go, Flutter, Android and iOS are proved only as correctly blocked proposals and annotated discoveries. Capable-runner evidence for those four and the Mac-only checks remain the exit.

title: M6 — Integrated components, scoped memory and client parity
text:
### M6 — Integrated components, scoped memory and client parity

**Depends on:** stable project/ticket/run contracts; client parity acceptance depends on the implemented product capabilities.

Integrate Missions tickets/dependencies with serialized revision checks; migrate any temporary SQLite ticket authority into a reconciled projection. Add Atlas user/project/process memory with provenance, isolation, promotion/deletion and lexical retrieval. Render versioned Beacon prompts into explicit Pi resources. Use compatible APIs/data formats rather than independent writable copies or imported historical task records.

Complete browser and TUI actions against a shared capability catalog, alongside the desktop. Include plans, approval, repository views, diff/review, settings, memory, cancel, recovery and publication controls.

**Exit:** external Missions edits cause a detected conflict; stale prompts/schema mismatches fail visibly; private memory never crosses project/export scope; every cataloged action and failure path has parity evidence; reconnect yields the same authoritative state. Map to R02/R14/R15.

title: M6 — Integrated components, scoped memory and client parity
text: **Status (October 21, 2026): closed for the cataloged actions on Windows and Linux.** Missions migration and reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon context (ADR 0014), memory promotion and the scope-safe export (ADR 0021), the capability catalog, shared failure explanations and the terminal client with parity tests and `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs` (ADR 0020) exist; see the status report. Open: a keyboard audit and tones for the interactive TUI, import of an export, memory retention policy.

title: M7 — Publication and portable installation
text:
### M7 — Publication and portable installation

**Depends on:** M3 evidence gates, M4 candidate sets, and a verified publication credential mechanism.

Implement push/linked PR creation, durable idempotency and remote reconciliation, partial-success recovery, CI observation and human-controlled merge tracking. Ship tested installers/doctor diagnostics and a host-specific independent-service/token/update strategy. Current permission to push this repository is not proof the future product publisher exists.

**Exit:** approved three-repo candidates create linked PRs once, timeout-after-success and partial publication recover without duplicates, failing CI is distinct from integration, and no automatic merge path exists. Clean supported Mac/Windows computers install, configure and run the fixture without NAS/cloud dependence. Map to R01/R11/R12.

**Status (October 21, 2026): implemented against a fake GitHub API and a local remote; installer built unsigned on Windows.** Publication with a durable intent ledger, reconciliation, CI and merge observation and no merge path, plus `luuna-runtime doctor`, exist and pass six scenarios ([ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md)); `scripts/package-windows.ps1` produces an NSIS development installer carrying the runtime, helper scripts and the pinned Pi tree. Open: real GitHub evidence, a clean-machine Windows installation, Mac packaging, signing.

title: M8 — Full-v1 release evidence
text:
### M8 — Full-v1 release evidence

**Depends on:** M4–M7 and every advertised capability's prerequisites.

Run all A01–A34 scenarios, supported-host/version matrix, real-project pilot, failure/recovery drills, migrations/backups, dependency/security review and performance measurements. Inspect resource growth, cancellation latency, event delivery and usage accounting; define targets from observed measurements.

**Exit:** every R01–R15 requirement has passing linked evidence on relevant hosts; unresolved required checks block the v1 label. Document limitations, credential/retention boundaries, installer provenance and reproducible recovery. No required path depends on synthetic model output.

**Status (October 21, 2026): report produced; the v1 label is not granted.** [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) links every requirement and scenario to the evidence that exists, `node scripts/release-evidence.mjs` runs the checks and harnesses into one requirement-mapped report, and the blocking items (Mac, clean-machine installation, real GitHub, capable runners for Flutter/Android/iOS, a genuine run on the current tree, a real-project pilot) are named there.

title: Implementation process and evidence
text:
## Implementation process and evidence

Make each M2 substage and each subsequent bounded behavior independently reviewable. Before coding, inspect current code, applicable instructions, relevant schema/API/role contract, and baseline evidence. Describe the behavior, affected files/boundaries, negative cases, and exit command; do not ask the user to repeat accepted architecture decisions.

Implement runtime policy and durable transitions before connecting client actions. Use synthetic fixtures for deterministic failure cases and real tools/providers for compatibility evidence. Run relevant checks, get independent review, fix material findings, and update status and handoff before advancing. Add crates/packages when a real implementation needs them. Consume the independent component repositories through the exact-commit submodules of ADR 0012.

Each completion report must identify:

- Revision and dirty-state context; delivered behavior and requirement IDs.
- Commands actually run, exit results, counts, OS/architecture and pinned tool/provider/model versions.
- Run/attempt IDs, event cursors, exact plan/candidate hashes, and sanitized artifact locations.
- Negative/failure/recovery cases exercised; independent reviewer findings and resolution.
- Passing, failing, blocked and unavailable checks separately, with the next concrete assignment.

title: Implementation process and evidence
text: Commit only sanitized summaries, synthetic fixtures and useful reproducible tests. Keep tokens, keys, personal paths, private provider transcripts and raw local state out of Git. Record private evidence references without copying secrets. A documentation report cannot replace missing execution evidence.

title: Reproducible starting commands
text:
## Reproducible starting commands

Pins: Rust **1.90.0**, Node **24.19.0**, npm **11.9.0**, Bun **1.4.3**, Pi **1.3.0**. Root and native Cargo workspaces have separate locks; root npm, Pi and each Bun component also have their own committed locks.

For the configured cloud checkout, `bash scripts/setup-cloud.sh` installs frozen dependencies and builds the runtime without component lifecycle hooks. Use the saved environment startup instructions for tool/cache paths. On other hosts follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and platform prerequisites rather than assuming `/workspace` exists.

From the repository root:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --workspace
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run build
node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs
git diff --check
```

For a changed component, run in its own directory:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run verify
```

Run the native check on a capable host; root Rust checks exclude that workspace:

```sh
cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
```

With `LUUNA_PI_COMMAND` pointing to the installed pinned executable:

```sh
cargo run --locked -p luuna-engine-pi --example probe
```

title: Reproducible starting commands
text: That probe makes **no model request**. For genuine M1 proof, securely set the provider credential (or its `LUUNA_PI_<NAME>` alias) in the runtime environment, build the runtime, and run `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider <provider> --model <model>`, which starts the runtime itself and writes a sanitized report; or start `cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime` manually with `LUUNA_API_TOKEN`, provider and model set. Launch `npm run dev` or `npm run desktop` separately. The runtime does not automatically load `.env`. See the [runtime README](../crates/luuna-runtime/README.md), [desktop README](../apps/desktop/README.md), and [Pi fixtures](../fixtures/pi-rpc/README.md).

title: Planning ranges, assumptions and critical path
text:
## Planning ranges, assumptions and critical path

These are engineering estimates from this foundation, **not promised dates**. Assume one experienced full-time engineer using AI assistance, about 40 scheduled hours/week with **30 focused engineering hours**, a stable model/provider budget, Mac and Windows capable hosts, and timely feedback. AI assistance is included in the assumption; it does not remove integration, review, native packaging, or failure-testing work. Waiting for credentials, network changes, host access, signing, or external service approval adds elapsed time.

The earlier desktop proposal estimated **372–600 hours from scratch** for a meaningful single-repository MVP. Some bootstrap work now exists and its model path was proved on October 17, 2026; its native paths remain unproven. Use the following remaining-work range provisionally and re-estimate after the first real M2 writer.

title: Planning ranges, assumptions and critical path
text:
| Remaining work to a usable single-repo MVP | Focused hours before contingency |
| --- | ---: |
| Genuine M1 compatibility and evidence (Linux closed October 17, 2026; native-host step remains) | 0–8 |
| M2c approval revalidation, worktree ownership and scoped writer (closed on Linux October 17, 2026; native-host proof remains) | 0–8 |
| M3 independent review, repair and recovery | 64–104 |
| MVP client completion, native smoke and end-to-end hardening | 64–104 |
| Subtotal | 128–224 |
| Technical uncertainty allowance, approximately 20% | 26–45 |
| **Planning range** | **154–269** |

That is about **4–7 full 40-hour engineering weeks**, or **5–9 elapsed workweeks at 30 focused hours/week** under these assumptions. A connectivity preview can arrive sooner; it is not the usable MVP defined above.

| Additional work after the MVP to full v1 | Focused hours before contingency |
| --- | ---: |
| M4 multi-repository scheduler and integration | 96–160 |
| M5 creation and complete stack-profile matrix | 128–224 |
| M6 component/memory integration and browser/TUI parity | 128–224 |
| M7 linked publication, service packaging and installers | 96–168 |
| M8 pilot, acceptance, security/recovery and release hardening | 80–144 |
| Subtotal | 528–920 |
| Technical uncertainty allowance, approximately 20% | 106–184 |
| **Additional planning range** | **640–1,110** |

title: Planning ranges, assumptions and critical path
text:
The combined remaining full-v1 range is roughly **790–1,380 focused hours**, about **20–35 full engineering weeks** or **26–46 elapsed workweeks at the assumed focused capacity**. Treat the upper range seriously: native/mobile profiles, TUI parity, independent service installation and publication recovery are substantial product work. Requirements changes or missing platforms can exceed this range.

The execution critical path is **genuine M1 → import/baseline → exact approval/scoped writer → candidate checks/fresh review → reliable multi-repo integration**. Full-v1 release also depends on client parity, profile/platform proof and publication/installers. Stack/client contracts can be prepared alongside core work once stable, but one engineer's parallel tasks do not create extra capacity. Re-estimate from measured milestone throughput and preserve required gates; if time is short, narrow the MVP scope explicitly rather than declaring full v1 early.

text:

title: Preservation and destination verification
text:
## Preservation and destination verification

- Extracted component-scoped maintained history with `git subtree split` and checked the baseline Git tree against the original `HEAD:components/<name>` tree before changing standalone metadata. Both maintained commits are present in each destination. Earlier pre-branding import provenance remains in UPSTREAM.md and Luuna's retained history.
- Compared Git object identities for each `src` tree, `bun.lock` and `LICENSE` against the source baseline: all identical. Runtime/data implementation, JSON formats, aliases, source versions and dependency graphs did not change.
- Scanned every extracted commit for tracked authoring/session stores, real environment files and recognizable credential patterns before the authorized public push. Only the component history was pushed, with no original Luuna refs. This is a bounded repository hygiene check, not a universal secret-detection claim.
- Verified the authenticated owner, destination visibility, push access and remote `main` SHA. Each destination is public and owned by brodynelly, who owns CI and release decisions. Registry packages remain private, self-upgrade remains disabled, and public consumption needs no release secret or deploy key.

title: Setup, updates and rollback
text:
## Setup, updates and rollback

Run `npm run components:setup` after a fresh Luuna clone. Plain `git clone --recurse-submodules` retrieves source but still needs frozen dependency installation. `npm run components:run -- luuna-missions -- --help` invokes the approved pinned source; atlas and beacon follow the same interface. The root npm workspace remains separate from these Bun packages.

To update, review the component's own change and CI, fetch/check out its exact commit in the submodule, update the manifest commit, and commit both manifest and gitlink in the Luuna PR. Setup never uses a floating branch or silently overwrites local changes. Reverting the extraction commit restores Luuna's original tracked component trees; no original monorepo history is rewritten. Local source rollback copies remain outside tracking during migration.

Full M6 runtime ticket reconciliation, scoped memory retrieval and explicit prompt resources remain planned. The migration preserves the existing CLI/library boundary and verifies real consumption; it does not claim those runtime adapters now exist. No provider or native desktop result is inferred from CLI tests.

title: PR review corrections, October 21, 2026
text:
## PR review corrections, October 21, 2026

Review found that setup performed checkout before detecting local edits, and that the developer launcher captured stdin/output and collapsed nonzero CLI statuses into its own error handling. Setup now validates all component identities, manifest completeness, gitlinks, URLs and initialized worktree cleanliness before any checkout/install. Regression tests cover dirty and uninitialized checkouts and missing/duplicate manifest entries. Clean prior pins can still be updated through the committed gitlinks.

The developer CLI now inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, preserves the component exit status, and uses npm's INIT_CWD so `npm --prefix` operates on the calling project rather than Luuna's root. The bounded programmatic JSON helper remains separate. The real smoke additionally pipes an Atlas record through the launcher from a different package directory and checks a Missions JSON failure and exit code, raising the smoke to 14 operations. MIT and component README links now target the exact public repository revisions so they work on GitHub across submodule boundaries.

text:
The owner requested canonical luuna-* repository names during PR review. GitHub repository renames preserve repository identity and maintained history; all active submodule URLs, package repository/homepage/issue metadata, documentation and consumer pins use luuna-missions, luuna-atlas and luuna-beacon. The launcher accepts those full primary names and retains the short component selectors as compatibility aliases. Internal components paths and upstream data formats remain stable.

Final review validation: the branded repository pins passed frozen setup and 14/14 real CLI operations on both Windows and Linux. All eight setup/pin regressions passed on Windows, and the final Linux npm test passed 20 schema cases, 5 scope-guard tests, 8 component-pin tests, 13 desktop tests and 22 API-client tests at 2cb556e. The earlier reviewed code also passed frontend typecheck/build. All three renamed public repositories passed their full independent CI at the exact final component commits linked above. Private Luuna Actions remains blocked before job startup by account payment/spending limits; no billing settings or branch policies were altered.

title: Luuna desktop design system
text:
# Luuna desktop design system

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: current; decision recorded in [ADR 0013](decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md). This is the visual and interaction contract for the desktop client (`apps/desktop`). It is presentation only: the runtime decides every state, permission, reason and next step, and the client displays them.
