A design change may never change which control appears, when it is enabled, or what text the runtime's state produces.

title: Principles
text:
## Principles

1. **Green is earned.** The success tone means passed durable evidence: a passed check or baseline, a reviewed candidate or run, a `passed` review verdict, and a live authenticated connection. A completed demo session, an approval or a recorded candidate is not evidence and is never green. The UI's own copy says so: "A completed session is not a validation result."
2. **Six tones, three channels.** Every state is carried by a colour family, a shape mark and the unchanged runtime text. Colour is never the only signal, and no tone has two meanings.
3. **Identities are shown whole.** Hashes, commits, trees, fingerprints, sessions, worktree paths and artifact ids render in `code`: monospace, wrapping anywhere. CSS never truncates them. The only short forms are the leading-prefix slices that summary rows already make in code.
4. **Reason, then next step.** A recorded reason carries the tone of the state it explains. The next allowed step follows it on its own line, ruled in lavender.
5. **Interruption is not failure.** Outages, restarts, interrupted work and abandoned leases use the interrupted tone (plum, pause bars), never danger. Their work is durable.

title: Principles
text:
6. **Lavender means the developer acts; cyan means the runtime works.** The brand lavender marks primary actions, the next step, focus and selection. The active tone is cyan, so runtime activity is never confused with a call to action. An action group has at most one primary button.
7. **Tokens only.** Literal colours, lengths and durations live in `design/tokens.css` alone. Every colour exists in the dark and the light scheme, and every text pair meets WCAG 2.1 AA.
8. **One page, one outline.** Heading levels follow the document outline in DOM order (h1, h2 per panel, h3 per subpanel, h4 inside a candidate). Visual order equals DOM order at every width.

title: Files and layers
text:
## Files and layers

```text
apps/desktop/src/
  styles.css                 manifest: @layer tokens, base, components, screens; then @import … layer(…)
  design/tokens.css          the only file with literals; dark :root, light under prefers-color-scheme
  design/base.css            element defaults: type, code/pre, focus, forms, buttons
  design/components.css      tone indirection and every reusable component
  design/tone.ts             Tone type and exhaustive maps from runtime unions to tones
  design/StatusBadge.tsx     the one status chip
  design/design-system.test.ts   enforcement (run by npm test)
  screens/app.css            shell: topbar, intro, connection, workspace, history, events, footer
  screens/projects.css       Projects panel
  screens/workflows.css      tickets, plan controls, plan review
  screens/candidate-review.css   candidate evidence, checks, diff, verdict
  screens/project-components.css tickets, scoped memory and versioned prompts
```

Vite inlines the imports into one bundled stylesheet served from `'self'`, which the Tauri CSP allows. Later layers win regardless of specificity, so a screen rule refines a component without `!important`. No font, script or stylesheet is fetched.

title: Tokens
text:
## Tokens

Dark is the default; the light scheme redefines every colour under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)`. Values are hex so the contrast test computes ratios from the file itself.

| Role | Dark | Light | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-bg` | `#101216` | `#f5f6f9` | page |
| `--color-surface` | `#191d24` | `#ffffff` | panel |
| `--color-surface-raised` | `#20252e` | `#f8f9fb` | record row, tray, hover |
| `--color-surface-sunken` | `#0d1014` | `#eceff4` | pre, scroll regions |
| `--color-field` / `-disabled` | `#0d1014` / `#191d24` | `#ffffff` / `#eef1f5` | text fields: enabled well, disabled |
| `--color-control` / `-hover` | `#262c36` / `#353c47` | `#f6f7f9` / `#eceff3` | secondary button (disabled buttons are ghosted: no fill) |
| `--color-selected` / `-border` | `#262e40` / `#435579` | `#e8ecf8` / `#8f9fd6` | selected card |
| `--color-border` | `#303640` | `#d3d9e2` | decorative dividers |
| `--color-border-control` | `#6e788a` | `#7d8697` | control edges (3:1 non-text) |
| `--color-text` | `#e9edf4` | `#191d24` | body text |
| `--color-text-muted` | `#a7b0bf` | `#4a5363` | labels, terms, scope, small |
| `--color-text-subtle` | `#8f9aac` | `#5c6576` | meta: times, event numbers, placeholders |
| `--color-text-disabled` | `#7a8494` | `#7d8697` | disabled controls (exempt from 1.4.3) |

title: Tokens
text:
| `--color-accent` / `-hover` | `#b7c8fb` / `#d1dcff` | `#3b4fa0` / `#30418a` | primary, next step, links, selection |
| `--color-on-accent` | `#101216` | `#ffffff` | text on accent |
| `--color-focus` | `#c3d1ff` | `#3b4fa0` | focus ring |

Each tone has `--tone-<name>-fg` (text), `-bg` (tint), `-border` and `-mark` (shape) in both schemes; see `tokens.css`.

Scales: type `--text-2xs` 11 px (badges, eyebrow, meta), `--text-xs` 12 px (evidence, labels, code), `--text-sm` 13 px (controls, card text, h4), `--text-md` 14 px (body, h3), `--text-lg` 16 px (h2), `--text-xl` fluid 26 to 34 px (h1); weights 400, 550, 650; space on a 4 px rhythm (`--space-1` 4 px to `--space-7` 48 px, plus 2 px and 6 px half steps); radii 4, 7, 11 px; `--border-width` 1 px, `--rule-width` 3 px, `--focus-width` 2 px; controls and single-line fields 34 px (28 px small buttons); layout `--layout-max` 1280 px with a gutter of 40, 24 and 16 px at full width, 920 px and 680 px; textareas start at their `rows` with a 68 px floor; `--scroll-max` 28 rem and `--plan-max` 24 rem for bounded regions; one motion duration, `--duration-fast` 120 ms, which is 0 ms under reduced motion.

title: Tones
text:
## Tones

| Tone | Meaning | Mark | Runtime values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| success (green) | passed durable evidence | filled circle | run `reviewed`; candidate `reviewed`; check and baseline `passed`; verdict `passed`; connection connected |
| active (cyan) | the runtime is working | ring | run `running`, `exploring`, `implementing`, `validating`, `reviewing`; candidate `validating`, `reviewing`; baseline `running`; lease `active` |
| danger (rose) | failed or blocked evidence | diamond | run `failed`, `testing_blocked`; candidate `failed`, `testing_blocked`; check and baseline `failed`, `blocked`; verdict `changes_required`, `blocked`; severity `blocking` |
| attention (amber) | waiting on the developer | triangle | run `plan_ready`, `approved`, `paused`; candidate `paused`; severity `warning`; recipe confidence `inferred`; project `unconfirmed` |
| neutral (slate) | recorded, not evidence | bar | run `queued`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `discovered`; candidate `pending`, `cancelled`; check `cancelled`; severity `info`; lease `released`; connection offline |
| interrupted (plum) | stopped by an outage or restart, recoverable | pause bars | `interrupted` everywhere; lease `abandoned`; connection reconnecting |

title: Tones
text: `design/tone.ts` holds these as `Record<Union, Tone>` maps over the `@luuna/api-client` unions, so a new runtime state fails `npm run typecheck` until it is given a tone. Descriptor chips (`manifest r2`, `ticket r1 · …`, `required · observed`) take no tone and render as outlined chips.

title: Components
text:
## Components

| Component | Markup | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status badge | `<StatusBadge tone={…}>{text}</StatusBadge>` renders `span.state[data-tone]` | Text is exactly the runtime value (underscores replaced as the screen already does); badges never transform case. Never add words inside the badge. |
| Tone mark | `i.tone-mark[data-tone]` (`aria-hidden`) | The badge's shape on its own, for a status dot outside a badge (the connection status). |
| Tag | `span.tag` | Static descriptor in a panel heading. |
| Panel | `section.panel[aria-labelledby]` > `.panel-heading` (h2, then tag/badge/action) > `.scope` > body | One h2 per panel. A panel is a grid spaced by `gap` (16 px); components carry no outer margin; a heading's description sits 8 px under it. No dimming, no hover. |
| Subpanel | `.subpanel` | Top rule and a 12 px grid rhythm for a section inside a panel or card (`.workflows`, `.candidate-review`). |
| Tray | `.tray` | A raised group of related settings inside a panel (the workflow run settings). |
| Meta line | `.meta` | A muted evidence sentence (run detail, plan meta, worktree, usage, diff meta); its `code` identities stay at full contrast, figures are tabular. |
| Button | `button` (secondary), `.primary`, `.danger`, `.text-button` | One `.primary` per action group. `.danger` and `.text-button` are small. Disabled uses the disabled colour tokens, never opacity. |

title: Components
text:
| Field | `label` wrapping `input`/`textarea` | Label text above the field. `spellCheck={false}` fields render monospace. A checkbox label is an inline row. |
| Field row | `.field-row` | Side-by-side fields that share the row and wrap one per line below 2 × 14 rem; a trailing `small` takes the full row. |
| Form footer | `.form-footer` > `small` + primary | Hint left, primary right even when it wraps. |
| Form group | `.form-group` | A bordered, unfilled group around a form (register, ticket). |
| Action row | `.actions` | Wrapping row; a trailing `small` takes the full row; `.danger` goes to the end. |
| Facts | `dl.facts` > `div` > `dt` + `dd` | Full identities in `dd code`. Term column 150 px, one column at 680 px (at 920 px inside a candidate, where every value is a full hash). |
| Record list | `ul.record-list` > `li.record` | Bordered rows: baselines, recipes, tickets, checks, findings. A nested record alternates its surface. `data-tone` on a leaf record (baseline, check, finding) adds a toned rule on its leading edge; a ticket card carries its state in its run badge, not a page-length rule. `.record-headed` puts the title and badge on the first line and every later child on its own full-width line. |

title: Components
text:
| Selectable card | `button.run-card[aria-pressed]` > `.run-prompt` + `.run-meta` | Selection shows by fill, border and a lavender inset rule, not colour alone. `.run-prompt` may clamp prose to two lines, never identities. |
| Reason and next step | `.failure-note[data-tone]` then `.recovery-note` | The reason carries an 8 px-inset rule and text in the tone of the state it explains; the next step follows flush under it, ruled in lavender, whether nested in the reason or its next sibling. |
| Callout | `.callout[data-tone]` | Toned box for outages, open questions and the runtime's activity status. |
| Alert banner | `.error[role=alert]` with a Dismiss `.text-button` | Refused actions and failed loads only; always dismissible. Outages are `role=status`, not alerts. |
| Disclosure | `details` > `summary`; `details.section` for a section heading (diff, check evidence, event record) | CSS caret, never text, so it adds nothing to the accessible name; the caret aligns with the content edge. |
| Scroll region | `ol.events`, `pre[aria-label][tabIndex=0]` | The only elements that scroll; bounded by `--scroll-max` (`--plan-max` for the plan). Focusable, with an inset focus ring. |
| Empty state | `.empty` (inline text), `.empty-box` (dashed box), `.activity-empty` | Muted text; the glyph is `aria-hidden`. |

title: Screens
text:
## Screens

- **App shell** (`App.tsx`, `screens/app.css`): skip link, topbar (wordmark, stage, connection status with a tone mark), intro, the runtime connection panel, Projects, then the workspace of session history and the main column (start form, session events). The workspace is two columns above 920 px and one column at 920 px and below, in DOM order, matching the Projects rail.
- **Projects** (`Projects.tsx`, `screens/projects.css`): a rail with the register form and project cards, and a detail column: facts first (the first `.facts` on the page), the "Rebind repository" disclosure, the action row (a running baseline adds its `.danger` cancel), baselines (each with its reason and next step and a log button per recipe stream, then the opened log), discovery (questions callout, problems, recipes, the manifest form), the Workflows subpanel, then the project event record.

title: Screens
text:
- **Workflows** (`Workflows.tsx`, `screens/workflows.css`): the ticket form (each field followed by its UTF-8 byte count), the run settings (paths, writes, approver, plan budgets, provider and model, automatic repair), then ticket cards. A ticket card holds its head, intent, actions with the run badge (the first writer's `.danger` cancel sits before the badge; a held-back "Plan r{n+1}" names its reason on its own line), the confirmation checkbox when the next revision would leave a pending, approved or reviewed revision behind, the writer's activity callout, the plan review with the complete plan in a bounded region, plan meta, earlier revisions with their badges, the reason and next step, worktree lines and the candidate.
- **Candidate review** (`CandidateReview.tsx`, `screens/candidate-review.css`): heading with badge, full identities, the action row, the runtime's activity callout, reason and next step, the diff, check evidence with logs, the independent review with findings, and usage.

title: Accessibility
text:
## Accessibility

- Every visible text run meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against its painted background in both schemes; marks, control edges and focus meet 3:1. Disabled controls are exempt and are marked with the `disabled` attribute.
- The first Tab stop is "Skip to main content", which focuses `main#main`. Focus is always visible.
- Every field has a label; every control has a name; scroll regions are focusable; heading levels never skip; every alert has a Dismiss button; `html[lang=en]`.
- No horizontal page scroll at the Tauri window's 760 px minimum width. Containers that can hold code use `min-width: 0` and `minmax(0, 1fr)`.
- Reduced motion turns the one transition off. Forced colours keep marks and selection visible.

title: Enforcement
text:
## Enforcement

`npm test` runs `design/design-system.test.ts`. It reads stylesheets with `node:fs`, because Vitest replaces `*.css?raw` imports with an empty string, and it fails on an empty sheet so no check can pass vacuously. It asserts:

- Outside `tokens.css`: no colour literal or function, no raw length or duration, font sizes only from `--text-*`, no `opacity`, no `!important`, approved media queries only, `outline: none` only on `main:focus`, scrolling only on labelled scroll regions, no truncation of `code`/`pre`, tone mapping only in `components.css`, no selector named after a runtime state, tone variables read only by a rule whose selector carries `[data-tone]`, and screen selectors scoped by a unique class with at most three child steps.
- Every `var()` resolves; both schemes define the same colour roles; every semantic pair meets its WCAG ratio in both schemes.
- Every component file is registered, and each screen keeps its heading levels, has no inline styles or positive `tabIndex`, renders badges through `StatusBadge`, and every alert carries Dismiss.
- The tone taxonomy: exactly the five evidence states are success; interruption is never danger; the badge renders the runtime text unchanged.

title: Enforcement
text: `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` checks the rendered result: contrast of every visible text run against its composited background in both schemes, that the client follows the system scheme, no horizontal scroll at 760 px, plus the existing keyboard, accessibility, DOM and lifecycle checks.

title: Changing the system
text:
## Changing the system

A new colour is a token in both schemes plus a contrast pair in the test. A new runtime state is a tone in `tone.ts`. A new component goes in `components.css` and this table. Do not style by runtime state name, add a heading level, or move the DOM elements the smoke reads (listed in `scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs`). Run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (Node 24.19.0) and the desktop smoke, and report each result.

title: MVP walkthrough: one repository from import to a reviewed candidate
text:
# MVP walkthrough: one repository from import to a reviewed candidate

Date: 2026-10-21. This is the representative single-repository workflow another developer follows end to end with the browser client, without editing the database or inventing data. `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` automates exactly these steps against the synthetic Pi fixture and records the result; a real provider follows the same steps with real model output. Read [AI-START-HERE.md](../AI-START-HERE.md) for the pins and [CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md](CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md) for what each step may and may not claim.

What the walkthrough does not cover is listed in [MVP-EVIDENCE.md](MVP-EVIDENCE.md): no publication or merge, one repository, no TUI, no memory integration, and no native Mac/Windows proof.

title: 0. Prerequisites
text:
## 0. Prerequisites

- Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0 with npm 11.9.0, Python 3, Git, and the pinned Pi 1.3.0 installed from `tools/pi` (`bash scripts/setup-cloud.sh` on the cloud image; [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) elsewhere). `npm ci --ignore-scripts` at the root.
- A provider credential for a real run, exported as `LUUNA_PI_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` (for example `LUUNA_PI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) in the shell that starts the runtime. Never type it into the client. Without a credential, rehearse with the synthetic fixture as described in [the credential-free rehearsal](#credential-free-rehearsal-with-the-synthetic-fixture); its runs are protocol evidence only.
- A repository to import with a test command that can pass on this host. The fixture used below is a small Python package with `python -m unittest -v`.

title: Credential-free rehearsal with the synthetic fixture
text:
### Credential-free rehearsal with the synthetic fixture

`fixtures/pi-rpc/mock_pi.py` stands in for Pi. It is not a model: it acts only on `fixture:<name>` markers in the ticket's acceptance criteria, and its writer only ever rewrites `src/main.py` (to print one line). Without a marker the writer changes nothing and the workflow fails with "writer settled without changing any file". Start the runtime of step 1 with these settings instead of a provider:

```sh
export LUUNA_PI_COMMAND=python3
export LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON="[\"$PWD/fixtures/pi-rpc/mock_pi.py\"]"   # run from the Luuna checkout
export LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER=test LUUNA_PI_MODEL=synthetic
```

Import a repository whose tests still pass after that rewrite, for example:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/luuna-rehearsal/src && cd /tmp/luuna-rehearsal
git init -q -b main && git remote add origin https://example.invalid/rehearsal.git
printf '__pycache__/\n' > .gitignore
printf '[project]\nname = "rehearsal"\n' > pyproject.toml
printf "print('fixture')\n" > src/main.py
cat > test_main.py <<'PY'
import subprocess, sys, unittest

class MainTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_main_prints(self):
        completed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "src/main.py"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        self.assertTrue(completed.stdout.strip())
PY
git add -A && git commit -qm "rehearsal fixture"
```

title: Credential-free rehearsal with the synthetic fixture
text:
Then follow the steps below with the manifest check `python3 -m unittest -v` (`required: true`), keep `src` in the writer paths, and put a marker on its own line in the acceptance criteria. The first `fixture:` marker selects the writer; the reviewer answers the first `fixture:review_*` marker and passes otherwise:

- `fixture:write_in_scope`: the writer rewrites `src/main.py` and the review passes, so the candidate reaches `reviewed`.
- `fixture:review_malformed_once`: the writer does the same, the first review is malformed and the next one passes, which rehearses re-validation (step 6).
- `fixture:review_blocking`: the review returns `changes_required` with a blocking finding, which rehearses repair.
- `fixture:review_hold`: the reviewer waits 60 s, long enough to cancel or stop the runtime mid-review (step 7).
- `fixture:slow`: the writer waits 60 s, long enough to cancel it from the ticket (step 5).
- `fixture:no_change` and `fixture:write_out_of_scope`: the writer fails closed with the no-change or scope reason and its next step.

title: 1. Start the runtime, then the client
text:
## 1. Start the runtime, then the client

```sh
export LUUNA_API_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"      # private; at least 32 bytes
export LUUNA_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.luuna"                   # SQLite, worktrees and private artifacts
export LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER=openrouter LUUNA_PI_MODEL=openai/gpt-4.1   # or set them per action in the client
cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime                    # listens on http://127.0.0.1:4242
```

In a second shell, `npm run dev` and open `http://127.0.0.1:1420`. Press Tab once: the first stop is "Skip to main content". Enter the runtime URL and the token in the connection form and press Enter. The header reads "Local runtime connected"; the token field disappears and the token is kept only in memory.

If the token is wrong the alert says so and names the next step: check the `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` the service was started with and connect again.

title: 2. Import the repository (M2a)
text:
## 2. Import the repository (M2a)

In Projects, enter a name, a repository ID (`app`) and the absolute path of the checkout, then "Register repository". The runtime inspects the checkout read-only (optional locks off, hooks neutralised) and shows the redacted remote, the HEAD commit, the branch and the dirty counts. A path that is not a repository root is refused with the runtime's reason ("Registration refused: …").

"Discover proposed map" proposes check recipes from the repository's manifests with evidence and confidence; nothing is executed. Edit the proposed manifest JSON so `checks` holds the commands the project really runs (for the fixture, `python -m unittest -v`, `required: true`), then "Confirm manifest". The facts line reads "revision 1" with the exact base commit, and the ticket form becomes enabled. A draft the runtime cannot read (a misspelled or missing field, or a quoted `"true"`) is refused with the runtime's reason naming the field. A confirmed proposal is spent: run Discover again for the next revision's draft; a stale draft is refused as a revision conflict with that next step.

title: 2. Import the repository (M2a)
text: If the checkout moved or its remote changed on purpose, open "Rebind repository" under the facts, enter the new root path (or leave it empty to re-inspect the registered one), tick the confirmation and rebind. The runtime re-inspects the checkout read-only and records the old and new identity; plans, baselines and approvals stay bound to exact commits, and a manifest whose remote no longer matches must be confirmed again. Every identity-mismatch refusal names this control as the recovery.

title: 3. Establish the baseline (M2b)
text:
## 3. Establish the baseline (M2b)

"Run baseline" executes the confirmed required recipes on the clean developer checkout through the supervised executor and lists the record: status, manifest revision, exact commit, and each recipe's status and exit code. "View unit stdout" and "View unit stderr" open each recipe's log by record identity. The baseline must be `passed` before any writer can start; a failed, blocked or empty suite blocks feature work, and the record says which recipe and why, with the next step (a missing tool or dependency asks for a dependency-preparation recipe such as `npm ci` before the tests). A dirty checkout is blocked until it is clean. "Cancel baseline" stops a running baseline; a second baseline for the same repository waits until the first settles. A baseline run that fails before it records anything (for example a changed repository identity) shows the reason from its final event.

title: 4. Ticket, plan and exact approval (M2c)
text:
## 4. Ticket, plan and exact approval (M2c)

Create a ticket with a title, the intent and one acceptance criterion per line. Each field shows its size in UTF-8 bytes, as the runtime counts it (a title takes at most 200 bytes, the intent and each criterion 16,000), so accented letters, CJK text and emoji count more than once.

Set the budgets for the next plan revision in the run settings: writer attempts (1 to 10, default 2), the time budget (1 to 86,400 seconds, default 600) and the cost budget (up to $1,000, default $1.00). Time and cost are cumulative across the whole workflow: the writer, every required check, the independent review and each repair spend from the same budget, so a suite that takes eight minutes needs more than the 600-second default. "Plan" records immutable plan revision 1 bound to the ticket revision, the manifest hash, the base commit, the required checks and those budgets, and opens the workflow run in `plan ready`; the plan line repeats the budgets. Retrying "Plan" after a lost answer replays the same revision instead of creating another. The complete plan JSON and its full `sha256:` hash are shown; the "Approve r1" button stays disabled until the acknowledgment checkbox is checked (Space toggles it, Enter approves). Approval binds to that exact hash; the run becomes `approved`.

title: 4. Ticket, plan and exact approval (M2c)
text: "Plan r2" stays disabled, with the reason beside it, while revision 1's writer, checks or review are running: a new revision would leave that work unreachable, so cancel it first to re-plan sooner. While revision 1 is approved, its candidate waits for validation, or it is reviewed, "Plan r2" first asks you to confirm what the new revision leaves behind (a pending candidate can then no longer be validated). Earlier revisions stay listed on the ticket with their final state.

title: 5. Implement in a Luuna-owned worktree
text:
## 5. Implement in a Luuna-owned worktree

"Implement" revalidates the approval, ticket revision, manifest, base commit, passed baseline and host fingerprint, leases a detached worktree under the data directory, and runs the pinned Pi writer with file tools and the scope guard. The ticket shows `implementing` with a line saying the writer runs and a "Cancel workflow" button, then `validating` with the worktree path and the candidate section: revision 1, the candidate hash, the commit and tree. "Inspect candidate diff" shows the exact diff bound to that hash. The developer checkout is untouched throughout. If another workflow's writer holds the repository, Implement is refused with that reason and the next step (wait for it or cancel it).

A writer that makes no in-scope change, or changes a path outside the approved task, fails closed with the reason shown under the ticket and a next step (re-plan with the paths the change needs).

title: 6. Validate and review (M3)
text:
## 6. Validate and review (M3)

"Validate and review" runs the required recipes inside the candidate worktree, records each result with its command, environment fingerprint, exit code, artifact hashes and detected test count, and only then starts a fresh read-only Pi reviewer with the requirements, diff and check evidence. While active, the candidate section says what the runtime is doing and offers "Cancel workflow"; an idle candidate has nothing to cancel.

Outcomes, all decided by the runtime from recorded evidence:

- `reviewed`: every required check passed and the reviewer's structured verdict is `passed`. The verdict, reviewer session and findings are shown; "View stdout" and "View stderr" open each check's log by record identity.
- `paused` with a `changes_required` or `blocked` verdict: read the findings, then "Repair candidate" (a new scoped writer under the same approval, which produces candidate revision 2 with fresh checks and review) or create the next plan revision. Tick "Repair automatically within approved budgets" before validating to let the runtime repair bounded failures itself; it stops at the attempt budget and pauses with the evidence.
- `failed` with a failed required check: open the log, then repair.

title: 6. Validate and review (M3)
text:
- `failed` with "invalid structured reviewer response" (or another reviewer failure that left no verdict) after passed checks: "Re-validate and review" starts a fresh validation generation of the same candidate under the same approval and budgets; no writer attempt is spent. The panel explains this next to the reason.
- `testing blocked`: a required check could not run meaningfully on this host (missing tool, empty suite). Fix the recipe or the host, run a new baseline, then plan again.

Every reason shown under a ticket or candidate carries the next allowed action, and never one the runtime would refuse: when repair or validation is not available (for example because the attempt budget is spent), the candidate says so with the runtime's reason and names the next plan revision instead. The usage line shows the whole workflow against its approved budgets: writer attempts, seconds, cost and repairs.

title: 7. Recovery: outage, restart and shutdown
text:
## 7. Recovery: outage, restart and shutdown

Stop the runtime at any point (Ctrl+C or SIGTERM for an orderly stop; a crash or `kill -9` for a hard one). The header switches to "Reconnecting to runtime" and the connection panel says that runs, candidates and worktrees are durable and nothing is lost. While the runtime is stopping it refuses new work with "runtime is shutting down" and the next step. Start the runtime again with the same data directory and token (step 1's `openssl` line makes a new token, so reuse the exported value): the client reconnects by itself, reloads every panel, and the work that was in flight is shown as `interrupted` with the recorded reason. If the runtime comes back with a different token, the client stops reconnecting and shows the connection form with "The service rejected this token"; enter the current token.

title: 7. Recovery: outage, restart and shutdown
text:
- A check or review interrupted by a hard kill or by an orderly shutdown keeps its candidate; "Validate and review" runs a fresh generation (new check records, a fresh reviewer) of the same revision. The orderly path records "interrupted by runtime shutdown"; a hard kill records "runtime restarted before attempt settled".
- A review interrupted mid-turn reserves the remaining approved cost budget, because the provider's spend is unknown. Validation is then not available: the candidate says so with the runtime's budget reason and names the next plan revision (a runtime that does not report its decisions refuses the click with the same reason).
- A writer interrupted mid-session keeps its worktree (files preserved, lease released) but the attempt is void; create the next plan revision and implement again.
- A baseline interrupted mid-run is recorded as `interrupted`; run it again.

Closing or reloading the browser never cancels anything; reopening the client replays the durable event record from the last sequence. "Disconnect" clears the token from memory and shows the runtime as offline; the runtime keeps running.

title: 7b. Backup, loss and restore (ADR 0016)
text:
## 7b. Backup, loss and restore (ADR 0016)

While the runtime runs, take a consistent snapshot of the database; it prints the schema version, size and SHA-256 of the file it wrote:

```sh
cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime -- backup --output ~/luuna-backups/before-upgrade.sqlite3 --data-dir "$LUUNA_DATA_DIR"
```

A restore is refused while a runtime owns the data directory. Stop the runtime first (the shutdown control, Ctrl+C or `Stop Luuna.cmd`), then:

```sh
cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime -- check --data-dir "$LUUNA_DATA_DIR"
cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime -- restore --input ~/luuna-backups/before-upgrade.sqlite3 --data-dir "$LUUNA_DATA_DIR"
```

`check` names a damaged database or one written by a newer Luuna and the restore step; the runtime refuses to start on either before writing anything. `restore` moves the current database and its sidecars into `backups/replaced-<timestamp>/` instead of deleting them, verifies the snapshot and installs it. After the runtime starts again the client shows the same projects, tickets, runs and event streams the snapshot held. A snapshot covers the database only; check artifacts and worktrees are files, so a complete backup is the data directory copied after an orderly stop. Upgrading a database from an earlier schema takes an automatic pre-migration snapshot under `backups/` first.

title: 7b. Backup, loss and restore (ADR 0016)
text: `node scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs` rehearses exactly this against a disposable data directory: durable state, an online backup, the refused live restore, an orderly stop, a deliberately damaged database and a database marked as written by a newer schema (both refused by `check` and by startup), the restore, identical authoritative state afterwards and new work on the restored database, then the storage suite's upgrade drill across every earlier schema version. It writes `report.md` and `report.json` to `--out`.

title: 8. What "done" means here
text:
## 8. What "done" means here

A `reviewed` candidate is evidence for its exact frozen commit and tree, under one approved plan revision: the required checks passed in the owned worktree and an independent reviewer found no blocking issue. It is a local commit in a Luuna-owned worktree, inspectable with Git at the path shown; publishing it, opening a pull request and merging stay with the developer until M7. The evidence survives client disconnects, runtime restarts and shutdowns, and nothing in the client can mark a candidate reviewed.

title: Reproducing this walkthrough automatically
text:
## Reproducing this walkthrough automatically

```sh
node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs --out /tmp/luuna-ui-smoke
```

The harness builds the runtime, starts it with the synthetic Pi fixture and a random token, starts the Vite client, and drives headless Chromium through steps 1 to 7 on two generated fixture repositories (step 7b has its own harness, `node scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs`), including a wrong token, a refused registration, an unreadable manifest draft, baseline logs, a plan with chosen budgets, cancelling the first writer from its ticket while the next revision is held back, an invalid review followed by re-validation, a hard kill and an orderly shutdown during checks, a hard kill during review with the budget refusal, keyboard operation of every control it touches, an accessibility audit of the rendered pages, a presentation audit (WCAG AA contrast against painted backgrounds in the dark and light schemes, scheme following, no horizontal scroll at the 760 px window minimum) and the final disconnect. It writes `report.md`, `report.json` and screenshots to the output directory. It is synthetic: the writer and reviewer are the fixture, so it proves the client and the runtime lifecycle, never a model.

title: @luuna/tui
text:
# @luuna/tui

The terminal client for the Luuna runtime. It exposes the same product actions as the desktop
client through the shared capability catalog (`schemas/capability-catalog.json`, ADR 0020) and
explains every refusal with the same shared text (`packages/api-client/src/failures.ts`).

```sh
export LUUNA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4242          # loopback only; this is the default
export LUUNA_API_TOKEN=...                       # never echoed; prompted (hidden) on a terminal when unset
npm run tui                                      # interactive workbench: arrows/j/k move, Enter selects, Esc back, r reload, q quit
npm run tui -- help                              # every command with its usage
npm run tui -- projects --json                   # one cataloged action for scripts; --json prints the runtime's record unchanged
npm run tui -- approve <plan> --acknowledge-hash sha256:<complete plan hash>
npm run tui -- follow <run>                      # live events over SSE, resumed after an outage from the last sequence
```

Exit codes: 0 done, 1 refused or failed (`<Action> refused: <reason> <next step>` on stderr), 2 usage.
Transport failures and 5xx responses are plain sentences; a server body is never shown.

title: @luuna/tui
text:
Adding an action: one catalog entry, one `LuunaClient` method, one object in `src/commands.mjs`
(with its `example`); `npm test` then checks the parity (`test/commands.test.mjs`). The end-to-end
evidence is `node scripts/tui-smoke.mjs` against a built runtime and the synthetic Pi fixture.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
# Local runtime connectivity foundation

The independent runtime is authenticated and loopback-only. It owns repository import, baseline checks, immutable approval, scoped writers, candidate-bound validation, fresh read-only review and bounded repair. The tool-free connectivity demo remains available as a separate profile: those sessions use a private empty cwd/config with repository tools disabled. Writer and reviewer scope guards are runtime policy, not an OS sandbox. Genuine-provider M3 acceptance remains separate from fixture coverage.

Install the supported `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.3.0` distribution.
The launcher verifies `--version` before each run. Configure these environment
variables locally; keep credentials out of repository files:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` | Required random token of at least 32 visible ASCII characters, with no spaces or line breaks; frontend enters it locally |
| `LUUNA_PI_COMMAND` | Pi executable, default `pi`; may be an absolute Node executable. On Windows a bare name is searched through PATH, executables first and then PATHEXT, and an npm `pi.cmd` shim is started as the Node executable and `dist/bundle/cli.js` it names; other `.cmd`/`.bat` launchers are refused |
| `LUUNA_GIT_COMMAND` | Host `git` used for read-only repository inspection, default `git` |

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
| `LUUNA_PI_ARGS_JSON` | Optional JSON array of launcher arguments, e.g. absolute `dist/cli.js` path |
| `LUUNA_PI_PROVIDER` / `LUUNA_PI_MODEL` | Optional explicit defaults; UI can supply them per run |
| `LUUNA_PI_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` | Optional alias for any supported provider key (for example `LUUNA_PI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LUUNA_PI_OPENAI_API_KEY`) for hosts that reserve the plain name; it becomes the child's standard variable, takes precedence over a direct key, and is never passed through under the alias name |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | Preserved for provider routing, including lowercase variants and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`; existing TLS trust variables remain enabled |
| `LUUNA_DATA_DIR` | Private durable state directory, default `.luuna`; on Unix it and its `worktrees` directory are made owner-only (0700) at startup, and a directory owned by another user is refused; keep it short on Windows, where worktrees below it count toward the 260-character path limit |
| `LUUNA_PORT` | Loopback port, default `4242` |
| `LUUNA_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Positive operation deadline, default `600`; version probe has a separate 15s deadline |

A setting that cannot be used stops startup with a message naming the variable
and the form it expects (for example `LUUNA_PORT must be a whole number from 0
to 65535 (got "abc")`); the token's value is never printed.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
Run `cargo run -p luuna-runtime`. Supply the selected provider's API key through
its standard environment variable, such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or
`OPENAI_API_KEY`; the runtime never accepts keys through the API. The current
demo inherits only an explicit list of direct provider key variables. OAuth,
cloud platform authentication, user Pi profiles, and model settings files are
not integrated. Missing provider credentials produce a persisted failed run.

`GET /api/v1/health` is public. Its `pi_version` field reports the required
supported version; the CLI is checked when starting a run. `native_execution: true`
states that approved writers and required checks run with the developer's host
permissions (the tool-free demo is one run profile; scope guards are not a sandbox). Its `build_identity`
field is the content digest of the sources the binary was built from, and
`build_rustc` names the compiler release and commit that built it
(`build_rustc_sha256` the SHA-256 of that compiler executable;
`build_rustc_wrapper` the names of any compiler wrapper variables Cargo used, or `none`;
`build_flags` the profile, opt-level, debug setting, whether RUSTFLAGS were set, the names of
any profile, linker or C toolchain override variables, and how many Cargo config files declare
an override). The route is unauthenticated, so it carries names and none/set status only, never
flag values, wrapper paths or config file paths. All other endpoints

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
require `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (the scheme name is case-insensitive).
Every 4xx/5xx response body is `{"error": "<reason>"}`, including malformed JSON,
unknown or mistyped fields, a missing content type, a body over 256 KiB, a bad
query and unknown routes or methods. A 500 says only that a storage or process
operation failed; the cause is written to the runtime's stderr with the request it
failed, never with payloads or credentials.

- `POST /api/v1/shutdown`: idempotently request an orderly service stop (202).
  Already admitted scheduling requests drain (at most five seconds; a request
  that never finishes its body cannot hold the stop open, and work it starts
  later begins already signalled to stop); new mutations receive
  503 `{"error":"runtime is shutting down"}`. Owned work settles as interrupted,
  preserving its evidence, every event stream ends, and main exits cleanly once
  connections drain (exit status 1 if a connection is still open ten seconds
  after owned work settled). This is separate from cancellation and from closing
  a client window.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
- `GET /api/v1/runs?limit=N`: persisted run records, newest first; `limit` (1..=10000) returns the most recent N.
- `POST /api/v1/runs`: `{ "prompt": "Hello", "provider": "...", "model": "..." }`.
- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}`: current run state.
- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/events?after=0&limit=N`: durable event replay by sequence; the optional `limit`
  (1..=10000) returns the first N events after the cursor, so a client pages from the last sequence it
  received. A cursor above 2^63-1 is a 400.
- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/stream?after=0`: SSE replay then live delivery; accepts `Last-Event-ID`. The
  stream ends when the run can never change again: a demo or baseline run at any terminal state, a
  workflow only at `completed`, `cancelled` or `reviewed` with no worker attached. A `failed` or
  `interrupted` workflow stays followed, because repair, re-validation and automatic repair continue on
  the same run id. Every stream ends when shutdown begins.
- `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel`: request abort; terminal cancellation follows process reaping.
  Repeating it, or cancelling a run whose worker already returned, answers with the settled run (200)
  or 409 for an idle run with no worker; it never fails with 500.
- `GET /api/v1/projects`, `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`: registered projects, machine-registry
  repositories, the current confirmed manifest and the latest discovery.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
- `POST /api/v1/projects`: `{ "id"?: "slug", "name": "...", "repositories": [{ "id": "app", "path": "/abs/root" }] }`
  inspects each repository root read-only (identity, HEAD, branch, dirty state) and registers it.
  Non-repositories, nested paths, bare or unborn repositories are rejected with 422, as are a
  repository inside `LUUNA_DATA_DIR` and one that contains it; a checkout already registered by
  any project is rejected with 409. Git's own refusals (for example dubious ownership) are reported.
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/discover`: re-observes the registered repositories and records a
  proposed manifest with per-recipe evidence, confidence and open questions. It reads manifest
  files only; it never runs a repository script. Evidence from files with uncommitted changes is
  only `inferred`.
- `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/manifest`: `{ "expected_revision": n, "manifest": {...} }` confirms
  revision `n+1` after re-checking identity, remote (by equivalence) and default branch (current,
  local, origin's HEAD or an `origin/<name>` remote-tracking branch), and records the exact HEAD
  commit per repository as the base. Stale revisions and changed identities return 409.
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repositories/{repository_id}/rebind`: `{ "local_path"?: "/abs/root" }`
  explicitly re-points a registered repository at the checkout now at that path (default: the

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
registered path), records `repository.rebound` with the old and new identity, and returns the
  project. It is the recovery every identity-mismatch error names; it is refused (409) while a
  run of the project is queued, running, exploring or implementing.
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events?after=0&limit=100`: durable project stream (`run_id` is
  `project:{id}`); `manifest.confirmed` carries the complete manifest for replay. `limit`
  (1..=10000) is optional; a cursor above 9223372036854775807 is a 400.

- `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines`: `{ "repository_id": "app", "include_optional": false }`
  starts a baseline run (202) that executes the confirmed required recipes for that
  repository on a clean checkout at its exact HEAD. It is an ordinary run: follow it with
  `/runs/{id}/events` or `/stream`, cancel it with `/runs/{id}/cancel`. A dirty checkout
  (the reason names the paths; Git-ignored files never count), missing executable or
  dependency (exit 127, `ModuleNotFoundError`, an unresolved Node package), incapable host,
  empty or skip-only suite or container profile is recorded as blocked; failures and
  deadlines are failed; nothing is ever promoted to passed. A second baseline for a
  repository whose baseline is still running is refused with 409 naming that run.
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines`: recorded baselines with their check results,

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
bound to manifest hash, commit, tree and environment fingerprint. Each result's
  `artifact_refs` (and the keys of `artifact_hashes`) are `{recipe}.{stdout|stderr}`;
  baselines recorded before 2026-10-21 carry `artifact:{run}:{recipe}:{stream}` refs keyed
  `stdout`/`stderr`; their logs are served under the new identity when the recipe ID is
  lower-case (other IDs now map to escaped file names, so case-insensitive filesystems
  and Windows device names cannot mix logs up).
- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{recipe}.{stdout|stderr}`: the private check log by
  record identity (text, capped at 16 MiB).

- `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`: `{ "idempotency_key", "title", "intent", "acceptance_criteria": [...], "repository_ids": [...] }`
  creates a legacy temporary ticket or an enabled project's Missions-backed ticket (201; 200 when the key repeats with the same content,
  409 when it repeats with different content). `GET` lists them; `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}`
  reads one, with `usage` (`workflows`, `attempts`, `elapsed_seconds`, `cost_usd_micros`,
  `cost_unreported`, `repairs`) summed over every workflow of its plan revisions. This is the
  only ticket creation route (ADR 0005).
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/components` reports activation/toolchain state. `POST` initializes
  private managed component stores and migrates legacy ticket IDs/revisions without importing

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
developer or personal stores. Incomplete activation freezes affected actions until reconciled.
- `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/source` observes authoritative Missions freshness/status/dependencies;
  `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/reconcile` with `{ "expected_revision" }` advances a changed projection.
  Ticket GET/list retain the last reconciled view; external changes block stale work and require
  a new plan after reconciliation. Missing components fail closed for enabled projects.
- `GET/POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/memory` retrieves/creates Atlas memory with explicit scope and
  provenance. User memory retrieval needs `include_user=true`; creation requires
  `{ "idempotency_key", "scope": "project|process|user", "content", "provenance" }`.
  `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}/memory/{memory_id}?expected_hash=...` checks the displayed hash.
  `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/memory/{memory_id}/promote` with `{ "idempotency_key", "expected_hash", "to_scope": "project|user" }`
  widens a memory one step (process to project, project to user), creating the wider record with
  provenance naming its origin and deleting the narrower one under the intent ledger (ADR 0021).
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/export`: the confirmed manifest, ticket projections, project and
  process memory and current prompts, with `omitted` naming what never leaves this host. The
  export is refused (409) rather than redacted when any string would carry user memory, a

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
credential value, the data directory, a registered checkout path, the home directory or an
  absolute path of this host's shapes.
- `POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose`: `{ "profile", "name", "parent_dir" }` returns a hashed
  `ScaffoldProposal` (files, baseline recipes, generator and network steps, tool probes,
  `ready|blocked`) and writes nothing. `POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold` with
  `{ "proposal_hash", "idempotency_key", "confirm": true, "confirm_network"? }` writes the files,
  commits, runs the baseline recipe through the supervised executor, registers the project, runs
  discovery and records `project.scaffolded`; a failing baseline is returned as such (ADR 0019).
  Discovery responses carry `host_capabilities` and each proposed check its `capability` and
  `missing_tools`.
- `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publish`: `{ "expected_hash", "idempotency_key" }` publishes a `reviewed`
  candidate with a `passed` review to GitHub (push of the exact commit to
  `luuna/<ticket>/<hash prefix>`, one linked pull request per repository), once per key, under a
  durable intent ledger. `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/publication` returns the record with CI and merge
  observation refreshed; `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publication/reconcile` retries only missing
  steps. There is no merge operation (ADR 0018). Needs `LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN`; `LUUNA_GITHUB_API_URL`
  selects the REST base for tests.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
- `GET/POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/prompts` lists/creates Beacon prompts. Creation/update requires
  `{ "idempotency_key", "name", "body", "expected_version"? }`; an existing name needs its current
  expected version. `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/prompts/{name}/render?version=...` previews exact
  current content/version/hash. A stale version is refused.
- `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans`: `{ "task": { "repository_id", "paths": [...], "operations": [...] }, "permissions"?, "budgets"?, "component_context"?, "idempotency_key"? }`
  records the next immutable plan revision bound by the runtime to the ticket revision, the
  current manifest hash, its recorded base commit and its recipes, and opens the workflow run
  (`plan_ready`). Returns `{ plan, run, ticket_usage }` (201); `ticket_usage` is the ticket's
  `usage` above, so an approver sees what earlier revisions spent before approving fresh
  budgets. An `idempotency_key` (1..=128 visible ASCII characters) replays: the same key and
  request return the plan and workflow it created (200), a different request is 409. Earlier
  revisions still `plan_ready` or `approved` can never be approved or implemented again and are
  settled `cancelled` with a `plan.superseded` event. `GET` lists a ticket's plans; `GET /api/v1/plans/{id}`
  reads the latest revision. Optional selection is `{ "memory_ids": [...], "prompt": { "name", "version", "hash" }? }`;

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
the runtime resolves exact content/provenance snapshots into the canonical immutable plan.
  Approval and worker/evidence boundaries recheck selected source freshness. The application
  sends only explicitly selected, approved content to the writer/reviewer (ADR 0014).
- `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/approvals`: `{ "plan_revision", "plan_hash", "approved_by" }` approves
  exactly that hash; permissions are copied from the plan. Returns `{ approval, run }` with the
  run `approved`; a stale hash or revision returns 409.
- `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement`: `{ "task_id"?, "provider"?, "model"? }` schedules the
  writer (202) after revalidating the approval, ticket revision, manifest, base commit, passed
  baseline, host fingerprint, repository HEAD, lease exclusivity and attempt budget; any refusal
  is 409/422 with the reason and leaves the run `approved`. One writer per repository is
  re-checked in the transaction that admits the writer, so a concurrent second workflow gets
  409 rather than a 202 whose writer then fails. The writer runs the pinned Pi inside a
  Luuna-owned detached worktree under the data directory with file tools only and the scope
  guard loaded; in-scope changes become a candidate commit and the run enters `validating`.
- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/worktrees`, `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/attempts`: the run's worktree
  leases (path, base, state, candidate commit) and its attempts. A settled attempt keeps the

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
provider, model, host fingerprint, Pi version and `trigger` (`implement`, `repair`,
  `automatic_repair`) it was admitted with beside its reason and usage.

Repository inspection runs `git` with optional locks disabled and repository-controlled
`core.fsmonitor`/hooks neutralised, so the developer's index and working tree stay
byte-identical. Remote URLs are redacted before storage. Registering or confirming a
project enables no write or plan transition. Feature implementation can be entered only
through the storage gate that checks the durable approval, the current manifest and a
passed, matching baseline per repository in one transaction (see ADR 0007); the first
writer that uses that gate is M2c.

Only one runtime can own a data directory. Startup recovery marks abandoned
active attempts interrupted after obtaining that exclusive ownership. A
Ctrl+C or SIGTERM shutdown (on Windows also Ctrl+Break, console close and system
shutdown, best effort because Windows ends the process within seconds; use the
endpoint above from a supervisor) closes admission, signals owned workers to
stop, waits for supervised cleanup (process groups reaped, at most five seconds),
and records the stopped work as `interrupted` with the reason "interrupted by
runtime shutdown …", the same resumable state a hard kill leaves after restart;
`cancelled` is reserved for the developer's cancel request (ADR 0004). Every

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
step is bounded, so the process always exits; a second Ctrl+C or SIGTERM exits
at once (status 130) without waiting, leaving any unsettled work to restart
recovery. Shutdown start, the number of signalled runs and the outcome are
written to stderr.

Every worker (demo run, baseline, writer, validation with its automatic
repairs) runs under a supervisor. If a worker panics, its run settles `failed`
with the reason "internal error: the runtime worker stopped unexpectedly", its
slot is released, and unreported spend is reserved as restart recovery reserves
it: a running attempt takes the remaining approved time and cost, a candidate
stage keeps its elapsed time (a review also the remaining cost) and an active
lease is abandoned with its files preserved. Deadlines derived from an approved
budget saturate instead of overflowing the platform clock.
At most four runs (demo, baseline, writer or validation) may be active at once. Prompt acknowledgements and low-level
`agent_end` events do not complete a run: Pi 1.3.0's `agent_settled` is required.
Completion means the connectivity request finished, not a feature passed
validation or a publication was approved.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
Each attempt records a `pi.spawned` event with the owned child's PID, the
required Pi version, and the names (never values) of provider credentials the
child received. The terminal `run.*` event is persisted only after that child
has been stopped and reaped, so a PID that is still alive after a terminal event
is a defect. On Unix, `SIGTERM` and Ctrl+C both take the orderly shutdown path.

Session system prompts reach Pi as a private file (`--system-prompt <path>`),
never as argv text. Pi runs offline, so its `grep` and `find` tools work only
where ripgrep (`rg`) and fd (`fd` or `fdfind`) are already on PATH; writers and
reviewers omit them otherwise, and `pi.spawned`/`review.started` list the
`omitted_tools` with the reason. When Pi exits or stops reading, the failure
reason includes its exit status and a redacted 2 KiB tail of its stderr (for
example an unknown provider). Records over 1 MiB fail the session, except the
session events whose size grows with the run (`agent_end` and `turn_end` repeat
every tool result): those are read as a bounded summary marked `luuna_summary`.

title: Local runtime connectivity foundation
text:
`node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider

--model ` drives a built runtime binary through the full M1 checklist (authentication, SSE streaming, settlement before completion, in-flight cancellation with reaping, provider failure, hard-kill restart interruption, exclusive ownership, orderly shutdown) and writes a sanitized `report.md`/`report.json`. `--mode fixture` runs the same checklist against the synthetic fixture and is never provider evidence. `cargo test -p luuna-runtime -p luuna-engine-pi` uses the labeled synthetic Python protocol fixture in `fixtures/pi-rpc`. Python 3 is required for these subprocess tests. The genuine credential-free RPC probe is documented there.

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text:
## Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)

After a writer records a candidate, `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/candidate` returns its exact commit/tree/hash, validation generation, checks, structured review, active state and the runtime's decisions: `validate_allowed`, `repair_allowed`, `revalidate_allowed` and `decision_reasons` (`validate`, `repair`, `revalidate`: the refusal the route would give, or `null`), computed by the same storage gates the routes apply; repository, host and component-source checks stay with the routes. It also reports `usage`: the whole workflow (writer attempts, validation and review) against the approved plan as `{ attempts, max_attempts, elapsed_seconds, timeout_seconds, cost_usd_micros, cost_budget_usd_micros, cost_unreported, repairs, max_repairs }`. `cost_unreported` is true once a writer or reviewer reported tokens without a cost (an unpriced, custom or local model; a `usage.cost_unreported` event records it): such a model is not refused, but the cost budget is enforced against Pi's price table only and does not meter that spend. Pi's compaction (summarization) usage is charged with the session's messages. `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/diff` returns the diff between the frozen base and candidate commits with repository-selected execution drivers, text conversion, filters and `-diff`/`binary` attributes neutralised (binary or non-UTF-8 content is summarised by blob ID), `truncated`, every changed

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text:
path in `files` with how it is shown (`text`, `summary`, `omitted`), `attention_paths` for changed `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore`/`.gitmodules`, and `worktree_drift` when the owned worktree no longer holds the candidate.

`POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` accepts `{ "candidate_hash": "sha256:…", "provider": "…", "model": "…", "auto_repair": false }`. Provider/model may use server defaults. Each validation generation first verifies the owned worktree's HEAD, tree and tracked content and removes every untracked and ignored path (`candidate.worktree_cleaned` records them), so checks and review see exactly the candidate tree. A worktree changed outside Luuna, or tracked content a check rewrites, fails the candidate with a `candidate content drift:` reason naming the paths and next step (repair or the next plan revision); such a candidate is never re-validated in place. Required checks execute in the owned worktree through the supervised executor. A fresh Pi process with read-only tools reviews requirements/code/check records and a diff bounded to 256 KiB of whole file sections plus every changed path, without the implementation conversation; its tool calls are recorded as `review.tool_call` events (tool name and path only), and output that is not a valid, self-consistent review (a `changes_required` or `blocked` verdict must name a finding) is kept as the private artifact `<reviewer session>.stdout` and leaves no verdict. A valid

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text: pass reaches `reviewed`; infrastructure failures, invalid output, stale identities and blocking findings never pass. The same request re-validates a `failed` candidate in place when every required recipe passed in its current generation and no review verdict was recorded (invalid or self-inconsistent reviewer output, a refused reviewer session): generation `n+1` of the same revision opens under the same approval and budgets, the checks run again, a fresh reviewer starts with the generation named in its prompt, and no writer attempt is spent. A failed, blocked or interrupted check, a recorded verdict of any kind, and reserved spend from a reviewer lost mid-turn are refused with 409/422, as for repair. The test-count heuristic recognises cargo, go, pytest, vitest/jest and Python `unittest` summaries; a passed command that reports zero tests is blocked as an empty suite.

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text: `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/repair` accepts the same candidate hash and optional model settings. The repair gate rechecks current approval, ticket/manifest/base, passed host-matching baseline and all aggregate budgets. Repairs create a fresh candidate revision and require fresh checks/review. The repair writer's prompt quotes the previous candidate's reason, check records, structured review and the last 2 KiB of each failed check's recorded stdout/stderr, at most 16 KiB in total measured after JSON encoding with the last entry cut from the front to fit, from at most 32 artifacts and 64 MiB read per repair on a blocking thread, each opened without following links and labelled from the check result's recorded `truncated_artifacts` when the executor cut it at its 16 MiB cap (with every configured provider credential value of any length and the service token redacted longest-first from the whole artifact before the tail is cut, PEM private-key blocks and bearer/API-token-shaped lines removed best effort, and only when the artifact still matches the digest recorded with the check result), because the writer has no shell and cannot read private artifacts; a repair that only saw an exit code could not act on it. Set `auto_repair: true` on validation to opt into bounded repair cycles for ordinary failed commands or `changes_required` reviews; infrastructure failures stop without automatic edits. The existing cancel endpoint covers the a

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text:
ctive pipeline, including automatic repairs. Candidate log artifact IDs include `c{revision}-g{generation}-{recipe}.{stdout|stderr}`.

While a validation or review stage runs, its durable heartbeat (`stage_checkpoint_at`) is stamped every five seconds; restart recovery charges an interrupted stage up to its last heartbeat plus one interval, so time the runtime was down is not charged, and the stage needs a fresh generation. A reviewer's provider spend is unknown from the durable `review.prompt_sent` marker, written just before its prompt, until `review.usage_settled`; only a restart in that window reserves the remaining approved cost budget, so recovery can require a new plan/approval rather than retry with fresh budget. A reviewer interrupted before its prompt can simply be validated again. Reviewer usage is persisted when a message completes, the session ends or the budget check fails, not per streaming record, and a provider error that Pi retries itself (`agent_end` with `willRetry`) does not fail the review. An automatic repair whose writer fails pauses with that writer's own reason (`automatic repair writer failed: …`) and whether another repair may follow; automatic repair writers run on the validation request's provider and model. A repair writer is told it starts from the previous candidate's commit, and quoted check output names files relative to the repository root rather than the previous attempt's worktree. Native

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text:
host permissions remain unchanged. No publication or merge endpoint is introduced. Real-provider M3 acceptance is recorded separately from deterministic fixture evidence. `node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider

--model ` drives a built runtime binary through the M3 checklist on a disposable fixture repository: register/confirm/baseline with a real `unittest` check, an approved feature → required check → fresh independent reviewer, a seeded failing check → manual repair revision 2 → fresh evidence, a blocking-review probe under bounded `auto_repair`, cancellation while the reviewer is in flight (child reaped), a hard-kill restart during review (interrupted, spend reserved, re-validation refused), developer-checkout integrity and orderly shutdown; in fixture mode only, a sixth scenario re-validates a candidate whose synthetic reviewer returned invalid output after passed checks (no real provider can be made to do that on demand). It writes a sanitized `report.md`/`report.json` that records credential names only and is scanned for leaked values. `--mode fixture` runs the same checklist against the synthetic fixture and is labeled synthetic; it is never provider evidence. The harness builds the runtime itself from the committed tree (`cargo build --locked -p luuna-runtime` with the pinned toolchain's own cargo and rustc, into a new empty target directory for every run, no `--config`, an allowlisted environment; `

title: Candidate checks, independent review and repair (M3)
text: --runtime` is refused), starts it once without any provider credential to verify its provenance, and gives credentials only to that verified binary: `build.rs` embeds a SHA-256 over every build input, `/health` reports it as `build_identity`, and each run fails unless it equals the digest of the checkout's build inputs and those inputs have no modified or untracked file. On Linux the leak scan and quarantine resolve paths through held directory handles; elsewhere the run records that they are unavailable and refuses recursive cleanup. On Linux the harness also re-executes itself under a `python3` child subreaper and kills every process of the run that survives the runtime before the leak scan (elsewhere containment cannot be established, so that check fails and the scan is marked untrusted), then re-checks that the Luuna checkout is still the recorded revision, clean, with the same build inputs, Git metadata, history (every object reachable from any ref, verified by `git fsck --full`) and ignored files (outside `target/`, `node_modules/` and `dist/`); a Cargo config file that mentions `paths`, `include`, `replace-with`, `patch`, `profile`, `rustc`, `linker` or `env`, or contains a backslash, fails the build-provenance check, as does a binary whose reported `build_rustc_sha256` differs from the pinned toolchain's `rustc` (located with `rustup which`), so evidence builds use a `CARGO_HOME` without such config.

title: Backup and restore
text:
## Backup and restore

The database (`<data>/luuna.sqlite3`) runs in WAL mode: recent commits can sit in `luuna.sqlite3-wal` until a checkpoint. Never copy only the main file while the runtime runs, and never put an older main file back beside a `-wal`; SQLite would replay the newer log onto it and corrupt it. Use these commands. Each takes `--data-dir <dir>`; the default is the service's own (`LUUNA_DATA_DIR`, else `.luuna`). See [ADR 0016](../../docs/decisions/0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md).

- `luuna-runtime backup --output <file>` writes a consistent snapshot while the runtime is running. It never overwrites a file, and it prints the schema version, size and SHA-256.
- `luuna-runtime restore --input <file>` needs the runtime stopped; it is refused while a runtime owns the data directory. It verifies the snapshot's integrity and schema version, moves the current database and any `-wal`/`-shm` to `<data>/backups/replaced-<timestamp>/`, and installs the snapshot. On the next start, work that was active in the snapshot is recorded `interrupted`, never successful.
- `luuna-runtime check` reports integrity (`PRAGMA quick_check`) and the schema version without writing. It is safe while the runtime runs and exits non-zero on a problem.

title: Backup and restore
text:
What a snapshot covers: the database snapshot holds projects, manifests, plans, approvals, runs, events, leases, attempts and the check/review evidence records. Check artifacts, worktrees, attempt directories and managed component stores are files in the data directory. A complete backup is a copy of the whole data directory taken after an orderly stop (`POST /api/v1/shutdown`, Ctrl+C or the stop script), which checkpoints the log. To restore a complete copy, stop the runtime and replace the directory as a whole.

Schema compatibility: at startup the runtime refuses a database that fails `quick_check` or that was written by a newer schema. The message names the file and `luuna-runtime restore`. Before migrating an existing database to a newer schema, the runtime saves `<data>/backups/pre-migration-v<old>-<timestamp>.sqlite3`. These snapshots are never deleted automatically. To step back to the build that wrote one, stop the runtime, run `luuna-runtime restore --input <snapshot>`, then start that older build.

Startup recovery skips a record it cannot decode instead of refusing to start. It logs the table and ID to stderr, never the content. Where the record has a state column, that column is settled: the record is interrupted or abandoned, never resumed.

title: Diagnostics
text:
## Diagnostics

`luuna-runtime doctor [--data-dir <dir>] [--json]` reports the host prerequisites (Git, Python, Node, the pinned Pi probe without a model call), the data directory and database, `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` and `LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN` presence, configured provider credential names, the service port and the component toolchain. It exits 1 when Git, Pi or a writable data directory is missing or an existing database is unusable, and never prints a credential value (ADR 0018).

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text:
# Luuna desktop foundation

The React frontend connects to the independent Rust runtime. It lists persisted runs, starts a tool-free Pi conversation, displays text and raw events, reconnects through durable cursor replay, and requests cancellation. The Projects panel registers an existing repository root by absolute path, shows the runtime's read-only observation (redacted remote, HEAD, branch, dirty counts), requests a discovery proposal, lets you edit the proposed manifest JSON and confirms it with the current revision guard; the project event record replays from the runtime. Run baseline starts the confirmed required recipes on a clean checkout and lists the recorded evidence; the baseline run appears in the session history with its check events.

The workflow section creates a temporary local ticket, records a plan revision for the registered repository, presents the complete immutable plan and full hash for acknowledgment and approval, then schedules the writer. Writers change only Luuna-owned worktrees under the runtime's data directory. Inspect candidate diff shows the exact candidate hash and commit. Validate and review requests the approved recipes followed by a fresh independent reviewer session; check commands, environment fingerprints, artifact hashes/logs, structured findings and recorded reasons remain bound to that candidate. Repair candidate requests another bounded writer attempt under the existing approval. T

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text:
he optional automatic repair checkbox lets validation request repairs within those same approved budgets; it is off initially. Workflow provider/model fields apply to the next action and can use the runtime defaults. Active work exposes cancellation; an idle candidate awaiting validation does not. An interrupted validation can be retried with fresh check and review evidence. A failed candidate whose required checks passed but whose reviewer produced no verdict (invalid or self-inconsistent output) shows Re-validate and review when the runtime allows it: a fresh validation generation for the same candidate revision under the existing approval and budgets, spending no writer attempt. Publication remains a later milestone.

From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:1420`. Start the runtime separately using the [root development instructions](../../README.md), then enter its URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:4242`) and `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` in the connection form. Provider/model fields may use the runtime defaults. Model credentials belong in the runtime environment; they are never entered in this UI. Only HTTP loopback runtime addresses are accepted. The service token stays in memory and is discarded on disconnect or reload.

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text:
The live view polls the authenticated replay API using its last event sequence every 700 ms. Reconnecting repeats events safely without losing ordering or duplicating records. The persisted run state determines completion; text from Pi does not establish that a run or validation succeeded.

A runtime that stops answering is shown as an outage beside the connection state ("Reconnecting to runtime", with a note that runs, candidates and worktrees are durable); the client keeps polling, and when the runtime answers again it reloads every panel, so work the runtime marked `interrupted` on restart appears with its reason and the next allowed action. Every refused action is reported as "<Action> refused: <the runtime's reason>" followed by what to do next (re-plan, repair, re-validate, run a baseline, wait for active work, reconnect); transport failures and server errors are described in plain words and no server body is ever shown. Every control is reachable and operable by keyboard: a "Skip to main content" link is the first Tab stop, buttons and checkboxes work with Enter and Space, and the event lists, diff, log and plan panes are focusable scroll regions; connection and activity changes are announced through live regions.

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text: Presentation follows the [desktop design system](../../docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) ([ADR 0013](../../docs/decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md)). Tokens live in `src/design/tokens.css`, and the client follows the operating system's light or dark scheme, dark by default. Every runtime state keeps its exact text and gains one of six tones: success, active, danger, attention, neutral or interrupted. Each tone has a colour and a shape mark, and only passed evidence and a live connection are green. Badges go through `StatusBadge`, and the state-to-tone maps in `src/design/tone.ts` are exhaustive over the API types. `src/design/design-system.test.ts`, run by `npm test`, rejects literal colours and sizes outside the tokens. It also enforces WCAG AA contrast for every semantic pair in both schemes, the heading levels and dismissible alerts.

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text:
`node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` drives this client in headless Chromium against a built runtime and the synthetic Pi fixture through the [MVP walkthrough](../../docs/MVP-WALKTHROUGH.md): keyboard connection, refused token and registration, import, baseline, ticket, plan, approval, writer, diff, an invalid review followed by re-validation, a hard kill and an orderly shutdown during checks with reconnection and resumption, a hard kill during review with the budget refusal, an accessibility audit, a presentation audit (WCAG AA contrast of every visible text run against its painted background in the dark and light schemes, scheme following, and no horizontal scroll at the 760 px window minimum) and disconnect. It needs the client port 1420 free (the runtime's CORS allowlist admits only that origin) and writes `report.md`, `report.json` and screenshots to `--out`. It is client and lifecycle evidence, never provider evidence.

For the native Tauri 2 window:

```sh
npm run desktop
```

This requires the pinned Rust toolchain and [Tauri system prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/). Linux additionally needs GTK 3, WebKitGTK 4.1 and their development packages; a headless cloud machine can use the browser frontend. The shell has no filesystem, process or shell plugin permissions. Runtime lifecycle is manual at this milestone and closing the desktop does not stop the service.

Validation:

title: Luuna desktop foundation
text:
```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm test
cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
```

The native application is a separate Cargo workspace with its own checked-in lockfile, so headless Rust runtime checks do not require GUI libraries. Native installers and automatic runtime startup remain later work.

title: Luuna repository instructions
text: # Luuna repository instructions

title: Read and preserve
text:
## Read and preserve

Read `docs/CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/decisions/`, and `AI-START-HERE.md` before implementation. Current architecture and accepted ADRs resolve conflicts in older proposals. Original requirements remain full-v1 obligations unless explicitly revised. Preserve historical reference documents and existing functionality.

Inspect `git status` before and after work. Preserve user changes. In cloud tasks, use the existing isolated checkout; do not create a Git worktree unless explicitly requested. Luuna's future managed execution worktrees are a separate product feature. Do not commit, push, publish, or create external resources without task authorization.

title: Build the foundation first
text:
## Build the foundation first

Prioritize bounded M0/M1 slices: deterministic contracts/policy, durable state, then genuine supervised Pi RPC streaming and cancellation. Do not scaffold unrelated empty crates or implement the complete roadmap in one pass. Keep domain rules in the runtime; clients display authoritative state.

Use pinned toolchains, lockfiles, and repository-supported commands. Required checks must match the affected code. Report actual commands and failures; a fixture, model statement, frontend build, or missing check cannot establish real-provider or platform success. Keep the original documentation validation report separate from product test evidence.

title: Enforce product policy
text:
## Enforce product policy
